requirements.text: If Home Core crashes/restarts, attached apps MUST enter a degraded/reconnecting state for Home-dependent features, preserve their own user data, and reconnect to restored shared services.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Dulche runtime control
requirements.text: Apps MUST NOT launch private replacement Dulche servers during recovery.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Permission and trust broker
requirements.text: Settings MUST expose a Permissions & Trust management surface where the user can inspect caller identity/origin, granted apps/actions/scopes, trust level, creation/expiry, last-use metadata where available, and revoke/block/unblock/narrow grants.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Permission and trust broker
requirements.text: Revocation MUST affect future actions immediately subject to in-flight action semantics defined by the target API.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Mesh
requirements.text: Every Mesh device MUST have a stable DeviceID bound to an authenticated device identity/key rather than a mutable device name.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Mesh
requirements.text: Pairing MUST require explicit user/account authorisation and establish an authenticated encrypted relationship.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Mesh
requirements.text: A device advertises supported 9to1 capabilities/services and versions; peers MUST NOT assume capabilities that were not advertised.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Mesh
requirements.text: Mesh data sharing/sync MUST be namespace/object scoped.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Mesh
requirements.text: Personal Mesh may sync selected personal Den/chat/context/project state; Team/Organisation modes may sync explicitly shared team/org state while preserving personal/private namespaces.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Mesh
requirements.text: Joining Mesh MUST NOT automatically share all local files, secrets, model context or app data.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Mesh
requirements.text: Remote capability invocation MUST use typed APIs and pass both caller-side and target-device permission/policy checks.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Mesh
requirements.text: Mesh MUST NOT become an implicit generic remote-desktop, mouse/keyboard or arbitrary-code-execution channel.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Mesh
requirements.text: Lost/revoked devices MUST be removable from Home.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Action Graph renderer
requirements.text: Any authorised app MAY host the shared renderer given an authorised RequestID/ActionGraphID.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Action Graph renderer
requirements.text: Home MUST NOT create a second execution history or mutate Dulche’s causal graph merely for presentation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Action Graph renderer
requirements.text: Events, Agents, Spaces and other surfaces MAY deep-link into the same renderer.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.text: Home owns the reusable base component/service contract for the global persistent bottom AI bar required by interactive 9to1 apps.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.text: Each host app MUST provide the bar with a permission-filtered semantic context snapshot and its typed supported actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.text: Home MUST NOT obtain app context through raw screen scraping when the host provides structured context.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Floating compose @ invocation menu
requirements.text: The shared Home-owned floating AI compose component MUST provide one searchable @ invocation menu for Plugins, Skills, Apps, Agents and Files.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Floating compose @ invocation menu
requirements.text: The rendered token MUST display the resource's icon where available plus its human-readable label, for example an Agent may render as '@[agent icon] John'.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Floating compose @ invocation menu
requirements.text: The token MUST use a distinct invoked visual state, including colour/style differentiation, while also using non-colour cues for accessibility.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Floating compose @ invocation menu
requirements.text: Invocation tokens MUST store stable canonical identities, not only display text: Plugin PackageID/version or resolved active version, SkillID/version, AppID, AgentID/DefinitionRevision where required and File/Artifact reference identity/revision or access token as appropriate.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Floating compose @ invocation menu
requirements.text: Duplicate display names MUST therefore remain unambiguous.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Floating compose @ invocation menu
requirements.text: The Apps section MUST contain every installed/available first-party 9to1 app plus user-installed applications that 9to1 can classify as safely operable through a typed API/integration or, when separately authorised, Computer Use.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Floating compose @ invocation menu
requirements.text: App entries MUST expose whether their interaction path is Typed/API, Computer Use Required, or both.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Floating compose @ invocation menu
requirements.text: Selecting an app whose only route is Computer Use MUST NOT activate Computer Use by itself; the request also requires the explicit @Computer Use invocation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Floating compose @ invocation menu
requirements.text: Game executables and anti-cheat-protected game surfaces MUST be excluded from the operable Apps invocation results even when discovered through Steam, Epic Games Launcher or another launcher/library.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Floating compose @ invocation menu
requirements.text: If 9to1 cannot confidently distinguish an eligible ordinary application from a game/anti-cheat target, it MUST omit or mark the target unavailable for Computer Use rather than risk automation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Floating compose @ invocation menu
requirements.text: Selecting it creates the explicit ComputerUseInvocationID required by the Dulche Computer Use contract and makes its active state visible in the compose field before the request is submitted.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Cross-app execution visualisation
requirements.text: Models operating inside any 9to1 app MAY invoke another 9to1 app only when the user's request explicitly names/invokes that app, directly asks for an outcome owned by that app, or unambiguously implies the owning app from the requested artifact/action.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Cross-app execution visualisation
requirements.text: For example, 'create a presentation' resolves to Present; 'make a spreadsheet' resolves to Data; an unrelated app MUST NOT be opened merely because the model thinks it might be useful.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Cross-app execution visualisation
requirements.text: Cross-app intent resolution MUST bind to the owning app's stable AppID and typed capability contract.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Cross-app execution visualisation
requirements.text: If the required app is not running, Home MAY launch/open it automatically when that is part of fulfilling the request.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Cross-app execution visualisation
requirements.text: Where an app has a visible editing surface, the user SHOULD be able to watch model-driven edits occur in real time.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Cross-app execution visualisation
requirements.text: Home/shared app infrastructure MUST provide an execution-visualisation stream that maps semantic actions to visible UI changes such as objects moving, text appearing, selections changing, slides being created or a virtual cursor hovering over the affected target.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Cross-app execution visualisation
requirements.text: A virtual cursor MUST be visually distinguishable from the user's real pointer and MUST NOT generate mouse/keyboard input merely to make the animation believable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Cross-app execution visualisation
requirements.text: The canonical typed API/action result remains authoritative; visual animation follows confirmed/provisional semantic events and MUST reconcile to final app state after errors, retries or rollback.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > AI conversation presentation settings
requirements.text: Home Settings MUST expose global conversation presentation preferences for Plain text versus Speech bubbles.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > AI conversation presentation settings
requirements.text: User-message alignment and model-message alignment MUST be independently configurable as Left or Right.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > AI conversation presentation settings
requirements.text: Alignment changes presentation only and MUST NOT alter message order, authorship, accessibility reading order or exported conversation data.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > AI conversation presentation settings
requirements.text: The selected Dulche thinking-log mode (Precise, Concise, Detailed or Ramble) MUST be configurable in the same AI/conversation settings family.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > AI conversation presentation settings
requirements.text: Thinking/work presentation MUST use lower visual emphasis than normal chat while remaining readable and accessible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > AI conversation presentation settings
requirements.text: Collapsed 'Thought for ...'/'Worked for ...', ETA status, blockers and Problem events MUST use the same shared renderer across apps so equivalent Runtime state is not represented differently by each product.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: App shells MAY provide different workflows and layout chrome, but a shared object type MUST use the same schema, formatting semantics, rendering rules and typed object actions wherever that type is supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: The initial required shared object families include rich text/paragraphs, headings, lists/checklists, code blocks, equations, tables, images/media, drawings/ink, graph objects and typed embedded 9to1 artifact references.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: The registry MUST be extensible so a new shared object type can be implemented once and enabled in multiple supporting surfaces without rewriting its core editor/renderer.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: Every shared object instance MUST have a stable ObjectID within its owning artifact plus a versioned ObjectType/schema identifier.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: Object content, formatting, accessibility metadata, asset references and app-neutral layout properties MUST be serialisable independently from transient UI state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: Unknown required schema versions MUST fail explicitly rather than being silently flattened or reinterpreted.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: Shared object schemas MUST preserve enough information for semantically identical rendering/editing across participating apps.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: If an app cannot support a property, it MUST retain that property in the object payload when round-tripping and surface the limitation instead of destructively stripping it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: The engine MUST provide a shared versioned style registry for reusable text/paragraph/object style definitions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: App-specific style extensions MAY exist but MUST preserve shared base properties when transferred.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: The engine MUST provide a versioned ProductivityObjectBundle clipboard/transfer format containing shared object payloads, style definitions, asset references, accessibility metadata and a portable fallback representation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: Copying a supported object from one participating app and pasting it into another MUST preserve the same shared-object semantics and appearance rather than converting it to an image or lossy app-specific approximation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: When the destination does not support that object type but supports embedded 9to1 artifacts, the UI MUST offer an embed/reference path.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: Spaces MUST use the Shared Productivity Engine for rich pasted/embedded content so tables, code blocks, drawings, graphs and other shared objects preserve their structure instead of degrading to plain text.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: Spaces may present a conversational shell around the object, but editing MUST route through the same shared object actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: The engine MUST provide shared selection, focus, formatting, object insertion/removal, resize/transform where applicable, clipboard, accessibility and undoable action primitives for shared object types.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: Shared actions MUST have stable typed representations so compatible apps can participate in undo/recovery and AI/Automation execution without reproducing hidden per-app commands.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: App-specific shells MAY add contextual commands, but MUST NOT fork the underlying object semantics into incompatible versions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: Object actions MUST be exposed through typed APIs and usable by UI, Spaces, Automations and Dulche-driven AI without raw UI simulation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: The shared engine MUST emit semantic selection/context information for the persistent AI bar and app-specific contextual toolbars.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: This context MUST contain stable object/selection identity rather than requiring consumers to infer meaning from rendered pixels.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: The shared engine MUST expose the Rnote-derived drawing/ink engine as a reusable shared object/layer so Canvas and Boards use the same stroke model, pen/eraser behaviours and serialisation primitives.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: Other productivity surfaces MAY opt into the same drawing object without implementing a separate ink stack.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: Home Core MUST expose the Shared Productivity Engine as a versioned shared platform capability.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: Apps may link/embed approved shared engine libraries/components as part of their package for rendering performance, but the canonical schema registry, compatibility negotiation and shared service/version authority remain Home-owned.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: Apps MUST validate compatible engine/schema versions during startup.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: Shared object schemas and ProductivityObjectBundle MUST be versioned independently of individual app versions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: Home MUST expose compatibility negotiation so an older app can detect a newer unsupported shared object type/property before editing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: Compatible unknown optional properties MUST be preserved; incompatible required features MUST produce a structured compatibility state rather than silent data loss.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: Each shared object type MUST also expose its typed creation/update/query actions through the owning app/API surface required by the global API-parity rule.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Settings
requirements.text: The Settings surface MUST include at least Account & Subscription, Appearance/CUI, AI & Models, Permissions & Trust, Apps & Updates, Storage, Mesh & Devices, Privacy, Accessibility, Notifications and Advanced/Diagnostics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Settings
requirements.text: Settings changes MUST use typed settings keys/schemas with validation and explicit scope (device, account, workspace/team or organisation where applicable).

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Settings
requirements.text: Unknown or incompatible settings versions MUST NOT be silently discarded during upgrade/downgrade.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Home-managed CUI theme preference
requirements.text: Home Settings → Appearance/CUI MUST let the user select their preferred complete CUI theme (Professional, Glow, Playful, Frosted Glass, Bubble, Metallic, Retro, Western or an available compatible custom theme).

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Home-managed CUI theme preference
requirements.text: Preference scope MUST be explicit: device-local when unauthenticated; when signed in, the applicable user/account preference MUST be available consistently to the user's supported 9to1 apps and devices via normal authorised settings synchronisation, without merging unrelated users' or organisations' preferences.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Home-managed CUI theme preference
requirements.text: Changing the preferred theme in Home MUST propagate to compatible running 9to1 app windows and newly opened app surfaces without requiring each app to implement its own theme picker, persist a competing selection or restart where live retheming is supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Home-managed CUI theme preference
requirements.text: Apps MUST render the effective preference through shared CUI theme resolution, honour accessibility/reduced-motion settings, and retain the selected theme across app closes/restarts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Account and subscription surface
requirements.text: Home MUST provide the primary native CAKE ID account/subscription surface.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Account and subscription surface
requirements.text: Home MUST NOT recalculate paid entitlements locally from a displayed tier label.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Account and subscription surface
requirements.text: Sign-out/session revocation actions MUST preserve local user data according to each app’s offline/storage policy rather than deleting it by default.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Notifications
requirements.text: Notifications MUST NOT encode consequential behaviour only as arbitrary executable callbacks.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Notifications
requirements.text: Home MUST support notification history, read/unread state, dismiss/clear subject to retention policy, per-source/category preferences and deep-link actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Notifications
requirements.text: Where Windows/9to1-OS system notifications are available, Home MAY bridge eligible notifications to the OS while retaining the canonical 9to1 notification record/state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared search and Go indexing
requirements.text: Apps MUST publish supported searchable entity metadata through a typed indexing contract rather than Home scraping arbitrary app databases.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared search and Go indexing
requirements.text: Search records MUST include stable source app, EntityID/type, title/display metadata, search/index text or vector references as permitted, modification state and current access-scope metadata.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared search and Go indexing
requirements.text: Search results MUST re-check current authorisation before exposing sensitive content or opening an entity; stale index access MUST NOT bypass revoked permissions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared search and Go indexing
requirements.text: On deletion/revocation, apps MUST be able to invalidate/remove affected index records.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Shared search and Go indexing
requirements.text: Home may maintain rebuildable indexes/caches, but the index MUST NOT become the only canonical copy of source content.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Service registry and compatibility handshake
requirements.text: Home Core MUST expose a machine-readable service registry describing Home-owned platform capabilities and versions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Service registry and compatibility handshake
requirements.text: Before normal startup, every native 9to1 app MUST complete a compatibility handshake against Home Core and declare the required service/capability versions it needs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Service registry and compatibility handshake
requirements.text: Missing/incompatible required services result in the global Home repair/update/bootstrap flow rather than undefined partial operation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Service registry and compatibility handshake
requirements.text: Service identity/version MUST be explicit; apps MUST NOT infer compatibility solely from the Home marketing version string.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Startup, background lifecycle and recovery
requirements.text: Home Core MUST auto-start on demand or at session startup when required by installed 9to1 apps.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Startup, background lifecycle and recovery
requirements.text: Closing the visible Home window MUST NOT necessarily stop Home Core.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Startup, background lifecycle and recovery
requirements.text: Home Core shutdown is allowed only when no required dependent operation is active or when the user/system explicitly requests full 9to1 service shutdown.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Startup, background lifecycle and recovery
requirements.text: Home Core persistent state MUST use crash-safe versioned storage.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Startup, background lifecycle and recovery
requirements.text: Corrupt or incompatible Home state MUST enter a diagnosable recovery/repair mode; Home MUST NOT silently discard permission grants, package state, device identities or other durable control-plane state to regain startup.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Startup, background lifecycle and recovery
requirements.text: If a Home service fails while apps are open, dependent apps MUST receive a structured service-unavailable/degraded signal.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Startup, background lifecycle and recovery
requirements.text: They MUST preserve their own artifact state and block only operations that require the failed service.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Home data/state model
requirements.text: Home MUST maintain stable IDs/versioned records for installed packages/apps, Home services, Dashboard layouts/tiles, Mesh devices/pairings, notification records, search index records, permission/trust grants, account/session cache metadata and other Home-owned settings/control-plane entities.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Home data/state model
requirements.text: Caches/indexes that are rebuildable MUST be marked as non-authoritative.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Home data/state model
requirements.text: Durable grants, package activation state, device trust and user layout/settings state MUST be recoverable and versioned.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Home data/state model
requirements.text: Home MUST distinguish device-local state from account/workspace-synchronised state explicitly.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Home API
requirements.text: Every additional user-visible Home operation MUST have an equivalent supported API/domain action under the global API-parity rule.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Home API
requirements.text: APIs MUST return structured state/errors and use stable IDs/revision checks for consequential or concurrent mutations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Security boundary
requirements.text: All local IPC/service calls MUST authenticate/identify the caller and evaluate the caller’s effective scopes before exposing privileged operations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Security boundary
requirements.text: Executable filename, window title or self-asserted display name MUST NOT be accepted as caller identity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Security boundary
requirements.text: Installed signed/registered apps MAY use package identity plus Home-issued process/session credentials.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Security boundary
requirements.text: Development/self-built callers MAY use an explicit registered developer/project identity with tamper-evident binding as defined by the global permission model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Security boundary
requirements.text: Trust MUST NOT silently transfer after a material caller identity/signing/content change.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Security boundary
requirements.text: Secrets/credentials MUST be stored through secure credential references and MUST NOT be persisted in plaintext Home configuration, logs, Events, Dashboard tiles or package manifests.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Security boundary
requirements.text: Home logs/audits MUST redact secret payloads while retaining accurate action/provenance records.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Platform behaviour
requirements.text: 9to1-OS: Home Core/shared service contracts remain authoritative platform services, but selected controls may be integrated into OS-native system surfaces.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Platform behaviour
requirements.text: The Universal Model Picker is OS-hosted while using the same canonical Dulche/model/provider state. 9to1-OS MUST NOT create divergent duplicate settings/package/model databases.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Platform behaviour
requirements.text: It MUST capability-negotiate and clearly mark local-only/native-only functions such as local package management, local models/devices or unavailable Home Core services rather than pretending they exist in-browser.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Failure behaviour
requirements.text: Home APIs/services MUST return structured failures including HomeServiceUnavailable, HomeServiceIncompatible, PackageIntegrityFailed, PackageDependencyConflict, PackageActivationFailed, DashboardRevisionConflict, TileProviderUnavailable, PermissionDenied, DeviceRevoked, MeshUnavailable, IndexUnavailable and AccountServiceUnavailable in addition to the global error contract.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Failure behaviour
requirements.text: Failures in one Home service MUST NOT automatically corrupt or erase unrelated Home state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Failure behaviour
requirements.text: For example, Discover/provider failure must not invalidate package state; search-index corruption must be recoverable by rebuilding the index; Dashboard tile-provider failure must degrade only affected tiles.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Acceptance requirements
requirements.text: An app with an incompatible required Home service version is blocked into update/repair instead of running against an undefined interface.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Node Graph Framework
requirements.text: The framework MUST provide a versioned graph data model, stable GraphID/NodeID/PortID identity, node registry, typed input/output ports, typed connections, node configuration schemas, pan/zoom/selection, grouping/comments, copy/paste/duplicate, undo/redo, validation, Draft/Active graph revision support, execution-state overlays and contextual AI-bar integration.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Node Graph Framework
requirements.text: Connections MUST be type-checked.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Node Graph Framework
requirements.text: Nodes and graph actions MUST reference canonical stable app/capability/entity IDs rather than screen coordinates or UI implementation details.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Node Graph Framework
requirements.text: The framework MUST support product-defined capability profiles.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Node Graph Framework
requirements.text: For example, built-in Spaces receive a constrained Events & Extensions node registry while user-created Spaces and Automations may receive broader registries.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Node Graph Framework
requirements.text: Graph mutation from the contextual AI bar MUST use typed graph APIs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Node Graph Framework
requirements.text: AI may add/remove/configure nodes and connections only within the current capability profile and permissions, and MUST NOT simulate mouse/keyboard graph editing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Node Graph Framework
requirements.text: Node Graph Framework compatibility and migration MUST be versioned.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Donor authority and parity
requirements.text: Unless a feature is explicitly replaced, excluded or made incompatible by an approved 9to1 architecture decision, Haven MUST retain mature Firefox functionality and quality-of-life behaviour.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Donor authority and parity
requirements.text: All Firefox proprietary or embedded AI surfaces are non-authoritative and MUST be removed or replaced by Dulche-backed 9to1 surfaces.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Donor authority and parity
requirements.text: The agent MUST NOT preserve a Firefox AI sidebar, chatbot, assistant or proprietary AI integration merely for donor parity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Web engine architecture
requirements.text: The normal user-facing choice SHOULD be labelled Firefox and Chromium; implementation and diagnostics MAY additionally expose the underlying Gecko and Blink engine names.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Web engine architecture
requirements.text: Engine-private runtime state such as DOM objects, JavaScript heaps and renderer-process memory is not required to transfer.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Web engine architecture
requirements.text: Haven MUST own canonical higher-level browser entities instead of allowing Gecko and Chromium to directly share raw profile databases.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Web engine architecture
requirements.text: At minimum the architecture must model BrowserProfile, BrowserTab, NavigationEntry, Bookmark, HistoryEntry, Download, SitePermission, Workspace, TabGroup, SplitView, SearchProvider, SiteEnhancer and EnginePreference as typed 9to1-owned entities or equivalent strongly typed contracts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Web engine architecture
requirements.text: Gecko and Chromium MUST be isolated internally.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Web engine architecture
requirements.text: They MUST NOT be pointed at the same physical cookie/profile/session database.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Web engine architecture
requirements.text: Users MUST be able to use Firefox for this tab, Chromium for this tab, always Firefox for a site/domain, always Chromium for a site/domain, and reset a persisted site engine preference.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Web engine architecture
requirements.text: A broken page SHOULD be switchable to the other engine with one obvious action without opening a separate browser product.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Automatic upstream maintenance
requirements.text: The Firefox/Gecko and Chromium/Blink frameworks MUST be maintained continuously against the latest appropriate upstream release and MUST automatically detect and ingest newer upstream versions when available.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Automatic upstream maintenance
requirements.text: The update pipeline MUST fetch/rebase or reapply maintained 9to1 changes, build the affected engine integration, run Haven compatibility and regression suites, verify CUI integration, engine switching, extension baselines, session/profile isolation, Site Enhancer behaviour, DevTools integration and Dulche browser capabilities, and promote the new engine only after the applicable acceptance gates pass.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Automatic upstream maintenance
requirements.text: The previous known-good engine build MUST remain rollback-capable until promotion is proven stable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > CUI and URI namespace contract
requirements.text: They MUST remain architecturally and security-distinct even when multiple namespaces ultimately render through CUI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > CUI and URI namespace contract
requirements.text: User-facing normal web navigation uses these web schemes; Haven-owned, CUI and native-app content MUST NOT masquerade as an HTTP(S) origin.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > CUI and URI namespace contract
requirements.text: Internal compatibility plumbing inherited from donors MAY exist only where technically unavoidable, but it MUST NOT be exposed as a competing public routing model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Native 9to1 app surfaces in tabs
requirements.text: Opening 9to1://<App> MUST instantiate the real CUI application surface and the real application services inside the Haven tab.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Native 9to1 app surfaces in tabs
requirements.text: It MUST NOT load a separately implemented web edition, feature-reduced embedded edition or imitation of the app.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Native 9to1 app surfaces in tabs
requirements.text: 9to1:// routes MUST be registered centrally by the application/router registry and support typed deep links to canonical resources where the owning app supports them.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Native 9to1 app surfaces in tabs
requirements.text: A tab title and icon should reflect the actual resource/app instead of exposing an opaque route string as its primary label.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Native 9to1 app surfaces in tabs
requirements.text: Native tabs and standalone executables MUST use the same app implementation, canonical resources and state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Native 9to1 app surfaces in tabs
requirements.text: Opening a resource through either entry point MUST NOT create a disconnected copy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Profiles and workspaces
requirements.text: A workspace may contain tabs from multiple profiles and owns organisational state such as open tabs, groups, split arrangements, workspace pins and layout.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Profiles and workspaces
requirements.text: Switching workspace MUST NOT inherently sign the user into or out of websites.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Profiles and workspaces
requirements.text: Profile identity MUST be visually discoverable on tabs and in relevant browser UI so the user can tell which account/session context will be used.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Profiles and workspaces
requirements.text: Consequential actions and Dulche-controlled actions SHOULD make the active profile context clear where confusion could cause the action to occur under the wrong identity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Profiles and workspaces
requirements.text: Changing a tab to another profile MUST reopen/recreate its web session under the destination profile rather than copying authentication material across profile boundaries.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Profiles and workspaces
requirements.text: Safe navigation/organisation metadata such as URL, group, workspace and split position may be preserved where applicable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Tabs, groups and placement
requirements.text: Haven MUST provide modern tab management in addition to Firefox donor parity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Tabs, groups and placement
requirements.text: Tab groups are first-class canonical entities with stable identity, naming, optional colour/icon metadata, collapse/expand state, persistence, restore, drag/drop and movement between windows/workspaces.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Tabs, groups and placement
requirements.text: Tab-strip placement MUST be a first-class configurable preference with full feature parity in all four orientations:

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Tabs, groups and placement
requirements.text: The interface MUST adapt properly to each orientation rather than mechanically moving a top strip.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Tabs, groups and placement
requirements.text: Groups, pinned tabs, profile indicators, drag/reorder, tab search, previews, context menus, engine state where surfaced, close/reopen, Dulche mentions and split operations MUST remain functional in every orientation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Tabs, groups and placement
requirements.text: Compact/collapsed and appropriate auto-expand behaviours may be provided as configurable presentation options.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Split View
requirements.text: A split may mix any compatible tab surface classes, including web + web, 9to1 app + web, 9to1 app + 9to1 app, Haven internal + web and tabs from different BrowserProfiles.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Split View
requirements.text: The two-pane experience is the required baseline.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Split View
requirements.text: The architecture SHOULD avoid assumptions that make future multi-pane layouts impossible, but more than two panes is not required unless separately specified.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > New Tab canvas
requirements.text: It SHOULD reuse shared 9to1 canvas/layout infrastructure where practical instead of creating an incompatible bespoke layout system.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > New Tab canvas
requirements.text: It may refresh manually, on New Tab open or on an allowed schedule and may expose source restrictions, maximum item count, presentation style and network/Dulche permissions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > New Tab canvas
requirements.text: Generative Areas MUST resolve real canonical entities when the requested content refers to tabs, Files, events, 9to1 objects or other structured data.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > New Tab canvas
requirements.text: They MUST NOT fabricate canonical objects merely to fill a container.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > New Tab canvas
requirements.text: Generated/recommended content SHOULD remain distinguishable from deterministic widget output.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Search and AI entry
requirements.text: The primary New Tab/address search entry MUST expose two explicit modes: Search and AI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Search and AI entry
requirements.text: Search mode performs normal navigation/search behaviour and MUST NOT invoke an LLM merely to execute an ordinary URL or provider query.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Search and AI entry
requirements.text: Haven MUST support a typed SearchProvider contract and allow the user to configure a default provider plus an optional secondary provider.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Search and AI entry
requirements.text: Providers may supply query construction, suggestions and declared privacy/capability metadata.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Search and AI entry
requirements.text: Extension-defined providers may participate through the same contract.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Search and AI entry
requirements.text: Haven MUST support searching two providers at once.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Search and AI entry
requirements.text: This MUST reuse normal BrowserTab and SplitView infrastructure rather than a bespoke dual-search renderer.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Dulche browser experience
requirements.text: Firefox-provided proprietary AI surfaces MUST be removed/replaced.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Dulche browser experience
requirements.text: Haven SHOULD provide both a persistent Dulche sidebar for larger tasks and a lightweight floating/command bar for contextual requests, using the shared Dulche runtime rather than launching a browser-specific model server.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Dulche browser experience
requirements.text: The Dulche UI MUST support @-mentioning canonical browser context.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Dulche browser experience
requirements.text: At minimum users can mention tabs and SHOULD be able to mention tab groups, workspaces, split panes and other supported Haven entities.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Dulche browser experience
requirements.text: Where the referenced surface is a native 9to1 app, Dulche MUST use that app's semantic APIs rather than screen-scraping its CUI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Permissioned autonomous browsing
requirements.text: A request such as 'scroll through YouTube and pick out some good videos' may inspect visible/accessible results, scroll, open candidates, compare them and return recommendations without requiring confirmation for every benign intermediate interaction.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Permissioned autonomous browsing
requirements.text: Permission scope MUST be explicit and composable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Permissioned autonomous browsing
requirements.text: The implementation must support equivalents of read this page, control this tab, control these selected tabs and control Haven for this task.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Permissioned autonomous browsing
requirements.text: Granting one scope MUST NOT silently grant permanent global browser control.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Permissioned autonomous browsing
requirements.text: Browser automation SHOULD use structured semantic capabilities such as Navigate, OpenTab, CloseTab, ActivateTab, ReadPage, ReadElement, Find, Scroll, Click, FillField, SelectOption, GoBack, GoForward and Reload when structured control exists.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Permissioned autonomous browsing
requirements.text: Purchases, publishing/sending, destructive account changes, security changes, credential disclosure/entry and comparable external side effects MUST NOT become implicitly authorised merely because Dulche was permitted to browse.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Extensions and CUI extension surfaces
requirements.text: Firefox/WebExtension compatibility MUST be retained to the maximum practical extent.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Extensions and CUI extension surfaces
requirements.text: Because a tab may use Firefox/Gecko or Chromium/Blink, extension capability MUST be explicit.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Extensions and CUI extension surfaces
requirements.text: An extension may be Gecko-compatible, Chromium-compatible through supported adapters, compatible with both, Haven/CUI-only, partially compatible or unsupported in the active engine.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Extensions and CUI extension surfaces
requirements.text: Switching one tab to Chromium MUST NOT silently uninstall an extension, disable it globally or make it disappear.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Extensions and CUI extension surfaces
requirements.text: Engine-specific limitations MUST be surfaced predictably.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Site Enhancer
requirements.text: Haven MUST provide a first-class Site Enhancer feature inspired by mature site-customisation systems such as Arc Boosts while remaining a 9to1-native capability.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Site Enhancer
requirements.text: They must declare permissions/capabilities and execute within a defined safety boundary.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Site Enhancer
requirements.text: Dulche MUST present the proposed effect/permissions at the appropriate confirmation boundary rather than silently installing arbitrary persistent scripts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Site Enhancer
requirements.text: Extensions may provide Site Enhancers through the same permissioned model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Files, drag/drop and cross-app integration
requirements.text: Split panes and tabs SHOULD support semantic drag/drop.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Files, drag/drop and cross-app integration
requirements.text: Web upload targets may receive files through normal browser security/permission rules.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Files, drag/drop and cross-app integration
requirements.text: Mature Firefox developer tools MUST be retained/adapted rather than replaced by a feature-poor custom inspector.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Security and origin isolation
requirements.text: Ordinary HTTP(S) pages MUST NOT be able to inspect native app state, call privileged CUI/Haven APIs, forge trusted 9to1:// content or inherit internal permissions simply by navigating to or linking an internal route.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Security and origin isolation
requirements.text: A web page may request navigation to an allowed registered internal route only through the normal navigation/policy boundary.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Security and origin isolation
requirements.text: Profile cookies/credentials and engine-private state MUST remain isolated according to their owning profile/backend.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Recovery and degraded states
requirements.text: Haven MUST handle Firefox renderer crashes, Chromium renderer crashes, whole-browser crashes, failed engine startup, unavailable selected engines, extension incompatibility, interrupted downloads, invalid/corrupt engine-private state and failed engine switches without corrupting the other engine or canonical Haven profile state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Recovery and degraded states
requirements.text: Session recovery SHOULD restore tabs, groups, workspaces, split arrangements, ProfileID and per-tab engine preference wherever safe.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Recovery and degraded states
requirements.text: If a preferred engine is unavailable, Haven MUST surface the degraded state and offer a safe fallback rather than silently losing the tab or rewriting profile data.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Haven and shared platform services > Persistent contextual AI bar > Recovery and degraded states
requirements.text: The earliest host/shell render MUST use the appropriate CUI theme with no avoidable white flash.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Purpose, design philosophy and framework boundary
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: CUI MUST compile directly to the CUI/Avalonia runtime representation and MUST NOT translate .cui into AXAML as an intermediate authoring/runtime contract.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Purpose, design philosophy and framework boundary
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Shipping application projects MUST reject .axaml, .xaml and .hui as application source.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Purpose, design philosophy and framework boundary
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Donor engines, renderer/runtime implementations, compilers and platform adapters may retain internal implementation languages behind registered typed CUI contracts; they must not provide application code-behind or an alternative authoring path.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Purpose, design philosophy and framework boundary
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Shipping authoring registries, schemas, parser/runtime loaders, code generation, hot reload, samples, designer output and documentation MUST expose the canonical CUI vocabulary and typed properties, not donor controls disguised by a file rename.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Purpose, design philosophy and framework boundary
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Custom (Definition) components remain supported, but MUST NOT be used to re-export the forbidden donor taxonomy as aliases.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Purpose, design philosophy and framework boundary
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: An explicit one-time source migration tool may read legacy input and emit canonical CUI with diagnostics; production compilation/loading MUST NOT silently accept or fall back to legacy syntax.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Purpose, design philosophy and framework boundary
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Keep the pinned Avalonia fork, its provenance/licensing and required mature low-level capabilities.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Purpose, design philosophy and framework boundary
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: No generic Object wrapper around an entire legacy app, second hidden UI tree or swallowed parser failure may bypass this boundary.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Purpose, design philosophy and framework boundary
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: The framework MUST make common UI concise without becoming ambiguous.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Purpose, design philosophy and framework boundary
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Shorthand may reduce typing but MUST NOT change semantics or permit guessing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Purpose, design philosophy and framework boundary
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: If a shorthand token has more than one valid resolution, compilation fails and the developer must use an explicit form.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Donor, source and compatibility contract
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: The implementation MUST obtain and include the selected appropriate Avalonia source revision in the CUI source tree/build graph under the global donor-source contract.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Donor, source and compatibility contract
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: The exact upstream repository, selected revision/release, licence obligations and local modifications MUST be traceable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Donor, source and compatibility contract
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: CUI MUST maintain an upstream-parity manifest for the low-level Avalonia capabilities it relies on and a CUI property-parity manifest for broadly applicable visual/layout/property families derived from Avalonia and mature CSS concepts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Donor, source and compatibility contract
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Upstream Avalonia changes MUST be adapted behind CUI contracts and MUST NOT silently alter public CUI syntax or semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Donor, source and compatibility contract
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: A registered Object Type may host an actual donor-backed document, canvas, browser or media engine; for example Object Type="WriteDocumentSurface" is a valid integration shape when that Type is registered.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Donor, source and compatibility contract
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Its contract MUST expose the applicable typed content/selection/actions, lifecycle, input/focus, accessibility, theme integration, errors and canonical state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Donor, source and compatibility contract
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Neither a static image nor a generic text box is a substitute for a required specialised engine.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Donor, source and compatibility contract
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: CUI themes MUST NOT rewrite user-authored document styling or other artifact content.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Core language vocabulary
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Audio — audio/media element where a visual/controller surface is required.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Basic markup and Container types
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Container MUST support at least Grid, Vertical Stack, Horizontal Stack and Absolute as built-in Types.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Basic markup and Container types
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Additional mature layout Types MAY be registered without changing the core element vocabulary.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Basic markup and Container types
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: For unquoted shorthand values, underscore MAY represent a space.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Basic markup and Container types
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: If both an underscored name and the corresponding spaced name exist in the active resolution scope, shorthand is ambiguous and MUST fail compilation rather than choosing one.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Comments, whitespace and escaping
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Comments use <# and #> and MAY span multiple lines.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Comments, whitespace and escaping
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: The compiler MUST provide an escaping mechanism for CUI-significant punctuation in free text/shorthand.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Comments, whitespace and escaping
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Formatter output MUST be deterministic.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > (Definition), custom elements and custom Types
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Built-in element and Type names cannot be silently shadowed by user definitions; an intentional framework-supported override must be explicit.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > (Definition), custom elements and custom Types
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Definitions SHOULD be authored using ordinary CUI elements/properties so authors do not have to learn a separate component language.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Themes and inherited theme structure
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Each built-in Theme MUST provide coherent effective typography, colours, surfaces, spacing, control shapes/templates, corner treatment, elevation, focus/hover/pressed/selected/disabled/validation states and motion defaults for supported CUI elements and Types, using explicit CUI inheritance/reuse where appropriate.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Themes and inherited theme structure
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Themes MUST NOT silently change a control's semantic meaning, required user workflow or user-authored artifact content.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Themes and inherited theme structure > CUI-owned theme implementation and renderer isolation
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: SimpleTheme and other donor themes must not own first-party presentation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Themes and inherited theme structure > CUI-owned theme implementation and renderer isolation
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: General control defaults belong in the active CUI theme; hidden hard-coded donor defaults must not defeat it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Themes and inherited theme structure > Home user-preference theme binding
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: CUI MUST accept the reserved dynamic theme-name input `user_preference` in any valid Theme scope, for example `<Theme Name="user_preference"> ... </Theme>`. `user_preference` is a resolver/reference, not an additional built-in theme or a literal visual style.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Themes and inherited theme structure > Home user-preference theme binding
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Resolution MUST use the canonical Home Core settings/theme service; app-specific hard-coded theme copies, duplicated preference stores and silent overrides are prohibited.
