requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Themes and inherited theme structure > Home user-preference theme binding
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Unless a particular nested region explicitly chooses another supported Theme, first-party 9to1 app shells and shared CUI components MUST inherit the user's effective preferred theme consistently (including Picture, Wave and Motion).

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Themes and inherited theme structure > Home user-preference theme binding
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: An explicit descendant Theme override remains scoped and retains the documented parent-theme inheritance when it ends; app-specific temporary/preview overrides MUST be visible and reversible, must not overwrite the user's Home preference, and must not silently disable user-selected accessibility settings.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Themes and inherited theme structure > Home user-preference theme binding
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: CUI/theme acceptance MUST exercise switching Home's preferred theme among Glow, Professional and a supported custom theme, applying `Name="user_preference"` in at least two independent running apps, observing correct live/restored styling across restart and signed-in supported surfaces, then testing offline cached preference, missing/invalid custom theme fallback, descendant explicit override and return to parent preference, plus reduced-motion/contrast/accessibility inheritance.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Themes and inherited theme structure > Home user-preference theme binding
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Theme updates MUST NOT change user content or canonical artifact state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Themes and inherited theme structure > Home user-preference theme binding
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Custom Themes SHOULD inherit another Theme when only deltas are needed.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Default typography
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: First-party 9to1 applications and the 9to1-OS shell SHOULD inherit the global CUI typography system rather than independently selecting unrelated UI fonts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Default typography
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: CUI MUST define a robust fallback font stack for environments where Montserrat is unavailable and must support specialised font roles such as monospace/code text.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Default typography
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Users may override the system/interface font through the supported customisation/theme framework without requiring application-specific hacks.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Prefabs and reusable shared CUI
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Prefabs are intended for components that should be implemented once and reused across apps, such as the shared Dulche AI bar.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Prefabs and reusable shared CUI
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Prefab Type MUST be static or dynamic.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Prefabs and reusable shared CUI
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Prefabs may contain normal elements, Definitions, nested Prefabs, variables, Styles, actions, Themes and specialised Objects.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Prefabs and reusable shared CUI
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Cyclic Prefab/Definition dependencies MUST be rejected.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Prefabs and reusable shared CUI
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: A Prefab exposes caller-settable inputs, actions/events and optional CUI-content/Children inputs explicitly.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Prefabs and reusable shared CUI
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: It MUST NOT implicitly capture arbitrary caller state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Prefab inputs and instantiation
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: A Prefab instance may provide declared inputs in markup or runtime load arguments.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Prefab inputs and instantiation
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Static Prefabs MUST reject conflicting per-instance mutable input semantics that would violate their shared-state contract; content requiring independent mutable state uses a dynamic Prefab.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Variables and variable-reference syntax
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Registered native values may be exposed through typed infrastructure bindings without creating an alternative application language.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Variables and variable-reference syntax
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Variable.ToInt and Variable Type="int" MUST resolve to the same typed conversion operation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Variables and variable-reference syntax
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Equivalent ToString, ToFloat, ToBool and other registered conversion forms MAY exist.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Variables and variable-reference syntax
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Conversion failure MUST return/produce a defined typed validation/conversion error; it MUST NOT silently substitute an unrelated default such as zero.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Live versus static references
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: CUI build tooling MUST instrument or generate change-notification plumbing for CUI-visible persistent fields/properties/observable collections referenced live.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Live dependency relationships
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Live MUST NOT invent a new scalar value when no recomputation semantics exist.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Live dependency relationships
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Dependency cycles MUST be rejected at compile/build time when statically discoverable and surfaced as typed dependency errors otherwise.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > ID/Name and Group addressing
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: An element may own zero or one ID/Name and any number of Groups.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > ID/Name and Group addressing
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Multiple elements may belong to the same Group.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > ID/Name and Group addressing
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: An ID and Group MUST NOT use the same identifier in one scope because direct runtime addressing would be ambiguous.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > ID/Name and Group addressing
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: The runtime MUST validate the entire target set before a persistent group mutation; incompatible required targets cause the operation to fail rather than silently producing partial state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > ID and Group scope
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Bare IDs/Groups resolve only in the current scope; cross-scope access must explicitly name the containing Page/Prefab instance.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Property declarations and shorthand
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Multiple property declarations may contribute different property types to the same Group.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Property declarations and shorthand
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: If a target Group exposes exactly one property type, a property mutation may omit the property name.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Property-target mutation directives
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: CUI markup may mutate an existing property target/Group declaratively.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Property-target mutation directives
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: For a multi-property Group such as Color plus Background, the explicit property is required.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Text and Children runtime content
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: A failed dynamic Children parse/validation MUST leave the previous valid child tree intact and return a typed error.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Active, Hidden and Interactive
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Active, Hidden and Interactive are separate properties and MUST NOT be collapsed into one Avalonia visibility/enabled flag.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Active, Hidden and Interactive
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Active(false) is an effective participation gate and MUST NOT overwrite stored Hidden, Interactive or other properties.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Parent lifecycle and independent activation
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: An independently active child/declaration is not forced inactive when its parent deactivates and must be deactivated separately. ! does not break Theme inheritance, symbol scope, Prefab ownership, variables, Groups, styling inheritance or event targeting.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Parent lifecycle and independent activation
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: For independently active visual descendants whose logical parent deactivates, the runtime preserves the required logical/positioning reference state without causing the inactive parent to re-enter ordinary sibling layout.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Layout property model
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: CUI's property catalogue MUST provide mature visual/layout coverage comparable in scope to broadly applicable CSS and Avalonia properties while retaining CUI's typed semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Layout property model
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Numeric layout units MUST be typed.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Grid and stack behaviour
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Invalid layout-property combinations MUST fail at compile time when statically knowable or return a typed runtime layout error when dynamically introduced.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Absolute positioning and coordinate system
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Bare X and Y use CUI's proportional coordinate system by default and MAY be decimal values.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Absolute positioning and coordinate system
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: An axis may alternatively use X-px/Y-px for CUI logical pixels or X-%/Y-% for percentage positioning.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Absolute positioning and coordinate system
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Coordinates in every mode MAY be decimals.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Absolute positioning and coordinate system
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: An element may define only one authoritative positioning mode per axis at a time.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Coordinate recalibration and inherited axes
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: X and Y may therefore resolve against different ancestor Containers.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Modal behaviour
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Nonmodal high-layer popups may sit above content without blocking unrelated lower-layer interaction outside their bounds.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Anchor and runtime placement
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Anchor is an optional named placement point, not a prerequisite for loading a Prefab or dynamically created UI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Anchor and runtime placement
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Runtime placement MUST support at least:

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Anchor and runtime placement
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: LoadIn(grid,row,column, optional spans/alignment).

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Style and property precedence
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Effective presentation MUST resolve deterministically in the following order from lowest to highest precedence:

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Style and property precedence
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: This complete CUI cascade MUST be enforced before renderer application; Avalonia/native themes, bindings, selectors and local-value priorities MUST NOT override or reinterpret it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Temporary versus Once events
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Once-prefixed events may execute on later qualifying occurrences; 'Once' denotes committed effect semantics, not a one-time lifetime subscription.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Event source, propagation and cancellation
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Event context MUST expose at least Event.Source, Event.Target, Event.Type and applicable Event.Value.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Typed actions and asynchronous work
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: ActionEvent MAY invoke a named typed application/domain action in addition to Style/property changes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Typed actions and asynchronous work
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: UI actions MUST converge on the same domain operations used by the app's API/Automation surface where an equivalent operation exists; CUI MUST NOT become a parallel private business-logic layer.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Typed actions and asynchronous work
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Long-running/async actions MUST NOT block the UI thread and must expose typed running/completed/failed/cancelled state/events usable by CUI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Conditional UI
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: CUI MUST provide structural conditional composition.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Repeated UI
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Repeat creates one generated UI instance per source item and MUST preserve item identity across live collection additions/removals/reordering.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Repeated UI
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Key may be omitted only when each item exposes an unambiguous stable ID.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Repeated UI
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: A live Repeat without stable identity MUST fail rather than recreate items with ambiguous state transfer.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Property catalogue and transform support
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: The CUI property registry MUST include mature CSS/Avalonia-like visual properties and transforms rather than limiting authors to basic colours and dimensions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Effect versus Background backdrop processing
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: They MUST NOT mutate, rotate, recolour, blur, move, restyle or otherwise change the actual underlying elements, their layout, hitboxes, state, events, Layer or accessibility tree.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Effect versus Background backdrop processing
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: If content behind the background changes because of user interaction, variable updates, animation, video, scrolling, layout or any other render change, the appearance seen through the Background MUST update automatically without calling Refresh().

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Effect versus Background backdrop processing
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: The compositor MAY cache safely but must invalidate affected backdrop dependencies correctly.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Effect versus Background backdrop processing
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: A fully transparent background exposes the processed backdrop directly; a semi-transparent colour/material composites over the processed backdrop; a fully opaque result may make the backdrop invisible and may be optimised away when observationally equivalent.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Blur, Refract and chained backdrop modifiers
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Visual properties with a defined backdrop-rendering interpretation may participate as modifiers.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Blur, Refract and chained backdrop modifiers
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: A property with no meaningful/registered backdrop interpretation MUST produce a typed compiler/runtime error rather than being silently ignored.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Gradients
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Stop positions MUST be deterministic and validated; duplicate positions MAY be used for hard transitions where supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Animation and Keyframes
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Keyframe positions may be percentages or absolute time in milliseconds.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Animation and Keyframes
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Animation control properties MUST cover at least Duration, Delay, Easing, Repeat/iteration, direction/playback and reduced-motion behaviour.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Theme, Definition and property interaction
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Theme defaults, Type/Definition defaults, explicit properties, property regions, Styles, animations and runtime changes MUST all resolve through the same registered CUI property system.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Theme, Definition and property interaction
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: There MUST NOT be separate incompatible colour/layout/transform implementations for each syntax.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Theme, Definition and property interaction
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Theme changes at runtime MUST invalidate only affected presentation state and preserve canonical app/domain state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Runtime loading and element methods
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Runtime APIs MUST provide property mutation plus lifecycle/content operations including Active(...), Refresh(), Text/Children Replace/Add and placement/load functions where supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Runtime loading and element methods
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Runtime calls and markup directives MUST converge on the same underlying CUI property/lifecycle/action operations so behaviour does not depend on how a mutation was initiated.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Imports and project file discovery
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Ambiguous symbols from multiple imports MUST fail until disambiguated, including by an explicit alias such as As:SharedUI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Accessibility, focus and keyboard semantics
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: CUI MUST make accessible behaviour the default.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Accessibility, focus and keyboard semantics
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Hidden-but-interactive controls are technically representable under CUI's Hidden semantics, but first-party accessibility lint MUST reject invisible focusable/interactive constructs unless an explicit justified accessibility contract is supplied.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Accessibility, focus and keyboard semantics
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Reduced motion, high contrast, scaling/zoom and non-colour-only state communication MUST be framework-level capabilities rather than app-specific reinventions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Localisation and directionality
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: CUI MUST support resource-backed/localisable user-visible strings, locale-aware number/date formatting and right-to-left directionality.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Localisation and directionality
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Literal developer/debug strings MAY remain literal; shipping product copy SHOULD use the localisation/resource system.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Security and dynamic CUI
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Compiled first-party CUI may reference its declared application contracts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Security and dynamic CUI
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Generative UI is structured data rendered through approved CUI components/actions and MUST NOT become arbitrary trusted .cui/C# execution.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Security and dynamic CUI
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: User/external text should normally use Text or an explicit AddText-equivalent.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Security and dynamic CUI
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Dynamic markup MUST be constrained to registered/authorised elements, properties, variables and actions of the current host.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Error boundaries and failure behaviour
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Runtime failures from dynamic CUI, plugin content, specialised Object hosts, data or async actions MUST be isolated at the nearest declared/default error boundary where feasible so one failed component does not unnecessarily destroy the entire window/application.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Error boundaries and failure behaviour
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: An invalid dynamic CUI update must preserve the last valid tree/content.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Hot reload and developer tooling
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: CUI tooling MUST include compiler/build integration, formatter, linter, hot reload, component/Prefab preview, semantic tree inspector, accessibility inspector, binding/variable dependency inspection, Theme/resource inspection and rendering/performance diagnostics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Testing and semantic selectors
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: CUI MUST expose a semantic test/accessibility tree so automated tests can locate elements by ID, role, accessible name and other stable semantic selectors rather than raw screen coordinates when semantic targeting exists.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Testing and semantic selectors
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: The test harness MUST be able to render a CUI Page/Prefab at declared dimensions, Theme, scale, accessibility/reduced-motion settings and platform capability profile; interact through semantic input; inspect resulting state; and capture deterministic visual evidence where applicable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Performance and rendering
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: CUI MUST use Avalonia's mature low-level rendering/composition foundations while adding CUI-level invalidation, dependency and component semantics without introducing unnecessary full-tree work.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Performance and rendering
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Virtualisable lists/grids/trees MUST use framework virtualisation rather than constructing every off-screen item by default.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Performance and rendering
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Backdrop Blur/Refract/Gradient processing MAY use compositor caching, but cache invalidation MUST remain live and correct when sampled content changes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Performance and rendering
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Animation/input loops MUST avoid blocking application/domain work on the UI thread.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Performance and rendering
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Caches must be bounded and revision/dependency invalidated.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Platform and Home runtime integration
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Web CUI MAY use a browser-specific implementation/runtime, but it MUST preserve the same public CUI semantics, component contracts, state identities and supported action/property behaviour except for explicitly declared platform capability differences.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Platform and Home runtime integration
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Platform differences such as unsupported backdrop effects, specialised renderer capabilities or input hardware MUST be capability-negotiated explicitly.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Platform and Home runtime integration
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: The runtime MUST NOT silently reinterpret unsupported CUI into materially different behaviour.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Language/runtime versioning
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Compiled CUI output MUST record at least CUI language version, CUI runtime ABI/component-registry version and required capability set.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Language/runtime versioning
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Custom distributed Themes/Prefabs/packages SHOULD carry their own version/dependency metadata.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > CUI compiler pipeline
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: The compiler MUST NOT silently accept unknown attributes/tags/types/events/properties.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > CUI compiler pipeline
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Typographical mistakes such as Type:Vertcal_Stack SHOULD produce an unknown-symbol error with an unambiguous suggestion such as Vertical Stack when available.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Acceptance criteria
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Acceptance MUST include compiler-negative tests for forbidden donor tags/namespaces/attached layout syntax, unknown tags/properties, ambiguous shorthand and production .axaml/.hui input; compiler-positive tests for all canonical elements, Types and legitimate Definitions; runtime property-cascade/theme-isolation tests; and inventory-based integration checks against real first-party applications.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Acceptance criteria
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Release validation MUST demonstrate at minimum:

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Acceptance criteria
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Any implementation that recreates CUI as an AXAML preprocessor, uses polling for ordinary live variables, treats Hidden as unloaded, treats Active as destructive property reset, mutates underlying elements through Background backdrop modifiers, snapshots Blur/Refract instead of keeping them live, silently guesses ambiguous shorthand, partially applies incompatible Group mutations, or exposes unreviewed donor/property capability gaps MUST fail release conformance.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Acceptance criteria
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Ctrl+wheel over the editing canvas zooms incrementally; pinch zoom on supported trackpads behaves appropriately and must not confuse two-finger scrolling with zoom.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Acceptance criteria
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Zoom SHOULD be anchored around the pointer location when practical, obey safe bounds, and share one state with the toolbar percent/Fit-to-Window controls.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > Acceptance criteria
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Changing zoom, scrolling, toggling panels or resizing window MUST NOT desynchronise object positions, hit-testing, resize handles or canvas centring.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > C. FLOATING INTERACTION SURFACES AND VISUAL LANGUAGE
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: First-party File/Edit/Insert/Slide/Arrange/View/Help menus, + Insert menu, shape gallery, font dropdowns, colour popovers, toolbar overflow, right-click context menus and related tool surfaces MUST follow the same CUI-driven design language.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > C. FLOATING INTERACTION SURFACES AND VISUAL LANGUAGE
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Short menus may be compact; this is not a requirement to oversize all popovers.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > C. FLOATING INTERACTION SURFACES AND VISUAL LANGUAGE
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Right-click on a selected shape/text/image or other object MUST open a context-specific menu with applicable Cut, Copy, Paste, Duplicate, Delete, Arrange/z-order, Align, Group and Format operations; text-editing right-click MUST offer text-appropriate commands; slide thumbnails MUST offer new, duplicate, delete, reorder/layout and related slide operations; empty canvas areas MUST offer relevant Paste/Insert/slide options.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > C. FLOATING INTERACTION SURFACES AND VISUAL LANGUAGE
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Each menu targets the intended ObjectID/SlideID and must position near its anchor without clipping; keyboard invocation/navigation, focus, escape/outside dismissal, checked/disabled/submenu states and correct z-order are mandatory.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > C. FLOATING INTERACTION SURFACES AND VISUAL LANGUAGE
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: The same canonical commands must power context menus, toolbar, shortcuts and inspector.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > C. FLOATING INTERACTION SURFACES AND VISUAL LANGUAGE
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: The selected/hovered states must remain accessible and sufficiently visible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > C. FLOATING INTERACTION SURFACES AND VISUAL LANGUAGE
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: CUI-EDITOR-104 — Icons must be reliable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > C. FLOATING INTERACTION SURFACES AND VISUAL LANGUAGE
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Icons SHOULD be coherent, moderately rounded, optically centred, consistent in stroke/weight and recognisable, optionally with restrained semantic colour accents.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > C. FLOATING INTERACTION SURFACES AND VISUAL LANGUAGE
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Reusable CUI EditorShell/EditorToolbar, grouped commands, contextual inspector, menu/popover, insertion catalogue, selection-adorners and viewport contracts SHOULD be extended/shared where justified, with clear source ownership and typed interfaces.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > C. FLOATING INTERACTION SURFACES AND VISUAL LANGUAGE
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: This sets shared standards for Write, Present, Data, Boards, Canvas and relevant apps, but MUST NOT force a Present three-row header or object-selection model onto applications whose category workflows require other layouts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > C. FLOATING INTERACTION SURFACES AND VISUAL LANGUAGE
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Avalonia MAY supply underlying rendering, input, windowing and specialised engine integration behind CUI; it MUST NOT be the default public styling/control vocabulary or override CUI states.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > D. REFRESH, STARTUP AND CROSS-APP PERFORMANCE
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Present must avoid prolonged blank refresh and theme flashes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > D. REFRESH, STARTUP AND CROSS-APP PERFORMANCE
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: AXAML/XAML and Avalonia native markup MUST NOT parse as CUI, including aliases or silent conversion.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > D. REFRESH, STARTUP AND CROSS-APP PERFORMANCE
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Specialised donor engines may compute, render content or perform domain operations behind typed CUI adapters; they may not surface independently styled UI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > D. REFRESH, STARTUP AND CROSS-APP PERFORMANCE
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Build/CI MUST parse all public UI definitions using the CUI grammar and registry, reject native markup vocabulary and attached-property syntax, inspect runtime UI boundaries, and smoke-test real rendered packaged apps.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > D. REFRESH, STARTUP AND CROSS-APP PERFORMANCE
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Valid registered CUI properties must not be rejected merely because their names resemble internal implementation details.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > D. REFRESH, STARTUP AND CROSS-APP PERFORMANCE
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Any specialised engine adapter must document lifecycle, content/selection/action contracts, focus/input, accessibility, errors, theme, state and recovery.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > D. REFRESH, STARTUP AND CROSS-APP PERFORMANCE
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: All active native and browser CUI-hosted applications, including Present, MUST use CUI-owned typed templates, materials, semantic tokens, states and lifecycle.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > D. REFRESH, STARTUP AND CROSS-APP PERFORMANCE
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: All Present entrypoints must use compliant CUI appearance without losing existing behaviour; all functioning control templates and state resources must be supplied by CUI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > D. REFRESH, STARTUP AND CROSS-APP PERFORMANCE
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Shared icons should be coherent vector assets with consistent weight, precise alignment and honest hit areas.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > D. REFRESH, STARTUP AND CROSS-APP PERFORMANCE
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Hover, focus, pressed, selected, disabled and validation states must be visible, consistent and accessible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > D. REFRESH, STARTUP AND CROSS-APP PERFORMANCE
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: The authored slide itself and every document object, image, foreground text, PDF/exported artifact and accessibility surface must remain crisp and retain document-authored colours.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > D. REFRESH, STARTUP AND CROSS-APP PERFORMANCE
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Whole menu rows must be clickable; shadows cannot clip; unsupported symbols must not appear as square glyphs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework > D. REFRESH, STARTUP AND CROSS-APP PERFORMANCE
requirements.top_section: CUI language, presentation and shared editor framework
requirements.text: Changing themes while a text field is focused must preserve caret, selection, typed content and ongoing operation state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Home runtime dependency
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: Before initialising the app’s normal UI or opening user artifacts, the app MUST complete a local Home availability/version handshake against the Home-managed shared services it requires.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Home runtime dependency
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: If Home is not installed, the app MUST refuse normal startup and display only a minimal bootstrap surface explaining that 9-1 Home is required.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Home runtime dependency
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: The bootstrap surface MUST provide an Install Home action that opens/starts the trusted Home installation flow.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Home runtime dependency
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: It MUST NOT create or mutate normal app data while Home is absent.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Home runtime dependency
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: If Home is installed but the required shared service/API version is missing, incompatible or damaged, the app MUST refuse unsafe normal startup and offer the appropriate Home update/repair flow with a structured reason.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Home runtime dependency
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: Apps MUST NOT silently launch private replacement services to bypass the missing Home dependency.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: Every interactive 9to1 app MUST expose the shared persistent floating contextual AI bar at the bottom of its primary content surface.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: It MUST be able to inspect the current artifact/surface semantically and, when permitted, edit it through the owning app's typed APIs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: The shared bar MUST expose an explicit persistent AI access-mode switcher with at least Read-only and Write mode.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: The current mode MUST remain visible enough that the user can tell whether Dulche may only inspect the surface or may also request mutations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: In Read-only mode, Dulche MAY read, search, compare, reason over, summarise, explain and navigate the full authorised semantic surface, including off-screen content that the owning app exposes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: It MAY generate proposed changes in conversation, but MUST NOT mutate the owning artifact, structure or app state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: Mutations MUST use stable semantic identities such as ArtifactID, PageID, SectionID, ObjectID, row/range/entity IDs or equivalent domain identifiers and the owning app's normal revision/conflict semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: Host-surface rules may narrow the effective mutation set further.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: Apps MUST provide a permission-filtered semantic context snapshot including the active artifact/page/entity, current selection, relevant stable object IDs, structure necessary to understand the task, current revision/state and supported typed actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: The bar MUST prefer this semantic context over screenshot/OCR/pixel interpretation and MUST NOT substitute raw mouse/keyboard/desktop automation when typed context/actions exist.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: The AI bar MUST remain visually separate from document/page content and MUST NOT change the underlying artifact layout merely by being shown.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: It MAY collapse to a compact state but MUST remain directly reachable without navigating to a separate AI page.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: Surface-specific mutation protections MAY be stricter than the shared Write-mode baseline and cannot be weakened by AI mode or trust state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: When the target is a live database, Data MUST additionally show a meaningful preview/diff, validate the operation and create a recoverable backup/snapshot/checkpoint before execution.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: If the required live-database backup cannot be created, the mutation MUST NOT proceed as though rollback exists.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: For Data live-database changes, the approval surface SHOULD identify the intended operation, affected tables/entities/rows where knowable, schema/dependency impact, external side effects and backup identity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: Execution MUST occur only after approval, then verify the actual result and preserve rollback/recovery information.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: Prior approval, Accept and Trust or Always Trust MUST NOT suppress this Data-specific per-action approval invariant.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: Equivalent bar actions MUST behave consistently across product surfaces, while menus and available operations remain context-sensitive to the owning app.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: Unsupported or inapplicable actions MUST not be exposed merely to make the bar look feature-complete.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Persistent contextual AI bar > Chat bar — expanded-mode formatting and emoji controls
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: These buttons must not appear in compact/mini mode, even when the compact/mini chat bar is focused.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Persistent contextual AI bar > Chat-bar control acceptance
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: The formatting toolbar and CUI emoji picker MUST work with keyboard input, labelled controls, focus return and preserved draft/selection state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Cross-app invocation and compose contract
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: Every interactive 9to1 app that hosts the shared persistent AI bar MUST use Home's canonical compose invocation component and cross-app dispatcher.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Cross-app invocation and compose contract
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: Plugins, Skills, Apps, Agents, Files and the reserved @Computer Use capability MUST therefore resolve consistently across apps rather than each product implementing a private @ syntax or resource picker.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Cross-app invocation and compose contract
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: A model may cross an app boundary only when that action is authorised by user intent: explicit @ invocation, an explicit instruction naming the target capability/app, or an unambiguous requested outcome whose canonical owner is another 9to1 app.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Cross-app invocation and compose contract
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: When a target 9to1 app owns the requested artifact/action, the originating model MUST use the target app's typed API/shared semantic action contract and MAY ask Home to launch/reveal the target app so the user can observe progress.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Cross-app invocation and compose contract
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: Computer Use MUST NOT be selected automatically as a fallback when typed app execution is unavailable, inconvenient or fails.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Cross-app invocation and compose contract
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: Model-driven typed edits MAY be visualised in the target app with live object motion, selection highlights, text insertion and a synthetic/virtual cursor.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Cross-app invocation and compose contract
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: This visualisation is not evidence that Dulche is literally controlling the pointer; the typed action/result remains authoritative and the synthetic cursor MUST be visually distinguishable from the user's actual input cursor.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Launch Screens
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: A temporary startup/loading splash, first-run onboarding, launch/home, backstage/file menu and active editor/workspace are different experiences and MUST retain their specified purposes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Launch Screens
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: Each required launch screen MUST have its own purposeful layout, hierarchy, recognisable app identity and the real app-specific entry points listed below or in its product section.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Launch Screens
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: The start experience must be composed for the available work region, not merely reserve a top strip while the unused editor remains below it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Launch Screens
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: They may reuse the same window, app shell, engine and canonical session; separate processes or OS windows are not required.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Launch Screens
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: An inactive editor must not occupy launch layout space or receive pointer input, document shortcuts, keyboard focus or accessibility navigation; inactive launch-only controls must likewise not remain attached to the editor.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Launch Screens
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: Shared chrome explicitly required by the specification may remain.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Launch Screens
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: Create, Open, Import and applicable template/recent/shared actions MUST establish or resolve the real authorised canonical artifact/session and transition to its functioning workspace, not just change the page heading or reveal an already-stacked test editor.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Launch Screens
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging
requirements.text: Reuse must preserve product-specific workflows, rather than flattening every app into the same dashboard.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging > Launch Screens
requirements.top_section: Shared application lifecycle, launch and modular packaging

requirements.text: Surface a clear “Temporarily showing weekly limit; five-hour limit remains pinned” notice, optionally with a warning/urgent symbol.

requirements.text: Multiple simultaneous candidates must be prioritised deterministically; no flickering/ring thrashing on every small telemetry update.

requirements.text: Where the system models projected exhaustion over time (especially across different units), it MUST use observable usage rate, active configured reset/window duration and request-specific measured or bounded costs where available, and label forecasts as estimated.

requirements.text: One Home-managed Dulche instance serves every 9-1 app through a broker API; apps must never launch their own competing local model servers.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Voice > Voice API
requirements.text: Additional APIs required for complete voice functionality may be added following Dulche’s existing API conventions and the global API-parity rule.

requirements.text: The primary user-facing product is the built-in Translate Space, while Write, Mail, Boards, Haven, Voice & Vision, AI Overlay, Build site workspace and other authorised surfaces may invoke Dulche Translate directly for contextual translation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate
requirements.text: It MUST use the shared model/provider layer and normal Home/Dulche permission and audit contracts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Translation Sets and variants
requirements.text: A translation request MAY target one or many languages/locales in a single operation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Translation Sets and variants
requirements.text: Every TranslationVariant MUST have stable TranslationVariantID, TranslationSetID, target language/locale, status, translated content or canonical output reference, revision, provenance, errors/warnings and segment map where available.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Translation Sets and variants
requirements.text: Retrying, regenerating, manually editing, applying or publishing one language MUST NOT discard successful sibling variants.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Translation Sets and variants
requirements.text: Language identity MUST use canonical language/locale identifiers.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Translation Sets and variants
requirements.text: When a user supplies an ambiguous or unsupported language label, Dulche Translate MUST request/return a structured resolution requirement rather than silently guessing another language.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Conversational Translate Space rendering
requirements.text: When one conversational request returns multiple TranslationVariants, each language variant MUST appear as its own assistant speech bubble.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Conversational Translate Space rendering
requirements.text: A prompt may temporarily target a subset/additional language without necessarily changing the Space's persistent language chips.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Conversational refinement and agentic actions
requirements.text: Translate MUST support natural follow-up refinement such as 'make the German version less formal', 'keep Action Graph untranslated everywhere', 'add Japanese', 'only redo French', or 'update these because the source changed'.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Conversational refinement and agentic actions
requirements.text: Translate Space MAY perform multi-step agentic localisation workflows using normal Space Plugins, Skills, persistent Dulche Agents, Automations and typed app actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Conversational refinement and agentic actions
requirements.text: For example, 'translate this page into French, Spanish, German and Italian, then push them to the live site' may resolve the current page semantically, create/update four TranslationVariants, validate each owning artifact/site route and invoke the authorised Build site workspace/WordPress/publishing APIs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Conversational refinement and agentic actions
requirements.text: Dulche Translate MUST NOT implement generic hidden publishing or file mutation that bypasses owning apps.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Conversational refinement and agentic actions
requirements.text: Partial downstream failure MUST preserve already-successful translations/actions and expose targeted retry.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Structured artifacts and semantic preservation
requirements.text: Dulche Translate MUST translate human-language content while preserving supported non-linguistic structure and identity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Structured artifacts and semantic preservation
requirements.text: For 9to1-native artifacts it should operate through the owning app/shared Productivity Engine using stable object identities rather than flattening the artifact into plain text.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Structured artifacts and semantic preservation
requirements.text: Code, commands, URLs, formulas, JSON keys, identifiers, markup/code fences and other structured technical content MUST follow explicit structure-aware rules and MUST NOT be casually translated as prose.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Structured artifacts and semantic preservation
requirements.text: The user may explicitly request translation of translatable string literals/comments where the owning format supports safe editing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Structured artifacts and semantic preservation
requirements.text: Whole-artifact translation SHOULD create a translated derivative/locale variant by default rather than destructively overwrite the source.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Segments, provenance and incremental updates
requirements.text: Where the source supports stable segmentation, Dulche Translate SHOULD preserve segment identity/alignment between source and each target variant.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Segments, provenance and incremental updates
requirements.text: Translated derivatives MUST retain provenance sufficient to identify source artifact/file/entity, source revision, source/target language, TranslationSetID/VariantID, glossary IDs, model policy and translation time.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Segments, provenance and incremental updates
requirements.text: When the source changes, Translate MUST be able to report that a translation is stale.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Segments, provenance and incremental updates
requirements.text: Where safe segment identity exists, updating a stale translation SHOULD retranslate only changed/affected source segments while preserving unaffected translated content and user edits.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Segments, provenance and incremental updates
requirements.text: Conflicts between manual target edits and changed source content MUST be surfaced rather than silently overwritten.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Glossaries and protected terminology
requirements.text: Dulche Translate MUST support reusable and request-scoped glossaries.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Glossaries and protected terminology
requirements.text: Glossary entries MAY define source term, required/preferred target translation by locale, Do Not Translate, notes/context and applicability scope.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Glossaries and protected terminology
requirements.text: Protected terminology MUST support names, trademarks, product names, case names, technical identifiers, commands and other content that should remain unchanged.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Glossaries and protected terminology
requirements.text: Glossary/protected-term application MUST be recorded in translation provenance so unexpected terminology can be diagnosed.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Text, image, document and media translation
requirements.text: Dulche Translate MUST support direct text and semantic selection translation.
