requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Text, image, document and media translation
requirements.text: Image/screenshot translation MAY return extracted translated text and, where the selected model/tooling supports it, a translated visual derivative with mapped text regions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Text, image, document and media translation
requirements.text: PDF handling MUST distinguish text, scanned and mixed PDFs where detectable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Text, image, document and media translation
requirements.text: Structured text PDFs should preserve layout/structure as far as supported; scanned/mixed PDFs may require vision/OCR-style extraction.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Text, image, document and media translation
requirements.text: Any layout fidelity loss or uncertain extraction MUST be surfaced before export/apply.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Text, image, document and media translation
requirements.text: Audio translation may produce translated text and, where supported, translated speech.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Text, image, document and media translation
requirements.text: Video translation MAY produce translated transcript/subtitles and advanced dubbed output where supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Model routing and privacy
requirements.text: Ordinary translation requests SHOULD resolve the highest-quality compatible configured route for the requested languages, modality, context size, latency, privacy/locality, entitlement/cost and tool requirements without forcing the user to manually choose a model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Model routing and privacy
requirements.text: An explicit local-only/private policy MUST NOT silently fall back to cloud translation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Translation jobs and recovery
requirements.text: Long or multi-artifact translation MUST use durable TranslationJob state with stable TranslationJobID and statuses such as Preparing, Translating, ReviewAvailable, Applying/Exporting, Completed, Paused, Failed and Cancelled as applicable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Translation jobs and recovery
requirements.text: Progress MUST derive from real segments/pages/slides/files/variants rather than invented percentages.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Translation jobs and recovery
requirements.text: Partial failure MUST preserve successful completed segments/variants.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Translation jobs and recovery
requirements.text: Pause/resume/retry MUST not repeat already-completed consequential downstream actions without idempotency/operation identity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Translate > Failure behaviour
requirements.text: Dulche Translate MUST return structured failures including LanguageUnsupported, LanguageAmbiguous, LocaleUnsupported, TranslationModelUnavailable, TranslationCapabilityUnavailable, GlossaryUnavailable, SourceUnavailable, SourceRevisionConflict, SegmentAlignmentUnavailable, VariantNotFound, TranslationSetNotFound, TranslationJobNotFound, TranslationJobNotResumable, StructuredFormatUnsupported, LayoutPreservationUnavailable, PartialTranslationFailure, PrivacyPolicyDenied and ProviderUnavailable in addition to normal Dulche/tool/action failures.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents
requirements.text: AI Studio is not the runtime host, and closing AI Studio MUST NOT stop, hide or delete an Agent.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents
requirements.text: Agents have stable identity, durable configuration/memory/scope and may exist across many runs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Canonical Agent identity and Den persistence
requirements.text: Every Agent MUST have stable AgentID independent of name plus versioned DefinitionRevision.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Canonical Agent identity and Den persistence
requirements.text: The Den-backed Agent entity MUST retain at least name, icon/avatar, description, instructions, availability bindings, default model policy, Plugins/Connectors, Skills, Knowledge/Files references, Quick Actions, memory policy, capability/permission policy, delegation policy, graph reference where present, sharing metadata, revision history and lifecycle state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Canonical Agent identity and Den persistence
requirements.text: Renaming, moving scope or changing icon MUST NOT create another Agent.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Canonical Agent identity and Den persistence
requirements.text: Agent display names MAY collide; AgentID remains canonical.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Canonical Agent identity and Den persistence
requirements.text: An Agent definition revision used by an active/historical run MUST remain attributable even after later edits.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Canonical Agent identity and Den persistence
requirements.text: Den MUST separate Agent definition/configuration from secrets and device-specific executable state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Availability scopes and cascading
requirements.text: Dulche MUST support Agent availability scopes including Global, Surface, Space and Project/Entity or equivalent narrower canonical scope bindings.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Availability scopes and cascading
requirements.text: An Agent MAY have multiple compatible bindings when explicitly configured.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Availability scopes and cascading
requirements.text: Dulche MUST return origin/scope metadata so CUI can group Agents by Global, current surface and contextual scopes rather than present an unexplained flat list.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Availability scopes and cascading
requirements.text: Global cascading references the same canonical AgentID everywhere; it MUST NOT create per-app copies.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Availability versus permission
requirements.text: A visible Agent may still have actions disabled in the current invocation context.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Availability versus permission
requirements.text: Effective permissions/capabilities MUST be no broader than the intersection of the Agent definition/instance policy, current surface capabilities, current Space policy, current project/entity scope, caller/user/organisation policy and Home permission/trust state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Availability versus permission
requirements.text: Agents MUST support both static image icons and animated avatars.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Availability versus permission
requirements.text: Users MUST be able to choose the presentation for each Agent.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Availability versus permission
requirements.text: Animated avatars MUST react to the Agent's actual activity and relevant conversational events.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Availability versus permission
requirements.text: Task-state transitions and conversational reactions MUST be configurable and previewable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Availability versus permission
requirements.text: Animation MUST respect the existing reduced-motion controls and provide a static fallback without losing the Agent's accessible identity or readable activity status.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Agent presentation API and acceptance
requirements.text: The canonical Dulche Agent API MUST cover static/animated avatar selection, referenced asset and definition management, animation-state transitions and event/reaction mappings.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Agent presentation API and acceptance
requirements.text: Use Den-backed stable identities and versioned configuration shared with AI Studio’s visual builder; presentation changes MUST NOT fork the Agent, alter its permissions or leak private content.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Surface integration and Agent picker
requirements.text: Every compatible interactive 9to1 surface SHOULD expose applicable Dulche Agents through the shared AI/Agent picker or a surface-appropriate invocation UI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Surface integration and Agent picker
requirements.text: The invocation context MUST be typed and may include SurfaceID, SpaceID, Project/Entity references, ArtifactID, selected ObjectIDs, current semantic context and available typed actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Surface integration and Agent picker
requirements.text: Surfaces MAY recommend specialist scoped Agents more prominently than generic Global Agents.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Surface integration and Agent picker
requirements.text: Recommendation/order MUST NOT change Agent identity or silently select an Agent with broader permissions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Scoped surface Agents
requirements.text: First-party apps MAY ship/register useful surface-scoped Dulche Agent definitions/bindings.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Scoped surface Agents
requirements.text: Write MAY expose specialist writing Agents such as Editor, Proofreader, Long-form Writer or user-created writing Agents.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Scoped surface Agents
requirements.text: Voice & Vision MAY expose a Podcast Agent or similar specialist Voice Agents.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Scoped surface Agents
requirements.text: A Podcast Agent can accept typed inputs such as Topic, optional Sources, target Duration and Style, then use the Voice Monologue mode to research/plan/generate/play a coherent long-form podcast.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Agent invocation interfaces
requirements.text: An Agent definition MAY declare a typed InvocationSchema and optional CUI/Generative UI invocation interface.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Agent invocation interfaces
requirements.text: Surfaces SHOULD render the declared inputs rather than force every Agent through a blank chat box.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Agent invocation interfaces
requirements.text: Invocation UI definitions MUST bind only to declared Agent inputs and approved typed actions; they MUST NOT grant new permissions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Quick Actions
requirements.text: Every QuickAction MUST have stable QuickActionID, AgentID, label, optional icon/description, predefined instruction or named graph entry point, optional typed InputSchema, context requirements, confirmation policy and ordering metadata.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Quick Actions
requirements.text: Quick Actions may be context-sensitive.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Quick Actions
requirements.text: For example, Rewrite selection should appear only where an editable selection exists; a Podcast Agent may expose Make podcast, Continue latest podcast or Create briefing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Quick Actions
requirements.text: An Automation MAY invoke an Agent/Quick Action through the same Dulche APIs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Default model resolution
requirements.text: An Agent may define Default Model = Inherit or an explicit Universal Model Picker policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Default model resolution
requirements.text: An explicit Agent default takes precedence over inherited defaults where allowed, while request-specific overrides may take precedence only if Agent/security policy permits.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Default model resolution
requirements.text: Dulche MUST capability-check the effective model against the Agent/run requirements such as tools, vision, audio, context or structured output.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Default model resolution
requirements.text: It MUST not silently cross local/private to cloud boundaries or substitute an explicitly forbidden fallback.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Plugins, Connectors, Skills and Knowledge
requirements.text: The Agent may retrieve current source revisions through owning APIs rather than rely on stale copies.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Plugins, Connectors, Skills and Knowledge
requirements.text: Missing/revoked/incompatible sources or packages MUST be represented explicitly.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Agent memory
requirements.text: Each persistent Agent MUST have an Agent-specific Den memory namespace governed by its memory policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Agent memory
requirements.text: Memory writes MUST carry scope/provenance and MUST respect personal/team/shared boundaries.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Agent memory
requirements.text: A shared Agent MUST NOT silently copy a participant's private personal Den context, private connected-account data or secrets into shared Agent memory.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Agent memory
requirements.text: Agent memory SHOULD support inspection, conflict handling, deduplication, recency/provenance metadata and removal/disable operations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Agent memory
requirements.text: Secrets encountered in tools/results MUST NOT automatically become durable Agent memory.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Tasks, work queues and runs
requirements.text: A persistent Agent MAY maintain a durable work queue in Dulche.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Tasks, work queues and runs
requirements.text: Queue items MUST have stable QueueItemID, AgentID, objective, optional TaskID, priority, creator/trigger provenance, dependencies, status and timestamps.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Tasks, work queues and runs
requirements.text: Work may arrive from a user, Space/Task, Automation, another authorised Agent or recovery flow.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Tasks, work queues and runs
requirements.text: The relationship MUST remain explicit: a Task/objective may be assigned to an Agent, which creates one or more AgentRuns.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Tasks, work queues and runs
requirements.text: Each AgentRun MUST have stable AgentRunID, AgentID, DefinitionRevision, objective, trigger/source, optional TaskID/QueueItemID, status, start/end timestamps, effective model/capabilities/permissions, ActionGraphID, outputs, blockers, approvals, usage/budget metadata and recovery/checkpoint state where supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Run states and controls
requirements.text: Canonical user-facing Agent/run states MUST distinguish at least Idle, Queued, Running, Waiting, Blocked, Paused, Awaiting Approval, Completed, Failed/Error and Disabled as appropriate.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Run states and controls
requirements.text: Blocked and Awaiting Approval MUST NOT be conflated.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Run states and controls
requirements.text: Run controls MUST support Pause/Resume, safe Stop and explicit Cancel where the runtime permits them.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Run states and controls
requirements.text: Resume continues the same AgentRunID and MUST NOT repeat already-completed consequential actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Run states and controls
requirements.text: Progress UI MUST show truthful objective/current step/known plan progress.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Run states and controls
requirements.text: It MUST NOT invent a percentage where the Agent cannot estimate completion meaningfully.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Blockers and approvals
requirements.text: Dulche Agent runs MUST create first-class Blocker records for conditions preventing progress, including category, description, time, whether the Agent can self-resolve, required human action and related entities.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Blockers and approvals
requirements.text: Agents SHOULD attempt safe recovery of foreseeable recoverable blockers when their contract allows it instead of immediately escalating every failure.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Blockers and approvals
requirements.text: Human-required blockers and pending consequential actions MUST surface through relevant invoking surfaces and Home Events/Notifications/approval UX.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Agent-to-Agent delegation
requirements.text: Delegation MUST retain explicit parent/child AgentRun identities and a typed handoff containing objective, required context references, narrowed capability scope and expected output.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Agent-to-Agent delegation
requirements.text: DelegationPolicy MUST be able to constrain allowed persistent Agents/classes, whether Subagents are allowed, maximum concurrency, maximum depth and applicable token/time/cost/tool budgets.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Action Graph, outputs and operational visibility
requirements.text: Every AgentRun MUST use the canonical Dulche Action Graph/log/audit pipeline. 9to1 surfaces may render a concise human-readable Activity view and/or the full Action Graph, but they MUST NOT invent a second execution history.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Action Graph, outputs and operational visibility
requirements.text: Run outputs MUST be typed references to their canonical owning entities where possible, including Files, documents, Boards, code changes, Planner/Task items, messages, research outputs and other artifacts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Action Graph, outputs and operational visibility
requirements.text: Agent runs, blockers, approvals and outputs may be surfaced contextually in Spaces, Agent Builder Preview, Automations that triggered them, Home Events/Notifications and the invoking app.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Action Graph, outputs and operational visibility
requirements.text: No standalone Agents app is required or authoritative.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Lifecycle, recovery and budgets
requirements.text: Long-running/background-capable AgentRuns MUST checkpoint enough state to recover or truthfully fail across app closure, Home/Dulche restart, machine restart where supported, provider disconnect or temporary tool failure.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Lifecycle, recovery and budgets
requirements.text: Recovery states SHOULD distinguish Reconnecting, Recovering, Recovered and Cannot recover rather than silently restarting from scratch.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Lifecycle, recovery and budgets
requirements.text: Agents MUST support configured runtime/model/tool/delegation budgets such as maximum runtime, spend/tokens, tool calls, concurrent children or delegation depth where the platform can enforce them.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Canonical Dulche Agent API
requirements.text: All Agent Builder and 9to1 surface Agent operations MUST resolve through the same Dulche/Den contracts rather than creating app-private Agent stores or runtimes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Agents > Failure behaviour
requirements.text: Dulche Agents MUST return structured failures including AgentNotFound, DefinitionRevisionUnavailable, AgentDisabled, AgentUnavailableInScope, AgentBusy, AgentRunNotFound, RunNotResumable, RunRecoveryFailed, QueueItemNotFound, CapabilityUnavailable, PermissionDenied, ApprovalRequired, BlockerUnresolved, DelegationDenied, DelegationDepthExceeded, ConcurrencyLimitExceeded, BudgetExceeded, ModelUnavailable, ToolUnavailable, MemoryScopeDenied, QuickActionUnavailable, InvalidInvocationContext and RevisionConflict in addition to the global Dulche error contract.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Action Graph > Shared rendering
requirements.text: Any app may surface the renderer where useful.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Action Graph > Shared rendering
requirements.text: For example, Spaces may expose a Show Action Graph button for a response, while Home can expose the same graph from logs or activity history.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Endpoint lifecycle
requirements.text: Any legacy raw-percentage conversion must be separately versioned and cannot override canonical preset mapping.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Endpoint configuration
requirements.text: // Other supported model/endpoint properties may also be configured here.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Capabilities
requirements.text: MCPs, Plugins and Skills are first-class extension types with stable identity, lifecycle, permissions, validation and dedicated APIs; they MUST NOT exist only as ad-hoc wrappers around generic tool calls.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Capabilities
requirements.text: Capabilities can be disabled within scope when they are not permitted or required.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: Dulche MUST expose a canonical request-aware Tool Registry describing the tools, executable capabilities and usable resources that a model can employ to satisfy a request.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: Every registry entry MUST use stable identity and structured metadata.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: At minimum it exposes ToolID/CapabilityID, source type and owner, version/revision, human-readable name, action IDs, semantic capability/intent tags, supported input/output types, parameter schemas, prerequisites, permission scopes, side-effect/risk classification, platform/scope constraints, availability/health and whether user approval or additional configuration is currently required.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: Display name and wording of an action MUST NOT be the sole mechanism used to decide what a tool can do.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: Dulche MUST derive an EffectiveCapabilitySet for each request from the canonical registry.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: Installed-but-unavailable, available-but-unapproved and immediately executable capabilities MUST remain distinguishable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: The active model/orchestrator MUST be given an inspectable, context-budget-aware representation of the EffectiveCapabilitySet.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: Dulche MAY provide a compact high-level catalogue initially and expose query/search APIs for deeper inspection so very large tool inventories do not consume the model's entire context.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: Capability discovery MUST nevertheless remain available throughout the request and MUST refresh when packages, permissions, target apps or connection state materially change.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: Tool selection MUST be intent-based rather than exact-name-based.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: Dulche MUST translate the user's requested outcome into one or more semantic intents and compare those intents against tool capability metadata, schemas and declared examples/aliases.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: For example, a request such as 'remind me tomorrow at 4 PM' MUST be resolvable to a time-triggered Automations operation even if no action is literally named CreateReminder.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: Likewise, 'create an image of ...' MUST resolve to an eligible image-generation capability such as the first-party image app/tool or an installed authorised image-generation Plugin, even if the tool's action is named Generate, Render, Imagine or another equivalent verb.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: Capability resolution MUST support composition.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: If no single tool can fulfil the complete request but a sequence of authorised capabilities can, Dulche MUST be able to construct a typed ResolutionPlan whose steps pass structured outputs/references between tools.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: For example, a request to 'create an image and put it on the title slide' may resolve to image generation followed by Present insertion; a request to 'find the file and email it' may resolve to Files search followed by a Mail/Plugin send action, subject to normal permissions and approvals.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: ResolutionPlan steps MUST identify the selected ToolID/CapabilityID, action, required arguments, expected outputs, dependencies, permission/approval state and why the step satisfies part of the user's intent.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: Capability resolution is planning, not execution: selecting a feasible tool MUST NOT bypass its normal permission, approval, confirmation, privacy, cost or side-effect rules.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: Before a model states or implies that 9to1 cannot perform a requested digital action, it MUST first perform capability feasibility resolution against the current EffectiveCapabilitySet unless the impossibility is already established by a current authoritative hard constraint.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: The model MUST NOT answer 'I cannot directly create images', 'I cannot create reminders', 'I cannot access files' or equivalent merely because the base model itself lacks that native capability when Dulche exposes an authorised tool path that can perform it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: A capability that exists but is missing a prerequisite MUST be described as blocked/configuration-required rather than impossible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: When the missing prerequisite can be resolved within the current request and permission bounds, Dulche SHOULD resolve it or ask only for the specific user decision/input required and then continue.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: If several feasible tools can perform the same intent, Dulche MUST select according to explicit user invocation/instruction first, then applicable app ownership/canonical-data rules, privacy/locality policy, capability fitness, permissions, reliability and configured user preferences.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: Cost/latency MAY participate where policy allows.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: Dulche MUST NOT choose an unrelated or lower-fidelity tool merely because its action name more closely resembles the user's wording.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: 'Create a presentation', 'set a reminder', 'generate an image' and similar outcome requests MUST be sufficient for Dulche to discover and use the appropriate capability when one is available.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: A Skill may contribute instructions/workflow/tool dependencies; an Agent may be invoked as a delegated execution capability; a File/resource may provide required input/context; an App/Plugin/MCP/native action may perform the mutation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: The resolver MUST be able to combine these heterogeneous entries into one plan while preserving their distinct identities, permissions and audit records.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: Dulche MUST expose canonical discovery operations equivalent to Dulche.Tool.List(context?), Dulche.Tool.Search(intent, context?), Dulche.Tool.Get(toolID), Dulche.Tool.Resolve(intent, context?) and Dulche.Tool.ExplainResolution(resolutionID).

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: Resolve MUST return either one or more ranked feasible ResolutionPlans or a structured no-feasible-path result containing the evaluated hard constraints and missing prerequisites.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: Search/Resolve MUST use semantic capability metadata in addition to lexical names.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: The Runtime MUST cache capability metadata efficiently but MUST version/invalidate the cache when relevant package versions, app capabilities, connection state, permissions, policy or provider health change.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: A model MUST NOT continue relying on a stale 'tool unavailable' conclusion after the capability registry has materially changed during the request.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: A tool-result or retrieved document MUST NOT be able to self-register new authority merely by claiming that another tool exists or should be allowed.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: Semantic discovery MUST therefore improve capability use without creating a prompt-injection route to invented tools or escalated permissions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: Failure to resolve a tool path MUST be truthful and inspectable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: Dulche MUST distinguish NoMatchingCapability from MatchingCapabilityUnavailable, MissingPrerequisite, PermissionBlocked and PolicyBlocked.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: When no feasible path exists, the model MAY explain the limitation, but it MUST NOT fabricate a tool or claim to have performed the action.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: The Resolution attempt and selected/no-selected candidates MUST be visible in FullLog/Action Graph at an appropriate level of detail.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution
requirements.text: Acceptance coverage MUST verify at minimum that: a reminder request resolves to an Automations time-based workflow without requiring the phrase 'automation'; an image-generation request invokes an eligible image capability rather than returning a false inability statement; a presentation request can resolve to Present from another app; a multi-tool request produces a dependency-ordered ResolutionPlan; explicit @ invocation overrides automatic source choice; permission/configuration blockers are distinguished from true impossibility; Computer Use does not appear unless explicitly invoked; and removal/disablement of the only matching capability causes a structured no-feasible-path result rather than a fabricated success.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: The public API MUST use the names Subagent and Dulche.Subagent for this capability so callers cannot confuse subagent parallelisation with persistent Agents.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: A Subagent MAY execute one or more model/tool steps and MAY create nested Subagents within inherited limits.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Detached/orphan Subagents are outside the current contract; child work MUST remain causally attached to its parent tree.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Constructing a Subagent object MUST NOT execute work.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: WaitAll returns one terminal outcome per requested child and MUST preserve child identity even when one or more children fail.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Join operations MUST NOT flatten or discard per-child errors, blockers, logs, token usage, model provenance or tool records.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Every Subagent MUST expose SubagentID, ParentSubagentID?, ParentRequestID, RootRequestID, SessionID, EndpointID, Depth, State, CreatedAt, StartedAt?, FinishedAt?, Model and its effective tool/permission/budget configuration.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: IDs MUST be stable for the lifetime/history of that execution and MUST NOT be derived from display names, array position or queue position.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Subagent State MUST distinguish at least Created, Queued, Running, Waiting, Pausing, Paused, Completed, Failed, Blocked, Cancelled and TimedOut.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Waiting means the Subagent is suspended awaiting dependencies/children and MUST NOT retain an execution slot that prevents those dependencies from running.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: A parent waiting on a child that requires the same endpoint MUST yield its execution slot so the child can run; this is mandatory anti-deadlock behaviour.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Sibling Subagents assigned to different eligible endpoints MAY execute concurrently subject to resource, provider and configured concurrency limits.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: An explicitly selected Model or Endpoint MUST NOT be silently replaced merely to increase parallelism; inability to satisfy the explicit selection returns a structured scheduling/capability failure.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Runtime-wide endpoint/resource limits MAY further reduce actual concurrency but MUST NOT increase it above the declared limit.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: None starts without parent conversational context except identity/control metadata required by Runtime.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Child completion MUST NOT silently rewrite earlier parent messages or a sibling’s context.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Multiple children MUST NOT concurrently mutate the same session history without an explicit revision/conflict mechanism.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: A Subagent MUST NOT acquire more authority than its parent/caller.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Subagent creation MUST NOT provide privilege escalation or approval bypass.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: A child MAY request stricter limits than its parent; it MUST NOT enlarge any hard parent/root limit.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: SubagentBudget MUST support MaxTokens, MaxTime, MaxSteps, MaxToolCalls and MaxCost where those quantities are enforceable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Runtime resource policy MAY additionally constrain CPU, GPU, RAM, VRAM and endpoint occupancy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Provider-unavailable cost/token telemetry MUST use the Runtime’s existing null/Na rules and MUST NOT be treated as zero consumption.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Actual descendant consumption MUST be attributed to both the child and its ancestor aggregates without double-counting the same invocation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: If the system reserves budget before dispatch, reservation and settlement MUST be visible separately from actual settled usage.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: SubagentLimits MUST support MaxChildren, MaxParallelChildren and MaxDepth.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Creating a child that would exceed a hard limit MUST fail before child execution begins.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: The Runtime MUST also enforce implementation-wide safety ceilings even when the caller requests larger values.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Parallel sibling execution MUST retain independent terminal outcomes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: One child failure MUST NOT erase successful sibling results.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: SubagentFailurePolicy MUST support at least Collect, FailFast, RequireAll and BestEffort.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: RequireAll treats any non-successful required child as a failed join.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Failure policy changes orchestration/join behaviour only; it MUST NOT suppress logs, errors, blockers or completed side effects.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Stopping a root request MUST stop all unfinished dependent descendants.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Stopping a Subagent MUST stop its unfinished descendants but MUST NOT automatically stop its parent or independent siblings; the parent receives the child’s Cancelled outcome and applies its configured failure policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Pausing a parent MUST prevent it from dispatching new child work.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Restart MUST NOT replay already completed consequential tool/external actions automatically.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Replacement/cancellation of an ancestor MUST invalidate stale descendant approvals and provisional output.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Dulche Den MUST persist the execution-tree metadata required to inspect and recover Subagent work: stable identities, parent/child relationships, request/attempt revisions, effective configuration, states, checkpoints, results, blockers/errors, tool/action records and durable side-effect evidence.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Exact continuation is allowed only when the underlying model/backend/tool supports it; otherwise Restore MUST expose that it is a continuation/restart from checkpoint rather than claiming byte-for-byte execution resumption.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: On crash/restart, completed external/tool side effects MUST be reconciled from durable records before any step is retried.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: A restored tree MUST NOT repeat a non-idempotent completed action merely because the parent process lost volatile state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Action Graph MUST render Subagent execution as an explicit causal tree/graph.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Each Subagent is a distinct node/branch linked to its parent and MAY contain model calls, tool calls, approvals, outputs, child Subagents, blockers and errors.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Parallel siblings MUST be visually distinguishable as concurrent branches rather than flattened into a fabricated sequential order.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Subagent graph nodes MUST expose at least SubagentID, state, parent/root identity, model/endpoint, start/end/duration, token/usage data, tools/actions, errors/blockers and child count subject to permissions/redaction.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Restart-from-here on a Subagent node creates a new attempt/branch under the existing historical tree and MUST NOT rewrite the original branch.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Runtime FullLog MUST retain causal parent IDs and per-execution sequence numbers.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Parallel/nested timing MAY overlap; aggregate timing MUST NOT sum overlapping spans as if they were serial.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: Token/model/tool aggregation MUST use the existing no-double-counting rules for parent and child invocations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Subagents and parallelisation
requirements.text: These follow the Runtime error contract and MUST NOT rely on free-form string parsing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime > Acceptance requirements
requirements.text: Permission/tool inheritance cannot exceed parent/caller authority and still triggers required approval.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den
requirements.text: The user's Den may store models using both a stable ID and a user-facing name.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den
requirements.text: User-facing names are not required to be unique.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den
requirements.text: A property may describe a capability, such as reasoning support, or an identifying property such as an ID.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Model replacement
requirements.text: Immutable artifact/model identity MUST NOT be copied from the old model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Model replacement
requirements.text: safe MAY be specified explicitly as the preservation policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Model replacement
requirements.text: Under safe, only fields classified by the replacement schema as model-independent/safe-to-carry MAY be preserved; all model-derived or compatibility-sensitive fields MUST be recalculated or reset.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > API authority and compatibility
requirements.text: Documented API names, argument order, Result field names and explicit behaviours are binding and must be implemented verbatim.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > API authority and compatibility
requirements.text: This is not an exhaustive API list: compatible overloads and missing APIs may be added.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Requests, sessions and endpoints
requirements.text: No private context/file is sent remotely without the required permission.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Result contract and metric availability
requirements.text: The question mark denotes optional content, not part of the field name.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Result contract and metric availability
requirements.text: This applies to all metrics, including those not originally marked optional and nested model metrics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Result contract and metric availability
requirements.text: Collections with no applicable entries may be null; numeric counts may be a measured zero.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Response content and identity
requirements.text: No text may have been produced for a blocked, cancelled or non-text-only response.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Timing and tokens
requirements.text: Parallel and nested spans may overlap, so phase totals need not sum to TimeElapsed; report timing basis and estimate status.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Timing and tokens
requirements.text: If a contributing provider withholds a required metric, the complete aggregate is Na; return a separate known subtotal and coverage when useful.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Model parameters, location and storage
requirements.text: Shared/unified memory must not be double-counted.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Model parameters, location and storage
requirements.text: State the denominator: an active-set distribution normalises to the active set; active weights expressed as a share of all parameters must be labelled accordingly.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Model parameters, location and storage
requirements.text: Unknown remote storage makes the complete total Na, while a known local subtotal may be shown.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Logs, blockers and errors
requirements.text: Expected operational failures must not depend on string parsing or unhandled exceptions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Streaming and delivery
requirements.text: The submission handle exposes RequestID, Status, a final-result awaitable and optional event stream.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Response controls and queues
requirements.text: The default stacked interruption resumes the interrupted request afterwards where supported and still applicable; superseded/cancelled work must not be revived.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Response controls and queues
requirements.text: Failure/cancellation must not silently discard queued input: expose its dependency/state and revalidate its context before starting.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Response controls and queues
requirements.text: Other endpoints may work independently within resource limits.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Response controls and queues
requirements.text: Paused work may yield to independent sessions, but dependent work in the same session cannot overtake it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Lifecycle, configuration and resources
requirements.text: Manual pause requires resume; inactivity pause may auto-resume on new work with an event.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Lifecycle, configuration and resources
requirements.text: A provider exposing only discrete levels must not be presented as continuous reasoning.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Lifecycle, configuration and resources
requirements.text: Legacy raw-percentage input, if retained, is an explicitly versioned compatibility conversion and must never remap a displayed preset to another level.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Lifecycle, configuration and resources
requirements.text: Pause does not promise memory release while weights remain loaded; pressure must not silently switch models or discard private context.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Providers, permissions and Generative UI
requirements.text: Model/provider fallback must be configured and permission-compatible, never silently send local/private context to a cloud.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Acquisition, replacement and observability
requirements.text: Pin/verify source revisions and expose download progress, cancellation, resumption and required storage.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Acquisition, replacement and observability
requirements.text: Logical IDs/aliases may survive; immutable artifact identity must reflect the replacement.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent request execution
requirements.text: PersistencePolicy MUST support at least Standard and Persistent.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent request execution
requirements.text: Persistent is a durable root-request policy intended for work that should continue until its user-visible completion predicate has been satisfied.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent request execution
requirements.text: A Persistent request MUST define or derive an inspectable CompletionContract from the user's request, active Skill requirements and target-app acceptance criteria.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent request execution
requirements.text: Completed is valid only when required outputs exist, required validation/verification has run where applicable, required target mutations are confirmed and no required work item remains Pending, Running, Retryable or Blocked.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent request execution
requirements.text: Soft request duration limits, provider execution leases and internal scheduling slices MUST NOT terminate a Persistent request merely because a continuation boundary was reached.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent request execution
requirements.text: When continued execution requires a new model invocation, endpoint lease or recovered process, Dulche MUST create a linked attempt under the same RootRequestID, restore the latest safe state/checkpoint and continue.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent request execution
requirements.text: Completed consequential actions MUST be reconciled before retry so persistence does not duplicate side effects.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent request execution
requirements.text: Persistent requests MUST remain cancellable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent request execution
requirements.text: Persistence MUST NOT reinterpret an explicit user Stop as a transient interruption to auto-resume.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent request execution
requirements.text: They MUST NOT be implemented as ReplacePrompt or StopResponse, and MUST NOT cause already completed actions to replay.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent request execution
requirements.text: Persistent orchestration MUST maintain a dependency-aware work graph.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent request execution
requirements.text: Persistence MUST NOT convert a denied action into an allowed action or silently purchase/consume resources beyond configured policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent request execution
requirements.text: Persistent state MUST survive supported Home/Dulche restarts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent request execution
requirements.text: Den MUST retain RootRequestID, request revision, CompletionContract, task/dependency state, SteeringMessages, blockers, checkpoints, completed side-effect evidence, active Skill versions and attempt lineage required to resume without fabricating progress or repeating consequential work.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Context compaction and Context Summarisation
requirements.text: Dulche MUST track the effective context budget for every model invocation and MAY initiate automatic compaction before hard exhaustion using model/provider-specific safety margins.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Context compaction and Context Summarisation
requirements.text: Compaction MUST preserve semantic obligations required to continue the task: current user instructions and constraints, active permissions/trust decisions, CompletionContract, outstanding tasks and blockers, accepted decisions, stable object/file/artifact IDs, current revisions, completed consequential actions, verification evidence, relevant source provenance and any exact values whose precision is required.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Context compaction and Context Summarisation
requirements.text: Redundant conversational phrasing, duplicated status chatter and obsolete intermediate reasoning MAY be reduced.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Context compaction and Context Summarisation
requirements.text: Compaction MUST be non-destructive to durable history.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Context compaction and Context Summarisation
requirements.text: A model MUST NOT be told that omitted content never existed merely because it is outside the active compacted view.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Context compaction and Context Summarisation
requirements.text: If ordinary compaction cannot create enough safe context without materially losing required information or required media fidelity, Dulche MUST transition to Context Summarisation rather than silently dropping required content or returning ContextExceeded immediately.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Context compaction and Context Summarisation
requirements.text: Section boundaries MUST be deterministic and provenance-preserving.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Context compaction and Context Summarisation
requirements.text: A merge MUST NOT discard a requirement merely because it appears only once.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Context compaction and Context Summarisation
requirements.text: Conflicting instructions or facts MUST remain represented as a conflict with source references instead of being flattened into an invented resolution.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Context compaction and Context Summarisation
requirements.text: Exact code, identifiers, numeric values, legal/technical constraints or other precision-sensitive content that cannot be safely paraphrased MUST remain as pinned excerpts or stable references rather than approximate prose.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Context compaction and Context Summarisation
requirements.text: Images, audio, video and other large artifacts SHOULD remain out-of-band as stable artifact references wherever the target model can retrieve them on demand.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Context compaction and Context Summarisation
requirements.text: Context Summarisation MAY summarise authorised derived observations/metadata, but MUST NOT claim that visual or media detail was preserved if the summariser could not inspect it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Context compaction and Context Summarisation
requirements.text: A local summariser model MAY be used automatically when an eligible local model is available under the configured routing/policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Context compaction and Context Summarisation
requirements.text: If cloud summarisation is required to continue, permission is absent and no eligible local summariser can satisfy the job, Dulche MUST surface ContextSummarisationPermissionRequired/ContextCapacityBlocked as a non-destructive blocker.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Context compaction and Context Summarisation
requirements.text: Dulche MUST expose canonical operations equivalent to Dulche.Context.Compact(sessionID, options?), Dulche.Context.Summarise(sessionID, options?) and Dulche.Context.GetState(sessionID).

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Context compaction and Context Summarisation
requirements.text: Results MUST report source ranges/revisions, target model/context limit, method, summariser ModelID when used, retained pinned items, omitted/referenced artifacts, token estimates where available and whether the resulting context is sufficient for the next invocation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Computer Use
requirements.text: Computer Use is a first-class Dulche capability but MUST be opt-in per request.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Computer Use
requirements.text: An ordinary natural-language request, an @App mention or failure of a typed app API MUST NOT silently activate Computer Use.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Computer Use
requirements.text: The Computer Use capability may control eligible graphical applications through supported pointer, keyboard, accessibility/automation and visual-interaction primitives.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Computer Use
requirements.text: It SHOULD use the fastest reliable state channel available, including accessibility/automation metadata where appropriate, avoid unnecessary human-speed delays, batch safe independent interactions where supported and verify state transitions instead of relying on fixed sleeps.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Computer Use
requirements.text: Speed MUST NOT weaken verification or permission gates.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Computer Use
requirements.text: Home settings MUST allow the user to change this policy to automatic approval for eligible apps and to an Approve All eligible-apps policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Computer Use
requirements.text: Auto-approve and Approve All MUST NOT bypass hard exclusions, administrator policy, OS security boundaries or other non-overridable safeguards.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Computer Use
requirements.text: Generic Computer Use MUST NOT attach to, send input to, automate or manipulate game executables or anti-cheat-protected game surfaces, including games launched or managed through platforms such as Steam or Epic Games Launcher.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Computer Use
requirements.text: Play interaction MUST occur through Play's typed GameDefinition/Match/contestant actions and capability isolation, not by using generic Computer Use to drive an external game client.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Computer Use
requirements.text: Every Computer Use run MUST produce an inspectable action stream with target app/window identity, action type, timestamps, relevant pre/post state evidence, approvals, failures and side effects.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Computer Use
requirements.text: Sensitive screen regions, credentials and typed secrets MUST follow the normal redaction and permission rules; logs MUST NOT become a second plaintext credential store.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Computer Use
requirements.text: Dulche Autoreview MUST inspect proposed and recent Computer Use actions continuously.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Computer Use
requirements.text: It MUST flag patterns including repeated identical or near-identical actions without progress, repeated failing commands, oscillation between states, privilege escalation, bulk/destructive deletion, destructive shell commands such as rm -rf or platform equivalents, security-setting changes, suspicious executable/download flows and other high-risk sequences.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Computer Use
requirements.text: High-confidence imminent destructive risk MUST be able to pause the next action for review rather than merely add a passive warning.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Computer Use
requirements.text: Autoreview findings are structured ProblemEvents and MUST feed the shared Problem handling contract.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Computer Use
requirements.text: A Computer Use recovery intervention MUST preserve the current request, state and logs and SHOULD redirect to a safer or more direct interaction strategy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Computer Use
requirements.text: It MUST NOT hide that a risky action was proposed or attempted.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Thinking logs, work state and ETA
requirements.text: Home MUST expose one global user preference with the modes Precise, Concise, Detailed and Ramble; compatible apps inherit it unless an explicitly supported per-surface override exists.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Thinking logs, work state and ETA
requirements.text: It MUST suppress repetitive self-talk and events that do not change task state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Thinking logs, work state and ETA
requirements.text: These summaries MAY be generated from richer telemetry but MUST remain faithful to the underlying action/state.
