requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Thinking logs, work state and ETA
requirements.text: It MUST still distinguish observed facts, tool results, summaries and model reasoning.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Thinking logs, work state and ETA
requirements.text: Ramble MUST NOT reconstruct, infer or falsely label undisclosed private chain-of-thought as if it had been exposed by the model/provider.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Thinking logs, work state and ETA
requirements.text: It MUST NOT change the model's configured reasoning effort, tool permissions, stored audit truth, Action Graph or provider privacy rules.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Thinking logs, work state and ETA
requirements.text: The visual treatment MUST be lower-emphasis/ghost-like relative to user/model message text while still meeting accessibility contrast requirements and MUST use non-colour cues so users can distinguish message content from thinking/work content.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Thinking logs, work state and ETA
requirements.text: After 60 seconds of continuous active execution in one foreground 9to1 turn, Dulche MUST request an ETA from the active orchestrating model through a canonical ETA request.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Thinking logs, work state and ETA
requirements.text: The model returns an estimated completion timestamp plus optional confidence/reason.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Thinking logs, work state and ETA
requirements.text: Dulche MUST expose an operation equivalent to Dulche.RequestETA(requestID).

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Thinking logs, work state and ETA
requirements.text: An ETA response includes RequestID, AttemptID, EstimatedCompletionAt, GeneratedAt and optional Confidence/Reason.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Thinking logs, work state and ETA
requirements.text: If the active model cannot provide a meaningful estimate, the result is explicitly unavailable; Dulche MUST NOT invent a timestamp.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Thinking logs, work state and ETA
requirements.text: Material replanning MAY request an updated ETA and MUST replace rather than stack stale estimates in the primary UI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Problem detection, autoreview and recovery
requirements.text: The canonical ProblemType set MUST support at least Looping, NoProgress/Stuck, Repetition, HallucinationOrFabrication, OverAgreement/Sycophancy, InstructionDrift, ContradictionWithGroundedState, RepeatedToolFailure, UnsafeActionPattern and Other/UserReported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Problem detection, autoreview and recovery
requirements.text: Additional typed categories MAY be added versionably without collapsing distinct existing meanings.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Problem detection, autoreview and recovery
requirements.text: Loop detection MUST consider semantic and action-level repetition, not only identical text.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Problem detection, autoreview and recovery
requirements.text: Hallucination/fabrication detection SHOULD use available grounded evidence such as tool results, canonical app state, source provenance, stable object IDs and completion evidence.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Problem detection, autoreview and recovery
requirements.text: Dulche MUST flag fabricated claims of completed actions, nonexistent files/entities/tool results or unsupported factual assertions when confidence is sufficient; it MUST NOT treat disagreement with an unverified model statement as proof that the user is wrong.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Problem detection, autoreview and recovery
requirements.text: OverAgreement/Sycophancy detection SHOULD flag responses that materially adopt or endorse a user's factual premise, conclusion or requested assessment without adequate evidence when the task calls for grounded evaluation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Problem detection, autoreview and recovery
requirements.text: Recovery prompts the model to re-evaluate the evidence and user request; it MUST NOT mechanically disagree with the user merely to appear independent.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Problem detection, autoreview and recovery
requirements.text: The directive tells the model what failure pattern was detected, relevant evidence and the required correction, such as stop repeating the command, reassess grounded state, use a different strategy or verify the claimed result.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Problem detection, autoreview and recovery
requirements.text: Runtime recovery directives MUST NOT be forged as user-authored messages.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Problem detection, autoreview and recovery
requirements.text: If the detected problem is associated with a proposed consequential or dangerous tool/Computer Use action, Dulche MAY pause dispatch before the action and require re-planning or applicable approval.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Problem detection, autoreview and recovery
requirements.text: Lower-risk reasoning-quality problems SHOULD normally correct the active request without cancelling the turn or discarding valid completed work.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Problem detection, autoreview and recovery
requirements.text: Every conversational 9to1 AI surface MUST expose a small Problem pill above/adjacent to the compose bar.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Problem detection, autoreview and recovery
requirements.text: The user can invoke it even when automatic detection did not fire, select a ProblemType and optionally add a note.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Problem detection, autoreview and recovery
requirements.text: ProblemEvents MUST record stable ProblemEventID, RequestID/AttemptID, category, detector source (automatic, autoreview or user), timestamp, safe evidence references, confidence when machine-detected, intervention taken, affected action/node and resolution outcome.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Problem detection, autoreview and recovery
requirements.text: They MUST appear in FullLog/Action Graph with sensitive content redacted as required.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Problem detection, autoreview and recovery
requirements.text: Problem detection MUST itself be bounded and loop-safe.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Problem detection, autoreview and recovery
requirements.text: A false-positive recovery that does not improve state MUST NOT trigger an endless reviewer/model ping-pong.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Problem detection, autoreview and recovery
requirements.text: Repeated unresolved problems should escalate to a visible blocker, alternate model/strategy where permitted, or user decision while preserving completed work.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Model catalogue
requirements.text: IDs provide unambiguous model references; names are intended for human-facing use and may be duplicated, which is why name lookup returns a list rather than assuming a single match.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Den privacy, encryption and consent — mandatory security contract
requirements.text: DEN-PRIV-001 — Encryption: Den personal data, including memory, context, conversations, embeddings, indexes, journals, attachments, backups and snapshots, MUST use authenticated encryption at rest.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Den privacy, encryption and consent — mandatory security contract
requirements.text: Keys MUST be held in an OS-backed secure key store or equivalent, never hardcoded or logged.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Den privacy, encryption and consent — mandatory security contract
requirements.text: Exports MUST be encrypted by default; authorised plaintext export requires explicit informed confirmation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Den privacy, encryption and consent — mandatory security contract
requirements.text: DEN-PRIV-002 — Opt-in continuity: Cross-app, cross-Agent, cross-harness, cross-device and cross-provider access to Den personal context MUST be disabled by default.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Den privacy, encryption and consent — mandatory security contract
requirements.text: Installing an app, signing in, selecting a model or enabling Den persistence MUST NOT silently enable sharing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Den privacy, encryption and consent — mandatory security contract
requirements.text: DEN-PRIV-003 — App permissions: Every consuming app, Agent, Assistant, Plugin, MCP, connector or tool MUST receive explicit, scoped user authorisation to request personal Den context.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Den privacy, encryption and consent — mandatory security contract
requirements.text: Grants MUST distinguish read, write, create-memory, cross-app reuse and share/export as relevant; show recipient, purpose, scope and expiry; support inspection, revocation and deletion.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Den privacy, encryption and consent — mandatory security contract
requirements.text: DEN-PRIV-004 — Model-only semantic access: Personal Den content may be disclosed only as minimum-necessary context directly to the explicitly authorised model inference request through the trusted Dulche broker, and NOT as raw data to other application APIs, Plugins, MCPs, tools, telemetry, analytics, arbitrary app code or external services.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Den privacy, encryption and consent — mandatory security contract
requirements.text: Broker-side permission and data-minimisation checks MUST enforce this boundary.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Den privacy, encryption and consent — mandatory security contract
requirements.text: DEN-PRIV-005 — No onward disclosure: Models/Agents MUST be instructed not to quote, forward, paraphrase, embed in tool arguments or otherwise relay protected Den content to other app components, tools, APIs, third parties, other users or recipients without specific user authorisation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Den privacy, encryption and consent — mandatory security contract
requirements.text: Crucially, instructions alone are insufficient: Dulche MUST enforce tool-input/output and action-argument information-flow restrictions and deny unapproved onward transmission.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Den privacy, encryption and consent — mandatory security contract
requirements.text: Sensitive context must not be exposed in generated UI, logs, traces or diagnostics by default.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Den privacy, encryption and consent — mandatory security contract
requirements.text: DEN-PRIV-006 — User control: Users MUST be able to see which apps/models can access which Den scopes, view why data was used, grant and revoke access, selectively forget/delete entries and disable cross-app continuity without disabling all local functionality.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Den privacy, encryption and consent — mandatory security contract
requirements.text: Consent must be separate from a generic terms-of-service agreement; changes to access scope require renewed consent.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Den privacy, encryption and consent — mandatory security contract
requirements.text: DEN-PRIV-008 — Acceptance: Tests MUST verify default-deny cross-app isolation, per-app prompts and revocation, encrypted on-disk files/backups, prohibited tool/API exfiltration, prompt-injection resistance, cloud-provider opt-in, permission-aware retrieval, and correct behaviour when permissions change mid-run.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Storage structure and portability
requirements.text: Portable records use UTF-8 JSON; local databases and indexes may accelerate access but must not be the only readable copy or create an incompatible private format.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Storage structure and portability
requirements.text: The manifest identifies DenID, FormatVersion, SchemaVersion, minimum reader/writer versions, namespaces, storage locations and required capabilities.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Identity, namespaces and model records
requirements.text: Model replacement may retain logical ID/name but records changed artifact/provider identity, retained/reset settings and rollback history.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent Memory
requirements.text: Persistent Memory is a core Dulche Den subsystem for durable cross-session information about the user, recurring entities, preferences, decisions, projects and other scoped context that Dulche should be able to retrieve in future conversations or authorised surfaces.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent Memory
requirements.text: A persistent MemoryEntry should carry stable identity, content or structured value, subject/entity, memory type/category, scope, source/provenance, confidence where applicable, created/updated state, supersession/correction relationships, retention state and user-edited/locked state where supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent Memory > Scopes
requirements.text: Supported scopes should include global/user memory plus narrower project, Agent, app/surface or other explicit contexts where appropriate.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent Memory > Scopes
requirements.text: Retrieval MUST respect both scope and permission.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent Memory > Creation and retrieval
requirements.text: Dulche may create or update memories from eligible conversations/context according to the user's Memory Frequency and memory policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent Memory > Creation and retrieval
requirements.text: Retrieval is relevance-based: only memories useful to the active request/context should be injected, rather than the complete memory store.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent Memory > Creation and retrieval
requirements.text: Den MUST retain enough provenance/revision information to distinguish an explicit user statement from an inference and to avoid repeatedly resurfacing a memory that has been corrected, superseded or deleted.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent Memory > Memory Frequency
requirements.text: Settings MUST expose a Memory Frequency preference with exactly four user-facing levels: Never, Sometimes, Often and Always.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent Memory > Memory Frequency
requirements.text: Never: Dulche MUST NOT autonomously create, reinforce or update Persistent Memory from ordinary interactions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent Memory > Memory Frequency
requirements.text: Changing Memory Frequency affects future autonomous memory behaviour; it MUST NOT silently delete existing memories.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent Memory > Temporary chats in Spaces
requirements.text: While a chat is temporary, Dulche MUST NOT autonomously create, update, reinforce, merge or promote Persistent Memory from that conversation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent Memory > Temporary chats in Spaces
requirements.text: Any explicit action that would save new Persistent Memory from a Temporary Chat must be unavailable or clearly report that memory creation is disabled for temporary chats.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent Memory > Temporary chats in Spaces
requirements.text: Temporary-chat memory-write suppression MUST NOT be bypassed by an Agent, plugin, Skill, tool or Background Learning pipeline.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent Memory > Temporary chats in Spaces
requirements.text: Whether existing authorised memories are retrieved into a temporary chat is a separate context/privacy policy and MUST NOT be inferred from the memory-write prohibition.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent Memory > Management and lifecycle
requirements.text: Users must be able to inspect, search, edit/correct, supersede and delete persistent memories through the appropriate settings/Den surfaces.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Persistent Memory > Management and lifecycle
requirements.text: Memory export/import must preserve scopes, provenance and deletion/supersession semantics rather than flattening entries into plain prose.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Synchronisation and conflicts
requirements.text: Cross-device/team sync is optional and namespace-scoped.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Compatibility and migration
requirements.text: Compatible writers preserve unknown optional fields; unknown security-critical fields or required capabilities block unsafe writes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Compatibility and migration
requirements.text: Unsupported newer versions may open read-only when safe, never discard fields to force a downgrade.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Generative UI
requirements.text: Generated interfaces may be visual, interactive and stateful, but MUST be expressed through a validated declarative Generative UI schema and MUST NOT execute arbitrary model-generated application code.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Rendering and trust boundary
requirements.text: Any authorised 9to1 app may host a GenerativeContainer without implementing its own incompatible renderer.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Rendering and trust boundary
requirements.text: Dulche may choose the structure and composition of the interface, including novel layouts, but the model output is data/schema rather than executable JavaScript, Python, shell commands, native binaries or arbitrary application code.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Primitive composition
requirements.text: The supported primitive set should include, where appropriate, text/heading blocks, icons or generated illustrations, cards, badges/tags, buttons, inputs, dropdowns, toggles, sliders, chips, lists, tables, grids, tabs, accordions, progress indicators, layout containers, drag containers, drop zones, connectors/relationships, semantic-object views and other safe CUI primitives.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Primitive composition
requirements.text: Unsupported component types MUST be rejected or downgraded safely; a model cannot create a new privileged executable component merely by naming it in the schema.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > State and interaction
requirements.text: Generated surfaces may maintain bounded typed state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Progressive conversational evolution
requirements.text: A generated surface is a first-class conversation artifact and may evolve across turns.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Progressive conversational evolution
requirements.text: Dulche should be able to patch or transform an existing surface instead of rebuilding unrelated output from scratch.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Progressive conversational evolution
requirements.text: Updates must address stable SurfaceID/component/state identities or equivalent schema identities so user interaction state is retained wherever the requested transformation allows it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Typed actions and side effects
requirements.text: An action definition includes stable identity, expected input schema, allowed state mutation or API binding, required capability/permission and result/error contract.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Typed actions and side effects
requirements.text: Pure presentation and local interaction may execute inside the Generative UI runtime without external side effects.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Typed actions and side effects
requirements.text: Generative UI MUST NOT be a path around security prompts or tool permissions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Data binding and semantic objects
requirements.text: A rendered card or table row that represents a canonical object should reference that object rather than silently creating a disconnected copy unless the user explicitly asks for a snapshot.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Ephemeral and saved artifacts
requirements.text: A generated surface may remain ephemeral to the current response/session or be promoted through an explicit supported conversion/save path.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Third-party visual examples and assets
requirements.text: Generative UI may reproduce the functional idea or spatial structure needed to explain a third-party product/game without copying proprietary artwork merely to imitate the source.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Third-party visual examples and assets
requirements.text: Where licensed/authorised assets are not available, it should use generic, stylised, text-labelled or newly generated representations sufficient to communicate the concept.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Third-party visual examples and assets
requirements.text: Example: if the user asks how an item is crafted in Minecraft, Dulche may create a visual 3x3 crafting-grid representation using generic/stylised ingredient tokens and an output slot rather than copied official item textures or proprietary interface artwork.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Third-party visual examples and assets
requirements.text: In later turns the same surface may be made interactive using approved drag/drop primitives so the user can move ingredient tokens, receive validation, request hints or turn the recipe into a quiz.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Accessibility and visual consistency
requirements.text: Generated UI MUST inherit the host CUI theme/design system and remain accessible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Accessibility and visual consistency
requirements.text: The runtime should enforce semantic roles, labels, focusability/order, keyboard operation, screen-reader information, non-colour-only meaning and accessible alternatives for interactions such as drag/drop wherever the component library supports them.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Failure and fallback
requirements.text: Invalid, unsupported or unsafe generated schemas MUST fail closed without executing arbitrary content.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Failure and fallback
requirements.text: Dulche may repair/regenerate the affected surface or fall back to a non-interactive/native representation while preserving the user-visible answer where possible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche Den > Result contract and acceptance
requirements.text: The payload must identify schema version, surface identity, component tree, declared state/bindings and declared actions/capabilities required to reproduce the surface safely.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Background Learning > Eligible learning classes
requirements.text: For example, repeated questions about cars may lead to an Interest record for cars and a local Cars Knowledge Bank containing useful terminology, concepts and sourced reference material.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Background Learning > Eligible learning classes
requirements.text: Other relevant personalisation information: additional permitted information that materially improves responses, such as preferred terminology, recurring goals, explanation preferences, established project conventions, frequently used tools, entity relationships and corrections that should influence future response behaviour.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Background Learning > Usage and project learning
requirements.text: The usage-learning layer SHOULD retain useful semantic state rather than an indiscriminate permanent clickstream.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Background Learning > Usage and project learning
requirements.text: For example, it may learn that Build is frequently used for a particular project or that a project is currently active.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Background Learning > Usage and project learning
requirements.text: Raw activity used to derive these signals should be retained only to the extent required by the configured retention/privacy model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Background Learning > Usage and project learning
requirements.text: It MUST remain scope-aware: project-specific learning does not automatically become unrelated global context.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Background Learning > Interest Knowledge Banks
requirements.text: Knowledge Banks may be created automatically from recurring interests or explicitly managed by the user.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Background Learning > Interest Knowledge Banks
requirements.text: Knowledge Bank entries may include reusable summaries, terminology, relationships, reference facts and other material previously obtained from authorised local sources, user interactions or trusted retrieval.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Background Learning > Interest Knowledge Banks
requirements.text: Factual entries MUST retain enough provenance/freshness information for Dulche to distinguish durable knowledge from information that may need refreshing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Background Learning > Interest Knowledge Banks
requirements.text: Dulche may use both when relevant, but they remain separately inspectable and manageable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Background Learning > Structured learned state
requirements.text: Background Learning MUST store structured learned records rather than relying on one opaque free-form profile.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Background Learning > Structured learned state
requirements.text: Records should carry stable identity, category/type, subject/entity, learned value, provenance, confidence, creation/update state, last reinforcement/use where useful, freshness/expiry semantics and user-edited/locked state where applicable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Background Learning > Structured learned state
requirements.text: If a user corrects an inferred preference, project status or interest, the system MUST revise/supersede the stale inference instead of allowing both to compete indefinitely as equally valid facts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Background Learning > Selective retrieval
requirements.text: The complete learning store MUST NOT be injected into every request.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Background Learning > Selective retrieval
requirements.text: Dulche must retrieve only learning context relevant to the active request, Agent, app and permission scope.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Background Learning > Selective retrieval
requirements.text: Retrieval should use current entities/topics/project context to select the smallest useful set of records and Knowledge Bank material.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Background Learning > Privacy and cloud boundaries
requirements.text: It MUST NOT be sold, used to build advertising profiles or indiscriminately uploaded to third parties.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Background Learning > Privacy and cloud boundaries
requirements.text: The implementation MUST distinguish permission to learn/store information from permission to disclose that information externally.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Background Learning > Privacy and cloud boundaries
requirements.text: Any optional cross-device synchronisation of Background Learning state must be user-controlled and protected by the applicable authenticated/encrypted 9to1 sync/storage architecture.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Background Learning > Privacy and cloud boundaries
requirements.text: The feature MUST remain useful locally and must not require insecure cloud upload merely to personalise responses.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Background Learning > User controls
requirements.text: Users must be able to enable/disable Background Learning, pause new learning, inspect learned information, inspect and manage topic Knowledge Banks, correct inaccurate learning, delete individual learned records or a complete topic bank, clear learned categories and configure which apps/projects/categories may contribute where supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Background Learning > User controls
requirements.text: Disabling learning stops creation/reinforcement of new learned state but MUST NOT silently delete existing Persistent Memory or unrelated user data.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Background Learning > Relationship to Persistent Memory
requirements.text: Neither feature may silently enable, disable, clear or substitute for the other.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Background Learning > Relationship to Persistent Memory
requirements.text: Background Learning may identify information that would be useful as a durable memory, but any conversion into Persistent Memory must use the Memory subsystem and preserve that the source was an inference rather than an explicit user statement.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support
requirements.text: Dulche MUST support acting as an MCP client for authorised local/remote MCP servers and acting as an MCP server when 9-1 intentionally exposes approved capabilities to external MCP clients.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support
requirements.text: MCP execution MUST use the same permission, audit, cancellation, timeout and structured-error contracts as native Dulche tools.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support > Identity and lifecycle
requirements.text: Every configured MCP connection MUST have a stable ServerID independent of display name or transport address.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support > Identity and lifecycle
requirements.text: Configuration MUST record role (client/server), transport/process/endpoint definition, credential references, trust state, capability snapshot/version and owner/scope.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support > Identity and lifecycle
requirements.text: Credentials MUST be stored by secure reference and MUST NOT be embedded as plaintext in project manifests or logs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support > Identity and lifecycle
requirements.text: Client connections MUST expose at least Disconnected, Connecting, Ready, Degraded, Reconnecting, Failed and Stopped states.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support > Identity and lifecycle
requirements.text: Reconnect MUST NOT replay a previously completed consequential tool call.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support > Identity and lifecycle
requirements.text: A broken connection returns structured transport/provider failures and MUST NOT be reported as Ready.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support > Capability discovery and schemas
requirements.text: Dulche MUST discover and represent the capabilities actually exposed by an MCP server, including tools and, where supported by the negotiated MCP version/server, resources and prompts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support > Capability discovery and schemas
requirements.text: Tool input/output schemas MUST be validated before dispatch/consumption.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support > Capability discovery and schemas
requirements.text: Capability changes MUST invalidate stale cached schemas before later calls use them.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support > Capability discovery and schemas
requirements.text: Capability identity is server-scoped: two MCP servers MAY expose the same human-readable tool name without collision because the canonical identity includes ServerID plus capability identity/name.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support > Capability discovery and schemas
requirements.text: User-facing aliases MAY exist but MUST NOT replace stable server-scoped identity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support > Permissions and execution
requirements.text: Each tool/resource capability MUST resolve through Dulche/Home permission and risk evaluation according to its effective read/write/external-side-effect scope.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support > Permissions and execution
requirements.text: Server-provided descriptions/content MUST NOT grant permissions, alter trust state or override caller restrictions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support > Permissions and execution
requirements.text: MCP tool execution MUST support cancellation/timeouts when supported by the active transport/server and MUST record when cancellation is best-effort or too late because an external action already completed.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support > Permissions and execution
requirements.text: Results, approvals, failures, blockers and side effects MUST appear in ToolLog, AuditLog, FullLog and Action Graph like equivalent native tools.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support > Canonical MCP API
requirements.text: Unsupported capabilities MUST return UnsupportedCapability rather than fabricated empty results.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support > Canonical MCP API
requirements.text: Protocol-version-specific functionality MAY extend this API while preserving compatibility with the stable core.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support > Tool Builder integration and acceptance
requirements.text: MCP projects produced by AI Studio Tool Builder MUST validate against the same Dulche MCP connection/schema/permission contract used at runtime.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support > Plugins and web integrations — WebMCP and site-hosted MCP servers
requirements.text: Support MUST be added for WebMCP-enabled web pages and for remote MCP servers hosted by websites.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support > Plugins and web integrations — WebMCP and site-hosted MCP servers
requirements.text: The existing Plugin/MCP integration system MUST expose discovery/inspection, connection or permission setup, tool invocation, cancellation where supported, and disconnect/revocation for the appropriate surface.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support > Plugins and web integrations — WebMCP and site-hosted MCP servers
requirements.text: WebMCP integration MUST use the supported browser capability with explicit capability detection and origin boundaries.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support > Plugins and web integrations — WebMCP and site-hosted MCP servers
requirements.text: Site-hosted MCP connections MUST support the applicable remote HTTP transport and protocol-version/authentication contracts rather than assuming that a page URL is itself a valid MCP endpoint.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support > Plugins and web integrations — WebMCP and site-hosted MCP servers
requirements.text: The implementation MUST record supported browser/protocol versions and visibly report unsupported capabilities instead of claiming a successful integration.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support > Plugins and web integrations — WebMCP and site-hosted MCP servers
requirements.text: Both routes MUST retain Home-brokered permissions, declared scopes, caller/site identity, secret protection and consequential-action approval.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support > Plugins and web integrations — WebMCP and site-hosted MCP servers
requirements.text: Tool descriptions, page content and tool results MUST NOT be treated as authority to expand permissions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support > Web integration API and acceptance
requirements.text: Browser-side WebMCP bindings MUST preserve browser origin/document identity; remote MCP bindings MUST preserve ServerID, endpoint identity and negotiated protocol/transport metadata.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > MCP Support > Web integration API and acceptance
requirements.text: Neither route may claim success from a placeholder, silently use a page URL as an MCP endpoint or expose secrets in logs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins
requirements.text: A Plugin packages executable or integrated capabilities and MAY expose typed tools/actions, CUI surfaces or external-service functionality.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins
requirements.text: Neither type is interchangeable with MCP, although a Skill or Plugin MAY declare an MCP dependency.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Common package contract
requirements.text: Every Skill and Plugin MUST have a versioned manifest containing stable PackageID, package type, version, minimum/compatible Dulche versions, provenance/origin, declared capabilities, required/requested permissions, dependencies, entry points/resources, update metadata and integrity/signature information when the distribution channel supports signing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Common package contract
requirements.text: Display name MUST NOT be used as package identity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Common package contract
requirements.text: Manifest parsing and dependency resolution MUST be deterministic.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Common package contract
requirements.text: Unknown required manifest fields/capabilities block installation or enablement with a structured compatibility failure; unknown optional fields MAY be preserved for forward compatibility.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Common package contract
requirements.text: Packages MUST NOT execute code merely because their manifest was inspected or imported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Lifecycle, trust and permissions
requirements.text: Installing a package registers its files/manifest but MUST NOT automatically enable it for every caller, grant requested permissions, connect external accounts or grant Accept and Always Trust.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Lifecycle, trust and permissions
requirements.text: Package lifecycle MUST expose at least Installed, Disabled, Enabled, Updating, Failed and Quarantined states.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Lifecycle, trust and permissions
requirements.text: A package that fails integrity/signature/compatibility validation MUST NOT become Enabled.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Lifecycle, trust and permissions
requirements.text: Updates MUST be version-aware and transactional.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Lifecycle, trust and permissions
requirements.text: Dulche MUST validate/stage the new version and dependency graph before switching the active version.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Lifecycle, trust and permissions
requirements.text: Failure during update MUST leave the previous known-good version available when rollback is technically possible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Lifecycle, trust and permissions
requirements.text: Package updates MUST NOT silently expand effective permissions; newly requested scopes require a new permission decision.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Lifecycle, trust and permissions
requirements.text: Uninstall MUST define what happens to package-owned persistent data.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Lifecycle, trust and permissions
requirements.text: Shared/user-authored data MUST NOT be silently deleted merely because a package is removed.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Lifecycle, trust and permissions
requirements.text: Orphaned package state MAY be retained for recovery/reinstall according to explicit retention policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Skill model
requirements.text: It MAY contain instructions, workflow definitions, templates/prompts, context-selection rules, examples, resources/files and references to permitted tools/Plugins/MCP capabilities.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Skill model
requirements.text: A Skill MUST NOT gain arbitrary code execution solely by being a Skill; executable behaviour requires an explicitly declared/authorised executable extension capability such as a Plugin/tool dependency.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Skill model
requirements.text: Skill activation MUST be explicit and observable in request/run metadata.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Skill model
requirements.text: Dulche MUST record which Skill IDs/versions contributed to a request so Result provenance, logs and Action Graph can identify the active Skill set.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Skill model
requirements.text: Conflicting or incompatible Skills MUST resolve through a deterministic precedence/compatibility rule or return Conflict; Dulche MUST NOT silently merge contradictory required policies.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Built-in Persistent skill
requirements.text: Dulche MUST ship a first-party built-in Skill with the canonical display name Persistent and a stable reserved SkillID.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Built-in Persistent skill
requirements.text: Persistent activation MUST be explicit and visible in request metadata, the compose invocation state, FullLog and Action Graph.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Built-in Persistent skill
requirements.text: It MAY be invoked through the shared @ resource picker as @Persistent.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Built-in Persistent skill
requirements.text: The active version MUST be recorded like every other Skill so later inspection can prove which persistence contract governed the run.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Built-in Persistent skill
requirements.text: The Persistent Skill MUST use the canonical Dulche persistent-request contract.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Built-in Persistent skill
requirements.text: In particular, an ordinary checkpoint, context compaction boundary, provider lease expiry, model restart, recoverable tool timeout or similar continuation boundary MUST NOT be treated as successful completion of the turn.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Built-in Persistent skill
requirements.text: While a Persistent turn is running, an ordinary follow-up message sent by the user MUST join the same root turn as a SteeringMessage and MUST NOT implicitly cancel, replace or interrupt the active work.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Built-in Persistent skill
requirements.text: A blocker that cannot be resolved within the request's effective permission and capability bounds MUST be surfaced to the user as a structured blocker immediately.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Built-in Persistent skill
requirements.text: The blocker MUST isolate only the dependent work.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Built-in Persistent skill
requirements.text: Dulche MUST continue any independent runnable work in the same persistent turn; if no independent work remains, the turn enters AwaitingUser without being misreported as complete or timed out.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Built-in Persistent skill
requirements.text: Persistent MUST remain compatible with automatic context compaction, Context Summarisation, Subagents, checkpoints, crash recovery and provider/model fallback.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Built-in Persistent skill
requirements.text: None of those mechanisms may erase completed side-effect evidence, duplicate consequential actions or weaken permission/approval requirements.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Plugin model
requirements.text: A Plugin MAY expose typed tools/actions, external-service connectors and optional CUI surfaces.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Plugin model
requirements.text: Every exposed callable capability MUST declare input/output schemas, permission scopes, risk/side-effect classification and cancellation/timeout semantics where applicable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Plugin model
requirements.text: Plugin tool calls MUST enter the same ToolLog, AuditLog, FullLog and Action Graph pipeline as native tools and MCP calls.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Plugin model
requirements.text: Plugin CUI surfaces MUST render through approved CUI contracts and MUST NOT inject arbitrary trusted application code/markup outside the declared host surface.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Plugin model
requirements.text: External-service Plugins MUST use secure credential references and explicit connection/account scopes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Plugin model
requirements.text: Provider tokens/secrets MUST NOT be stored in plaintext package files, logs or project definitions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Dependencies and persistence
requirements.text: Package dependencies MUST be expressed by stable PackageID plus version/range and dependency type.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Dependencies and persistence
requirements.text: Dulche MUST detect missing, cyclic and incompatible dependencies before enablement.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Dependencies and persistence
requirements.text: Optional dependencies MUST be distinguishable from required dependencies so absence does not masquerade as a broken install.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Dependencies and persistence
requirements.text: Dulche Den MUST persist the installed package registry, active versions, enablement scopes, package provenance, dependency graph and relevant package state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Dependencies and persistence
requirements.text: Device-specific executable paths/caches remain device-local; shared Den state MUST NOT imply that executable packages are installed on another device unless that device independently satisfies installation/integrity requirements.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Canonical Plugin API
requirements.text: Tool Builder and other first-party clients MUST use the same package/runtime contracts rather than manipulating private package files or registries directly.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Skills + Plugins > Tool Builder integration and acceptance
requirements.text: Skills and Plugins produced by AI Studio Tool Builder MUST validate against the exact manifest/schema/dependency/permission contracts used by Dulche after installation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche multi-engine inference runtime
requirements.text: Dulche MUST provide a Dulche-owned inference-runtime abstraction so model definitions and higher-level Dulche features do not depend directly on one execution engine. llama.cpp remains the broad/default local backend.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Dulche multi-engine inference runtime
requirements.text: Dulche MUST also include an upstream-trackable Strata fork as a specialised backend for model architectures where Strata is supported and materially better suited.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime abstraction and dispatcher
requirements.text: Dulche MUST expose one stable internal runtime contract for model loading, prompt/prefill, decode, context/KV handling, multimodal inputs where supported, cancellation, streaming, usage/telemetry, errors and shutdown.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime abstraction and dispatcher
requirements.text: Agents, Spaces, Plugins, Skills and other Dulche callers MUST target the Dulche runtime contract rather than importing llama.cpp- or Strata-specific APIs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime abstraction and dispatcher
requirements.text: A Runtime Dispatcher MUST select the effective inference engine per model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime abstraction and dispatcher
requirements.text: Selection MUST be capability-based rather than a simple dense-versus-MoE rule.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime abstraction and dispatcher
requirements.text: The compatibility registry MUST be able to consider model architecture/family, file/weight format, quantisation, required runtime features, OS, available VRAM, system RAM, CPU capabilities and any other hard backend requirement.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Runtime abstraction and dispatcher
requirements.text: A model manifest MAY declare a preferred engine and fallback engines, but the manifest MUST NOT make the model permanently dependent on one backend.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Automatic selection
requirements.text: Dulche MUST first remove incompatible engines, then choose between compatible engines using declared capability fit and locally measured performance where useful.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Automatic selection
requirements.text: Calibration MAY benchmark compatible engines for a model/quantisation/hardware fingerprint and cache the result so repeated launches do not re-run expensive benchmarks.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Automatic selection
requirements.text: Prefill and decode MUST be measured separately where they have materially different performance characteristics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Automatic selection
requirements.text: Automatic selection MUST NOT enable quality-reducing or behaviour-changing experimental flags merely to win a performance comparison.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Automatic selection
requirements.text: Runtime choice MUST remain inspectable through diagnostics/logging, including the selected engine and the reason it was selected.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Manual engine selection
requirements.text: Users and callers MUST also be able to override automatic selection and swap the active inference engine explicitly.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Manual engine selection
requirements.text: The public Dulche API MUST include the following forms:

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Manual engine selection
requirements.text: The UI/runtime settings MUST also make the effective engine and whether it was selected Automatically or Manually inspectable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Manual engine selection
requirements.text: A manual override MUST NOT be silently ignored.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Manual engine selection
requirements.text: If the requested engine cannot run the selected model or current hardware configuration, Dulche MUST return a structured incompatibility result explaining the unmet requirement.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Manual engine selection
requirements.text: It MUST NOT silently substitute another engine and pretend the requested engine was used.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Manual engine selection
requirements.text: Returning to Automatic selection MUST be available through the corresponding runtime/settings control.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Strata fork
requirements.text: Dulche MUST carry a maintained Strata fork rather than treating a separately installed Strata application as a required user dependency.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Strata fork
requirements.text: The fork MUST preserve applicable upstream and third-party licence notices, keep model-weight licences separate, and remain intentionally close enough to upstream that security, correctness and performance improvements can be reviewed and merged without repeatedly re-forking the project.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Strata fork
requirements.text: The Dulche Strata adapter MUST expose Strata through the same Dulche runtime contract used by llama.cpp.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Strata fork
requirements.text: Strata-specific optimisations such as expert caching/residency, concurrent CPU/GPU expert execution, specialised prefill, MTP/speculative execution and model-specific memory placement MAY be used when supported, but they MUST remain implementation details behind the common runtime boundary.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Fallback and failure behaviour
requirements.text: In Automatic mode, if the preferred engine fails to initialise or becomes invalid for the selected model/hardware, Dulche MAY try the next compatible registered engine and MUST record the fallback and reason.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Fallback and failure behaviour
requirements.text: A fallback MUST preserve model identity and required capabilities; Dulche MUST NOT silently load a different model merely to make an engine work.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Fallback and failure behaviour
requirements.text: Engine crashes, load failures, out-of-memory conditions and unsupported-feature errors MUST surface through the normal structured Dulche error model and MUST leave the runtime in a recoverable state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: The user may Add Items, Remove Items, Rearrange/drag (including keyboard reordering), restore defaults and manage overflow.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: Maintain sensible shared user/account defaults, with optional supported per-Space overrides under Home/Spaces preference precedence; preserve customisation through restart, account-scope synchronisation where authorised, theme switch, collapse, touch and viewport change.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: Invisible/disabled actions must have truthful applicability/permissions and never simulate success.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: The user can add an OPTIONAL measured average TOKENS PER SECOND text to AI responses and can insert authorised CUSTOM AUTOMATION actions into the AI toolbar.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: Per-message token-speed values must be based on actual provider/Dulche output-token counts and measured generation duration, distinguish unknown/unavailable from zero, and label the metric sufficiently to avoid treating tool wait time or model reasoning effort % as generation throughput.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: RETRY supports the SAME or a DIFFERENT eligible model (through the canonical Universal Model Picker), with an optional custom retry instruction; original attempts/provenance remain inspectable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: Retry/Regenerate/Resume are NOT conflated: retries and regenerated alternatives use an appropriate new attempt/branch, while a true Resume continues from saved state; completed consequential tool actions must not blindly repeat.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: They may improve authorised user-level response-style preferences, but no reaction automatically grants memory access, deduces protected personal traits or authorises training/disclosure unrelated to the user's settings.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: The AI MUST be able to respond contextually to a reaction as a subsequent message when appropriate; do not force unwanted chatter or fabricate a model response on every click.

requirements.group_title: USER MESSAGE ACTIONS AND NONDESTRUCTIVE HISTORY
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: DELETE offers “Delete message” and “Delete message and response”; deletion from the visible active conversation is not assumed to destroy audit, approval or external action history, and genuine data erasure must follow canonical authorised storage/retention/privacy lifecycle.

requirements.group_title: USER MESSAGE ACTIONS AND NONDESTRUCTIVE HISTORY
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: For responses with multiple alternatives, deletion targets must be explicit.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: Model/Assistant/Specialist entries are distinct types; user may reorder to prioritise an Assistant's named identity or a Specialist in suitable contexts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: /Tabs — toggle optional Tab View;

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: Use canonical names above as documented aliases, while maintaining any required existing API compatibility. /Reasoning maps to the actual model's discrete provider LevelIDs per SPUI-133; do not pass percentages through incompatible rounding. /Tabs hides/reveals view without destroying tabs; /Voice uses the full shared Voice & Vision session; /Summary toggles the existing top-right floating widget, not an invented extra sidebar.

requirements.group_title: SLASH COMMAND EXECUTION, CONTEXT AND SAFETY
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: Quoted text, pasted scripts, Markdown/code blocks and normal text containing slashes MUST NOT accidentally execute; preserve slash-literal entry, autocomplete escape/cancel, reliable selections, undo/draft retention and keyboard/IME.

requirements.group_title: SLASH COMMAND EXECUTION, CONTEXT AND SAFETY
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: Contextual availability must be truthful across Spaces, Assistants, Teams and other shared composing surfaces. /NewChat, /Move, /Branch and /BackgroundChat preserve canonical object IDs, target permissions and current conversation draft; BackgroundChat requires correct chosen target/new chat and actual authorised send, never a simulated background delivery. /Stop, /Restart and /ResolveIssues honour stopped/resumable/cancelled/failed distinctions and consequential side-effect idempotency; /Restart is not secretly Resume and must preserve source history. /ResetContext does NOT itself delete original messages, memories or source history. /Memory and /Permission expose only scopes the signed-in user may legitimately modify; /Bug previews reporting data and requires permission where needed. /Read uses the genuine speech runtime with cancellation.

requirements.group_title: CLICK-TO-CONFIGURE PLUGIN TILES; PERMISSION AND TIMEOUT
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: It must not become blanket permission to control unrelated apps, new accounts, credentials, destructive actions or future changed scopes.

requirements.group_title: CLICK-TO-CONFIGURE PLUGIN TILES; PERMISSION AND TIMEOUT
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: Review/revoke/update and clear effect descriptions are required. “Timeout per Call = None” disables only the user-imposed time limit, NOT mandatory runtime watchdogs, safe cancellation, execution backstops, network constraints or recovery limits.

requirements.group_title: PEER REVIEW PLUGIN: MODES, MODEL CHOICE AND SCHEDULE
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: The worker and reviewer MAY discuss disputed findings and request evidence, but the reviewer MUST independently inspect observable work, requirements and tests rather than simply accept a worker's assertion.

requirements.group_title: PEER REVIEW PLUGIN: MODES, MODEL CHOICE AND SCHEDULE
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: Peer Review settings MUST expose “Models” with user-selectable configured reviewers and “+ Add Model”; default illustrated selection “Qwen 3.8 27B” is an EXAMPLE, not a mandate to install/claim availability.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: Add optional “Multiple Responses” Plugin producing multiple distinguishable assistant answers to one eligible request.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: Add optional “Plan” Plugin implementing a REAL Plan → Review → Execute workflow analogous in purpose to mature AI coding tools' plan modes, without copying proprietary visuals.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: Planning may perform only separately authorised supporting reads/research; it does not imply blanket write/deployment permission.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: Provide an optional Fullscreen control that temporarily enlarges the authoring surface; leaving fullscreen preserves every object and edit.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: The current ordinary text draft moves into a floating bottom MESSAGE TEXT BAR associated with the same pending message when Canvas mode is enabled; text may be added/edited there.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: Undo/redo, touch/stylus/mouse input, accessible equivalent creation, text focus, responsive resizing, privacy and error/recovery are required.

requirements.group_title: DULCHE SHARED CONTEXT RUNTIME (.UCML), TRUST BOUNDARY AND CRYPTO CORRECTION
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: Daily user-scoped rotation of a DERIVED DATA-ACCESS/ENVELOPE KEY or equivalent sound cryptographic design MAY fulfil the owner's desired daily refreshed unique key, with secure retention of the ability to decrypt legitimately retained older records; never rotate destructively or imply every user gets the same secret.

requirements.group_title: DULCHE SHARED CONTEXT RUNTIME (.UCML), TRUST BOUNDARY AND CRYPTO CORRECTION
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: MODELS MUST NEVER BE GIVEN, DISPLAYED OR INJECTED A MASTER KEY, DECRYPTION KEY, CREDENTIAL OR RAW AUTHENTICATION SECRET.

requirements.group_title: DULCHE SHARED CONTEXT RUNTIME (.UCML), TRUST BOUNDARY AND CRYPTO CORRECTION
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: A closed-source bundled MCP may be used as the owner's deployment choice, but CLOSED SOURCE DOES NOT CONSTITUTE the security boundary.

requirements.group_title: DULCHE SHARED CONTEXT RUNTIME (.UCML), TRUST BOUNDARY AND CRYPTO CORRECTION
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
requirements.text: Opaque capability/handle references may be passed where safe, but must not be reusable bearer secrets the model can leak.

requirements.group_title: UCML APP PERMISSIONS, OUTPUT CONTROL, AND PROMPT-INJECTION DEFENCE
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Dulche, nodes and agentic runtime > Shared conversation actions, composer, peer review and Dulche context
