requirements.text: ALL Expert visual logic pages MUST reuse the EXISTING 9to1 HOME-OWNED NODE GRAPH FRAMEWORK, as in AUTOMATIONS, not a new separate or proprietary graph engine.

requirements.group_title: EXPERT USES THE EXISTING 9TO1 AUTOMATIONS NODE SYSTEM
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Custom Space Builder
requirements.text: Actual executable nodes must be registered against valid typed node APIs.

requirements.group_title: HARNESS LOGIC: EDIT BEHAVIOUR AND REAL SPACE UI
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Custom Space Builder
requirements.text: The user may design and edit the custom Space's SIDEBAR, MESSAGE COMPOSER/BOX and GENERATIVE UI surfaces through suitable graph nodes and supported CUI templates.

requirements.group_title: HARNESS LOGIC: EDIT BEHAVIOUR AND REAL SPACE UI
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Custom Space Builder
requirements.text: Changes to “message box” can alter permitted formatting/controls/layout/events for the user-created Space, but MUST preserve protected accessible send, privacy, identity, attachment/action permission and recovery contracts.

requirements.group_title: HARNESS LOGIC: EDIT BEHAVIOUR AND REAL SPACE UI
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Custom Space Builder
requirements.text: Sidebar graph integrations must reuse Plugin/Spaces stable SidebarItemID and existing typed AppSurface/CUI/GenerativeUI integration rather than a second sidebar runtime.

requirements.group_title: HARNESS LOGIC: EDIT BEHAVIOUR AND REAL SPACE UI
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Custom Space Builder
requirements.text: All graph behaviour must respect Home-managed approvals, Dulche model/Task/Run constraints, actual user permission, CUI controlled UI, no unsafe execution loops, and no new privileges inferred from custom generated controls.

requirements.group_title: HARNESS LOGIC: EDIT BEHAVIOUR AND REAL SPACE UI
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Custom Space Builder
requirements.text: Combined advanced-setting and graph behaviour must be validated for contradictions and show effective routing.

requirements.group_title: MODEL LOGIC: ROUTING, INSTRUCTIONS AND REAL MODEL PARAMETERS
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Custom Space Builder
requirements.text: A “force model” node may restrict routing but cannot manufacture unsupported capabilities or bypass privacy.

requirements.group_title: MODEL LOGIC: ROUTING, INSTRUCTIONS AND REAL MODEL PARAMETERS
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Custom Space Builder
requirements.text: Graph-level source/model provenance, prompt version and request override scope must remain visible and testable.

requirements.group_title: USER MESSAGE LOGIC: NONDESTRUCTIVE INPUT PIPELINE
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Custom Space Builder
requirements.text: Source USER MESSAGE must remain immutable in original canonical MessageID/history.

requirements.group_title: USER MESSAGE LOGIC: NONDESTRUCTIVE INPUT PIPELINE
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Custom Space Builder
requirements.text: Truncation must signal what was omitted; numeric extraction must specify locale/format uncertainty; word matching must have documented matching semantics; filters cannot leak unauthorized messages to app/tool/MCP endpoints.

requirements.group_title: FILES PAGE: FULL FOLDER / RESOURCE SYSTEM AND OWNERSHIP
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Custom Space Builder
requirements.text: All imported assets must be validated/scanned according to applicable policy, with package type, scope, owner, version, dependencies, compatibility and permissions clearly indicated.

requirements.group_title: FILES PAGE: FULL FOLDER / RESOURCE SYSTEM AND OWNERSHIP
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Custom Space Builder
requirements.text: Files and installed plugins/skills/models remain canonical objects owned by Files, Home/Dulche or relevant product; displaying them in Space folders must not make private incompatible clones, auto-trust packages, import executable custom code without sandbox/policy validation or confer access to connected accounts.

requirements.group_title: FILES PAGE: FULL FOLDER / RESOURCE SYSTEM AND OWNERSHIP
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Custom Space Builder
requirements.text: Plugin/MCP/mini-app/CUI resources must respect the prior exact 9to1 CUI registry, package manifest, safe rendering and app sandbox trust boundaries.

requirements.group_title: FILES PAGE: FULL FOLDER / RESOURCE SYSTEM AND OWNERSHIP
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Custom Space Builder
requirements.text: Folder-based source references and retrieval should be lazy, permission-aware and revision-tracked rather than duplicating all folder contents into model context.

requirements.group_title: CREATION, TEMPLATES, ASSISTED CONFIGURATION, PREVIEW AND PUBLISH
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Custom Space Builder
requirements.text: Preserve a clear path from BLANK SPACE, optionally eligible starter templates, or plain-language “Describe the Space you want” AI assistance (as inspired by supplied agent-builder screenshots) without requiring a conversational wizard; users can work directly in Basic/Advanced/Expert.

requirements.group_title: CREATION, TEMPLATES, ASSISTED CONFIGURATION, PREVIEW AND PUBLISH
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Custom Space Builder
requirements.text: AI-assisted modifications must produce inspectable typed configuration/graph changes and respect manifest/permissions; they must not silently choose insecure access scopes or publish a user Space.

requirements.group_title: CREATION, TEMPLATES, ASSISTED CONFIGURATION, PREVIEW AND PUBLISH
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Custom Space Builder
requirements.text: Versioned revision history and rollback must preserve relevant conversations, TaskIDs, run history, sources and external side effects; never suggest reverting a graph undoes effects already performed. “Schedule” or automatically triggered behaviour uses canonical Automations, not a private Space timer.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Custom Space Builder
requirements.text: Independent acceptance MUST exercise:

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Custom Space Builder
requirements.text: Test PC/tablet/narrow layout, native/browser platform where required, CUI Professional/Glow inheritance, reduced motion, screen reader/focus/touch, import/install errors, revocation, policy conflicts, invalid graph connections/cycles, rollback and independent acceptance.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Custom Space Builder
requirements.text: It spans threads, projects, tasks, scheduled work, permitted memory, artifacts/checkpoints and optional Mini Computer.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Custom Space Builder
requirements.text: The library provides create/open/recent/search, threads/tasks, working/blocked state, configuration, permissions/resources, proactivity, optional Mini Computer and pause/disable/archive/delete/recover.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Custom Space Builder
requirements.text: Approvals may surface separately without moving the primary reply.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > User Interface > Mini Sidebar
requirements.text: Settings MUST persist the rail/dropdown preference.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > User Interface > Mini Sidebar
requirements.text: Overflow, keyboard navigation, touch targets and screen-reader names MUST work without relying on icons alone.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > User Interface > Horizontal Tabs
requirements.text: Thanks to a shared ui framework, the design should be able to adapt to fit seamlessly with the rest of the spaces interface.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > User Interface > Horizontal Tabs
requirements.text: UI can also be generated into a separate tab if the context makes sense for that, but that should not replace inline generative UI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > User Interface > Horizontal Tabs
requirements.text: A Spaces tab MUST have stable TabID, target type/identity, source Space/context, current view mode and restorable navigation state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > User Interface > Horizontal Tabs
requirements.text: Ordinary Open focuses an existing equivalent target tab; an explicit new-view action may open another view of the same canonical entity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > User Interface > Horizontal Tabs
requirements.text: Switching or closing a tab MUST NOT delete its artifact or cancel an explicitly background-capable Dulche run.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > User Interface > Horizontal Tabs
requirements.text: Preserve drafts; closing an unsaved editor must save safely or offer Save/Discard/Cancel where a decision is required.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > User Interface > Horizontal Tabs
requirements.text: Restoration MUST NOT replay prompts, external actions or historical tool calls.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > User Interface > Horizontal Tabs
requirements.text: The active tab's source Space, account and semantic target MUST be clear to the user and AI bar; unrelated tabs do not silently contribute private context.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > User Interface > Horizontal Tabs
requirements.text: Host and embedded chrome MUST avoid duplicate overlapping AI bars or inaccessible Save/Close controls.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > User Interface > Horizontal Tabs
requirements.text: It may supplement, but MUST NOT replace, inline conversational Generative UI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > User Interface > Horizontal Tabs
requirements.text: Inactive tabs MUST release avoidable render work and use bounded caches rather than running every hidden surface at full activity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > User Interface > Main Sidebar
requirements.text: The main sidebar should be fully customisable via a visual drag/drop editor.

requirements.group_title: Custom sidebar editor and section rules
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > User Interface > Main Sidebar
requirements.text: The visual editor MUST expose + Add for a section, chat/reference, app/CUI/Generative UI surface, or authorised Plugin/Automation action.

requirements.group_title: Custom sidebar editor and section rules
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > User Interface > Main Sidebar
requirements.text: Keyboard/touch alternatives, undo and Reset to Default are required.

requirements.group_title: Custom sidebar editor and section rules
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > User Interface > Main Sidebar
requirements.text: The Pinned and College examples must support View All, a top-five chat list and New Assignment; they are not fabricated demo data.

requirements.group_title: Custom sidebar editor and section rules
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > User Interface > Main Sidebar
requirements.text: An item may reference another Space without copying its content or changing its owner.

requirements.group_title: Custom sidebar editor and section rules
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > User Interface > Main Sidebar
requirements.text: Removing an inactive chat from a section MUST NOT archive, delete or move the source chat.

requirements.group_title: Custom sidebar editor and section rules
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > User Interface > Main Sidebar
requirements.text: Manual and rule-based contributions must resolve to one visible reference per section; changing/disabling a rule must not erase unrelated manual membership.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Usage
requirements.text: A usage bar should be displayed floating at the bottom of the chat list’s section of the screen.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Usage
requirements.text: It should show the usage for 9to1 (daily/weekly/monthly, etc), plus any other measurable usage limits from other connected providers.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Usage
requirements.text: Multiple accounts and resources MUST NOT be combined into an unexplained percentage.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Usage
requirements.text: Stale, offline, exhausted and provider-unavailable states must be visible; switching account removes the old account's values.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Usage
requirements.text: Acceptance covers a real 9to1 allowance, a measurable external limit, unavailable metrics, a reset and an account switch; UI tests must prove the bar does not obstruct narrow or scaled layouts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Local/Cloud Chats
requirements.text: 9to1 MUST support Local, Mesh and Cloud chat storage.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Local/Cloud Chats
requirements.text: Local chats remain on the current device and MUST NOT enter account storage without an explicit eligible Send to Cloud action.

requirements.group_title: Chat storage, transfer and privacy contract
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Local/Cloud Chats
requirements.text: The UI MUST distinguish future sync policy from deletion of existing replicas.

requirements.group_title: Chat storage, transfer and privacy contract
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Local/Cloud Chats
requirements.text: Their messages, attachments and derived chat state MUST NOT enter Mesh, account backup or durable cross-Space memory while temporary.

requirements.group_title: Chat storage, transfer and privacy contract
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Local/Cloud Chats
requirements.text: A Local chat MUST NOT be uploaded for account storage or silently exposed through sync, search indexes, telemetry, memory or logging.

requirements.group_title: Chat storage, transfer and privacy contract
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Local/Cloud Chats
requirements.text: User copy must describe verified behaviour, not promise absolute privacy or treat restrained wording as permission for accidental uploads.

requirements.group_title: Chat storage, transfer and privacy contract
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Local/Cloud Chats
requirements.text: All 9to1 chat services must automatically compact working context while retaining complete original messages and retrievable history, so conversations can continue for months or years without arbitrary message-count caps.

requirements.group_title: Chat storage, transfer and privacy contract
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Local/Cloud Chats
requirements.text: Finite model context and resource limitations must be handled honestly; summaries must never replace source history.

requirements.group_title: Chat storage, transfer and privacy contract
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Local/Cloud Chats
requirements.text: Assistants must retain all inherited Agents functionality, with complete feature-parity auditing and user-facing management for identity, instructions, knowledge/files, memory, models, tools/apps, Skills, Quick Actions, permissions, approvals, budgets, queues, delegation, history, background execution, steering, recovery, proactive contact and optional Mini Computer.

requirements.group_title: Chat storage, transfer and privacy contract
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Spaces and Space Builder > Local/Cloud Chats
requirements.text: Approvals/notifications may appear separately without moving the reply.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: The split should be

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Quizzes should be built using Forms.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Clicking on a revision material should open it in its respective app (embedded into the spaces app, but the user can choose to open it directly in that app via either right clicking on the revision material and selecting it or right clicking the tab the embed opened in and clicking open in app) - usually as a viewer/interacter rather than an editor by default and then the user can switch to editing mode.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: It includes created revision materials, existing materials explicitly enrolled/imported and future materials classified by an authorised rule; it MUST NOT silently expose unrelated private documents.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Create New MUST remain right-aligned on the category row and expose Describe a Resource, Flashcard, Quiz, Document, Presentation, Canvas, Board and Other (Build).

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: A failed or cancelled creation must not leave a false completed Bank entry.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: STUDY-UI-201 — Study MUST support the connected learner workflow PLANNING → LEARNING → PRACTISING → REVIEWING, with feedback and recorded evidence flowing into consistent topic state and revision scheduling.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Users should be able to enter an ordinary conversation without first navigating through rigid forms or a complex course-management dashboard.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Study may be used with formal courses (including A-level/GCSE) or general learning subjects; no course-specific UI may become a universal assumption.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: STUDY-UI-202 — Retain the shared Spaces architecture: far-left pinned Space rail, user-customisable/collapsible contextual sidebar, main Space workspace, optional Spaces tab view, top-right floating Summary, shared model selector/reasoning controls, canonical composer, multimodal Voice pill, permissions and shared Action Graph.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Accessibility, keyboard navigation, narrow/touch layouts and reduced motion are required.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Topics should be selectable, searchable/filterable and navigable as a tree/outline without relying on colour alone.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Course/spec metadata may be user-defined or sourced; do not fabricate official syllabus coverage or claim authoritative exam-board alignment without a trusted reference.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Subject/Topic IDs must stay stable across reordering/renaming; links, attempts and material references follow the IDs rather than titles.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Switching between Study Home, Subject Workspace, Study Session, Revision Bank or embedded apps must not delete the conversation/draft, run state, artifacts or study attempts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: STUDY-UI-207 — Subjects must be substantive navigation, NOT merely a list of arbitrary folders.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Unassessed topics MUST NOT be falsely labelled weak.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: An AI-generated recommendation may supplement but not overwrite the authoritative ranking/evidence.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: STUDY-UI-209 — Sidebar grouping and default entry points must remain visually balanced: primary actions prominent, headings modest, independent scroll if needed, working region dominant.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Any changes must follow CUI theme/spacing and be tested at desktop/narrow/touch widths.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: The mode must be visually readable and accessible; unsupported mode actions explain why.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: STUDY-UI-211 — LEARN: conversational guided teaching, source-backed explanations, meaningful worked examples, concepts illustrated through supported shared objects, optional step-by-step scaffolding and low-friction understanding checks.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: STUDY-UI-212 — PRACTISE: targeted individual or short-series exercises, applicable difficulty and topic selection, optional hints/partial step feedback, meaningful error diagnosis and next practice suggestions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Questions may accept structured maths steps, code, freeform reasoning, multiple choice, graph/media interactions or typed responses appropriate to the subject and supported product capabilities.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Hints must not silently count as an unaided correct answer.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: STUDY-UI-213 — TEST: a more formal assessment experience, optionally timed, with an inspectable scoring/marking rubric, rules and supported marking policies.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Errors/uncertain LLM-assessed free responses should display limitations and review opportunities.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Timing should not silently make an otherwise informal session high pressure.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Provide optional review of notes/explanations when requested, but do not score showing a page or merely flipping a card as demonstrated learning.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: STUDY-UI-215 — Source-policy selector must be VISIBLE AND UNDERSTANDABLE in Study sessions: “My sources only” versus “Wider knowledge allowed”, building on the existing V2 source-only/closed corpus policy and Allowed/Ask/Disabled web controls.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: My sources only means outside web/knowledge retrieval is not presented as cited source evidence; the model must respect the configured closed-corpus answer policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Wider knowledge may combine authorised supplied sources and appropriate outside knowledge, distinguishing what came from supplied material vs external research vs general generated explanation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Mode/source changes must preserve conversation/answer provenance and any higher-priority permissions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: STUDY-UI-216 — Four-mode selection, subject/topic, source policy and question interactions must remain compatible with the common Spaces model selector, reasoning effort, local/cloud context policy, user-created Group/Project scoping where applicable and canonical floating Voice & Vision pill.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Red/amber/green must be backed by recorded events/rules, not user interface impression, AI flattering the learner, material opens or arbitrary confidence claims.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: A cautious, evidence-based proficiency estimate must not be presented as an exact scientific measurement.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Records should identify evidence type (quiz attempt, answered practice question, Cards review rating, manual assessment where permitted), source artifact/question IDs, timestamp, conditions (hints/open-book where relevant) and the applicable TopicID.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Confidence and performance should both be inspectable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: STUDY-UI-219 — Topic details should show the effective status, evidence supporting it, recent attempts, review history, last review, next suggested review, related resources and recommended actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: STUDY-UI-220 — A later successful assessment can improve evidence; errors, incorrect answers, stale review or contradictory evidence may change recommendations, but progression must use documented scoring/review policy and avoid abrupt unexplained flips.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: The user must be able to inspect why a label changed rather than seeing a mystery AI score.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Study records must preserve student privacy across accounts/Space sharing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Provide custom sections such as Homework, stable category membership and optional auto-added uncovered resource categories as defined in LE-09. Recommended draws from recorded difficult/neglected topics and linked sources, not fake recommendations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Resource previews/open actions must use real owners and permissions; if no safe/authorised preview exists, explain.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: An imported existing resource is enrolled only through authorised reference; Bank category mutation must not copy/degrade its original.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Moving from embedded to standalone must preserve exact canonical ArtifactID, current revision and permissions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Suggested review timing should be based on recorded attempts/review evidence and documented policy, not fake deadlines.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: STUDY-UI-229 — Study Home should surface upcoming relevant work and review sessions via the same Planner records; changes in Planner or Study propagate to both.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Mark overdue only when due dates are real and known; absent/unknown schedules must not create red warning visuals.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: STUDY-UI-230 — While the shared conversation is the primary interaction, exercises should use subject-appropriate, editable and accessible real UI components: a maths problem may need structured equations, intermediate working, graphs and correctly marked final answer; a programming exercise may require syntax-aware code editor/input and, where safely supported, actual execution/evaluation through canonical Build/allowed tools; an essay/legal-reasoning problem may require text response, criteria-based argument feedback and cited sources.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: The interface should adapt without multiplying separate private editors.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Feedback should distinguish conceptual misunderstanding, missing steps, incorrect calculations, inconsistent reasoning and procedural mistakes when supported by visible working.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Any goal/task/revision recommendation must be editable, dismissible or changeable using normal permissions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: Preserve normal Spaces floating Summary anchored top-right, optional app/browser/artifact tabs, collapsible contextual sidebar and bottom shared composer/Voice pill.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: STUDY-UI-234 — All screens must have clear major headings/actions, generous spacing, consistent icons, readable Montserrat where supported, accurate hover/focus/pressed/selected/disabled/validation states, genuine cursor/click targets, accessible names, screen reader reading order, reduced motion, keyboard and touch alternatives.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: The top 3 learning recommendations and upcoming work must not obstruct normal dialogue/composer.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: STUDY-UI-235 — Empty/first-use, no sources, source unavailable, offline local-only, provider unavailable, denied permission, failed quiz/marking, unavailable embedded app and missing Planner/Files state must all be truthful and recoverable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: STUDY-AC-206 — In Learn, ask source-based follow-up and inspect a worked example + optional understanding check; ensure showing examples alone does not improve mastery.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: STUDY-AC-209 — In Review, practise an overdue and a recorded weak topic via real Cards or stored attempts, update review history appropriately; flip-only content must not produce false mastery.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: New learner with no answers must have no false green/RAG proficiency.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Study Space > Revision Bank
requirements.text: All CUI controls must be genuine interactive and data-bound; no placeholder nav, no pretending source presence, status or completed work.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Product role
requirements.text: Voice & Vision MUST use the same canonical conversations, Spaces, model/provider state, Plugins, Skills, Agents, permissions, Action Graph and Dulche Den context as the rest of 9to1. Starting Voice MUST NOT create an isolated voice-only conversation database.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Session-first modern interface
requirements.text: The full Voice & Vision app MUST use a modern session-first CUI interface focused on the active interaction rather than a conventional text-chat layout.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Session-first modern interface
requirements.text: Transcript, current visual sources, model/voice, Space/conversation, tools/actions, Action Graph and device/session details SHOULD be available through collapsible secondary surfaces so the primary experience remains uncluttered.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Starting and continuing sessions
requirements.text: A multimodal session may start from Voice & Vision, the global AI bar, Spaces, AI Overlay or another app's contextual AI controls.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Starting and continuing sessions
requirements.text: Callers MAY supply SpaceID, ConversationID, current artifact/entity references, selected objects and suggested mode.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Starting and continuing sessions
requirements.text: Supplied semantic context MUST be preferred over redundant visual capture.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Starting and continuing sessions
requirements.text: Moving between full Voice & Vision, floating voice pill, Overlay and Spaces MUST preserve the same canonical session/conversation where the user is continuing the same interaction.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Multimodal session model
requirements.text: MultimodalSession MUST contain at least SessionID, ConversationID, SpaceID, VoiceMode, Voice runtime/session reference, effective model policy, selected VoiceModelID/VoiceID where applicable, microphone/camera/screen states, active visual sources, input/output devices, status, created timestamp and revision/state metadata.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Multimodal session model
requirements.text: The UI MUST make microphone/capture/listening state unambiguous and MUST NOT rely on a purely decorative animation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Voice modes
requirements.text: Voice MUST support four first-class modes: Conversational, Monologue, Live Listener and Live Translate.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Monologue mode
requirements.text: It MUST support substantially longer uninterrupted output, section/chapter planning, pause/resume, user interruption and continuation from the prior position without losing the planned structure.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Monologue mode
requirements.text: Monologue MAY expose optional target duration and style controls such as briefing, podcast, lecture or explanation while still inferring these settings from the user's request when clear.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Monologue mode
requirements.text: A MonologueRun SHOULD retain Objective, optional TargetDuration, ordered Sections, CurrentSection, playback/progress state and SourceRefs so Resume has deterministic semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Listener mode
requirements.text: It MUST continuously derive relevant semantic information and permitted actions without behaving as a default permanent recorder/transcriber.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Listener mode
requirements.text: Live Listener MUST be capable of extracting useful structured information such as current topic, important points, key dates, homework/tasks, decisions, questions, referenced resources and potential actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Listener mode
requirements.text: It MAY react to contextual cues through typed actions, for example opening Canvas when a lesson moves to whiteboard work or creating a Planner item when homework/deadline information is clearly detected and authorised.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Listener mode
requirements.text: Live Listener MUST contextually distinguish likely primary relevant speech from background conversation, incidental noise, repeated information, action cues and uncertain material using available audio characteristics, continuity, current Space/topic and semantic relevance.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Listener mode
requirements.text: It MUST represent uncertainty rather than treating every audible statement as authoritative/relevant.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Listener ephemeral audio and privacy
requirements.text: Live Listener MUST NOT persist a room conversation as a transcript or permanent audio recording by default.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Listener ephemeral audio and privacy
requirements.text: Ambient audio is processed through a short-lived ephemeral rolling buffer required for understanding; once no longer needed for semantic extraction/runtime continuity, raw audio is discarded.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Listener ephemeral audio and privacy
requirements.text: Durable Live Listener output should be the useful derived result such as notes, tasks, dates, decisions, references or explicit user-approved retained snippets, not a verbatim transcript of everyone in the room.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Listener ephemeral audio and privacy
requirements.text: Live Listener MUST NOT silently enable recording merely because retaining audio would improve later processing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Listener ephemeral audio and privacy
requirements.text: The Live Listener surface MUST clearly show Listening state, current Space/context, extraction categories/actions enabled, Recording audio state and Transcript retention state, with Pause and Stop controls.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Listener ephemeral audio and privacy
requirements.text: A compact activity feed MAY show semantic events/actions without reproducing ambient speech verbatim.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Listener notes and actions
requirements.text: Users MUST be able to choose where Live Listener writes durable notes/results, including temporary session notes or supported canonical destinations such as a Write document, Board page or Study Space notes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Listener notes and actions
requirements.text: Updates MUST use the destination app's typed API and revision semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Listener notes and actions
requirements.text: Automatic Live Listener action policy MUST be configurable through normal Home permissions/trust.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Listener notes and actions
requirements.text: Low-risk actions such as adding notes, recording homework, opening relevant 9to1 apps or adding authorised Planner dates MAY run automatically where trusted; consequential external communication, submission, deletion, purchase or similarly high-risk actions retain their normal confirmation/trust requirements.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Listener notes and actions
requirements.text: Space graphs may subscribe to safe Live Listener events and invoke typed actions within their capability profile.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Translate mode
requirements.text: Live Translate MUST support one-way, bidirectional and multilingual interpretation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Translate mode
requirements.text: A one-way session may translate one source language into one or more output languages.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Translate mode
requirements.text: Multilingual mode may contain more than two active languages and MUST support multiple simultaneous target outputs when the active model/runtime can do so.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Translate mode
requirements.text: A Live Translate session MUST expose the selected language/locale set clearly and allow languages to be added or removed without ending the session where supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Translate mode
requirements.text: Source language MAY be Auto Detect, but an explicit expected language set SHOULD be used to improve reliability in noisy multilingual environments.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Translate mode
requirements.text: Translated speech, translated captions and original-language captions MUST be independently controllable where supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Translate mode
requirements.text: One source utterance MAY produce simultaneous caption/output streams in multiple target languages.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Translate mode
requirements.text: Each connected/authorised output client MAY choose its preferred target language when platform/session architecture supports per-client outputs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Translate mode
requirements.text: Live Translate SHOULD preserve short-lived conversational translation context so pronouns, corrections, terminology and follow-up statements remain coherent.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Translate mode
requirements.text: It MUST represent uncertainty rather than inventing a confident translation when language/speaker/meaning is materially ambiguous.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Translate mode
requirements.text: Live Translate MUST handle natural corrections and partial speech without prematurely treating unstable hypotheses as final durable content.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Translate mode
requirements.text: For example, a speaker correcting a date within the same turn should yield a coherent corrected translation rather than two contradictory final statements.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Translate mode
requirements.text: Live Translate MAY use Vision sources to translate signs, menus, presentation slides, shared screens and other visible text during the same session.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Translate mode
requirements.text: A user may ask for an action based on translated context, such as saving translated notes, sending an approved translated message or applying translated content to an owning artifact.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Translate mode
requirements.text: Agentic actions MUST use the normal owning-app APIs, permissions, approvals, idempotency and Action Graph; translation does not grant broader authority.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Translate mode
requirements.text: Live Translate MAY use selected Dulche Translate glossaries/protected-term rules so product names, legal terms, code identifiers or domain terminology remain consistent across speech and captions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Translate mode
requirements.text: Live Translate raw audio and ordinary conversation transcript MUST be ephemeral by default.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Translate mode
requirements.text: The runtime may retain a short-lived rolling audio/translation-context buffer required for realtime interpretation and then discard it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Live Translate mode
requirements.text: Either may use normal Agents/tools, but one mode MUST NOT silently change into the other.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Text input during Voice
requirements.text: Every active Voice session MUST support typed text input without ending the session.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Text input during Voice
requirements.text: Text input is required for precise names, URLs/code, private instructions, corrections, attachments and situations where the user wants speech output without speaking aloud.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Text input during Voice
requirements.text: Voice MUST support modality combinations including Voice in + Voice out, Voice in + Text out, Text in + Voice out and Voice with captions where the active model/configuration supports them.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Interruption, stop and resume
requirements.text: Users MUST be able to interrupt assistant speech naturally.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Interruption, stop and resume
requirements.text: Dulche should stop/duck current speech output and process the new input without requiring a manual Stop first, subject to runtime capability.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Interruption, stop and resume
requirements.text: If a generated response/run is manually stopped but resumable, Voice & Vision uses the same Stop → Play/Resume semantics as Spaces and MUST NOT repeat already-completed consequential actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Floating voice pill
requirements.text: When the full Voice & Vision app is not foregrounded, an active session MAY collapse to a lightweight floating voice pill.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Floating voice pill
requirements.text: The pill MUST expose true listening/speaking/status indication, mute/unmute, pause/resume where applicable, return to full Voice & Vision and End session.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Floating voice pill
requirements.text: Opening the pill/full app returns to the same SessionID and MUST NOT silently start a second Voice session.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Transcript and captions
requirements.text: Conversational/Monologue sessions MAY expose a live transcript as an optional/collapsible conversation view distinguishing user, assistant and tool/action events.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Transcript and captions
requirements.text: Partial speech-recognition hypotheses may update live, but only stable/final user content should enter durable conversation history unless a revision model explicitly supports corrections.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Transcript and captions
requirements.text: Live captions may be enabled independently of durable transcript retention.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Transcript and captions
requirements.text: In Live Translate, original-language and translated captions are independently controllable where supported; caption display alone MUST NOT imply that a permanent transcript is being saved.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Audio devices and processing
requirements.text: Voice & Vision MUST support input microphone selection, output device selection, default/automatic device, hot-switching during a session, permission/unavailable/disconnected states and appropriate input/output level feedback.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Audio devices and processing
requirements.text: Device loss MUST degrade/recover gracefully rather than corrupt the conversation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Audio devices and processing
requirements.text: Noise suppression, echo cancellation, automatic gain and voice-activity detection MAY be provided when supported by the platform/runtime, with sensible defaults and inspectable advanced settings.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Universal Model Picker integration and named voices
requirements.text: The selected Voice Model/configuration MUST be capability-checked for the requested mode and modalities, including realtime audio, Monologue, Live Listener, Live Translate, vision, tools/actions, required language/translation support and interruption where relevant.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Universal Model Picker integration and named voices
requirements.text: Discover/Home SHOULD recommend the highest-quality compatible Voice Model/configuration for the requested mode/constraints when the user has not explicitly overridden it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Universal Model Picker integration and named voices
requirements.text: Switching named Voice MUST NOT be misrepresented as changing the underlying model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Vision sources
requirements.text: Every active source MUST have session-local stable identity, provenance/source type and visible active/paused state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Vision sources
requirements.text: The UI MUST make clear what AI can currently see.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Vision sources
requirements.text: Continuous sharing is distinct from a single screenshot and must expose source, pause, change source and stop-sharing controls.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Screenshots, screen sharing and camera
requirements.text: Screenshot capture SHOULD support full display, selected window and selected region, with easy region capture from Overlay.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Screenshots, screen sharing and camera
requirements.text: Captures MAY be cropped/annotated before submission where supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Screenshots, screen sharing and camera
requirements.text: Continuous screen sharing MUST show an unmistakable persistent capture indicator and source identity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Screenshots, screen sharing and camera
requirements.text: Pausing/stopping sharing MUST stop new visual frames from reaching the runtime.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Screenshots, screen sharing and camera
requirements.text: Camera mode MUST support available camera selection, snapshot, supported continuous camera context, pause and camera switching.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Screenshots, screen sharing and camera
requirements.text: Microphone/camera/screen capture MUST never activate solely because the model decides additional context would help.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Adaptive visual sampling
requirements.text: For continuous camera/screen input, Dulche MAY use adaptive frame sampling/change detection and model/provider limits to reduce redundant processing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Adaptive visual sampling
requirements.text: Sampling is an optimisation only; stale visual state MUST NOT be represented as current.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Semantic context before pixels
requirements.text: When a 9to1 app exposes semantic context such as ArtifactID, selection/object IDs, structured document context and available typed actions, Voice & Vision MUST prefer that structured context over screenshot/OCR/screen scraping.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Semantic context before pixels
requirements.text: Deliberately attached images/screenshots may persist as conversation sources.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Semantic context before pixels
requirements.text: Continuous camera/screen frames MUST remain ephemeral by default and MUST NOT all become permanent attachments.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Privacy and local/cloud boundaries
requirements.text: Voice & Vision MUST visibly indicate active microphone, camera and screen/window sharing plus relevant cloud-model use when required by privacy policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Privacy and local/cloud boundaries
requirements.text: Pausing/stopping a source must actually stop new data delivery.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Privacy and local/cloud boundaries
requirements.text: Local-only/private model policy MUST NOT silently fall back to a cloud model for audio, camera or screen processing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > AI Overlay
requirements.text: For non-9to1 apps or unavailable semantic APIs, explicit Vision capture may provide visual context.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > AI Overlay
requirements.text: Overlay MUST be fast, compact and capable of rendering CUI/Generative UI result/action cards.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > AI Overlay
requirements.text: Overlay actions MUST invoke typed 9to1 APIs/Automations rather than arbitrary mouse/keyboard automation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Overlay automation execution
requirements.text: Overlay MUST be able to discover and execute existing Automations relevant to the current typed selection/context.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Overlay automation execution
requirements.text: Missing required Automation inputs MUST be requested from the user rather than guessed when unsafe.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Overlay automation execution
requirements.text: Overlay MUST NOT independently emulate the Automation's actions or use it to bypass consequential-action confirmation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Overlay continuity
requirements.text: Overlay MUST support Continue in Spaces, preserving the same conversation/request context and retained explicit sources.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Overlay continuity
requirements.text: If a Voice session is already active, invoking Overlay MAY augment the same session, for example allowing the user to select a screen region while saying 'look at this bit' without spawning a second assistant.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Voice tools and consequential actions
requirements.text: Spoken or typed Voice requests may execute normal authorised 9to1 app/tool actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Voice tools and consequential actions
requirements.text: High-risk confirmation prompts MUST identify the concrete target/action rather than relying on ambiguous verbal confirmation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > AI-assisted dictation
requirements.text: It MUST be available to supported editable text surfaces such as Write, Spaces, Mail, Boards, Present speaker notes, Planner descriptions, Build site workspace, AI Studio and other CUI text editors through the shared platform capability.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > AI-assisted dictation
requirements.text: Dictation SHOULD support Raw, Clean and Polished modes or equivalent: Raw remains close to literal transcription; Clean removes filler/repetition/false starts and adds punctuation; Polished may lightly restructure rambling speech into well-written prose while preserving intended meaning.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > AI-assisted dictation
requirements.text: Dictation MUST support contextual correction/commands such as new paragraph, bullet list, heading changes, delete/replace recent text and spoken self-corrections, applied through the host app/shared productivity engine rather than being inserted literally when recognised as commands.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > AI-assisted dictation
requirements.text: Dictation MAY use limited authorised current-editor context to improve terminology, names and punctuation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > AI-assisted dictation
requirements.text: It MUST NOT use unrelated private context merely to improve transcription.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Background/session continuity
requirements.text: An explicitly active Voice session may continue when the Voice & Vision window loses focus according to platform permission/background rules.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Background/session continuity
requirements.text: Camera/screen sharing continues only while its visible capture state remains active; OS/session lock must suspend/stop sensitive capture according to platform policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Background/session continuity
requirements.text: If Home/Dulche temporarily restarts, Voice & Vision MUST preserve durable conversation/session metadata, show truthful Reconnecting/failed state and reconnect where supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Background/session continuity
requirements.text: It MUST NOT indicate that microphone/model processing is active while disconnected.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Accessibility
requirements.text: Voice & Vision MUST support captions, keyboard-only controls, screen-reader-labelled session/capture states, visual equivalents for audio state, adjustable caption/text sizing where applicable, reduced motion and non-colour-only state indication.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Accessibility
requirements.text: No required action may be voice-only.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Platform capability behaviour
requirements.text: Native Windows/9to1-OS may provide the full OS-global Overlay, native window/display capture and background voice capabilities.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Platform capability behaviour
requirements.text: Web may provide microphone, camera and browser-authorised screen sharing but MUST NOT claim an OS-global Overlay outside the browser.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Platform capability behaviour
requirements.text: Voice & Vision APIs own user-facing session/capture/presentation state and MUST NOT duplicate the Dulche runtime as a second incompatible engine.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Failure behaviour
requirements.text: Voice & Vision MUST return structured failures including MicrophonePermissionDenied, CameraPermissionDenied, ScreenCapturePermissionDenied, InputDeviceUnavailable, OutputDeviceUnavailable, CameraUnavailable, CaptureSourceUnavailable, VoiceModelUnavailable, VisionCapabilityUnavailable, ModelCapabilityMismatch, SessionDisconnected, SessionNotFound, VisualSourceUnavailable, CaptureStopped, ProviderUnavailable, PrivacyPolicyDenied, AutomationInputMissing, DictationUnavailable, LiveTranslateLanguageUnsupported, LiveTranslateLanguageAmbiguous, LiveTranslateCapabilityUnavailable and LiveTranslateOutputUnavailable in addition to normal Dulche/Translate/tool/action errors.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Voice & Vision > Acceptance requirements
requirements.text: Mic/camera/screen/listening states and all required controls are accessible and not communicated by colour alone.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build
requirements.text: Existing 9to1.Dev.*, 9to1.Sites.* and 9to1.Stack.* may remain versioned domain/compatibility APIs behind Build, preserving validation, grants, revisions, errors and side-effect contracts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build
requirements.text: Canonical discovery and alias mapping must be documented, and existing saved graphs, IDs, links and integrations preserved.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build
requirements.text: Contextual actions may say Edit source, Open visual editor or Review changes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Product role and engineering principle
requirements.text: It MUST be fully useful without AI and provide mature project/workspace management, source editing, language tooling, build/run/test, debugging, terminal access, package/dependency management, source-control integration, visual CUI development, extension development, remote/container environments and structured agentic coding.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Product role and engineering principle
requirements.text: Repository-aware AI mutations MUST use typed code/file/project/task actions and MUST expose the resulting reviewable change set.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Product role and engineering principle
requirements.text: Opaque desktop automation MUST NOT be used when a structured development action exists.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Canonical workspace and project model
requirements.text: A workspace may contain multiple folders, repositories and related projects.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Canonical workspace and project model
requirements.text: Monorepos, client/server solutions and multi-language workspaces MUST NOT require flattening into one artificial project type.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Canonical workspace and project model
requirements.text: Build SHOULD consume existing ecosystem project files rather than replacing them with a proprietary project model where an established project format exists.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > New Project workflow and project catalogue
requirements.text: Project providers/extensions may register compatible CUI application templates and additional infrastructure or external-source workflows.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > New Project workflow and project catalogue
requirements.text: New providers must obey the global CUI authoring mandate rather than registering an application-language bypass.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > New Project workflow and project catalogue
requirements.text: Missing required SDK/toolchain components are shown explicitly with install/configure actions where supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > 9to1 Extension project type
requirements.text: Generated scaffolding MUST contain only selected contributions rather than a giant all-products starter.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Editor and navigation
requirements.text: The source editor includes tabs, preview/pinned tabs, split editors, editor groups, breadcrumbs, outline/symbol view, optional minimap, line numbers, indentation/whitespace guides, bracket matching, folding, multi-cursor, rectangular selection, snippets, configurable keybindings, encoding/line-ending awareness, large-file mode and undo/redo.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Language intelligence and parsing
requirements.text: Tree-sitter or an equivalent maintained parser MAY provide fast syntax structure, incremental parsing, selections and editor features where suitable, while language-specific semantic operations remain owned by the relevant language/tooling provider.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Language intelligence and parsing
requirements.text: Build MUST NOT implement language semantics using fragile regex parsing where a maintained compiler/LSP/parser exists.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Toolchain Manager and built-in/provisionable toolchains
requirements.text: Core supported ecosystems SHOULD be usable out of the box through bundled or one-click provisionable toolchains where licensing/platform constraints permit.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Toolchain Manager and built-in/provisionable toolchains
requirements.text: Native/package compilation tools may be added where project requirements need them.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Toolchain Manager and built-in/provisionable toolchains
requirements.text: Platform-native toolchains such as MSVC may be discovered and used when installed.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Missing compiler/runtime indication
requirements.text: Build MUST make toolchain readiness obvious before build/run.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Missing compiler/runtime indication
requirements.text: It must distinguish missing compiler/runtime, wrong version, missing debugger, missing language server, missing package manager, registry/authentication failure and general build failure.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Missing compiler/runtime indication
requirements.text: The UI shows Ready or explicit environment issues with required versus installed versions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Missing compiler/runtime indication
requirements.text: Errors such as command-not-found or process spawn failure MUST NOT be the primary user experience when Build can determine that a required toolchain component is missing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Build pipeline and tasks
requirements.text: A pipeline may contain Restore, Generate, Compile, Link, Package, Test, Sign or other project-defined stages with dependencies, parallelism rules, environment, working directory, cancellation, timeout and diagnostics matching.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Run configurations and target-aware Run
requirements.text: Build MUST NOT silently run a different configuration because another panel gained focus.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Operating-system and kernel project support
requirements.text: Their Run pipeline may build the configured kernel/EFI/bootloader/ISO/disk image, verify the output artifact, start the configured virtual machine, attach the boot media and expose display/serial/debug channels in Build.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Virtual machine provider and OS preview
requirements.text: Additional providers may register through extensions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Virtual machine provider and OS preview
requirements.text: Provider-specific advanced settings may still be exposed where necessary.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Virtual machine provider and OS preview
requirements.text: The VM may render in an embedded Build run/preview panel or a pop-out window and exposes power/reset/pause, display, serial console, boot logs, configured device state, basic performance information, snapshots and debugger status.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Virtual machine provider and OS preview
requirements.text: Workspace trust rules apply: opening an unknown repository MUST NOT automatically execute build scripts, boot images or VM configurations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Debugger
requirements.text: Capabilities are negotiated per debugger/provider; Build MUST NOT expose controls that imply unsupported debugger semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Terminal integration
requirements.text: Build MUST NOT implement a separate competing project/branch model that diverges from Build.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Diff and review editor
requirements.text: Each comparison MUST identify its left/right revisions explicitly.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Diff and review editor
requirements.text: AI-generated changes MUST NOT bypass normal diff/review visibility.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > AI review workflow
requirements.text: AI may attach explanatory review annotations to hunks without inserting those explanations as source comments.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > AI review workflow
requirements.text: Build MUST NOT claim tests/builds succeeded unless those executions occurred.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Structured AI coding and agentic development
requirements.text: They MUST NOT blindly race edits against the same canonical files.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Symbol-aware editing and refactoring
requirements.text: AI and manual operations SHOULD target semantic symbols where possible rather than fragile character offsets.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Symbol-aware editing and refactoring
requirements.text: Global text replacement MUST NOT substitute for a supported semantic refactor.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Package and dependency management
requirements.text: Build MUST NOT create a proprietary dependency declaration that masks or conflicts with the project's native package manager.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Package and dependency management
requirements.text: Dependency graph view MAY reuse the shared Node Graph Framework to show direct/transitive relationships and version conflicts while preserving the actual underlying manifests.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > NuGet and .NET dependency support
requirements.text: Build MUST support NuGet for .NET projects where the configured .NET toolchain supports it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Other package ecosystems
requirements.text: Dependency failures distinguish registry unavailable, authentication required, package/version missing, incompatible version and restore incomplete.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Other package ecosystems
requirements.text: AI/agent package changes MUST use the configured package manager and preserve the project's lockfile/dependency conventions unless the task explicitly requests migration.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Dependency integrity and reproducibility
requirements.text: Package operations SHOULD be reproducible and show manifest/lockfile diffs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Dependency integrity and reproducibility
requirements.text: When authoritative advisory metadata is available Build may surface known vulnerabilities, deprecated/yanked versions, licence metadata and conflicts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Dependency integrity and reproducibility
requirements.text: It MUST distinguish an external advisory from an AI-generated suspicion.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Native 9to1 extension platform
requirements.text: Extensions MAY contribute language/toolchain/debugger/formatter/linter providers, project templates, package providers, editors, commands, tool windows, CUI/visual-builder components, AI context/tools, Node Graph node types and product-specific contributions exposed by host APIs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Native 9to1 extension platform
requirements.text: One extension package may target multiple 9to1 products through explicit contribution contracts; products do not need separate unrelated plugin formats for the same extension.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Extension permissions, isolation and trust
requirements.text: Extensions declare required capabilities such as workspace read/write, process execution, network, terminal, credential access, Files, Build or AI/model access.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Extension permissions, isolation and trust
requirements.text: The host can present permissions during install/enable; low-risk themes/components MUST NOT silently inherit arbitrary process/filesystem/network rights.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Extension permissions, isolation and trust
requirements.text: A broken extension SHOULD NOT crash-loop the whole Build process.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Discover distribution and private extensions
requirements.text: Organisations/workspaces may distribute private extensions according to the shared identity/permission model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Discover distribution and private extensions
requirements.text: Build site workspace visual edits and Build source edits SHOULD round-trip when the underlying representation is intentionally round-trippable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Discover distribution and private extensions
requirements.text: Unsupported visual-only structures MUST be represented as managed boundaries rather than silently destroyed by source editing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Discover distribution and private extensions
