requirements.text: Web/Build site workspace-compatible Run/Preview may use Build site workspace preview/runtime infrastructure for responsive preview, route inspection, development server integration, preview environments and deployment-oriented diagnostics without Build duplicating the entire Build site workspace authoring product.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > AI Studio integration
requirements.text: Build may embed selected AI testing/inspection panels such as test conversation, structured output, tool calls, latency/token metadata where available, but MUST NOT reimplement the complete AI Studio product.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Visual CUI Builder
requirements.text: Build MUST include a native visual CUI builder for CUI applications/components.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Visual CUI Builder
requirements.text: Build MUST NOT maintain a hidden proprietary canvas model that drifts from or overwrites hand-written CUI source.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Visual CUI layout, properties and bindings
requirements.text: Simple event-handler creation can generate/navigate to real source handlers; graph-based behaviour may use the shared Node Graph Framework where the project architecture chooses it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Two-way source and visual round-trip
requirements.text: Selecting a component in source/tree SHOULD highlight it in the visual preview where source mapping exists; selecting/inspecting a rendered element SHOULD reveal the owning component/source symbol/range where safe.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Two-way source and visual round-trip
requirements.text: The builder MUST NOT delete or rewrite unsupported code merely to force visual round-tripping.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Live split view and preview providers
requirements.text: In Code | Preview mode, the developer can resize/swap panes and optionally Follow editor or Pin a particular component/page/application preview while editing related files.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Visual diff and AI preview validation
requirements.text: UI-oriented change review MAY offer Code diff | Visual diff and/or Diff | Preview.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Visual diff and AI preview validation
requirements.text: AI-generated UI work SHOULD perform build/runtime/visual validation when the required preview/inspection capability is available and within scope.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Remote, container and reproducible environments
requirements.text: Remote development SHOULD run language servers/build tools near the project filesystem rather than blindly copying whole repositories to the client.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Workspace trust and execution security
requirements.text: Secrets/tokens use shared credential infrastructure where possible and MUST NOT be unnecessarily exposed to AI context, logs, source control, telemetry or generated diffs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > API and HTTP developer tooling
requirements.text: Build SHOULD provide a native developer-oriented HTTP/API request tool for method, URL, headers, auth, body, environment variables, saved requests and response inspection, with WebSocket/event-stream capability where supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Notebook and interactive execution
requirements.text: Where relevant to supported ecosystems, Build MAY provide notebook/cell-oriented interactive execution with code cells, rich outputs, plots and variable/kernel state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Notebook and interactive execution
requirements.text: Notebook capability is developer-oriented and MUST NOT duplicate Data's full analytical spreadsheet/database experience.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Database developer handoff
requirements.text: Basic database/schema/query context may be surfaced for development, but Data remains the full database/analysis product.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Accessibility
requirements.text: Diagnostics, breakpoints, source-control state, diff additions/deletions and build/test state MUST NOT rely only on colour/gutter glyphs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Accessibility
requirements.text: Visual builder/preview functionality provides source/tree/Inspector alternatives so required project editing does not depend solely on pointer manipulation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Performance and large-workspace behaviour
requirements.text: Opening a large monorepo MUST NOT synchronously parse millions of files on the UI thread.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Recovery and failure behaviour
requirements.text: Failed AI or bulk refactors preserve a recoverable change set and MUST NOT report completion when only part of a requested patch applied.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Platform capability behaviour
requirements.text: It MUST NOT silently pretend a build/debug/run occurred on an unsupported target.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Source development workspace > Acceptance requirements
requirements.text: New Project can filter/select a language/project type/framework and refuses or warns clearly when its required toolchain is unavailable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Donors
requirements.text: Secondary donor/reference: Gitnuro may be used for local desktop Git workflows and UX patterns where useful.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Donors
requirements.text: Donor parity must be explicitly audited.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Donors
requirements.text: Every mature donor feature must be preserved, replaced by a 9to1-native equivalent, or explicitly recorded as not applicable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Project and storage model
requirements.text: A Build project may use:

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Project and storage model
requirements.text: Build must never combine unrelated Build projects into one shared repository.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Project and storage model
requirements.text: Public Build projects MUST expose a dedicated user-facing source-browsing, forking and contribution interface.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Project and storage model
requirements.text: Normal participation MUST NOT require direct access to Build-managed backing folders, manifests or dependency branches.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Project and storage model
requirements.text: Public projection is generated only from resources whose effective visibility permits publication; private files, objects, commits, credentials, metadata and historical objects MUST be excluded from the public Git/source projection, not merely hidden in the UI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Project and storage model
requirements.text: Before publishing or mirroring a mixed-visibility project, Build MUST validate the projected commit/object graph and block publication if private ancestry/content would be reachable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Project and storage model
requirements.text: If Last State would reopen a tab/state that is known to have caused a repeatable crash, Build must suppress or close the offending tab rather than crash-loop.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Source lineage
requirements.text: main may contain normal project source and Roots. main may NEVER contain Twigs, Leaves or Subroots.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Cascade semantics
requirements.text: Deletion and rename semantics must be represented explicitly so inherited files do not incorrectly reappear after a child intentionally deletes or renames them.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Project sidebar
requirements.text: Displayed +A/-D totals MUST represent only the delta owned by that node relative to its effective parent.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Project sidebar
requirements.text: Inherited ancestor changes MUST NOT increase a child node’s own displayed totals.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Conflict handling
requirements.text: AI conflict resolutions must never silently merge without this explicit review step.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Roots
requirements.text: Unless changed through the Root/Subroot workflow, Root content MUST cascade unchanged into descendant domains and descendants MUST NOT override it directly.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Roots
requirements.text: A Root may exist in main or another domain.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Roots
requirements.text: Root enforcement must derive from stored metadata, not only from transient UI state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Freeze
requirements.text: A Freeze may have an expiry point/time/condition after which editing is restored automatically.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Freeze
requirements.text: Build must clearly show:

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Freeze
requirements.text: A Freeze records stable FreezeID, target Root/resource/domain, selected descendant scope, creator, reason, creation revision, optional expiry/condition and state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Subroots
requirements.text: Build must prevent overlapping Subroots from claiming the same Root.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Subroots
requirements.text: Completing a Subroot requires a diff against the owning Root, configured validation/check results, conflict resolution and the required approvals.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Subroots
requirements.text: The user may instead abandon the Subroot, which discards its proposed Root changes while preserving audit/history.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Files-backed storage
requirements.text: The UI MUST identify them as managed/internal state and MUST prevent ordinary project-editing flows from casually deleting or editing them.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Files-backed storage
requirements.text: Explicit diagnostic/recovery tooling MAY expose controlled access.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Files-backed storage
requirements.text: The exact nested on-disk schema for Branch/Twig/Leaf/Subroot domains and their per-domain metadata must be versioned and documented.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Files-backed storage
requirements.text: Build MUST validate its managed folders/manifests when opening/synchronising a project.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Files-backed storage
requirements.text: If required infrastructure is missing, moved, altered or partially deleted, Build MUST enter a recoverable/diagnostic state, identify the damaged objects and attempt deterministic reconstruction from retained metadata/object IDs where reconstruction is possible; it MUST NOT silently treat damaged infrastructure as ordinary project source.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > GitHub-backed storage
requirements.text: The canonical Git ref for that companion branch is `stack/twigs-and-leaves-dependency`; the UI presents it as managed infrastructure (for example “Twigs and Leaves (DEPENDENCY)”) and MUST NOT expose it as an ordinary user Branch.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > GitHub-backed storage
requirements.text: The dependency branch must contain a prominent README explaining that it is Build-managed infrastructure and must not be deleted, merged into normal branches, rebased, renamed or manually edited.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > GitHub-backed storage
requirements.text: It must also contain a Build manifest/schema sufficient to identify the project, version the storage format, map Branch/Twig/Leaf/Subroot IDs and recover safely.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > GitHub-backed storage
requirements.text: If the dependency tree/manifest appears in a normal branch because somebody merged or moved it, Build must recognise the signature, warn the user and recover/relink the dependency branch where possible rather than treating those files as normal project source.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > GitHub-backed storage
requirements.text: If the dependency branch is deleted, Build MUST detect the missing managed ref and MUST attempt reconstruction from retained commit/object IDs, manifests and configured Files-backed recovery metadata.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > GitHub-backed storage
requirements.text: If complete reconstruction is impossible, Build MUST preserve recoverable evidence, identify unrecoverable objects explicitly and block unsafe writes that could overwrite remaining recovery state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > GitHub-backed storage
requirements.text: The GitHub adapter MUST preserve Build semantics rather than mirror the Files backing layout literally.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > GitHub-backed storage
requirements.text: Other entities MUST use a native GitHub/Git construct only when that construct preserves the canonical Build identity, permissions and lifecycle semantics; otherwise Build-managed metadata remains authoritative.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Sweeping and pruning
requirements.text: Pruning must not immediately destroy the backing source.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Sweeping and pruning
requirements.text: The underlying Files/GitHub data must remain recoverable/auditable according to the project's retention policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Public collaboration
requirements.text: Where project components have different public/private visibility, Build must preserve hard security boundaries and never rely on UI hiding.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Public collaboration
requirements.text: At minimum, Build site workspace must be able to use Build projects as source projects, open the relevant source domain, and maintain source ownership/history rather than publishing opaque generated output.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Public collaboration
requirements.text: Branch/Twig/Leaf domains may create isolated preview deployments where policy permits; production deployments default to an approved Main revision unless the project explicitly authorises another release source.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Public collaboration
requirements.text: Build site workspace edits to source-backed projects are committed back into the currently bound Build domain as ordinary reviewable source changes; Build site workspace MUST NOT maintain an anonymous divergent copy of the project.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Gitea/Gitnuro donor parity
requirements.text: Gitea is the primary donor and must be forked from the latest appropriate source at implementation time.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Gitea/Gitnuro donor parity
requirements.text: Gitnuro may be used as a secondary donor/reference for local Git UX where its licence and architecture permit.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Gitea/Gitnuro donor parity
requirements.text: Donor parity must cover, where applicable:

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Gitea/Gitnuro donor parity
requirements.text: A feature may only be omitted when Build deliberately replaces it or records it as not applicable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Domain identity and effective source
requirements.text: Renaming or moving display labels MUST NOT change identity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Domain identity and effective source
requirements.text: View lineage MUST use canonical history rather than infer origin from current path text.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Domain creation, hierarchy guards and reparenting
requirements.text: Hierarchy is enforced by the model/API: Main may create Branches; a Branch may create Twigs; a Twig may create Leaves; a Leaf cannot create children.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Materialisation and concurrency model
requirements.text: Build MUST support opening, browsing, building and acting on multiple domains concurrently without requiring user-facing Git worktree switching.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Materialisation and concurrency model
requirements.text: Implementations MAY use overlay filesystems, virtual projections, content-addressed materialisation, temporary isolated checkout directories or another robust mechanism, but the materialisation is derived state and MUST NOT become a competing source of truth.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Materialisation and concurrency model
requirements.text: Two clients or agents editing the same domain/resource use revision/merge conflict semantics; isolated domains may proceed independently.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Materialisation and concurrency model
requirements.text: A failed materialisation or cache rebuild MUST be recoverable from canonical Build/Git/Files state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Commit history for Branches, Twigs, Leaves and Subroots
requirements.text: Rewriting or squashing history is explicit and permission-controlled; it MUST NOT silently invalidate descendants, releases or open Change Requests.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Promotion and Change Requests
requirements.text: A ChangeRequest has stable ChangeRequestID, source DomainID/revision, destination DomainID/revision, included changes/commits, diff, author, reviewers, comments, required checks, approvals, conflict state, policy state, outcome and resulting revision.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Promotion and Change Requests
requirements.text: Project policy MAY allow a deliberate bypass, but the UI/API must state which levels are being bypassed, calculate the complete destination diff and record the bypass in audit history.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Promotion and Change Requests
requirements.text: The source domain may remain open, be marked completed or be swept/pruned according to user/project policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Review, approvals and merge strategy
requirements.text: Available integration strategies may include merge commit, fast-forward, rebase or squash only where the target/domain policy and Build lineage model can preserve stable identity and ancestry.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Cascade implementation and update state
requirements.text: If a resource conflicts, cascade for that affected resource/path pauses and the descendant records UpstreamConflict while unrelated safe updates MAY continue.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Conflict objects and resolver
requirements.text: Structured 9to1 resources SHOULD use semantic conflict resolution when a canonical domain API can represent it faithfully.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Conflict objects and resolver
requirements.text: Dulche may Summarise or propose Fix with AI through typed actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Root authority model
requirements.text: The owning domain may update its Root through authorised Root workflows, after which descendants inherit the new authoritative state through normal cascade rules.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Root authority model
requirements.text: Root scope may include a file, folder or registered structured resource.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Subroot lifecycle
requirements.text: Completing a Subroot requires a diff against the owning Root, required tests/checks, conflict resolution and configured approvals.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Freeze lifecycle and permissions
requirements.text: Freeze records have stable FreezeID, target resource/domain, selected descendant scope, creator, reason, creation revision, optional expiry/condition, policy and state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Files and GitHub dual-authority/synchronisation
requirements.text: Bidirectional mode uses stable object/revision mapping and MUST surface concurrent divergent edits as sync conflicts; last-writer-wins is not an acceptable default.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Files and GitHub dual-authority/synchronisation
requirements.text: Partial sync leaves a resumable SyncConflict/Failed state and MUST NOT claim both backends are current.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Git compatibility and advanced Git operations
requirements.text: Checking out an arbitrary Git branch inside a Build-managed materialisation MUST NOT silently change the active Build DomainID.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Team permissions and sensitive operations
requirements.text: A child MUST NOT grant broader access to private ancestor material than the parent/project permits.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Team permissions and sensitive operations
requirements.text: Sensitive operations such as permanent purge, private→public exposure, protected-domain override, remote replacement and destructive Root history rewrite require elevated permission and stronger confirmation; project policy MAY require 2FA.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > CI, build and test checks
requirements.text: Change Requests show required and optional checks.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > CI, build and test checks
requirements.text: A check result from an older source revision MUST NOT satisfy a requirement for a newer reviewed revision.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Releases, tags and packages
requirements.text: Project policy MAY permit another explicitly selected stable domain/revision, but the Release records its exact source identity and does not float with later domain changes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > GitHub mirroring, backup and restore
requirements.text: It MUST NOT fabricate successful restoration.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > GitHub mirroring, backup and restore
requirements.text: Build site workspace MUST NOT maintain a hidden divergent source copy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Issues and Boards integration
requirements.text: Build preserves source-oriented Issues, labels, milestones and repository issue workflows required by donor parity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Issues and Boards integration
requirements.text: Issues may link to commits, domains, Change Requests, releases and affected paths/resources.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Issues and Boards integration
requirements.text: The products MUST NOT silently duplicate and diverge two full project-management databases.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Automations and webhooks
requirements.text: Delivery has retry/idempotency identifiers and observable failure state; a failed webhook MUST NOT roll back an already-completed source operation unless an explicit transactional integration contract exists.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Sweep, prune, retention and purge
requirements.text: It MUST NOT discard unmerged descendant work silently.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Large repositories, binary data and LFS
requirements.text: Build MUST NOT materialise every domain or download every large object merely to open a project.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Dulche and AI-assisted source control
requirements.text: AI MUST NOT manipulate Build-managed companion branches/folders through opaque shell/UI automation when a semantic action exists.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Dulche and AI-assisted source control
requirements.text: AI claims about build/test/review readiness must reference actual executed check results for the pinned revision.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Autocommit
requirements.text: Autocommit is disabled by default and must be enabled explicitly per repository/domain.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Autocommit
requirements.text: It supports a configured elapsed interval or inactivity duration; settings may display friendly minutes while runtime stores precise duration.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Autocommit
requirements.text: Failed push/sync leaves the commit local with explicit Ahead/SyncFailed state; Build MUST NOT claim the domain is synced.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Accessibility
requirements.text: Addition/deletion/conflict/upstream/local/remote states MUST NOT rely only on colour or icons. +A/-D counts, status text and accessible descriptions identify state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Performance and resilience
requirements.text: Crash/restart MUST not lose canonical domain metadata, pending conflict state or accepted commits.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Performance and resilience
requirements.text: Derived materialisations/caches may be discarded and reconstructed.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Recovery and typed failures
requirements.text: Build MUST NOT report rollback, restore, sync or merge success unless the resulting canonical and provider state was verified as required by that operation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Platform capability behaviour
requirements.text: Where a platform cannot safely materialise or execute a local action, Build uses an explicitly configured service/remote provider or reports CapabilityUnavailable; it MUST NOT silently change source-control semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Acceptance requirements
requirements.text: Leaf → Twig → Branch → Main promotion uses revision-pinned Change Requests, required approvals/checks and produces an auditable resulting revision.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Build and source-collaboration workspace > Acceptance requirements
requirements.text: A Subroot claims non-overlapping Roots, runs required review/checks, completes into the owning Root and releases its claims; Main cannot create Subroots.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Product role and ownership principle
requirements.text: It MUST support professional source-backed websites and web applications while remaining approachable for users who prefer visual authoring.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Product role and ownership principle
requirements.text: A SiteProject MUST remain user-owned and addressable as real structured project/source state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Product role and ownership principle
requirements.text: Build site workspace MUST NOT make opaque generated output the only canonical representation or require an export-to-code step for ordinary Build interoperability.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Primary donor: cakemods site plugin
requirements.text: Its visual Page Editor, reusable-section/component model, design-system integration, preview behaviour, editor-shell/public-route separation, authoring quality-of-life and proven website-management behaviours MUST be preserved, expanded or replaced by demonstrably equivalent 9to1-native implementations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Primary donor: cakemods site plugin
requirements.text: Implementation MUST inspect/fetch the current donor source at implementation time if it is not present in the canonical development environment, subject to licensing and the global donor rules.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Primary donor: cakemods site plugin
requirements.text: Build site workspace may replace WordPress/PHP-specific storage, admin or runtime coupling with 9to1-native project, CUI, API and provider infrastructure, but donor functionality and useful interaction semantics must survive unless explicitly documented as not applicable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Donor parity audit
requirements.text: A donor-parity inventory MUST classify every meaningful cakemods site/editor capability as Preserved, Expanded, Replaced by 9to1-native equivalent, or Not applicable with a recorded reason.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Donor parity audit
requirements.text: Missing donor source is not permission to invent a toy substitute; the autonomous implementation process must obtain the latest appropriate donor source where the global donor contract permits.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > New Site and framework/project creation
requirements.text: Provider adapters may compile CUI to web deployment output with versioned source maps.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > New Site and framework/project creation
requirements.text: Existing source projects may be opened from Build.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > New Site and framework/project creation
requirements.text: Build site workspace MUST detect whether the selected framework/provider supports full visual round-trip, partial visual representation or preview-only mode and state the capability clearly.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Component and section model
requirements.text: User/org component libraries may provide reusable headers, footers, heroes, pricing blocks, FAQs, CTAs and domain-specific components.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Reusable components and sections
requirements.text: A reusable component/section definition has stable definition identity and may be instantiated across pages.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Reusable components and sections
requirements.text: Editing a linked definition updates its instances according to override rules; Detach creates an independent component tree and must be an explicit operation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Reusable components and sections
requirements.text: Build site workspace MUST NOT duplicate an entire reusable definition into each instance merely to support one overridden property.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Editor-shell and public-route context ownership
requirements.text: Build site workspace MUST preserve the donor architecture's strict separation between editor/admin chrome and the public site being edited.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Editor-shell and public-route context ownership
requirements.text: Public headers, footers, theme chrome and public-only CSS MUST NOT leak into the Build site workspace editor shell unless rendered inside the isolated public preview.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Editor-shell and public-route context ownership
requirements.text: A component or style registered only for a public route MUST NOT accidentally become part of the editor shell merely because the preview is open.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Layout and page composition
requirements.text: Build site workspace MUST NOT represent ordinary pages as arbitrary fixed coordinates that only happen to fit one viewport.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Responsive design and breakpoints
requirements.text: Breakpoints come from the active project/design system and may be provider-defined.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Design system and tokens
requirements.text: Components SHOULD reference semantic design tokens rather than duplicating unrelated literal styling where the project/provider supports tokens.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Themes and component variants
requirements.text: Theme changes MUST NOT destroy page content or component structure.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Themes and component variants
requirements.text: Components may define named variants and states such as primary/secondary button, compact/feature card, Default/Hover/Focused/Disabled/Loading/Error/Selected.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Visual source round-trip and code-defined constructs
requirements.text: If a valid project construct cannot be represented visually, Build site workspace MUST preserve it and mark it Code-defined, Partially visual or another explicit capability state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Visual source round-trip and code-defined constructs
requirements.text: It MUST NOT delete, flatten or rewrite unsupported code simply to make the canvas editable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Pages, routes and navigation
requirements.text: A Page may render at one or more routes according to provider/project rules; Routes support static, nested and parameterised/dynamic paths, redirects and error/not-found routes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Pages, routes and navigation
requirements.text: Navigation items SHOULD reference PageID/RouteID for internal destinations rather than storing only fragile path strings.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Preview fidelity and asset manifest
requirements.text: Build site workspace preview MUST use the same applicable component styles, theme assets, route-specific assets, fonts and rendering rules as the corresponding public/live route wherever technically possible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Preview fidelity and asset manifest
requirements.text: Preview MUST NOT be a separately styled mock that can pass while the published page renders differently.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Preview fidelity and asset manifest
requirements.text: Route-specific assets such as homepage-only CSS/scripts are loaded only in applicable preview/live contexts and MUST NOT leak into unrelated pages or editor chrome.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Live preview and last-valid render
requirements.text: A SiteProject may bind directly to Build ProjectID/DomainID/revision.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Live preview and last-valid render
requirements.text: Build site workspace MUST NOT create an anonymous divergent copy when a source-backed Build project is active.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Live preview and last-valid render
requirements.text: Open in Build opens the same project/domain/source identity, optionally preserving selected page/component/source mapping.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Live preview and last-valid render
requirements.text: Build Code | Preview may use Build site workspace as the preview provider.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Simple interaction UI and graph parity
requirements.text: Simple interaction configuration MUST map to the same canonical behaviour/graph primitives used by the advanced Node Editor, or to a formally shared behaviour object represented consistently in both views.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Node execution contexts and trust boundaries
requirements.text: Build site workspace MUST NOT compile secrets or trusted permission checks into untrusted browser execution merely because a graph contains them.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Component state and node-driven animation
requirements.text: Simple animations remain configurable visually; advanced sequences may use graph/timeline primitives such as EnteredViewport → easing/spring → opacity/transform/property changes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > CMS relationships and dynamic content
requirements.text: Complex structured data/database requirements may delegate to Data; Build site workspace CMS remains optimised for web content authoring rather than duplicating Data's complete database product.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Rich content authoring
requirements.text: Long-form content MUST NOT require hand-authoring raw HTML for ordinary use.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Data integration
requirements.text: Build site workspace MUST NOT bypass Data safeguards by issuing hidden raw mutations directly to backing databases.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Forms integration
requirements.text: Site styling may provide theme/context integration without discarding Forms validation, accessibility, response versioning, anti-abuse, assessment or Data-binding semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Files and asset management
requirements.text: Moving/renaming a Files-backed asset MUST NOT break references that use stable identity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Image/media optimisation
requirements.text: Generated responsive thumbnails/encodings are derived build/cache assets with provenance; Build site workspace MUST NOT create untracked duplicate originals merely to satisfy one page size.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > SEO and discoverability
requirements.text: AI may propose SEO content but must not invent factual business claims or silently publish changes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Accessibility diagnostics and guardrails
requirements.text: Visual design freedom MUST NOT silently disable required semantic labels, focus order or other minimum accessibility behaviour.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Performance and web-quality diagnostics
requirements.text: Preview/build may expose measurable runtime metrics where the provider/runtime supports reliable collection.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Domains, redirects and HTTPS
requirements.text: Provider integrations may automate required DNS records only within the authorised scope and MUST NOT alter unrelated records.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Deployment environments
requirements.text: A preview URL MUST identify a concrete deployment/revision rather than silently floating to whatever source is latest.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Deployment providers and build pipeline
requirements.text: First-party/connected providers may offer static hosting, edge/server functions, object storage/CDN, DNS/domain integration and preview deployments according to capabilities.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Deployment providers and build pipeline
requirements.text: Build site workspace does not hard-code one provider's CLI/configuration as the canonical project model; provider-specific settings may be retained as explicit provider configuration.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Deployment history, rollback and publishing safeguards
requirements.text: Rollback normally redeploys a previously successful known source/config revision; it MUST NOT erase newer source history merely to return production to an earlier deployment.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Deployment history, rollback and publishing safeguards
requirements.text: AI MUST NOT silently publish to production without an explicit authorised action/automation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Custom code, scripts and server functions
requirements.text: Existing external-source compatibility projects may retain controlled CSS, JavaScript/TypeScript/modules and markup hooks supported by their provider.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Custom code, scripts and server functions
requirements.text: These paths must not become an alternative language for new application authoring.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Custom code, scripts and server functions
requirements.text: Consequential executable state must not exist only in a hidden proprietary database.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Custom code, scripts and server functions
requirements.text: Build site workspace may provide simplified configuration but does not invent an incompatible second backend language/runtime.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Environment variables and secrets
requirements.text: Secrets MUST NOT be exposed into browser bundles, logs, previews, AI context or generated diffs unless the operation explicitly requires the value and the caller/environment is authorised.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Authentication and member areas
requirements.text: Build site workspace may integrate with 9to1 identity/auth providers to create login/account/member experiences and restricted routes/components.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Analytics, scripts and consent
requirements.text: Consent configuration can categorise integrations/scripts such as Essential, Preferences, Analytics and Advertising and delay applicable execution until consent where configured/required.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Analytics, scripts and consent
requirements.text: Templates MUST NOT silently enable third-party tracking merely because the donor/template contained a tracking snippet.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Collaboration and revisions
requirements.text: Build site workspace MUST NOT silently overwrite another editor's changes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Collaboration and revisions
requirements.text: Comments/review may attach to PageID/ComponentID/content where supported; source-level review remains available through Build.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Dulche AI authoring and visual QA
requirements.text: AI may create/refactor pages, components, responsive layouts, themes, CMS schemas/content, bindings, node graphs, SEO metadata and project structure only through typed Build site workspace/shared-domain actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Dulche AI authoring and visual QA
requirements.text: UI-oriented AI changes SHOULD use available visual preview/QA in addition to build success.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Dulche AI authoring and visual QA
requirements.text: Overflow, clipped content, broken responsive layout, inaccessible contrast and visibly failed states must not be declared correct solely because compilation passed.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Shared extension system
requirements.text: Extensions may contribute components, component inspectors, CMS field types, Data sources/bindings, deployment providers, analytics/SEO integrations, project templates, visual-builder panels, node types and preview/runtime providers.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Shared extension system
requirements.text: A crashing extension must be containable/disableable according to the shared extension-host contract.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Shared extension system
requirements.text: Every publishable SiteProject receives or may reserve a first-party Build site workspace URL under https://sites.9to1.uk/<site-slug>.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Shared extension system
requirements.text: A segment MUST NOT begin or end with a hyphen, and empty/repeated path segments are rejected.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Shared extension system
requirements.text: For example, a project may publish at sites.9to1.uk/cake and expose routes such as sites.9to1.uk/cake/about or sites.9to1.uk/cake/contact-us.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > AI name and domain verification
requirements.text: Every requested first-party site slug and every custom domain binding MUST pass automated name-safety verification before it can become an active public identity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > AI name and domain verification
requirements.text: Clear safe names may pass automatically.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > AI name and domain verification
requirements.text: Sensitive model internals need not be exposed, but the user-visible result must be actionable and non-deceptive.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Custom domains and provider connections
requirements.text: Manual custom-domain ownership verification MUST use a secure provider-independent challenge, normally a purpose-specific DNS TXT record or equivalent proof whose random token is bound to the SiteID/account and expires/rotates according to policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Custom domains and provider connections
requirements.text: Build site workspace MAY connect to supported DNS/domain providers such as Cloudflare and later providers through typed provider integrations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Custom domains and provider connections
requirements.text: With explicitly scoped authorization, a connected provider may enumerate eligible zones, create/verify only the required challenge/serving records, inspect DNS/TLS readiness and maintain authorised redirects/routing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Custom domains and provider connections
requirements.text: Provider authorization MUST be least-privilege where the provider permits it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Custom domains and provider connections
requirements.text: Build site workspace-internal derived caches or provider credentials MUST NOT be mixed into user source as if they were canonical project content.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Custom domains and provider connections
requirements.text: The site MUST remain reconstructable and editable from the canonical Build site workspace/Files/Build project resources.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Custom domains and provider connections
requirements.text: An external host MUST NOT be the only surviving copy of the source project.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > External hosting and deployment authority
requirements.text: Provider-hosted state may include generated static output, server bundles/functions, optimized media, CDN/cache objects and runtime configuration.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > External hosting and deployment authority
requirements.text: Build site workspace MUST NOT silently adopt them as canonical.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > External hosting and deployment authority
requirements.text: Recovery MUST NOT depend on scraping the live public website to reconstruct the project.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Hosting, URL and domain API additions
requirements.text: The Build site workspace API MUST include typed operations equivalent to:

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > 9to1.Sites.ChangeHostingProvider(siteID, providerID, options?);
requirements.text: Provider-specific DNS/hosting mutations still use the shared credential/permission model and MUST NOT bypass Build site workspace deployment/domain safeguards.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Security and abuse boundaries
requirements.text: Public site content MUST NOT gain access to Build site workspace editor/admin privileges merely because it is rendered in preview.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Performance and large-site behaviour
requirements.text: Visual editing MUST remain responsive while builds/deployments/background indexing occur; long work exposes JobID/progress/status rather than blocking the editor.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Platform capability behaviour
requirements.text: A platform that cannot provide local build/runtime functionality uses an explicitly configured remote/provider capability or reports CapabilityUnavailable; it MUST NOT silently fake preview/build/deployment completion.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Build > Visual site and application workspace > Acceptance requirements
requirements.text: The external hosting provider stores/serves revision-pinned derived deployment artifacts and MUST NOT become the sole or independently editable canonical copy of the site.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Landing page: Home and Library
requirements.text: Home dashboard cards MUST open the canonical Automation or AutomationRun rather than creating separate dashboard state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Landing page: Home and Library
requirements.text: The landing page SHOULD make Create Automation prominent without forcing a user into an empty graph before they understand what they are creating.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Canonical entities
requirements.text: Automation MUST have stable AutomationID, Name, Description?, Icon?, Owner/Scope, Enabled/OperationalState, GraphID, DraftRevisionID, ActiveRevisionID?, InputSchema?, OutputSchema?, TriggerSummary, RequiredCapabilities, ExecutionPolicy, CreatedAt, ModifiedAt and Revision.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Canonical entities
requirements.text: AutomationRun MUST have stable RunID, AutomationID, pinned AutomationRevisionID, TriggerID/TriggerEventID, Status, StartedAt, FinishedAt?, typed Inputs, typed Outputs?, NodeExecutionStates, Error?, approval/wait state, causal ancestry and audit/ActionGraph references.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Canonical entities
requirements.text: Editing, renaming, moving, sharing or changing the landing-page position of an Automation MUST NOT change AutomationID.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Canonical entities
requirements.text: A Run is historical execution state and MUST remain bound to the exact Automation revision it executed.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Graph editor and simple creation
requirements.text: Automations MAY offer simple When / If / Then creation, templates or natural-language creation, but these are graph-authoring views over the same GraphID rather than separate simplified formats.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Graph editor and simple creation
requirements.text: Opening an Automation MUST always allow inspection of the real graph.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Node search and connector interaction
requirements.text: Node creation/search MUST follow an Unreal-style graph interaction pattern.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Node search and connector interaction
requirements.text: Results SHOULD be grouped by meaningful categories while search ranks direct action/event/type matches first.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Node search and connector interaction
requirements.text: Connector deletion MUST support Ctrl-click directly on a connection/connector to remove it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Node search and connector interaction
requirements.text: Keyboard-accessible selection plus Delete/Backspace MUST provide an equivalent non-pointer path.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Node search and connector interaction
requirements.text: Automations MUST NOT maintain a stale hard-coded copy of the ecosystem's available actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Trigger model
requirements.text: Event-driven state change MUST be preferred to wasteful polling when an owning capability provides an event/change feed.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Trigger model
requirements.text: Trigger delivery MUST have stable identity/deduplication semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Node families
requirements.text: The Automations capability profile MUST include registered node families needed for mature workflow composition, including:

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Device-level actions
requirements.text: Automations MUST expose an extensive device-level action catalogue sourced directly from the capabilities actually advertised by the current/selected Home or Mesh device.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Device-level actions
requirements.text: Every device action node records the required DeviceID/capability/action version or an explicit compatible-device targeting policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Device-level actions
requirements.text: The editor MUST warn when an action is device-specific or not portable and explain that it may not work on another device.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Device-level actions
requirements.text: Validation on another device MUST report capability mismatch rather than silently substituting a different action.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Device-level actions
requirements.text: Automations MUST NOT turn device actions into a generic remote-desktop or arbitrary-code-execution channel.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Third-party app and service actions
requirements.text: Automations MUST surface typed third-party app/service actions wherever an installed app, plugin, connector, MCP capability, operating-system integration or registered provider exposes them.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Third-party app and service actions
requirements.text: Example: a Schedule trigger at 16:00 may connect to a registered YouTube/compatible media action that plays a specified video on a selected compatible device.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Natural-language graph creation and editing
requirements.text: Dulche can create and modify Automations from natural-language requests, but the result MUST be a real editable Node Graph mutation using typed Node Graph APIs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Natural-language graph creation and editing
requirements.text: AI-generated graphs MUST validate node/action schemas, connection types, permissions/capabilities and target availability before activation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Natural-language graph creation and editing
requirements.text: The editor SHOULD visually highlight nodes/connections added or changed by the most recent AI operation and allow ordinary undo.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Data, variables and nullability
requirements.text: Missing data MUST NOT silently become zero, False or an empty string and accidentally take the wrong branch.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Durable Wait and resume
requirements.text: Wait/Delay MUST be durable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Durable Wait and resume
requirements.text: It MUST NOT depend on an application thread/process literally sleeping.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Durable Wait and resume
requirements.text: Restart/redeployment must resume a valid waiting Run from persisted state without repeating already-committed side effects.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Approval nodes
requirements.text: Approval expresses workflow-required human review; the broker determines whether the caller is authorised to execute the protected action.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Approval nodes
requirements.text: Either mechanism may independently block execution.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Permissions, connections and secret handling
requirements.text: Activating a revision MUST show/derive the capabilities and action scopes the active graph requires.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Permissions, connections and secret handling
requirements.text: Secrets, tokens and provider credentials MUST NOT be stored as plaintext node properties.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Execution location and device targeting
requirements.text: Execution policy MUST make where the workflow can run explicit.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Execution location and device targeting
requirements.text: Supported executors may include 9to1 cloud, the current Home/device runtime, a selected compatible Mesh device or a provider-native executor where that provider/action supports it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Execution location and device targeting
requirements.text: The UI MUST NOT claim that a device-bound Automation will execute while all required devices are offline.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Execution location and device targeting
requirements.text: Conversely, a cloud-capable workflow MUST NOT unnecessarily depend on an open desktop UI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Execution location and device targeting
requirements.text: A device-targetable node may require a specific DeviceID, any compatible paired device or the triggering device according to its declared targeting policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Run lifecycle and operational state
requirements.text: If Runs are already active, the UI must explicitly offer a policy such as allow existing Runs to finish, pause them where safe, or cancel them.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Run lifecycle and operational state
requirements.text: Home dashboard/Library status MUST be derived from canonical definition/run/connection state, not a separately editable status field.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Run history and execution inspection
requirements.text: Dulche may summarise it in natural language but MUST NOT invent events or hide failed/denied/cancelled nodes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Error handling, retry and idempotency
requirements.text: Authors may explicitly add retry, On Failure, fallback or continue semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Error handling, retry and idempotency
requirements.text: Retries of external or destructive actions MUST use the target action's idempotency/OperationID contract where available.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Error handling, retry and idempotency
requirements.text: If the runtime cannot determine whether a timed-out consequential action committed, it MUST enter a typed uncertain/Needs Attention state rather than blindly repeat an operation that could duplicate its external side effect.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Loop and cascade protection
requirements.text: The runtime MUST detect repeated event/run cycles, bound recursion/cascade depth and total execution budget, and deduplicate replayed trigger deliveries.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Test, validate and run
requirements.text: The editor MUST distinguish Validate, Test and Run for real.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Test, validate and run
requirements.text: Test executes with selected sample/current data and MUST use action preview/dry-run facilities where the target capability provides them.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Test, validate and run
requirements.text: If a Test reaches an action that cannot be safely simulated, Automations must identify that limitation and require explicit real-execution confirmation before performing the side effect.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Sharing, teams and run-as identity
requirements.text: Automations MAY be shared within supported personal/team/workspace scopes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Sharing, teams and run-as identity
requirements.text: Where shared execution supports multiple identities, run-as semantics MUST be explicit, such as triggering user versus Automation owner/service identity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Sharing, teams and run-as identity
requirements.text: The runtime MUST NOT silently choose whichever identity has greater authority.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Compatibility and migration
requirements.text: Migration may be automatic only when semantics are provably equivalent; otherwise the editor must show the affected nodes and require review before reactivation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.text: Automations MUST host the global persistent Dulche AI bar.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.text: Write mode may modify the graph only through typed Node Graph/Automation APIs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Persistent contextual AI bar
requirements.text: AI MUST NOT simulate graph mouse gestures.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Persistent contextual AI bar > Persistence and recovery
requirements.text: A crash/restart MUST NOT restart the graph from the beginning and duplicate already-committed actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Persistent contextual AI bar > Accessibility
requirements.text: The landing Home/Library, node graph and Run inspector MUST be keyboard-operable and accessible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Persistent contextual AI bar > Accessibility
requirements.text: Graph zoom/pan must not be required to discover the textual meaning of a node.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Persistent contextual AI bar > Accessibility
requirements.text: A structured accessible node/connection list or equivalent semantic representation MUST be available to assistive technology.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Persistent contextual AI bar > Performance and resource behaviour
requirements.text: Large graphs, Libraries and Run histories MUST virtualise where appropriate.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Persistent contextual AI bar > Performance and resource behaviour
requirements.text: Node catalogue search must remain responsive across extensive app/device/third-party action registries and should query/index incrementally rather than blocking on full capability rescans.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Persistent contextual AI bar > Performance and resource behaviour
requirements.text: Execution is event-driven/durable; idle/waiting Runs must not retain unnecessary UI/execution threads.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Automations > Persistent contextual AI bar > Failure behaviour
requirements.text: Automations MUST return structured failures including AutomationNotFound, RunNotFound, InvalidGraph, ValidationFailed, NodeTypeUnavailable, ConnectionTypeMismatch, CapabilityUnavailable, DeviceCapabilityUnavailable, DeviceOffline, ProviderConnectionUnavailable, PermissionRequired, ApprovalRejected, ApprovalTimedOut, WaitResumeFailed, RevisionConflict, TriggerDuplicate, LoopDetected, ExecutionBudgetExceeded, UnsafeRetryState and MigrationRequired in addition to target-action errors.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Product role
requirements.text: It MUST behave like a mature word processor rather than a web editor, site builder, Markdown editor, collection of HTML blocks or browser contenteditable surface.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Product role
requirements.text: The document surface MUST use an actual structured document model with paragraph/run/style/section/table/object/reference/review semantics and real layout/text measurement.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Product role
requirements.text: Caret movement, selection, rich clipboard, IME input, undo/redo transactions, object anchoring, line wrapping, pagination, spelling/grammar ranges, accessibility semantics and large-document behaviour MUST be implemented as document-editor behaviour, not emulated with disconnected DOM widgets.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Product role
requirements.text: A document MUST switch between supported views without changing its canonical content or losing document semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Donor parity and objective word-processor behaviour
requirements.text: All applicable LibreOffice Writer functionality, quality-of-life behaviour, keyboard interactions, menus/workflows and file-format depth MUST be preserved or appropriately adapted.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Donor parity and objective word-processor behaviour
requirements.text: The donor source is authoritative for inherited functionality; Write MUST NOT ship as a simplified rich-text clone simply because a smaller editor is easier to implement.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Donor parity and objective word-processor behaviour
requirements.text: Normal end-user installation must include the required engine dependencies through the approved packaging/runtime system, not require a separate manual donor installation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Launch and file entry
requirements.text: Entries MUST be backed by real Files/Drive data rather than mock cards.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Launch and file entry
requirements.text: The start screen and editor have separate compositions and active interaction scopes within the shared CUI shell: the document canvas and document-specific formatting tools MUST NOT sit below the start page, and launch-only content MUST NOT remain as a header above the editor.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Editor shell
requirements.text: Write MUST NOT use a permanent Office-style ribbon.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Editor shell
requirements.text: The editing shell consists of a document-title row, a floating contextual toolbar immediately below the title at the top of the document area, an optional collapsible Sections sidebar, the document canvas and the persistent shared AI bar at the bottom.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Floating contextual toolbar
requirements.text: An operation that cannot apply to the current selection MUST NOT appear merely because it exists elsewhere in Write; for example Crop image cannot appear when no image is selected.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Floating contextual toolbar
