requirements.text: The menu for a table selection differs from the menu for text or an image and MUST exclude inapplicable actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Pinned toolbar actions
requirements.text: Users MUST be able to pin supported contextual actions to the top bar and reorder/reset their pinned preferences.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Pinned toolbar actions
requirements.text: Pinning means prioritise this action whenever it is applicable; it MUST NOT force an irrelevant disabled action to occupy the toolbar in unrelated contexts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Pinned toolbar actions
requirements.text: Toolbar priority SHOULD resolve from the most important current-context control, then applicable user-pinned controls, then common contextual actions, followed by the persistent +, Eye and […] controls.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Universal Insert (+)
requirements.text: The complete palette MUST expose applicable content/structure/reference/9to1 artifact options while prioritising items relevant to the current caret/object context.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Universal Insert (+)
requirements.text: Insertion types SHOULD include tables, images, drawings, equations, code blocks, text boxes, shapes/callouts, horizontal lines, page/section breaks, columns, headers/footers, footnotes, citations, cross-references, bookmarks, captions, table of contents, special characters, fields, links/files and supported embedded 9to1 artifacts such as Canvas, Board, Data ranges/charts, Picture, Planner items, Maps and Graphs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Eye / visibility controls
requirements.text: Its menu MUST include the current Write View mode and may include Sections visibility, Comments, spelling/grammar marks, formatting marks, ruler, page boundaries, object anchors, alignment/snap guides and the floating word/character count where applicable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Eye / visibility controls
requirements.text: Most Eye settings are per-user view preferences and MUST NOT change what collaborators see.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Eye / visibility controls
requirements.text: Contextually useful visibility aids MAY appear only when relevant, for example object bounds/anchors/guides when an object is selected.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Floating document statistics
requirements.text: It SHOULD show document word and character counts, and when text is selected it SHOULD prioritise selection word/character counts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Floating document statistics
requirements.text: Clicking it MAY reveal expanded statistics such as characters without spaces and page count where meaningful.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Floating document statistics
requirements.text: The statistics indicator and bottom AI bar MUST coexist without overlap at supported sizes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Sections sidebar
requirements.text: A Section is a stable user-created structural division of the same Write document and MAY contain nested Sections.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Sections sidebar
requirements.text: Every Section MUST have stable SectionID, DocumentID, optional ParentSectionID, Name, optional icon/metadata, ordering and revision/state information.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Sections sidebar
requirements.text: Renaming/reordering/nesting MUST preserve SectionID so links, AI context and cross-references are not tied to visible names.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Sections sidebar
requirements.text: The Sections sidebar MUST be collapsible to a narrow edge/rail and resizable when expanded.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Sections sidebar
requirements.text: Collapsing immediately returns horizontal space to the document canvas; navigation/AI actions MUST NOT forcibly reopen it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > View modes
requirements.text: Continuous view MUST retain page-aware document features such as headers/footers, footnotes, page numbers, margins, section/page breaks and columns in the underlying document model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > View modes
requirements.text: The view may present them contextually rather than permanently rendering every page boundary.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > View modes
requirements.text: It MUST not use dated harsh page chrome merely because the donor does.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > View modes
requirements.text: Narrow displays MAY show one page at a time while preserving spread semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Locked and Unlocked layout
requirements.text: Write MUST implement the same first-class Locked/Unlocked layout concept as Boards.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Locked and Unlocked layout
requirements.text: Users may drag, resize, rotate, overlap, layer, align, distribute and snap these objects without converting the whole document into arbitrary floating text boxes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Locked and Unlocked layout
requirements.text: Unlocked object controls MUST support position/size/rotation; page/Section/paragraph/character anchoring where meaningful; inline/square/tight/behind/in-front/custom wrapping; aspect and position locks; z-order; align/distribute; grouping; snapping to margins, columns, guides, text bounds and other objects; and accessible non-drag alternatives.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Locked and Unlocked layout
requirements.text: Switching layout modes MUST preserve data and positions as far as the target representation supports.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Locked and Unlocked layout
requirements.text: If an object cannot be represented safely under the requested mode/foreign format, Write MUST warn rather than silently discard/flatten it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Styles and custom styles
requirements.text: Custom styles MUST be first-class and front-and-centre whenever the selected content supports styles.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Styles and custom styles
requirements.text: For text, the active semantic style control SHOULD normally be the first contextual toolbar control rather than leading with raw font/size controls.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Styles and custom styles
requirements.text: Write MUST support built-in and arbitrary custom character/paragraph/document styles with stable StyleID, inheritance/overrides where supported, modify/create/update-from-selection, usage inspection and import/copy of style sets.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Styles and custom styles
requirements.text: Styles MAY control typography, paragraph/line spacing, indentation, alignment, borders/background, list behaviour, pagination/keep-with-next, language, outline level and semantic/accessibility role.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Styles and custom styles
requirements.text: Changing a shared/custom style MUST update linked uses while preserving explicit local overrides according to the style model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Styles and custom styles
requirements.text: Write SHOULD preview the scope/impact of broad style changes where useful.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Styles and custom styles
requirements.text: Equivalent reusable style concepts SHOULD exist for tables and other supported object classes where they provide real value; these remain canonical style definitions rather than visual presets copied independently into each object.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Tables
requirements.text: Tables MUST support mature Writer/Office-level editing plus a stronger native .9to1w styling model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Tables
requirements.text: The contextual toolbar for a table SHOULD prioritise active Table Style plus common Borders, Fill, Padding, Alignment and structural actions, with less-common relevant actions in […].

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Tables
requirements.text: Whole-table controls MUST include width/height and fixed/content/flexible sizing as supported; alignment; wrapping; position/anchor; table padding/margins; background/opacity; border; shadow; caption; repeating header rows; pagination/split behaviour; and native rounded-corner support.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Tables
requirements.text: Native .9to1w tables MUST support table corner radius, including linked or independent top-left/top-right/bottom-right/bottom-left radii.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Tables
requirements.text: Foreign export MUST preserve this where the target format can represent it or explicitly warn/use a documented compatibility representation when it cannot.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Tables
requirements.text: Row/column controls SHOULD include explicit/flexible/min/max sizing, equal distribution, visibility/header designation, keep-together and appropriate responsive/fixed behaviour.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Tables
requirements.text: Cell controls MUST include independent top/right/bottom/left padding, horizontal/vertical alignment, text direction, background/fill, border per side, border width/style/colour/opacity, merge/split, minimum dimensions and defined overflow behaviour.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Tables
requirements.text: Border editing MUST distinguish outer border, inner horizontal, inner vertical and individual cell edges.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Tables
requirements.text: Cell padding MUST be directly discoverable and support linked/unlinked values rather than being buried in an obscure properties dialog.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Tables
requirements.text: Custom Table Styles MUST be reusable first-class definitions capable of controlling whole-table appearance, header rows, first/last columns, odd/even rows, typography, borders, corner radius, cell padding, alignment and backgrounds.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Images, drawings and positioned objects
requirements.text: Images and visual objects MUST support professional crop, resize, aspect ratio, wrap, anchor, positioning, z-order, caption, alt text, replacement and supported compression/export controls.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Images, drawings and positioned objects
requirements.text: Object controls and […] overflow remain contextual; irrelevant image controls MUST not appear for text/table selections.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > References and document structure
requirements.text: Citation/reference data MUST be structured rather than only formatted prose so Agents and APIs can insert, validate, update and export references safely.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > References and document structure
requirements.text: Section/heading links and cross-references SHOULD use stable IDs rather than visible text/page numbers as identity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Review, comments and collaboration
requirements.text: Write MUST support comments, tracked/suggested changes, accept/reject, previous/next change, document comparison and version history using real document/review semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Review, comments and collaboration
requirements.text: Realtime collaboration MUST use the normal 9to1 shared-artifact model for presence, cursors/selections, concurrent editing, comments, permissions/sharing and revision/conflict semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Native format and foreign document formats
requirements.text: .9to1w is the versioned native Write format and MUST preserve the full native document model, stable Productivity object identity, Sections, custom styles/table styles, embedded 9to1 artifact references, review/collaboration metadata, drawings/graphs, supported AI provenance and native features that foreign formats cannot represent.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Native format and foreign document formats
requirements.text: Migrations MUST be deterministic and preserve compatible unknown optional data.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Native format and foreign document formats
requirements.text: Write MUST support reliable DOCX and ODT import/export plus supported Markdown/TXT interchange and PDF export.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Native format and foreign document formats
requirements.text: Unsupported or lossy foreign-format behaviour MUST be surfaced rather than silently deleting content to force compatibility.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > PDF opening and editing
requirements.text: Write MUST open and edit PDFs as first-class fixed-layout documents; PDF support is not export-only and MUST NOT simply convert every PDF into HTML or an approximate web editor.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > PDF opening and editing
requirements.text: A digitally structured PDF SHOULD preserve selectable/editable native text, fonts, images, vector/page objects, links, annotations, forms/layers where supported and page geometry.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > PDF opening and editing
requirements.text: Scanned PDFs MUST be recognised as image/scanned content rather than falsely presented as native text.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > PDF opening and editing
requirements.text: Write SHOULD offer explicit Recognise text/OCR-style transformation, preserve correspondence to the original page image and expose uncertain/low-confidence recognition rather than claiming perfect extraction.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > PDF opening and editing
requirements.text: PDF editing MUST support useful fixed-layout workflows where technically supported: editing/moving existing text blocks, inserting/deleting text, images and objects, resize/crop, drawings/shapes, page rearrange/insert/delete/rotate, combine/extract pages, links, annotations/comments/highlights, proper redaction, supported form fields/signatures and headers/footers/page numbers.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > PDF opening and editing
requirements.text: Before the first destructive PDF save, Write MUST preserve an original recoverable revision/backup and maintain normal version history.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > PDF opening and editing
requirements.text: PDF AI operations use semantic PDF text/object structure when available and MUST NOT OCR screenshots of text that the PDF already exposes semantically.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > PDF opening and editing
requirements.text: Continuous MUST NOT be forced onto a fixed-layout PDF.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Persistent AI bar in Write
requirements.text: The AI context MUST expose stable DocumentID, document revision, current SectionID/heading/object, selection ranges/ObjectIDs, document structure, styles, comments, references, tables/images/embedded artifacts and available typed actions as authorised.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Persistent AI bar in Write
requirements.text: Visual rendering may supplement this when layout must be inspected, but semantic access is primary.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Persistent AI bar in Write
requirements.text: For example AI Write mode + Suggest creates tracked suggestions; AI Write mode + Edit may perform direct typed edits; AI Read-only always prohibits mutations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Persistent AI bar in Write
requirements.text: The bar MUST NOT use mouse/keyboard simulation instead of Write APIs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Agents, sources and Translate integration
requirements.text: Write MAY expose applicable Global, Write-scoped, Space and contextual Dulche Agents through the shared Agent picker.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Agents, sources and Translate integration
requirements.text: Documents MAY reference authorised source sets/files without unnecessarily duplicating them into the document.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Agents, sources and Translate integration
requirements.text: Source-backed AI work SHOULD preserve provenance where appropriate.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Embedded 9to1 artifacts and interoperability
requirements.text: Write MAY embed/reference supported Boards, Canvas, Data ranges/charts, Picture assets, Planner items, Maps, Graphs and other canonical 9to1 artifacts as live embeds, linked previews or explicit snapshots according to the target type and permissions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Embedded 9to1 artifacts and interoperability
requirements.text: Embedding MUST reference canonical entities rather than creating unmanaged duplicate state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Embedded 9to1 artifacts and interoperability
requirements.text: Shared Productivity Engine bundles and object identities MUST support rich cross-app copy/paste/conversion where semantics are compatible; unsupported conversion MUST fail explicitly rather than silently flattening required behaviour.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Navigation, search and long-document performance
requirements.text: Write MUST provide document search/find-replace and efficient navigation for large documents.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Navigation, search and long-document performance
requirements.text: Long documents MUST not require eagerly rendering every page/object to remain editable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Navigation, search and long-document performance
requirements.text: Switching Continuous/Pages/Book, opening/collapsing Sections, enabling counts/marks and changing selections MUST avoid unnecessary full-document re-rendering where the document engine can update incrementally.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Recovery, persistence and accessibility
requirements.text: Write MUST support autosave, unsaved-draft protection, crash recovery, revision/version history, conflict recovery and safe interrupted-save behaviour.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Recovery, persistence and accessibility
requirements.text: A crash or partial write MUST not casually lose a user's document.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Recovery, persistence and accessibility
requirements.text: The Sections drawer, toolbar, floating statistics and AI bar must remain usable without overlap at supported scale factors.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Canonical Write API
requirements.text: Every user-visible Write operation, including contextual toolbar, context-menu, Sections, view/layout, review, PDF and AI-triggered operations, MUST have equivalent typed API coverage under the global parity rule.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Failure behaviour
requirements.text: Write MUST return structured failures including DocumentNotFound, UnsupportedDocumentVersion, ImportUnsupported, ImportLossy, ExportUnsupported, ExportLossy, SectionNotFound, StyleNotFound, TableNotFound, ObjectNotFound, InvalidRange, RevisionConflict, PermissionDenied, ReadOnlyDocument, LayoutConversionLoss, PDFUnsupported, PDFObjectNotEditable, OCRUnavailable, OCRUncertain, PDFBackupFailed, RecoveryUnavailable and ProviderUnavailable in addition to shared Home/Dulche/Files failures.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements
requirements.text: Formatting must change the selected document runs/paragraphs/objects and render through the real document model; modifying only toolbar state or metadata is failure.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements
requirements.text: All applicable donor baseline features must remain discoverable and usable through the intended CUI product, not only backend APIs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements
requirements.text: Launch/start and editor MUST independently satisfy LAUNCH-001–006 and APP-AC-009, with separate runtime evidence and real navigation; a start-page heading above the document surface is a rejection case.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements
requirements.text: RCVP may defer only new 9to1 enhancements assigned to Full feature scope by the active directive.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements
requirements.text: Full must independently verify all specified Sections, Continuous/Pages/Book, Locked/Unlocked, custom text/table styles, PDF editing, review/collaboration, AI, interoperability and remaining Write requirements.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements
requirements.text: View/theme changes must preserve canonical content, identity and selection.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements
requirements.text: UI controls, typed APIs and resulting artifacts must demonstrate the same real operations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements > A. HEADER, EDITING TOOLBAR AND COMMAND HIERARCHY
requirements.text: Toolbar contents MUST follow actual semantic selection: text/heading, table, image, positioned object, references and review surface the right actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements > A. HEADER, EDITING TOOLBAR AND COMMAND HIERARCHY
requirements.text: Text must not show Crop; table context prioritises real Table Style, border/fill/padding/alignment/structure controls; images prioritise real image/anchor/crop/wrap controls.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements > A. HEADER, EDITING TOOLBAR AND COMMAND HIERARCHY
requirements.text: Toolbar, keyboard shortcuts, inspector, right-click and typed Write/Productivity APIs MUST route to identical undoable semantic document operations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements > A. HEADER, EDITING TOOLBAR AND COMMAND HIERARCHY
requirements.text: Common text commands should remain first-class at supported desktop widths.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements > A. HEADER, EDITING TOOLBAR AND COMMAND HIERARCHY
requirements.text: Opening/closing must not accidentally destroy the active editing selection or scroll position.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements > B. PROPERTIES INSPECTOR, SECTIONS, CANVAS AND START SCREEN
requirements.text: Central document must remain visually dominant.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements > B. PROPERTIES INSPECTOR, SECTIONS, CANVAS AND START SCREEN
requirements.text: Text and highlight colour use an actual swatch/palette/colour picker with live preview and optional hexadecimal/ARGB advanced entry; raw colour strings must not be the primary selection workflow.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements > B. PROPERTIES INSPECTOR, SECTIONS, CANVAS AND START SCREEN
requirements.text: The inspector, toolbar, stored style and rendered document must reflect identical values; investigate observed apparent colour-value discrepancies using source and rendered evidence.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements > B. PROPERTIES INSPECTOR, SECTIONS, CANVAS AND START SCREEN
requirements.text: Retain technically meaningful operations such as Split/Merge run if required, but place them in an appropriate Advanced/contextual surface rather than everyday formatting.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements > B. PROPERTIES INSPECTOR, SECTIONS, CANVAS AND START SCREEN
requirements.text: Opening, changing or dismissing the inspector must not erase selection, relocate caret, break scroll, create duplicate state or corrupt undo.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements > B. PROPERTIES INSPECTOR, SECTIONS, CANVAS AND START SCREEN
requirements.text: Scroll in the inspector must be independent from page scroll.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements > B. PROPERTIES INSPECTOR, SECTIONS, CANVAS AND START SCREEN
requirements.text: Existing stage-required create/rename/reorder/nest/heading navigate actions and keyboard/non-drag alternatives must genuinely work.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements > B. PROPERTIES INSPECTOR, SECTIONS, CANVAS AND START SCREEN
requirements.text: Organise New/Blank, real Templates, Recent, Favourites, Shared, Search, Open and Import paths under understandable primary-action hierarchy; useful recent metadata/previews must come from real files, not mocks.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements > B. PROPERTIES INSPECTOR, SECTIONS, CANVAS AND START SCREEN
requirements.text: WRITE-UX-115 — Accurate status bar, optional statistics and save truth.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements > B. PROPERTIES INSPECTOR, SECTIONS, CANVAS AND START SCREEN
requirements.text: Coordinate bottom status with Eye-enabled optional floating document/selection statistics and shared AI bar: no overlap, contradictory counts, duplicate chrome or insertion of status UI into document content.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements > B. PROPERTIES INSPECTOR, SECTIONS, CANVAS AND START SCREEN
requirements.text: Native controls may provide infrastructure but CUI alone owns public component composition, theme and style.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements > B. PROPERTIES INSPECTOR, SECTIONS, CANVAS AND START SCREEN
requirements.text: No supported feature may be removed for a cleaner screenshot.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements > B. PROPERTIES INSPECTOR, SECTIONS, CANVAS AND START SCREEN
requirements.text: Keep changes in Write and genuinely shared CUI infrastructure unless other scope is explicitly required.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements > B. PROPERTIES INSPECTOR, SECTIONS, CANVAS AND START SCREEN
requirements.text: The RCVP stage includes the mature donor baseline and required launch/CUI quality; Full includes all additional Write-specific extensions and independent acceptance.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements > C. EVIDENCE-BASED WRITE ACCEPTANCE
requirements.text: Verify swatches, optional HEX input, numeric +/- alignment, validation, mixed state, context-sensitive sections, independent scrolling and no selection/focus loss.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements > C. EVIDENCE-BASED WRITE ACCEPTANCE
requirements.text: Capture authentic screenshots or interaction recordings from the precise source/build/runtime: home, editor with full text toolbar, selected formatted content, properties with colour picker and numeric control, contextual table/image toolbar, insert/context menus, nested sidebar, page/continuous/book where stage-required, zoom/status and representative narrow layout.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements > C. EVIDENCE-BASED WRITE ACCEPTANCE
requirements.text: COMPLETED does not automatically mean VERIFIED; unavailable GUI validation must remain explicitly NOT VERIFIED.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements > C. EVIDENCE-BASED WRITE ACCEPTANCE
requirements.text: Write MUST use Home’s Shared Productivity Engine for every shared object type it supports.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Write > Acceptance requirements > C. EVIDENCE-BASED WRITE ACCEPTANCE
requirements.text: Shared objects copied between Write, Present, Canvas, Boards and Spaces MUST preserve the common object schema, formatting and behaviour rather than being converted into Write-only representations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Purpose, ownership and conformance
requirements.text: Applicable donor functionality MUST be preserved unless a scoped donor-parity exception is recorded in the canonical donor-parity manifest.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Purpose, ownership and conformance
requirements.text: Present MUST NOT ship as a reduced slide editor whose only conformance evidence is file opening or basic text/shape editing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Purpose, ownership and conformance
requirements.text: Present MUST use Home's Shared Productivity Engine for every registered shared object type that it supports.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Purpose, ownership and conformance
requirements.text: Shared text, tables, charts/graphs, images/media, drawings/ink and other shared objects copied between Present, Write, Canvas, Boards and Spaces MUST preserve the shared object schema, semantic identifiers, formatting, accessibility metadata and clipboard representation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Purpose, ownership and conformance
requirements.text: Present MUST NOT introduce a second private implementation of a Home-owned shared object or platform service.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Normative applicability and capability negotiation
requirements.text: A platform capability is supported only when the platform capability registry declares the required capability and version for the active device/runtime.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Normative applicability and capability negotiation
requirements.text: Failure of a required capability check MUST produce a typed unavailable/unsupported result and the specified fallback or CompatibilityIssue; silent omission is prohibited.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Normative applicability and capability negotiation
requirements.text: An implementation MUST NOT reinterpret a MUST requirement as optional merely because its current code path does not implement the required capability.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Landing page, file lifecycle and persistence
requirements.text: Present MUST implement the global launch-screen contract.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Landing page, file lifecycle and persistence
requirements.text: The launch surface MUST expose Create New, Open/Import, recent presentations and real template/theme discovery.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Landing page, file lifecycle and persistence
requirements.text: Recent items MUST be derived from persisted history; fabricated recent files are prohibited except for explicitly labelled onboarding or template content.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Landing page, file lifecycle and persistence
requirements.text: The release file contract MUST support native .9to1p plus PPTX and ODP import/export.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Landing page, file lifecycle and persistence
requirements.text: Static output MUST support PDF and image export.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Landing page, file lifecycle and persistence
requirements.text: Present MUST provide complete create -> edit -> save -> close -> reopen workflows with autosave, crash/interrupted-save recovery, revision tracking and conflict-safe persistence.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Landing page, file lifecycle and persistence
requirements.text: A failed save, partial media write, unresolved revision conflict or recovery failure MUST be surfaced as an explicit error state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Landing page, file lifecycle and persistence
requirements.text: Present MUST NOT report success until the target revision and all referenced persisted objects required for the save have been committed.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Landing page, file lifecycle and persistence
requirements.text: Recovery MUST preserve the last known-good durable revision and MUST NOT overwrite it with a partially reconstructed presentation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Canonical data model and identity
requirements.text: All persistent entities MUST use stable opaque IDs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Canonical data model and identity
requirements.text: Slide number, slide title, list position, object name and file path are mutable presentation attributes and MUST NOT be used as persistent identity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Canonical data model and identity
requirements.text: Reordering, renaming, hiding, duplicating or moving a slide MUST NOT mutate the identity of an existing SlideID.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Canonical data model and identity
requirements.text: Duplicating a slide MUST allocate a new SlideID and new IDs for duplicated slide-owned objects while preserving references that are explicitly shared by definition.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Canonical data model and identity
requirements.text: A reference to a slide or object MUST resolve by stable ID.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Canonical data model and identity
requirements.text: Position-based references such as 'slide 4' MAY be accepted as user input, but MUST be resolved to a stable ID before persistence or execution.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Canonical data model and identity
requirements.text: Changing a release default MUST create an explicit persisted setting override.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Canonical data model and identity
requirements.text: Absence of an override means the release default above; implementations MUST NOT infer a different default from platform, file origin or prior session state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Authoring shell and slide navigation
requirements.text: The editing shell MUST expose a persistent slide navigator, thumbnail view, slide sorter/grid view and searchable presentation outline.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Authoring shell and slide navigation
requirements.text: The same SlideID MUST back every representation of a slide.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Authoring shell and slide navigation
requirements.text: Preserve selection and focus predictably after slide mutations; deleting the active slide MUST move focus to a deterministic adjacent surviving slide.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Authoring shell and slide navigation
requirements.text: The authoring shell MUST provide undo/redo, zoom, fit slide, fit selection, rulers, guides, grid, snapping controls and a status surface showing at least current slide/total slide count, zoom and relevant selection/document state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Authoring shell and slide navigation
requirements.text: Keyboard-only navigation MUST cover the navigator, canvas, notes pane and inspectors.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Conventional object editing and layout
requirements.text: Present MUST provide mature slide-object editing for text, shapes, lines/connectors, images, shared tables/charts/graphs, drawings, media, code objects, 3D objects, Generative UI objects and supported embedded/shared objects.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Conventional object editing and layout
requirements.text: Every spatial object type that declares geometric editing MUST support the applicable subset of:

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Conventional object editing and layout
requirements.text: Shape and text styling MUST persist actual stored values.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Conventional object editing and layout
requirements.text: Inspectors, toolbars and keyboard commands MUST read from and write to the same canonical object properties; a visible control that does not mutate the corresponding stored property is non-conformant.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Conventional object editing and layout
requirements.text: Present MUST support object naming and a selection/object tree.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Conventional object editing and layout
requirements.text: The tree MUST expose stacking order, locked/hidden state and semantic object identity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Conventional object editing and layout
requirements.text: Reordering the tree MUST change z-order only when the selected object type participates in z-order.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Themes, masters, layouts and templates
requirements.text: Present MUST support theme colours, theme fonts, backgrounds, reusable style tokens, slide masters, slide layouts, placeholders and reusable templates.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Themes, masters, layouts and templates
requirements.text: A slide linked to a layout MUST inherit layout/master properties unless that property has an explicit slide-level override.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Themes, masters, layouts and templates
requirements.text: Changing a master or layout MUST update linked slides without deleting valid slide-level overrides.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Themes, masters, layouts and templates
requirements.text: Reset Layout MUST remove only slide-level overrides governed by the selected layout; it MUST NOT delete unrelated slide-owned objects.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Themes, masters, layouts and templates
requirements.text: PPTX/ODP import MUST preserve representable master/layout relationships instead of flattening every slide to unrelated absolute objects.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Themes, masters, layouts and templates
requirements.text: Notes-page and handout layout data present in an imported format MUST be retained when the source construct maps to a declared Present capability.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Themes, masters, layouts and templates
requirements.text: If no declared mapping exists, import MUST emit a CompatibilityIssue rather than silently dropping the construct.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Speaker notes and notes workflow
requirements.text: Every slide MUST have first-class speaker notes identified by a stable NotesID.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Speaker notes and notes workflow
requirements.text: Notes MUST be editable in a dedicated notes pane and a full Notes view.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Speaker notes and notes workflow
requirements.text: Notes MUST support shared rich-text editing, lists, links, proofing and supported shared embedded objects.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Speaker notes and notes workflow
requirements.text: Notes MUST be searchable and addressable by typed APIs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Speaker notes and notes workflow
requirements.text: The shared Dictation capability MUST operate in speaker notes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Speaker notes and notes workflow
requirements.text: Notes MUST appear in Presenter View and notes-page print/export when explicitly selected.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Speaker notes and notes workflow
requirements.text: Normal slideshow output, ordinary audience capture, PDF/image export and generated video MUST exclude speaker notes by default.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Speaker notes and notes workflow
requirements.text: A notes-inclusive export MUST require an explicit notes output mode; it MUST NOT be inferred from the presence of notes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Speaker notes and notes workflow
requirements.text: PPTX/ODP import/export MUST preserve speaker notes when the destination format supports them.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Speaker notes and notes workflow
requirements.text: Loss or degradation MUST be listed in the compatibility report.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Word, character and speaking statistics
requirements.text: Present MUST provide live text statistics for presentation content.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Word, character and speaking statistics
requirements.text: The statistics engine MUST expose the following explicit scopes: SELECTION, CURRENT_SLIDE, CURRENT_NOTES, ALL_SLIDES, ALL_NOTES and PRESENTATION_COMBINED.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Word, character and speaking statistics
requirements.text: Word boundaries MUST follow the platform Unicode word-segmentation implementation based on Unicode word-boundary rules.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Word, character and speaking statistics
requirements.text: Character counts MUST count user-perceived Unicode grapheme clusters rather than UTF-16 code units.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Word, character and speaking statistics
requirements.text: CharacterCountWithoutSpaces MUST exclude grapheme clusters classified by the platform Unicode implementation as whitespace.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Word, character and speaking statistics
requirements.text: Comments, alt text, object names, Actions node labels, code source, hidden implementation metadata and compatibility metadata MUST NOT be included in ordinary word/character counts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Word, character and speaking statistics
requirements.text: ALL_SLIDES MUST include hidden slides by default because they are part of the authored document; the statistics UI MUST provide an explicit Exclude hidden slides filter.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Word, character and speaking statistics
requirements.text: PRESENTATION_COMBINED MUST expose slide-text and notes counts separately in addition to the combined totals.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Word, character and speaking statistics
requirements.text: Estimated speaking time MUST be calculated from notes WordCount using SpeakerWordsPerMinute.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Word, character and speaking statistics
requirements.text: The user MUST be able to change this value without altering the note text.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Word, character and speaking statistics
requirements.text: Counts MUST update after a committed text edit without requiring a save/reopen cycle and MUST be accessible from normal authoring UI without inserting count text into the presentation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Search, proofing, comments and collaboration
requirements.text: Present MUST provide presentation-wide search and replace across slide text and speaker notes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Search, proofing, comments and collaboration
requirements.text: Every result MUST identify the SlideID, object/notes target and exact text range required to navigate to the match semantically.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Search, proofing, comments and collaboration
requirements.text: Spell-check/proofing MUST operate on slide text and speaker notes and MUST preserve per-range language metadata.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Search, proofing, comments and collaboration
requirements.text: Comments and replies MUST be anchorable to a SlideID, ObjectID and, where supported, a text range.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Search, proofing, comments and collaboration
requirements.text: Realtime collaboration MUST preserve concurrent object, text, notes and comment edits using revision/conflict semantics; naive timestamp last-writer-wins data loss is prohibited.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Search, proofing, comments and collaboration
requirements.text: Presence indicators and remote selections are session UI state and MUST NOT mutate presentation content.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Actions runtime and state model
requirements.text: Present MUST NOT implement an independent legacy animation engine or an independent transition runtime.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Actions runtime and state model
requirements.text: All dynamic, timed, interactive and transition behaviour MUST be represented by a canonical typed Actions graph executed by the shared graph runtime.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Actions runtime and state model
requirements.text: Slides, objects, interactive components, media, code objects, 3D objects and live-drawing surfaces MUST expose versioned typed events.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Actions runtime and state model
requirements.text: Event payloads MUST be schema-validated before graph execution.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Actions runtime and state model
requirements.text: The release event vocabulary MUST include at least:

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Actions runtime and state model
requirements.text: Actions MUST support conditions, branching, sequencing, parallel branches, delays/timers, reusable subgraphs and typed error paths.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Actions runtime and state model
requirements.text: Actions MUST address targets by stable semantic IDs and MUST NOT simulate mouse/keyboard input when a typed capability exists.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Actions runtime and state model
requirements.text: Graph execution MUST be deterministic for the same graph revision, initial local state and deterministic inputs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Actions runtime and state model
requirements.text: When multiple nodes become runnable simultaneously, ordering MUST be defined by explicit dependencies/priority and a stable NodeID tie-breaker.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Actions runtime and state model
requirements.text: Every event cascade MUST have a finite execution budget and loop detection.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Actions runtime and state model
requirements.text: Exceeding the budget MUST terminate the affected cascade with a typed runtime error rather than freezing the presentation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Transitions builder
requirements.text: The Transitions sidebar MUST remain available as a simple authoring surface, but it is a specialised Actions-graph editor.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Transitions builder
requirements.text: It MUST NOT invoke a second transition engine.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Transitions builder
requirements.text: Choosing or editing a transition MUST create/update a marked Actions subgraph owned by that transition definition.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Transitions builder
requirements.text: The sidebar MUST expose Open in Actions to reveal the exact generated subgraph.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Transitions builder
requirements.text: Simple-editor changes MUST modify only nodes owned by the transition definition and MUST preserve user-authored extension nodes connected outside that owned region.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Transitions builder
requirements.text: If an advanced graph edit makes the transition no longer representable by the simple sidebar, the sidebar MUST show a Custom/Advanced state rather than deleting or approximating the graph.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Transitions builder
requirements.text: Slide navigation MUST commit exactly once per NavigationRequestID.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Interactive and reusable components
requirements.text: Present MUST ship first-class accessible Button, Switch, Text Input, Dropdown, Slider and Flashcard component types.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Interactive and reusable components
requirements.text: Components MUST expose typed properties, state, focus/keyboard semantics, accessibility role/name/value and versioned events.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Interactive and reusable components
requirements.text: Built-in hover, focus, pressed and value behaviour MUST work without requiring an author to construct a graph.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Interactive and reusable components
requirements.text: The same primitives MUST be exposed to authors through Actions; built-in components MUST NOT depend on a hidden private animation system.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Interactive and reusable components
requirements.text: Users MUST be able to convert selected objects/components into a reusable Component Type.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Interactive and reusable components
requirements.text: An instance MUST retain ComponentInstanceID, ComponentTypeID, ComponentDefinitionRevision, property overrides and instance state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Interactive and reusable components
requirements.text: Linked instances MAY receive compatible definition updates only through an explicit update policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Interactive and reusable components
requirements.text: Detached/local copies MUST NOT receive future definition updates.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Interactive and reusable components
requirements.text: An incompatible component-definition update MUST NOT silently rewrite or invalidate an existing instance; it MUST require migration or retain the older definition revision.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Interactive and reusable components
requirements.text: Reusable component types MUST be storable in the user's/workspace component library.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Generative UI
requirements.text: Present's Insert surface MUST include Generative UI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Generative UI
requirements.text: The user may insert an existing generated UI artifact or request a new generated interactive surface through Dulche.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Generative UI
requirements.text: Generated UI MUST execute in the approved shared CUI/Generative UI runtime.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Generative UI
requirements.text: Generated UI events MUST be connectable to the presentation Actions graph.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Generative UI
requirements.text: A generated UI object MAY be saved as a reusable Component Type only when its visual, state, event and action schemas use ComponentType-supported constructs and pass component validation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Generative UI
requirements.text: Write, Present, Boards and Canvas MUST use the same canonical Generative UI representation rather than app-specific incompatible formats.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Runnable code, media, 3D and live ink
requirements.text: A runnable-code object MUST store source, registered language/runtime ID, declared inputs, typed outputs, permissions and execution limits.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Runnable code, media, 3D and live ink
requirements.text: Execution MUST occur in a sandbox.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Runnable code, media, 3D and live ink
requirements.text: Filesystem, network, account and device access are denied by default and may be granted only through declared platform capabilities.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Runnable code, media, 3D and live ink
requirements.text: CPU/time, memory and output limits MUST be enforced by the selected runtime provider.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Runnable code, media, 3D and live ink
requirements.text: Limit violations MUST return typed errors.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Runnable code, media, 3D and live ink
requirements.text: Code results/events MUST be consumable by Actions and MAY update authorised presentation objects through typed APIs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Runnable code, media, 3D and live ink
requirements.text: Media objects MUST expose Play, Pause, Stop, Seek, SetVolume and SetPlaybackRate.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Runnable code, media, 3D and live ink
requirements.text: Media events MUST include Started, Paused, PositionChanged, Ended and Error.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Runnable code, media, 3D and live ink
requirements.text: Missing, offline or unsupported media MUST produce an explicit media error state; silent broken placeholders are prohibited.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Runnable code, media, 3D and live ink
requirements.text: The initial supported interchange formats MUST include glTF and GLB.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Runnable code, media, 3D and live ink
requirements.text: 3D objects MUST support transform, camera/orbit controls, camera presets, lighting/environment, material rendering, hotspots and Actions integration.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Runnable code, media, 3D and live ink
requirements.text: Model-intrinsic animation/timeline playback MUST be controlled through typed 3D Actions; it MUST NOT create a legacy presentation-animation subsystem.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Runnable code, media, 3D and live ink
requirements.text: Present MUST use the shared Rnote-derived structured drawing/ink model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Runnable code, media, 3D and live ink
requirements.text: DrawingChanged MUST be available to Actions and, when authorised, Dulche.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Slideshow runtime and Presenter View
requirements.text: Present MUST support full-screen and windowed slideshow playback and presenter/audience display selection when multiple display targets are available.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Slideshow runtime and Presenter View
requirements.text: Presenter View MUST display current slide, next slide, speaker notes, slide navigator, elapsed timer, clock and presentation controls.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Slideshow runtime and Presenter View
requirements.text: Speaker notes, timers, controls, diagnostics and presenter-only overlays MUST NOT enter AudienceOutput unless the user explicitly selects a presenter-view recording/export mode.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Slideshow runtime and Presenter View
requirements.text: The runtime MUST support keyboard navigation, slide jumping, hidden-slide rules, black/white blank screen, presenter pointer/laser, permitted live ink, live captions/subtitles where configured and interactive components/Actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Slideshow runtime and Presenter View
requirements.text: Reduced-motion preference MUST be exposed to the Actions runtime.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Slideshow runtime and Presenter View
requirements.text: Motion-heavy Actions MUST provide a defined reduced-motion result rather than ignoring the preference.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Slideshow runtime and Presenter View
requirements.text: Presenter notes MUST support presenter-side text sizing and auto-scroll/teleprompter behaviour without mutating stored note content.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Slideshow runtime and Presenter View
requirements.text: A presentation session MUST execute against a defined SourceRevisionID.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Slideshow runtime and Presenter View
requirements.text: If the document changes during a live session, the runtime MUST either remain pinned to SourceRevisionID or apply an explicit safe live-update policy; it MUST NOT mix arbitrary object revisions silently.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Rehearsal, timings and recording
requirements.text: Present MUST support rehearsal of timings and structured session recording.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Rehearsal, timings and recording
requirements.text: Rehearsal MUST record navigation and Action-path timing without converting the authored presentation into a fixed linear deck.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Rehearsal, timings and recording
requirements.text: Recording MAY capture narration, camera, pointer/ink and the actual executed Action path subject to device permissions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Rehearsal, timings and recording
requirements.text: A recorded session MUST retain RouteHistory and timing data sufficient to replay or export the recorded route.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Rehearsal, timings and recording
requirements.text: Replacing an existing recording MUST be reviewable and undoable; destructive replacement without a recoverable prior revision is prohibited.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > AI-aware authoring and live presentation
requirements.text: The persistent AI bar MUST receive permission-filtered semantic context for all authorised slides, off-screen objects, speaker notes, Actions graphs, component definitions/state, media metadata, runnable code metadata, 3D objects, drawings and current presentation-session state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > AI-aware authoring and live presentation
requirements.text: Semantic context MUST be preferred over screenshot/OCR interpretation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > AI-aware authoring and live presentation
requirements.text: Read-only AI mode MAY inspect, explain, summarise, rehearse and propose changes, but MUST NOT mutate the presentation or live runtime state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > AI-aware authoring and live presentation
requirements.text: Write AI mode MAY create/edit slides, notes, objects, components and Actions only through typed Present APIs and the normal permission, revision, undo and conflict semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > AI-aware authoring and live presentation
requirements.text: Requests such as branching on an audience answer, converting objects into a flashcard component or highlighting diagram regions on click MUST produce canonical typed graph/component mutations rather than UI automation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > AI-aware authoring and live presentation
requirements.text: AI-generated edits MUST be attributable to a revision/audit event and MUST be reversible through the normal revision/undo model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Video, audio, podcast, print and static export
requirements.text: Present MUST generate Video, Audio and Podcast outputs from the canonical presentation model rather than from a detached textual summary.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Video, audio, podcast, print and static export
requirements.text: Video rendering MUST execute the actual presentation runtime and timed Actions for a selected route.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Video, audio, podcast, print and static export
requirements.text: Audio output MUST use presentation content and speaker/narration configuration without rendering slide visuals.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Video, audio, podcast, print and static export
requirements.text: Podcast output MUST transform presentation content into a conversational treatment using selected Dulche Voice models/voices.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Video, audio, podcast, print and static export
requirements.text: Generated narration/script and timeline MUST be previewable and editable before final rendering.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Video, audio, podcast, print and static export
requirements.text: An interactive presentation may have multiple valid routes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Video, audio, podcast, print and static export
requirements.text: Export MUST require one of RECORDED_SESSION, DEFAULT_ACTION_PATH or EXPLICIT_BRANCH_PATH.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Video, audio, podcast, print and static export
requirements.text: Present MUST NOT guess arbitrary button/quiz choices.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Video, audio, podcast, print and static export
requirements.text: Static output MUST support full slides, selected slides, notes pages, outline text and configurable handout layouts with multiple slides per page where the target supports them.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Video, audio, podcast, print and static export
requirements.text: PDF/image export MUST expose slide range, hidden-slide inclusion, background/transparency handling and notes inclusion.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Video, audio, podcast, print and static export
requirements.text: Page size, orientation, margins and scaling MUST be explicit and previewable for print/handout output.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Import/export compatibility contract
requirements.text: Import/export MUST produce an explicit CompatibilityReport whenever a source or destination format cannot represent the complete native model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Import/export compatibility contract
requirements.text: Compatibility severity semantics: INFO means the construct is translated without user-visible semantic loss; export/import may continue without acknowledgement.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Import/export compatibility contract
requirements.text: WARNING means the construct is degraded or omitted but the operation can still produce a usable artifact; the issue MUST identify the exact affected source/target and resulting behaviour.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Import/export compatibility contract
requirements.text: ERROR means continuing would violate the selected export/import policy, produce an invalid artifact or cause unaccepted destructive loss; the operation MUST block until the user changes the policy, removes the blocking feature or chooses a supported target.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Import/export compatibility contract
requirements.text: PPTX/ODP legacy transitions and animations MUST be translated into Actions graphs when representable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Import/export compatibility contract
requirements.text: Present MUST NOT retain a hidden executable legacy animation engine solely for compatibility.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Import/export compatibility contract
requirements.text: Unsupported or partially translated import behaviour MUST be listed in the CompatibilityReport.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Import/export compatibility contract
requirements.text: PPTX/ODP export MUST compile the representable Actions subset into destination-native constructs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Import/export compatibility contract
requirements.text: Custom components, arbitrary stateful branching, runnable code, Generative UI, AI behaviours and richer interactive 3D logic that cannot be represented MUST be reported explicitly; silent disappearance is prohibited.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Import/export compatibility contract
requirements.text: Import/export validation MUST cover slides, masters/layouts, text, speaker notes, media, supported charts/tables, links, accessibility metadata and representable Actions. .9to1p is the authoritative full-fidelity format.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Accessibility
requirements.text: Present MUST expose accessible semantics in both authoring and presentation runtimes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Accessibility
requirements.text: Relevant visual objects MUST support alt text/description.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Accessibility
requirements.text: Slides MUST have an explicit reading order; interactive content MUST have an explicit focus order when reading order is insufficient.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Accessibility
requirements.text: Interactive components MUST expose accessible role, name, state/value and keyboard interaction.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Accessibility
requirements.text: Authoring and presenting MUST be operable without a pointer for required workflows.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Accessibility
requirements.text: Focus MUST be visible; required state MUST NOT be communicated only by colour.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Accessibility
requirements.text: Zoom/text scaling and reduced-motion behaviour MUST be supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Accessibility
requirements.text: An accessibility checker MUST identify at least missing required alt text, problematic reading/focus order and inaccessible interactive controls.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Accessibility
requirements.text: Accessibility metadata MUST round-trip through .9to1p and MUST be preserved in PPTX/ODP when the destination construct can represent it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Security, permissions and external side effects
requirements.text: Present Actions, generated UI, runnable code, media, participant input and AI integrations MUST obey the platform permission broker and risk classification.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Security, permissions and external side effects
requirements.text: A presentation MUST NOT gain arbitrary filesystem, network, account or device control merely because it is opened or presented.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Security, permissions and external side effects
requirements.text: Viewer interaction MUST NOT grant permissions that the presenting user/session does not already possess.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Security, permissions and external side effects
requirements.text: External side effects invoked from a slideshow MUST use the same confirmation, idempotency, audit and typed-error rules as the equivalent app/Automation action.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Security, permissions and external side effects
requirements.text: A denied permission MUST produce an explicit denied/error result that Actions can handle; the runtime MUST NOT silently substitute a weaker or different side effect.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Security, permissions and external side effects
requirements.text: Presentation content from untrusted sources MUST NOT be able to modify Home permissions or disable sandbox restrictions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Typed Present API and mutation semantics
requirements.text: Present MUST expose versioned typed APIs sufficient for Spaces, Automations, Dulche and other authorised apps to inspect and mutate presentation state without UI simulation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Typed Present API and mutation semantics
requirements.text: Mutation operations MUST reject a stale incompatible BaseRevisionID with REVISION_CONFLICT rather than silently overwriting newer edits.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Typed Present API and mutation semantics
requirements.text: OperationID MUST support idempotent retry for operations declared retry-safe.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Typed Present API and mutation semantics
requirements.text: Typed errors MUST distinguish at least NOT_FOUND, INVALID_ARGUMENT, PERMISSION_DENIED, REVISION_CONFLICT, UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE, RUNTIME_ERROR and CANCELLED.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Typed Present API and mutation semantics
requirements.text: APIs MUST NOT collapse these states into a generic success=false result with no machine-readable reason.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Release acceptance criteria
requirements.text: The release validation suite MUST demonstrate, at minimum:

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Release acceptance criteria
requirements.text: All required built-in interactive components and one reusable custom Component Type with revisioned linked instances.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > Release acceptance criteria
requirements.text: Any acceptance case that fails by silently omitting data, silently degrading behaviour, bypassing typed APIs or exposing presenter-only/private state to the audience MUST block release conformance.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > A. PRESENT HEADER, WORKSPACE AND DIRECT EDITING UI
requirements.text: The normal Present editor MUST show (1) a compact document/application header with Home navigation, Present identity, editable document name, truthful save/autosave state (including unsaved, saving, saved and error/conflict), appropriate history/comments/collaboration controls when available and a prominent Present action; (2) a conventional compact menu row with File, Edit, Insert, Slide, Arrange, View and Help, each opening a real usable dropdown; (3) exactly ONE persistent primary editing toolbar below the menus.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > A. PRESENT HEADER, WORKSPACE AND DIRECT EDITING UI
requirements.text: These three rows form one coherent shell but the menu row MUST remain ABOVE the toolbar.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > A. PRESENT HEADER, WORKSPACE AND DIRECT EDITING UI
requirements.text: Document identity and save state form a deliberately aligned cohesive group; header controls and top-right Save/History/Present MUST share predictable vertical alignment and spacing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > A. PRESENT HEADER, WORKSPACE AND DIRECT EDITING UI
requirements.text: The toolbar MUST look like a single softly rounded floating CUI surface, separated subtly from the workspace with consistent margins/surface elevation; it MUST be predominantly icon-led, with modestly generous spacing, optically centred consistent icon hit areas, logical grouped separators, accessible names, shortcuts/tooltips and visible hover/focus/pressed/selected/disabled states.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > A. PRESENT HEADER, WORKSPACE AND DIRECT EDITING UI
requirements.text: It MUST contain a substantial, useful set of daily commands rather than a sparse six-button strip.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > A. PRESENT HEADER, WORKSPACE AND DIRECT EDITING UI
requirements.text: Responsive width changes MUST use priority-based overflow instead of wrapping another toolbar row or clipping icons.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > A. PRESENT HEADER, WORKSPACE AND DIRECT EDITING UI
requirements.text: Major commands MUST remain accessible in menus/shortcuts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > A. PRESENT HEADER, WORKSPACE AND DIRECT EDITING UI
requirements.text: Common formatting operations MUST be directly usable from the toolbar and/or contextual command surfaces without repeatedly opening or scrolling an inspector.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > A. PRESENT HEADER, WORKSPACE AND DIRECT EDITING UI
requirements.text: The optional resizable Properties inspector is for precise position/size/rotation, detailed typography, shape fill/stroke, image/crop options, slide settings and advanced configuration.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > A. PRESENT HEADER, WORKSPACE AND DIRECT EDITING UI
requirements.text: Its sections MUST be logically grouped/collapsible as useful, with readable fields, appropriate labels, controlled scrolling and no arbitrary unrelated command dump (for example Import/Export/Present MUST NOT be inspector-only miscellany).

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > A. PRESENT HEADER, WORKSPACE AND DIRECT EDITING UI
requirements.text: The toolbar, inspector, context menu and keyboard shortcuts MUST be views of ONE authoritative canonical object/document state; changes must immediately synchronise and support logical undo.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > A. PRESENT HEADER, WORKSPACE AND DIRECT EDITING UI
requirements.text: Routine changes such as fill colour SHOULD preview/apply directly instead of requiring a redundant Apply button.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > A. PRESENT HEADER, WORKSPACE AND DIRECT EDITING UI
requirements.text: Popovers may use explicit Apply only when an actual staged operation justifies it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > A. PRESENT HEADER, WORKSPACE AND DIRECT EDITING UI
requirements.text: A prominent + control MUST open a fully working, categorised Insert menu; the menu bar's Insert menu exposes the same domain actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > A. PRESENT HEADER, WORKSPACE AND DIRECT EDITING UI
