requirements.text: Selecting Shapes MUST open a proper icon/preview gallery (e.g. rectangles, rounded rectangles, ellipses, polygons, lines, arrows, callouts, flowchart forms and other applicable donor-supported shapes); never insert a single default rectangle merely by opening Shapes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > A. PRESENT HEADER, WORKSPACE AND DIRECT EDITING UI
requirements.text: Selecting a shape MUST activate predictable draw-to-insert or explicit click-to-insert behaviour, with live preview, correct post-insertion selection and Escape cancellation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > A. PRESENT HEADER, WORKSPACE AND DIRECT EDITING UI
requirements.text: Visible actions MUST have real implementations or clearly truthful unavailable/capability states; no dead illustrative buttons.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > A. PRESENT HEADER, WORKSPACE AND DIRECT EDITING UI
requirements.text: Keep the slide thumbnail/navigator on the left, the actual central 16:9 or document-aspect slide canvas visually dominant, optional contextual inspector on the right and collapsible/resizable speaker notes below.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > A. PRESENT HEADER, WORKSPACE AND DIRECT EDITING UI
requirements.text: Thumbnails MUST use consistent mildly rounded corners, accurate previews, clear but restrained selected states, clean slide number/title spacing, readable truncated long labels and reliable thumbnail scrolling.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > A. PRESENT HEADER, WORKSPACE AND DIRECT EDITING UI
requirements.text: Pane sizes and slide centring MUST respond to window, sidebar/inspector and notes changes without distorting the slide.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > A. PRESENT HEADER, WORKSPACE AND DIRECT EDITING UI
requirements.text: Each selected slide's existing notes MUST appear immediately from the canonical NotesID/SlideID mapping in a real editable speaker-notes surface; 'Add Notes' or equivalent is an empty-state placeholder ONLY when content is empty.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > A. PRESENT HEADER, WORKSPACE AND DIRECT EDITING UI
requirements.text: Notes MUST not be replaced by a decorative card or lose state during navigation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: The engine MUST distinguish each persistent slide ObjectID (e.g. text-box parent object, shape, image), its actual editable/rendered child content, and transient interaction adorners/selection overlay.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: Text content MUST be edited as the content of its parent text box, not treated as an indistinguishable competing flat object when selected.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: MUST distinguish idle, hover/preselection, selected object, text-editing, moving, resizing, rotating, multi-selection, insertion, panning and zooming.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: Dragging to select text in editing mode MUST NOT move the parent object.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: Dragging the body/border of a selected non-editing object MUST move it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: Clicking empty slide space should clear selection predictably.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: Toolbar/inspector/selection UI MUST track the same state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: Document object events and any runtime Actions events MUST not be confused with authoring gestures.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: Screen/window/viewport/slide/object coordinates and zoom/scroll/rotation transforms MUST be converted consistently, with no arbitrary pixel-offset patches or stale geometry.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: Hovering over a selectable object MUST show an unobtrusive preselection outline before click; a selected object MUST show a stronger accurate bounding outline and resize handles, clearly distinct from hover, without flicker or content mutation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: Handles MUST have usable pointer hit targets, correct directional semantics and cursor feedback.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: Very narrow/tiny objects MUST NOT produce overlapping unusable handles; use an adapted adorner/hit target strategy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: Outlines/handles MUST stay attached to actual selected geometry at all zooms, after transforms and across slide changes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: The selection overlay MUST NOT be stored as slide content.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: Moving, resizing, rotating and applicable object/formatting previews MUST update visibly DURING pointer gestures (not only after release), with accurate content, outlines and property previews.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: MUST handle Shift-click multi-selection, suitable area selection, overlapping objects, group/ungroup, duplication, delete, copy/paste, z-order and keyboard nudging where required by the donor/spec.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: They MUST NOT interrupt, replace, reset, overwrite or silently invalidate one another's in-flight work.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: A true independent reviewer must exercise the exact integrated artifact and apply existing seven APP-AC gates.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: An RCVP CHECKPOINT can be visible while work continues, but MUST NOT be labelled VERIFIED until its entire applicable baseline and the above essential user journeys pass on the real app.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: A working new feature must NOT replace a compliant CUI layout with older Fluent/native design.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: PRESENT-DES-203 — Present MUST show a polished left scrollable rail with accurate actual slide previews, slide number/name metadata, clear understated selected state, clean spacing, truncated long names, reorder and real context actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: Right-click thumbnail > Rename slide must change only Slide.Title metadata, with undo/save/reopen intact, never a genuine editable title object.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: Fit-to-Window computes from measured free viewport after toolbar, left rail, optional right Properties inspector, expanded notes and actual window size.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: Notes may not be blanked by slide switching or replaced with decorative empty-state text when content exists.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: All share the actual canvas zoom state, including fit scale; updating minimum, switching modes, resizing or changing theme must never reset the slider maximum to 100%.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: Ctrl+wheel/pinch, manual zoom and Fit must behave coherently; no old screenshot-as-widget, fake percent or redundant text Fit control.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: Only working AI/comments/history actions may look enabled; partially implemented functions must be truthfully marked unavailable, without sacrificing existing working features.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: Single-click selection, double-click or Enter text editing, body dragging when not editing, escape/cancel, move/resize/rotate, selection clearing and text caret actions MUST follow one deterministic gesture/focus state machine.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: Object dragging must not accidentally select text; text editing must not move the parent.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: Cut, Copy, Paste and keyboard shortcuts must work immediately after dismissal.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: Updates must call canonical editor commands, save state and history.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: Earliest rendered surfaces must respect selected CUI theme rather than flashing a native/Fluent white host.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Present > B. PRESENT POINTER HIERARCHY AND MANIPULATION ENGINE
requirements.text: It must be reachable independently of the developer's PC; obscurity of the hostname is not authentication.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Product role and donor contract
requirements.text: Boards MUST preserve applicable AppFlowy features, quality-of-life behaviours and non-proprietary block types from the selected donor revision unless a scoped donor-parity exception is recorded.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Product role and donor contract
requirements.text: The implementation MUST maintain a donor-parity manifest for Boards identifying the selected AppFlowy revision and classifying each applicable user-visible feature/block as Preserve, Replace with 9to1-native equivalent or Not applicable. “Most AppFlowy features” MUST NOT be interpreted as permission to omit unreviewed donor functionality.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Visual shell
requirements.text: Boards MUST use native CUI and a clean, seamless workspace surface.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Visual shell
requirements.text: Native Board pages MUST NOT render as a paper/card floating inside another background, and MUST NOT add a persistent page border, shadow or sheet frame around the editable content area.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Visual shell
requirements.text: AppFlowy MUST be the primary interaction, block-editing and navigation-layout reference for Boards; OneNote, Notion and Milanote MAY inform complementary notebook, information-organisation and visual-composition conventions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Visual shell
requirements.text: Boards MUST still use its independent 9to1/CUI design language, not clone donor branding or styling.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Visual shell
requirements.text: Editor presentation and identity: The application shell MUST use compact global chrome with coherent Boards > active Board > active Page breadcrumbs and a single prominent, naturally editable Page title.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Visual shell
requirements.text: Board name, Page title, editor placeholder and content heading MUST NOT be redundantly displayed as if they are the same entity (for example repeated "Untitled board" labels).

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Visual shell
requirements.text: The title MUST look like an integrated editor heading rather than a huge full-width grey form field.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Visual shell
requirements.text: Native content MUST begin at a comfortable position below the floating tool island, use a readable central content width without a card frame, and avoid excessive unused vertical or horizontal gaps.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Visual shell
requirements.text: CUI presentation quality: The dark interface MUST establish a clear hierarchy between global app chrome, quieter sidebar, primary editing surface, contextual floating island and bottom AI bar.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Visual shell
requirements.text: Sidebar navigation rows, primary commands and utility actions MUST have different visual weights; replacing a page tree with a stack of equally prominent oversized rectangular buttons is non-conformant.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Visual shell
requirements.text: Buttons, dropdowns, popovers, focus/hover/pressed/disabled states and pointer cursors MUST be consistent, aligned and accessible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Visual shell
requirements.text: Icons MUST come from validated coherent assets (not missing-glyph boxes or arbitrary placeholder symbols).

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Landing page
requirements.text: Boards MUST implement the global launch-screen contract.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Landing page
requirements.text: The default landing view MUST expose Boards plus a Recent pages/components view.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Landing page
requirements.text: Templates and other discovery/idea surfaces MAY be added only when backed by real persisted/template data.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Landing page
requirements.text: The landing page MUST NOT fabricate recent/sample boards except explicitly labelled onboarding/template content.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Landing page
requirements.text: Rare utility actions (manual refresh, low-level storage/capability diagnostics and similar) MUST NOT compete visually with primary create/open/navigation actions; locate them contextually.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Sidebar and board switching
requirements.text: The Boards sidebar MUST show the currently selected Board as a dedicated board switcher control above that Board’s page tree.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Sidebar and board switching
requirements.text: The sidebar page tree is scoped to ActiveBoardID and MUST support nested pages/subpages, selection, add page, rename, reorder/move and delete/recover according to the user’s permissions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Sidebar and board switching
requirements.text: Switching Board changes the page tree atomically to the selected Board and MUST NOT mix pages from multiple Boards in the active hierarchy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Sidebar and board switching
requirements.text: Board/Page identity MUST remain stable across rename, reorder and sidebar position changes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Sidebar and board switching
requirements.text: Sidebar presentation and navigation: The Board switcher MUST occupy a distinct header area above a compact, legible nested Page tree.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Sidebar and board switching
requirements.text: The tree MUST visually distinguish selected Page, parent/child nesting, disclosure state and available contextual actions, with hover/focus-accessible add-page, rename, move/reorder, duplicate, Trash and recovery workflows wherever supported by the applicable permissions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Sidebar and board switching
requirements.text: Single-click page activation, deliberate rename affordances, deterministic drag/drop targets and keyboard alternatives MUST avoid accidental navigation or text edits.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Sidebar and board switching
requirements.text: The sidebar MUST scroll independently where appropriate, support a useful narrow-window/collapsed state, and never render page management as a flat wall of large generic buttons.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Sidebar and board switching
requirements.text: Board/Page hierarchy presentation MUST update atomically on a Board switch: sidebar page tree, breadcrumb, Page title, active editor content, style/selection context and AI context MUST reflect the newly active Board/Page.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Sidebar and board switching
requirements.text: Page title or icon changes MUST update visible navigation without changing stable identity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Canonical Board and Page model
requirements.text: Board MUST contain at least BoardID, Name, Icon?, CreatedAt, ModifiedAt, owner/scope, ordered RootPageIDs, settings and revision metadata.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Canonical Board and Page model
requirements.text: BoardID is stable and MUST NOT derive from the Board name or Files path.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Canonical Board and Page model
requirements.text: BoardPage MUST contain at least PageID, BoardID, ParentPageID?, PageType, Title, Icon?, SortKey, CreatedAt, ModifiedAt, permission metadata, revision and the type-specific content/reference payload.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Canonical Board and Page model
requirements.text: In the release-candidate scope, PageType MUST support Native, Write, Canvas, Chat and ScopedChat.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Canonical Board and Page model
requirements.text: Native Board pages MUST store a versioned BlockTree, page-level DrawingLayer, layout settings and view settings.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: Boards MUST use Home’s Shared Productivity Engine.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: A table, code block, graph, image, drawing or other shared object copied between supported surfaces MUST retain its shared representation rather than being rebuilt as a Boards-only object.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Shared Productivity Engine
requirements.text: Boards MAY add Boards-specific container/layout metadata around a shared object, but MUST NOT fork the shared object payload itself.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Edit and View modes
requirements.text: Every Board page surface MUST expose a persistent Edit/View switch in the top-right app/page chrome.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Edit and View modes
requirements.text: View mode MAY unlock runtime interactions that are intentionally non-authoring.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Edit and View modes
requirements.text: Such interaction state is session-local by default and MUST NOT modify the stored document or default graph configuration unless an explicit authorised save action is invoked in Edit mode.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Edit and View modes
requirements.text: In View mode it is read-only with respect to Board/page content; an AI-requested mutation MUST require an authorised transition/action under Edit semantics rather than silently bypassing View mode.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Locked and Unlocked layout modes
requirements.text: Native Board pages MUST support a separate LayoutMode with values Locked and Unlocked.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Locked and Unlocked layout modes
requirements.text: Switching from Unlocked back to Locked MUST NOT snap, reflow, discard or convert Absolute blocks.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Locked and Unlocked layout modes
requirements.text: Unlocked drag/drop MAY convert a Flow block to Absolute only through an explicit spatial placement gesture.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Locked and Unlocked layout modes
requirements.text: Converting an Absolute block back to Flow MUST be an explicit action because it changes document layout semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Free drawing and ink
requirements.text: Native Board pages MUST support free drawing directly over the page canvas using the Home Shared Productivity Engine’s Rnote-derived drawing/ink implementation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Free drawing and ink
requirements.text: Ink is stored in the page DrawingLayer using stable stroke/object IDs and MUST remain editable after save/restart.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Free drawing and ink
requirements.text: Drawing MUST work in both Locked and Unlocked layout modes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Free drawing and ink
requirements.text: Layout locking MUST NOT disable pen/eraser/ink editing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Free drawing and ink
requirements.text: View mode remains non-authoring and therefore MUST NOT create/erase strokes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Free drawing and ink
requirements.text: Drawing coordinates MUST remain anchored to the page/canvas coordinate system so strokes do not drift when surrounding Flow blocks are edited.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Free drawing and ink
requirements.text: Where ink is attached/anchored to a specific object, that relationship MUST be explicit in the drawing object rather than inferred from screen pixels.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Floating contextual formatting island
requirements.text: Boards MUST expose a persistent floating contextual tool island near the top of the content surface while in Edit mode.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Floating contextual formatting island
requirements.text: Common authoring/formatting controls MUST be directly reachable from this island rather than requiring the block insertion (+) menu.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Floating contextual formatting island
requirements.text: When no editable object is selected, the island MAY show page-level/default insertion/layout controls.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Floating contextual formatting island
requirements.text: The + menu remains an insertion/discovery surface; it MUST NOT be the sole location for routine formatting of the currently selected content.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Floating contextual formatting island
requirements.text: In drawing mode the island MUST expose the active Rnote-derived pen/eraser/ink controls.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Floating contextual formatting island
requirements.text: Text-mode tool island composition: The always-accessible floating island MUST include a current text/block-type dropdown whose label reflects the caret/selected block (Paragraph, Heading 1–6 or a selected named custom paragraph/header style).

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Floating contextual formatting island
requirements.text: It MUST expose the prominently grouped emphasis controls B (Bold), I (Italic), S (Strikethrough) and U (Underline), plus practical list/checklist, link, relevant text colour/highlight/alignment and paragraph actions, Undo/Redo and an obvious + Insert command according to the applicable donor/shared-engine capabilities.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Floating contextual formatting island
requirements.text: Text selection and conversion semantics: Clicking or caret-navigating between Paragraph/H1/H2/H3/H4/H5/H6 and custom-style blocks MUST update the displayed text type immediately.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Floating contextual formatting island
requirements.text: Choosing a type MUST genuinely convert the selected eligible block(s), preserving text content, valid inline marks, shared-engine semantics, history and persistence.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Floating contextual formatting island
requirements.text: The B/I/S/U states MUST accurately reflect selection/caret formatting, including mixed selections; applying formatting MUST affect only intended selected text or eligible ranges.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Floating contextual formatting island
requirements.text: Using the island MUST NOT unexpectedly collapse, lose or redirect the editing selection.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Floating contextual formatting island
requirements.text: Focus restoration, keyboard shortcuts, toggle-off, valid disabled/unavailable states and undo/redo MUST be functional and testable, including after scrolling.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Floating contextual formatting island
requirements.text: Island positioning and accessibility: The island MUST remain visually floating and available during Edit-mode scrolling without obscuring the caret or document content, creating unpredictable layout shifts or jumping on selection changes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Persistent AI bar
requirements.text: Boards MUST implement the global persistent bottom AI bar.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Persistent AI bar
requirements.text: Its semantic context MUST include the active Board, active Page, selected block/object IDs, Edit/View state, LayoutMode and the user-authorised Board/Den context relevant to the request.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Persistent AI bar
requirements.text: AI mutations MUST use 9to1.Boards.* or the owning embedded artifact APIs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Persistent AI bar
requirements.text: Proprietary AppFlowy AI actions MUST NOT be invoked or emulated through hidden donor services.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Block system and AppFlowy block parity
requirements.text: Boards MUST include every non-proprietary-AI AppFlowy block type available in the selected legally usable donor revision, with its applicable editing behaviour and quality-of-life interactions, unless the donor-parity manifest records a concrete exception.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Block system and AppFlowy block parity
requirements.text: The implementation MUST NOT maintain a manually shortened hard-coded parity list that silently falls behind the selected donor source.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Block system and AppFlowy block parity
requirements.text: Boards additionally MUST support built-in Heading 4, Heading 5 and Heading 6 block/text styles, in addition to the donor-compatible heading levels, and MUST support user-defined named header and paragraph styles.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Block system and AppFlowy block parity
requirements.text: Custom styles MUST be stored as versioned style definitions referenced by stable StyleID so renaming a style does not detach existing blocks.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Block system and AppFlowy block parity
requirements.text: A custom text style definition MUST be capable of specifying the applicable shared text properties including font family/reference, size, weight, emphasis, foreground/background/highlight, paragraph spacing, line spacing, alignment and other supported shared-engine text attributes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Block system and AppFlowy block parity
requirements.text: Unsupported properties MUST be preserved during cross-app round-tripping.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Block system and AppFlowy block parity
requirements.text: New shared object/block types registered in Home’s Shared Productivity Engine MUST become available to Boards through the common registry whenever Boards declares support for that type.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Block system and AppFlowy block parity
requirements.text: Boards-specific wrappers MAY supply page/layout controls, but duplicate object engines are non-conformant.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Block system and AppFlowy block parity
requirements.text: Inline block controls and direct manipulation: Boards MUST retain an inline + add-block affordance AND an inline six-dot/:: block grip, in addition to the persistent floating top toolbar.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Block system and AppFlowy block parity
requirements.text: The inline controls MUST be discoverable on block hover/focus with keyboard-accessible equivalents and adequate target size.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Block system and AppFlowy block parity
requirements.text: Editor gesture boundaries and keyboard behaviour: Text editing, caret movement, selection, block selection, drag/reorder, absolute positioning and resizing MUST remain distinguishable; editing or selecting text must not accidentally move a block, and ordinary clicking a grip must not start an unintentional drag.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Block system and AppFlowy block parity
requirements.text: Insert menus MUST cover applicable registered/donor-parity blocks rather than a shortened hard-coded demonstration list, and MUST support good search/category discovery, outside-click/Escape dismissal, keyboard focus and valid screen-edge placement.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Graph block
requirements.text: Boards MUST provide a shared-engine Graph block for mathematical/analytical graphing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Graph block
requirements.text: A Graph block MUST support multiple simultaneous expressions/series, independently styled plots, points/markers, labelled axes, configurable viewport/domain/range and shaded regions/inequalities.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Graph block
requirements.text: GraphBlock data MUST include stable GraphID, ordered plot/expression definitions, variables, optional slider definitions, viewport/axes settings and style metadata.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Graph block
requirements.text: Multiple expressions MUST coexist in one graph without being flattened into a rendered image.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Graph block
requirements.text: A slider definition MUST include VariableID/name, minimum, maximum, step and default value.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Graph block
requirements.text: In View mode viewers MAY manipulate enabled sliders; temporary slider values are per-view session unless explicitly saved as new defaults by an authorised Edit action.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Graph block
requirements.text: Graph blocks MUST support shared-engine copy/paste and remain editable after transfer to another participating surface that declares Graph support.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Enhanced image formatting
requirements.text: Image objects in Boards MUST support, at minimum, resize with aspect-ratio control, crop, rotate, fit/fill behaviour, alignment/positioning, caption, alt text/accessibility description and link/reference metadata.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Enhanced image formatting
requirements.text: Non-destructive image transforms MUST preserve the source asset until the user explicitly exports/rasterises a transformed copy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Enhanced table formatting
requirements.text: Table objects MUST support add/remove/reorder rows and columns, row/column resize, merge/split where structurally valid, horizontal/vertical cell alignment, text formatting, cell background/fill, borders, header row/column styling and table width/alignment controls.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Enhanced table formatting
requirements.text: Formatting MUST remain separate from the cell data/value payload so copy/paste and automation can manipulate either deterministically.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Cross-app parity blocks
requirements.text: Boards MUST expose shared-engine blocks/objects that have equivalents in the other productivity surfaces instead of creating incompatible lookalikes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Cross-app parity blocks
requirements.text: App-specific artifacts MAY be embedded as canonical artifact references.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Cross-app parity blocks
requirements.text: An embedded mutable artifact MUST retain its owning app identity/capabilities and MUST NOT be flattened to a screenshot/static copy except through an explicit static export action.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Write and Canvas page types
requirements.text: Add Page MUST offer Write and Canvas as first-class PageType options alongside Native.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Write and Canvas page types
requirements.text: Write/Canvas Board pages MUST use the same Home Shared Productivity Engine and underlying artifact behaviour as the standalone apps, not a visually similar Boards reimplementation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Write and Canvas page types
requirements.text: The Board page is a container/reference to the canonical artifact; edits made inside Boards and edits made through the standalone owning app or Spaces MUST resolve to the same artifact/revision history.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Write and Canvas page types
requirements.text: Opening a Write/Canvas page inside Boards MUST NOT launch a second external app window merely to obtain basic editing behaviour.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Chat page type
requirements.text: It MAY also use the user’s connected apps/integrations and relevant persistent context registered in Dulche Den when the Agent/tool permissions permit those actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Chat page type
requirements.text: Chat MUST use typed 9to1 app/integration actions for consequential work.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Chat page type
requirements.text: Board membership or Chat context MUST NOT grant implicit access to an external app, tool or Den namespace that the caller/Agent is not otherwise authorised to use.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Chat page type
requirements.text: Renaming/moving the page MUST NOT create a new Agent or lose history.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Scoped Chat page type
requirements.text: Its answers MUST be grounded only in the authorised contents of the containing Board plus the explicit source collection attached to that Scoped Chat.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Scoped Chat page type
requirements.text: It MUST NOT search the public web, invoke external-information retrieval tools or consult unrelated connected-app content to fill evidence gaps.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Scoped Chat page type
requirements.text: When the permitted corpus does not contain enough information to support an answer, Scoped Chat MUST report that the available sources do not support the requested point rather than silently answering from general model knowledge.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Scoped Chat page type
requirements.text: Scoped Chat responses MUST expose source provenance at the Board page/source-object level so the user can navigate back to the material supporting the response.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Chat source subpages
requirements.text: Chat and Scoped Chat MUST support additional source subpages beneath the Chat page.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Chat source subpages
requirements.text: Source ingestion MUST be asynchronous/observable for large files and MUST distinguish Pending, Ready, Failed and Removed states.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Chat source subpages
requirements.text: Failed ingestion MUST NOT make the source appear successfully available to the Agent.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Chat source subpages
requirements.text: Removing/revoking a source prevents future reads while preserving audit/history semantics required by Dulche Den.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Data-backed structured items
requirements.text: Where the AppFlowy donor exposes database-like blocks, records or views, Boards MUST implement the applicable user-facing behaviour by hosting or referencing canonical 9to1 Data artifacts/views through the Shared Productivity Engine and typed Data APIs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Data-backed structured items
requirements.text: A Board item may therefore display and interact with a Data table/range/view while the underlying rows, fields, formulas, permissions and revisions remain owned by Data.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Data-backed structured items
requirements.text: Donor parity still applies to the Boards-facing workflow: applicable filtering, sorting, grouping, view selection, record presentation and related quality-of-life behaviour MUST either map to supported Data capabilities or be recorded as a concrete donor-parity exception.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Data-backed structured items
requirements.text: Boards MUST NOT silently fork Data state into an incompatible local database merely to imitate donor UI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Board document-space coordinates
requirements.text: Persisted Native-page spatial placement MUST use Board document-space coordinates, not CUI's -1000…1000 proportional screen coordinate system.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Board document-space coordinates
requirements.text: X, Y, Width and Height MAY be decimal document-space values and MAY extend outside the initial viewport where the page supports panning/free placement.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Board document-space coordinates
requirements.text: Zoom, DPI scaling, window resizing and panning are view transforms only and MUST NOT rewrite persisted Board coordinates.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Embedded artifact ownership and lifecycle
requirements.text: Every mutable embedded/hosted app artifact MUST carry explicit ownership semantics independent from its BoardPage reference.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Embedded artifact ownership and lifecycle
requirements.text: Attaching an existing Write/Canvas/Data/etc. artifact creates a reference and MUST NOT transfer ownership merely because it appears inside Boards.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Embedded artifact ownership and lifecycle
requirements.text: Permanent purge MAY cascade to BoardOwned artifacts only through an explicit destructive operation whose impact preview names the affected artifacts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Embedded artifact ownership and lifecycle
requirements.text: Referenced artifacts MUST NOT be deleted by deleting the Board/page.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Collaboration and concurrency
requirements.text: Boards collaboration MUST resolve concurrent work at the narrowest stable entity possible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Collaboration and concurrency
requirements.text: Independent block/object edits and independent ink strokes SHOULD merge without forcing a whole-page conflict.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Collaboration and concurrency
requirements.text: Page-tree operations MUST use deterministic stable ordering/parent semantics so simultaneous moves/inserts do not silently reorder unrelated pages.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Collaboration and concurrency
requirements.text: Concurrent incompatible edits to the same canonical block/object/artifact MUST surface the owning object's merge/conflict behaviour rather than blind last-write-wins.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Collaboration and concurrency
requirements.text: Presence, remote cursors, selections and transient viewport state are ephemeral collaboration state and MUST NOT be written into canonical Board content.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Collaboration and concurrency
requirements.text: Reconnect/offline replay MUST preserve operation identity so retries cannot duplicate mutations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Platform capability behaviour
requirements.text: Boards MUST ship useful supported native behaviour on Windows and 9to1-OS and a useful web version under the global web-product contract.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Platform capability behaviour
requirements.text: Platform capability differences MUST be explicit and queryable rather than silently dropping features.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Platform capability behaviour
requirements.text: Browser/native differences may include pen pressure/tilt, OS file drag-and-drop, clipboard richness, filesystem access, windowing and availability of specialised embedded surfaces.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Platform capability behaviour
requirements.text: When a capability is unavailable, Boards MUST provide the closest useful supported interaction or a clear unsupported-capability state without corrupting or flattening the underlying artifact.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Performance and resource behaviour
requirements.text: Large Boards MUST use incremental/lazy loading and virtualisation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Performance and resource behaviour
requirements.text: Opening a Board MUST NOT eagerly instantiate every nested page, every off-screen block, every source document or every embedded app surface.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Performance and resource behaviour
requirements.text: Large block lists, Data-backed views and page trees SHOULD virtualise off-screen content while preserving correct selection, search, keyboard navigation and accessibility semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Performance and resource behaviour
requirements.text: Drawing rendering MUST cull/incrementally render off-screen strokes; previews and embedded-surface caches MUST be bounded and revision-invalidated; Board/search/source indexing MUST update incrementally; and expensive embedded artifacts SHOULD hydrate on demand.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Performance and resource behaviour
requirements.text: Performance acceptance MUST include representative large-Board, large-page, drawing-heavy and collaboration scenarios on the declared supported-platform baseline.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Persistence, history and recovery
requirements.text: Board/page/block edits MUST use revisioned, crash-safe persistence through the owning storage layer.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Persistence, history and recovery
requirements.text: A process/app crash MUST NOT corrupt the entire Board because one page/block write was interrupted.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Persistence, history and recovery
requirements.text: Recovery MUST identify the affected Board/Page and restore the latest consistent revision or surface a structured conflict/recovery state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Persistence, history and recovery
requirements.text: Delete semantics for Boards and Pages MUST be recoverable by default unless an explicit permanent-delete/purge action is invoked under the applicable high-risk permission flow.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Persistence, history and recovery
requirements.text: Deleting a Board container MUST NOT silently permanently delete separately owned embedded artifacts without explicit cascade semantics and user-visible impact.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Persistence, history and recovery
requirements.text: Concurrent edits MUST use revision/conflict semantics rather than blind last-write-wins when the same canonical object is changed by multiple clients/Spaces/Automations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Persistence, history and recovery
requirements.text: Visible persistence and startup truthfulness: Autosave/status controls MUST distinguish actual dirty, saving, saved, failed, offline/reconnecting and revision-conflict states; the interface MUST NOT show success while changes are not durably stored.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Persistence, history and recovery
requirements.text: Save status should be subtly integrated with existing page chrome, not an oversized persistent diagnostic/status strip; storage/capabilities diagnostics belong in an appropriate utility surface.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Boards API
requirements.text: Every additional user-visible Boards operation — including donor-parity actions and contextual-island controls — MUST have an equivalent supported API/domain action under the global API-parity rule.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Boards API
requirements.text: APIs MUST use stable IDs, revision checks where required and structured partial/error results.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Permissions and risk
requirements.text: Read, edit, share/admin, external-action and destructive permissions MUST remain distinct.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Permissions and risk
requirements.text: Permanent Board/Page purge, destructive bulk actions, permission/share changes and consequential external actions initiated from Chat/AI MUST use the elevated-risk approval rules defined globally.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Failure behaviour
requirements.text: Boards MUST return structured failures for BoardNotFound, PageNotFound, BlockNotFound, UnsupportedPageType, UnsupportedBlockType, InvalidLayoutTransition, RevisionConflict, PermissionDenied, SourceIngestionFailed, ScopedChatExternalAccessDenied, DependencyUnavailable and SharedEngineIncompatible, plus the global error contract.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Failure behaviour
requirements.text: If Home or the Shared Productivity Engine becomes unavailable after Boards has opened, Boards MUST stop new unsafe mutations, preserve already loaded unsaved state for recovery where possible and surface a repair/reconnect state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Failure behaviour
requirements.text: It MUST NOT silently switch to an incompatible private document engine.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Boards > Acceptance requirements
requirements.text: When Home is absent at process start, Boards refuses normal launch and enters the required Install Home bootstrap flow.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Purpose, ownership and boundaries
requirements.text: Canvas is not a Boards replacement and MUST NOT become a generic workspace/page system.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Purpose, ownership and boundaries
requirements.text: Boards MAY host a live Canvas artifact, but the embedded Canvas remains owned by Canvas and retains its Canvas ArtifactID.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Purpose, ownership and boundaries
requirements.text: Canvas MUST use CUI for the visible application shell, menus, toolbars, inspectors, dialogs, launch screen and ordinary controls.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Purpose, ownership and boundaries
requirements.text: A specialised accelerated drawing/rendering surface MAY exist as a CUI control for performance; .cui markup MUST NOT require each stroke sample to become an independent generic UI widget.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Donor and upstream contract
requirements.text: The implementation agent MUST obtain the latest appropriate stable Rnote source when the Canvas implementation pass begins, record the exact upstream repository, commit/release identifier and licence, and include the selected donor source in the Canvas source tree/build graph in accordance with the global Source & Donor Apps contract.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Donor and upstream contract
requirements.text: Canvas MUST maintain a donor-parity manifest generated from inspection of the selected Rnote revision.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Donor and upstream contract
requirements.text: Every user-visible donor capability MUST be classified as PRESERVE, REPLACE_WITH_9TO1_NATIVE_EQUIVALENT or NOT_APPLICABLE.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Donor and upstream contract
requirements.text: Proprietary donor AI MUST NOT be copied.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Supported platforms and capability negotiation
requirements.text: Canvas MUST ship on every 9to1 platform for which the app is not explicitly exempt under the global platform/web rules.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Supported platforms and capability negotiation
requirements.text: Desktop/native and web implementations MUST share the same Canvas artifact schema, stable identities, domain API semantics and server-side canonical entities.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Supported platforms and capability negotiation
requirements.text: Platform-specific input or rendering capability differences MUST be negotiated explicitly.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Supported platforms and capability negotiation
requirements.text: Hardware capability absence MUST NOT be misrepresented as format incapability.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Supported platforms and capability negotiation
requirements.text: If tilt, barrel buttons, palm rejection assistance or another device capability is unavailable, the UI MUST disable or omit only the dependent control and expose a capability-unavailable reason where the absence is user-relevant.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Supported platforms and capability negotiation
requirements.text: Opening an artifact on a lower-capability platform MUST preserve unsupported stored data for later use on a capable platform.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Canonical artifact model and identity
requirements.text: Persisted Canvas data MUST be schema-versioned.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Canonical artifact model and identity
requirements.text: Readers MUST migrate, preserve or reject incompatible schema versions explicitly and MUST NOT guess the meaning of unknown fields.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Canonical artifact model and identity
requirements.text: ArtifactID, PageID, LayerID, ObjectID and StrokeID MUST remain stable across rename, move, reorder, zoom, pan, style change and save/reopen.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Canonical artifact model and identity
requirements.text: Display names, page positions, z-order and file paths MUST NOT be used as persistent identity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Document mode and page-type model
requirements.text: Canvas MUST support both INFINITE and PAGED document modes as first-class modes selectable through the top-right quick-settings surface.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Document mode and page-type model
requirements.text: INFINITE mode provides a spatially unbounded working area for normal user workflows and MUST NOT expose an artificial page edge as document structure.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Document mode and page-type model
requirements.text: The conversion workflow MUST preview the mapping of existing content, identify content that would cross/clash with generated page boundaries, and require explicit confirmation before committing a conversion that changes layout.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Document mode and page-type model
requirements.text: Conversion MUST be undoable/recoverable through document history and MUST NOT clip, discard or rasterise existing objects silently.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Persistence, autosave and recovery
requirements.text: Canvas persistence MUST be atomic at the smallest user-visible document mutation/revision boundary supported by the storage architecture.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Persistence, autosave and recovery
requirements.text: A partially written resource MUST NOT make the last known-good artifact revision unreadable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Persistence, autosave and recovery
requirements.text: Autosave MUST persist committed document mutations without requiring a manual Save command.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Persistence, autosave and recovery
requirements.text: A save failure MUST surface an explicit unsaved/error state and retain recoverable local work.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Persistence, autosave and recovery
requirements.text: Crash recovery MUST restore the last durable revision and recover newer journaled/temporary operations where available.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Persistence, autosave and recovery
requirements.text: Imported source files MUST NOT be destructively overwritten merely because they were opened.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Persistence, autosave and recovery
requirements.text: Closing an artifact while durable persistence is unresolved MUST provide an explicit recovery choice rather than silently discarding changes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Launch screen and document lifecycle
requirements.text: Canvas MUST implement the global launch-screen contract and LAUNCH-001–006 using real Files/storage state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Launch screen and document lifecycle
requirements.text: Create Blank MUST create a real Canvas artifact with a new ArtifactID and selected/default CanvasMode.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Launch screen and document lifecycle
requirements.text: Launch entries MUST NOT be mock cards.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Launch screen and document lifecycle
requirements.text: Opening, renaming, moving, favouriting, sharing and deleting an entire Canvas artifact MUST integrate with Files' canonical artifact/storage semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Launch screen and document lifecycle
requirements.text: Moving or renaming a file MUST NOT change ArtifactID.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Primary Canvas shell
requirements.text: The normal editing surface MUST prioritise the canvas and MUST NOT permanently reserve a ribbon, large left tool rail or large inspector panel for routine drawing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Primary Canvas shell
requirements.text: Changing DisplayName MUST NOT change ArtifactID.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Primary Canvas shell
requirements.text: The currently selected tool MUST display both its icon and human-readable name.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Primary Canvas shell
requirements.text: Non-selected tools MAY display icon-only in the compact state, but their names and primary shortcut MUST be exposed by hover and keyboard-focus tooltips.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Primary Canvas shell
requirements.text: The toolbar MUST remain usable with mouse, touch, stylus and keyboard navigation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Primary Canvas shell
requirements.text: Responsive compaction MAY use controlled overflow or horizontal scrolling; tools MUST NOT silently disappear.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Contextual tool-options host
requirements.text: When the active tool exposes contextual options, Canvas MUST render one secondary floating options surface immediately above the primary bottom toolbar.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Contextual tool-options host
requirements.text: Tool implementations MUST declare their options through a common option schema rather than constructing unrelated private popup systems.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Contextual tool-options host
requirements.text: Re-selecting the active tool MUST open/focus its deeper option surface when that tool has options.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Contextual tool-options host
requirements.text: A long-press or context menu MAY expose secondary actions, but no required capability may exist only behind long-press.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Select and Pan
requirements.text: It MUST support the applicable Rnote-derived selection modes plus shared-object selection semantics, including single selection, multi-selection and lasso/area selection where supported by the donor/object type.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Select and Pan
requirements.text: Applicable selected content MUST support move, resize, rotate, duplicate, delete/recover, cut/copy/paste, group/ungroup, z-order/layer movement, alignment/distribution where meaningful and lock/unlock.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Select and Pan
requirements.text: An operation unsupported by a selected object type MUST be disabled with a defined capability reason rather than appearing to succeed.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Select and Pan
requirements.text: Pointer/stylus movement while Pan is active MUST navigate the viewport and MUST NOT create or modify drawing content.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Pen system and preset pens
requirements.text: Pen is the primary structured ink-authoring tool and MUST preserve applicable Rnote pen/brush behaviour.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Pen system and preset pens
requirements.text: Canvas MUST ship with useful preset pens derived from the available drawing engines in the selected donor revision.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Pen system and preset pens
requirements.text: Presets MUST cover the major donor-supported writing/drawing instrument classes that remain applicable, such as ordinary ink/ballpoint-style writing, fountain/variable-width ink, pencil and highlighter/marker behaviour where the donor supports them.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Pen system and preset pens
requirements.text: The Pen menu MUST provide a Custom Pen workflow.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Pen system and preset pens
requirements.text: Users MUST be able to create, preview, save, duplicate, rename, reorder, favourite, edit and delete/recover custom pen presets.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Pen system and preset pens
requirements.text: The custom-pen editor MUST expose only properties supported by the selected ToolEngineID.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Pen system and preset pens
requirements.text: Saving a pen preset MUST NOT retroactively alter existing strokes unexpectedly.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Pen system and preset pens
requirements.text: Preset and custom pen selection MUST be keyboard and touch accessible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Eraser
requirements.text: The Eraser tool MUST expose at least two user-facing modes in its contextual options:

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Eraser
requirements.text: Quick Eraser deletion MUST use the same document history/domain delete operation as other Canvas deletion and therefore MUST remain undoable/recoverable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Eraser
requirements.text: The target-resolution rule MUST be deterministic when objects overlap.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Insert catalogue and parity
requirements.text: Its first-level menu MUST use the following category order and each category opens a submenu to the right on desktop:

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Insert catalogue and parity
requirements.text: Selecting/hovering a category MUST NOT insert a default object silently.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Insert catalogue and parity
requirements.text: Heading — text object with a semantic heading role and heading defaults; it MUST NOT be implemented only as visually larger text.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Insert catalogue and parity
requirements.text: Shapes MUST use the same canonical shared shape definitions and editing behaviour used by other 9to1 productivity surfaces rather than a reduced Canvas-only shape model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Insert catalogue and parity
requirements.text: Media objects MUST use the corresponding shared media representation and preserve editable metadata/behaviour rather than flattening to a thumbnail.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Insert catalogue and parity
requirements.text: Canvas MUST expose the shared table creation experience and the full Canvas-applicable shared table feature set.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Insert catalogue and parity
requirements.text: Canvas MUST NOT implement a reduced Canvas-only table type.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Insert catalogue and parity
requirements.text: Graph MUST be available through Other using the canonical shared graph representation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Insert catalogue and parity
requirements.text: Other MAY include Link, File/Artifact, Embed, Equation, Code, Generative UI and additional registered shared types when the shared capability registry declares them Canvas-compatible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Insert catalogue and parity
requirements.text: Drawing MUST NOT appear as a separate Insert item because freeform pen/drawing is already a primary Canvas capability.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Insert catalogue and parity
requirements.text: Catalogue parity — every shared productivity object type declared Canvas-compatible by the shared capability registry MUST be reachable through Insert.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Insert catalogue and parity
requirements.text: Behaviour parity — after insertion, the object MUST retain the shared object's complete applicable behaviour.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Insert catalogue and parity
requirements.text: Canvas MUST NOT replace a shared object with a feature-reduced Canvas-specific approximation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Insert catalogue and parity
requirements.text: The Insert UI MUST be generated from registered insertion capabilities plus the fixed category taxonomy above.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Insert catalogue and parity
requirements.text: Adding a registered shared object MUST NOT require a separate incompatible Canvas object implementation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Insert catalogue and parity
requirements.text: Desktop cascading menus MUST use conventional keyboard behaviour: Up/Down move, Right opens a submenu, Left returns, Enter/Space invokes and Escape closes the current menu level.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Insert catalogue and parity
requirements.text: Touch interaction MUST provide an explicit navigable submenu/back model and MUST NOT depend on hover.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Tools family
requirements.text: The exact list MUST be derived from the selected Rnote donor parity manifest and shared Canvas capabilities rather than an arbitrary hand-written subset.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Tools family
requirements.text: Applicable geometry, line/arrow, ruler/measurement, fill/colour-picker, specialised selection and other donor tools MAY be organised here while retaining their donor behaviour.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Tools family
requirements.text: A tool moved into Tools is not optional merely because it is not a top-level button.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Tools family
requirements.text: A future pin/favourite mechanism MAY allow users to promote specialised tools to the primary toolbar, but the default canonical toolbar remains Select, Pan, Pen, Eraser, Insert, Tools, AI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Top-right quick-settings pill
requirements.text: A compact switch/settings pill MUST appear at the top-right of the Canvas editing surface.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Top-right quick-settings pill
requirements.text: Document-scoped quick settings MUST include:

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Top-right quick-settings pill
requirements.text: Editor/user-scoped quick settings MUST include:

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Top-right quick-settings pill
requirements.text: Document-scoped settings MUST persist with/collaborate through the artifact.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Top-right quick-settings pill
requirements.text: Editor/user-scoped settings MUST persist as user/device preferences unless an individual setting explicitly declares document scope.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Smart Pen
requirements.text: Smart Pen MUST preserve handwriting as structured editable ink.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Smart Pen
requirements.text: Smart Pen MUST NOT silently replace ink with text or discard original authored stroke semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Smart Pen
requirements.text: The adjustment algorithm MAY smooth geometry, regularise locally unstable stroke motion and make other constrained handwriting clean-up changes that preserve the user's intended writing rather than redrawing arbitrary content.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Smart Pen
requirements.text: The resulting adjustment MUST be immediately undoable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Smart Pen
requirements.text: The active undo/history window MUST retain enough pre-adjustment data to restore the user's original committed stroke.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Input, stylus and gesture contract
requirements.text: Canvas MUST preserve applicable high-fidelity stylus information provided by the runtime, including pressure and tilt when available.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Input, stylus and gesture contract
requirements.text: Pen/stylus drawing, touch navigation and mouse/trackpad interaction MUST be distinguishable so ordinary navigation does not create unintended ink.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Input, stylus and gesture contract
requirements.text: Applicable eraser/barrel-button semantics from the selected donor must remain available.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Input, stylus and gesture contract
requirements.text: Palm rejection MUST use platform/donor capabilities where available and MUST fail predictably when hardware/runtime support is absent.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Input, stylus and gesture contract
requirements.text: Pan, zoom and rotate gestures MUST NOT mutate document content unless the active tool/action explicitly maps the gesture to a content mutation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Input, stylus and gesture contract
requirements.text: Stored pressure/tilt data MUST survive save/reopen and lower-capability viewing even if the current device cannot generate equivalent samples.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Layers, ordering and object manipulation
requirements.text: Canvas MUST preserve applicable Rnote layer functionality.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Layers, ordering and object manipulation
requirements.text: Users MUST be able to create, rename, reorder, hide/show, lock/unlock and delete/recover layers where supported by the donor model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Layers, ordering and object manipulation
requirements.text: Hidden/locked layers MUST obey the same selection/edit restrictions through UI and API.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Layers, ordering and object manipulation
requirements.text: Z-order within a layer and layer order are distinct concepts and MUST NOT be conflated by APIs or UI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Shared Productivity Engine and cross-app object semantics
requirements.text: Canvas MUST use Home's Shared Productivity Engine for every shared object type it supports.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Shared Productivity Engine and cross-app object semantics
requirements.text: Shared rich text, shapes, tables, media, graphs, equations, code, Generative UI and other registered shared objects MUST retain their shared schema when copied, embedded or referenced across supporting 9to1 apps.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Shared Productivity Engine and cross-app object semantics
requirements.text: The shared Rnote-derived ink model MUST allow structured ink to remain editable ink in Boards, Present, Write or Spaces where the destination declares ink support.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Shared Productivity Engine and cross-app object semantics
requirements.text: Unsupported destination/object combinations MUST fail explicitly or require an explicit user-selected flatten/export operation; silent rasterisation or semantic loss is prohibited.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Shared Productivity Engine and cross-app object semantics
requirements.text: Clipboard and drag/drop MUST carry a typed multi-representation payload containing stable/source references plus portable shared-object representations as applicable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Shared Productivity Engine and cross-app object semantics
requirements.text: The destination chooses the highest-fidelity compatible representation; it MUST NOT silently choose a lower-fidelity bitmap when a supported structured representation exists.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Files and Boards integration
requirements.text: Boards MUST be able to host a live Canvas artifact/reference.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Files and Boards integration
requirements.text: Opening the same ArtifactID in Canvas and Boards MUST resolve to the same underlying artifact.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Dulche contextual AI
requirements.text: Canvas MUST NOT show a second permanently expanded AI bar while the bottom toolbar is present.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Dulche contextual AI
requirements.text: Selecting a different Canvas tool hides the expanded AI bar but MUST NOT automatically cancel an authorised active AI session.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Dulche contextual AI
requirements.text: If SurfaceVisibility = HIDDEN and Lifecycle is ACTIVE or WAITING_FOR_USER, Canvas MUST show a compact sparkle session indicator immediately beside the top-right quick-settings pill.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Dulche contextual AI
requirements.text: It MUST NOT create a duplicate session.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Dulche contextual AI
requirements.text: If a hidden session completes or fails, the indicator MUST enter a non-intrusive completed/error attention state until inspected/dismissed; it MUST NOT force the AI bar open or steal editing focus.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Dulche contextual AI
requirements.text: Dulche MUST receive permission-filtered semantic Canvas context including the active ArtifactID/PageID, stable object/stroke IDs, spatial relationships, text/shared-object semantics, current selection, document revision, current Canvas tool state where relevant and the Canvas actions allowed by the current AI access mode.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Dulche contextual AI
requirements.text: Read-only mode MAY inspect, search, reason, explain, navigate and propose changes but MUST NOT mutate the artifact or editor state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Dulche contextual AI
requirements.text: Write mode MAY mutate Canvas only through typed Canvas/shared-object actions and the normal revision, permission, undo and conflict model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Dulche contextual AI
requirements.text: A user reference such as 'these four boxes' MUST resolve to stable target IDs at request/execution binding time.
