requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Dulche contextual AI
requirements.text: Later selection changes MUST NOT silently retarget the running operation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Dulche contextual AI
requirements.text: If targeted objects change incompatibly before an AI commit, the operation MUST return a revision/conflict result rather than blindly overwriting newer edits.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Dulche contextual AI
requirements.text: Derived recognition MUST NOT silently replace canonical ink.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Spaces and Automations integration
requirements.text: Spaces MUST be able to open/reference an authorised Canvas artifact and edit it conversationally using 9to1.Canvas typed actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Spaces and Automations integration
requirements.text: Spaces MUST NOT use mouse/keyboard simulation when the equivalent Canvas action exists.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Spaces and Automations integration
requirements.text: Automations MUST receive exhaustive Canvas UI/API parity subject to the same permissions and platform capabilities.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Spaces and Automations integration
requirements.text: Canvas MUST publish typed events for meaningful document changes and MUST NOT flood workflows with raw pointer-move events.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Collaboration and conflict semantics
requirements.text: Canvas collaboration MUST operate on canonical structured document entities rather than exchanging flattened screenshots or whole-document last-write-wins blobs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Collaboration and conflict semantics
requirements.text: Concurrent edits to independent strokes/objects/pages SHOULD merge without destroying unrelated work.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Collaboration and conflict semantics
requirements.text: Conflicting edits to the same canonical entity MUST be detected using revision/operation semantics and resolved deterministically or surfaced as a conflict.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Collaboration and conflict semantics
requirements.text: Naive timestamp last-write-wins MUST NOT be the default conflict strategy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Collaboration and conflict semantics
requirements.text: Remote cursors, selections and transient viewport positions are collaboration presence/session state and MUST NOT alter canonical document content.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Collaboration and conflict semantics
requirements.text: The implementation MAY use CRDTs, operation logs or another maintainable internal algorithm provided the observable collaboration, revision and recovery contract is satisfied.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Undo, redo and history
requirements.text: All ordinary Canvas document mutations initiated by UI, AI, Spaces or Automation MUST enter the same canonical history/revision system unless an operation explicitly declares non-document session state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Undo, redo and history
requirements.text: Undo/redo MUST operate on semantic user-visible operations, not arbitrary internal rendering steps.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Undo, redo and history
requirements.text: AI/API mutations MUST be attributable in history/audit metadata.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Undo, redo and history
requirements.text: Structural mode conversion, bulk manipulation and imported-content insertion MUST be represented as coherent reversible operations or explicit multi-operation transactions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Import and export
requirements.text: Canvas MUST retain all applicable Rnote import/export capabilities from the selected donor revision in addition to 9to1-native integrations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Import and export
requirements.text: Import/export MUST preserve supported structured content and MUST produce an explicit compatibility report when the source or destination cannot represent part of the native Canvas model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Import and export
requirements.text: Unsupported features MUST be classified as translated, degraded, omitted or blocked with the affected entity identified.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Import and export
requirements.text: A successful file creation/open is not sufficient validation; representative round trips MUST compare semantic content.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Accessibility
requirements.text: Canvas MUST make ordinary authoring and document-management workflows operable by keyboard and assistive technology even though the primary document is spatial/visual.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Accessibility
requirements.text: Meaningful Canvas objects MUST be inspectable through an accessible structured object/list view exposing object name/type, authored text, alt description and relevant ordering/spatial relationship information.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Accessibility
requirements.text: Visual objects MUST support alt text/description where appropriate.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Accessibility
requirements.text: Pure freehand ink is not required to become authoritative text automatically.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Accessibility
requirements.text: AI/OCR descriptions MUST remain clearly derived metadata unless the user explicitly adopts/converts them.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Accessibility
requirements.text: Required state MUST NOT be communicated only by colour; focus must be visible; zoom/display scaling and reduced-motion preferences must be respected.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Security and permissions
requirements.text: Canvas MUST declare action risk classifications and MUST NOT bypass Home for protected external or destructive operations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Security and permissions
requirements.text: Opening a Canvas file MUST NOT grant embedded code, Generative UI, media or linked artifacts arbitrary filesystem/network/account access.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Security and permissions
requirements.text: Untrusted imported Canvas content MUST NOT change Home trust grants, security policy or sandbox restrictions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Typed Canvas API
requirements.text: Canvas MUST expose a versioned first-party API namespace with UI parity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Typed Canvas API
requirements.text: Actions that enumerate unbounded collections MUST paginate/stream.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Typed Canvas API
requirements.text: Long-running import/export/render work MUST return JobID, status and cancellation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Typed Canvas API
requirements.text: Retry-safe mutations MUST use OperationID idempotency.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Typed Canvas API
requirements.text: Typed errors MUST distinguish at least NOT_FOUND, INVALID_ARGUMENT, PERMISSION_DENIED, REVISION_CONFLICT, CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE, UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE, FORMAT_INCOMPATIBLE, IO_ERROR, RUNTIME_ERROR and CANCELLED.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Performance and resource constraints
requirements.text: Canvas MUST remain responsive for realistically large documents and MUST NOT render/process the entire spatial document every frame solely because it exists.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Performance and resource constraints
requirements.text: Viewport rendering MUST use spatial culling/virtualisation and appropriate caching so distant off-screen objects do not impose per-frame work proportional to total document size.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Performance and resource constraints
requirements.text: Incremental edits such as adding one stroke SHOULD avoid rewriting/re-rendering unrelated content where the persistence/rendering architecture can preserve correctness without doing so.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Performance and resource constraints
requirements.text: Caches MUST be bounded and invalidated by semantic revisions rather than growing without limit.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Performance and resource constraints
requirements.text: Large images/media MUST use progressive/appropriate decoding and MUST NOT block the interactive input loop unnecessarily.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Performance and resource constraints
requirements.text: The implementation test suite MUST include large-canvas fixtures with high stroke/object counts, embedded images/shared objects and widely separated spatial extents.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Failure and recovery behaviour
requirements.text: If a shared object renderer fails, Canvas MUST preserve the object data and show a typed recoverable error representation rather than deleting or flattening it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Failure and recovery behaviour
requirements.text: If a donor tool/backend capability fails to initialise, Canvas MUST report the unavailable capability and keep unaffected tools usable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Failure and recovery behaviour
requirements.text: Transient save/sync failures MUST use bounded retry/backoff and expose unresolved state; infinite retries are prohibited.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Failure and recovery behaviour
requirements.text: If collaboration connectivity is lost, local permitted editing MAY continue when the storage/conflict model supports it, but unsynchronised state MUST be visible and reconciliation MUST use revision/conflict rules on reconnect.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Failure and recovery behaviour
requirements.text: If an import is partially parseable, Canvas MUST follow the declared import policy: either commit an explicitly reported partial result as a new artifact or fail atomically.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Failure and recovery behaviour
requirements.text: It MUST NOT silently present a partial result as full-fidelity success.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Release acceptance criteria
requirements.text: The release validation suite MUST demonstrate at minimum:

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Release acceptance criteria
requirements.text: Keyboard-only operation of required shell/menu/tool workflows and assistive-technology inspection of meaningful Canvas objects.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Canvas > Release acceptance criteria
requirements.text: Any acceptance path that silently drops user data, silently flattens a supported structured object, reports a disconnected UI control as working, creates duplicate canonical artifacts during live embedding, loses a running AI session solely because its UI is hidden, or omits an unreviewed donor feature MUST block release conformance.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Product role and data paradigms
requirements.text: Data MUST support four native data paradigms without forcing one paradigm onto every project: spreadsheet/grid data, relational database data, hierarchical/rich structured data and multidimensional analytical data.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Product role and data paradigms
requirements.text: These paradigms may interoperate through explicit projections, relationships and transformations, but their semantics MUST NOT be silently conflated.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Product role and data paradigms
requirements.text: Native .9to1d projects MAY represent richer structures than XLSX/ODS; compatibility formats MUST NOT constrain the native model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Shared engines, donor source and implementation authority
requirements.text: Configured providers MAY add PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, SQLite, SQL Server and other supported external database systems through typed connection adapters.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Shared engines, donor source and implementation authority
requirements.text: The 9to1 source tree MUST contain or fetch the appropriate maintained LibreOffice Calc donor source required by the architecture, subject to the global donor-source and licensing contract.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Shared engines, donor source and implementation authority
requirements.text: The implementation agent MUST NOT treat a missing LibreOffice installation or missing checked-out donor source as permission to build a miniature replacement spreadsheet engine.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Shared engines, donor source and implementation authority
requirements.text: If the required donor source is absent during an autonomous development pass, the agent MUST obtain/fork the latest appropriate compatible source and record the exact upstream/version used before continuing dependent implementation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Shared engines, donor source and implementation authority
requirements.text: Data MUST integrate donor capability into the 9to1 product model, CUI and typed APIs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Shared engines, donor source and implementation authority
requirements.text: Shared charting, Node Graph, Files, identity/permissions, credential storage, AI/model, action/audit and other cross-product infrastructure MUST be reused where canonical rather than privately reimplemented.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Canonical Data project model
requirements.text: A project MAY contain only a workbook, only database/query resources, only a multidimensional model, or any compatible combination.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Canonical Data project model
requirements.text: A user MUST NOT need to create unrelated projects merely because one analysis starts in a spreadsheet and later uses SQL or a transformation pipeline.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Workbook and spreadsheet model
requirements.text: Reordering or renaming a sheet MUST NOT invalidate stable references that use SheetID.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Rich native cells and multiple values
requirements.text: A native .9to1d cell MAY contain a typed value object rather than only one scalar.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Rich native cells and multiple values
requirements.text: A list/set/record cell can expose member ordering, labels/keys, type validation, per-member editing, filtering/query semantics and explicit expansion into rows/columns when required.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Rich native cells and multiple values
requirements.text: The grid MAY display a concise collapsed summary such as '3 values' or '5 related records'; selecting or expanding the cell exposes the complete structured value without altering the underlying schema.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Rich native cells and multiple values
requirements.text: Formula, filter, Visualise and SQL-projection semantics for structured cells MUST be defined explicitly.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Nested cells, nested tables and hierarchical data
requirements.text: A cell MAY own a nested table/record structure with stable nested identity and schema.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Nested cells, nested tables and hierarchical data
requirements.text: Data MUST distinguish nested owned data from references to separate related records.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Nested cells, nested tables and hierarchical data
requirements.text: A nested child table is part of the parent value/object lifecycle; a relation/reference points to independently canonical records and MUST NOT duplicate them merely for display.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Nested cells, nested tables and hierarchical data
requirements.text: Hierarchical structures MAY nest beyond one level when the schema requires it, subject to performance and usability limits.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Nested cells, nested tables and hierarchical data
requirements.text: The UI MUST avoid expanding an entire deep hierarchy by default.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Multidimensional and 3D analytical data
requirements.text: Data MUST support native multidimensional datasets beyond a two-dimensional row-by-column grid.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Multidimensional and 3D analytical data
requirements.text: A common three-dimensional example is Product × Region × Month, but the model MUST support additional dimensions such as Scenario, Currency or Channel.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Multidimensional and 3D analytical data
requirements.text: Multidimensional state remains canonical and may be queried through explicit relational projections/views.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Multidimensional and 3D analytical data
requirements.text: DataCube projections to spreadsheet, SQL, pivot or Visualise views MUST preserve source identity and declare the projection rules.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Multiple views over one canonical dataset
requirements.text: The same canonical dataset MAY be viewed as an ordinary spreadsheet grid, structured/nested table, relational table, pivot, hierarchy/tree, multidimensional slice, SQL relation, transformation graph or Visualise view.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Multiple views over one canonical dataset
requirements.text: Creating a new view MUST NOT silently duplicate source data unless the user explicitly requests a snapshot/materialised copy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Formula engine and calculation
requirements.text: Data MUST preserve Calc-compatible formula semantics wherever spreadsheet compatibility is claimed.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Formula engine and calculation
requirements.text: Formula dependencies MUST be tracked so recalculation can be dependency-aware.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Formula engine and calculation
requirements.text: Data MUST NOT blindly recalculate an entire large workbook after every unrelated edit when a narrower dependency recomputation is possible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Formula engine and calculation
requirements.text: Data MUST NOT collapse distinct formula failures into a generic error string.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Formula engine and calculation
requirements.text: Structured/native cell values may expose additional functions for contains/count/map/filter/member access and projection where explicitly supported; compatibility exports must detect when such formulas cannot be represented faithfully.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Tables, records and stable row identity
requirements.text: Sorting, filtering or moving a visible row MUST NOT change the record's identity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Tables, records and stable row identity
requirements.text: A SQL result may materialise into or back a query-linked DataTable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Relational schema and field design
requirements.text: Any eligible DataTable may be promoted/configured as a relational table with explicit field/schema metadata.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Relational schema and field design
requirements.text: Fields support name, data type, nullability/required state, default, validation/check rules, uniqueness, generated/computed definition, key role, references and backend-specific metadata where applicable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Relational schema and field design
requirements.text: Data MUST provide a Table Design/Schema view where field definitions, keys, required state, defaults, references and constraints can be inspected and edited directly without relying on scattered context menus.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Primary keys, candidate keys and indexes
requirements.text: Primary-key changes MUST validate duplicates, missing values and dependent references before commitment.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Primary keys, candidate keys and indexes
requirements.text: Data SHOULD explain index capability and likely purpose without automatically creating indexes everywhere.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Primary keys, candidate keys and indexes
requirements.text: Project-local structured tables MAY use stable RecordID independently of a user-visible relational primary key; external relational projection semantics MUST define which key is authoritative for joins and persistence.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Foreign keys and sheet/table relationships
requirements.text: The UI may display a friendly related value such as tutor name while storing the stable referenced key/record.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Relationship designer and ER diagrams
requirements.text: Data MUST provide a visual Relationship Designer showing tables/entities, key fields and typed relationship edges with cardinality/optionality.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Relationship designer and ER diagrams
requirements.text: The Relationship Designer SHOULD reuse the shared Node Graph Framework for pan/zoom/selection/grouping/connection mechanics while preserving Data-specific relationship semantics and constraints.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Referential integrity and cascade behaviour
requirements.text: Relationships may enforce referenced-key existence, restrict deletion/update, cascade delete/update or set-null according to backend/native capability.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Referential integrity and cascade behaviour
requirements.text: Consequential cascade operations MUST be previewable with affected-object/record impact where knowable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Referential integrity and cascade behaviour
requirements.text: If a relationship prevents deletion, Data MUST expose which dependency blocks the operation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Referential integrity and cascade behaviour
requirements.text: It MUST NOT silently disable referential integrity or orphan dependent records.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Normalisation and denormalisation
requirements.text: Data MUST include a Normalise tool that analyses selected relational/tabular structures for common design problems such as repeating groups, duplicated entities, non-atomic values where a relational design is desired, partial dependencies, transitive dependencies, duplicated lookup data and missing candidate keys.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Normalisation and denormalisation
requirements.text: Normalisation assistance may propose transformations toward 1NF, 2NF, 3NF and, where appropriate for advanced users, BCNF.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Normalisation and denormalisation
requirements.text: The proposal MUST show new tables, keys, relationships and record-migration effects before mutation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Normalisation and denormalisation
requirements.text: Data MUST explain assumptions rather than blindly applying a theoretical normal form to data that is intentionally hierarchical or multidimensional.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Lookups and related-record navigation
requirements.text: A foreign-key/reference field may display a user-friendly target field while retaining the stable referenced key/record internally.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Lookups and related-record navigation
requirements.text: Lookup display configuration MUST NOT replace the actual stored relationship.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Lookups and related-record navigation
requirements.text: Such displays reference canonical records; they MUST NOT copy the children into a nested owned structure unless the user explicitly converts the relationship.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Data sources and connections
requirements.text: Credentials/secrets MUST use the 9to1 credential/trust infrastructure and MUST NOT be embedded in .9to1d project content, query history or ordinary logs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > SQL workspace
requirements.text: Data MUST provide native SQL authoring/execution with syntax highlighting, dialect-aware parsing/validation, schema/object browser, table/column/function completion, relationship-aware join suggestions, query formatting, parameters where supported, saved queries, query history, execution timing/statistics, cancellation, paged/virtualised result sets, EXPLAIN/plan access where supported and result export/materialisation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > SQL workspace
requirements.text: DuckDB SHOULD make local analytical querying nearly frictionless: eligible project tables and supported local files can be queried directly without requiring users to provision an external database.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Persistent AI / SQL bar switcher
requirements.text: SQL mode treats the input as SQL and executes it natively against the explicitly selected SQL target; SQL text MUST NOT be sent to AI merely to emulate execution.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Persistent AI / SQL bar switcher
requirements.text: SQL mode MUST always display the active execution target, for example DuckDB · This Project or PostgreSQL · Production.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Persistent AI / SQL bar switcher
requirements.text: The selected connection/database/schema scope MUST be visible enough that users cannot reasonably confuse a local analytical target with a live external target.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Persistent AI / SQL bar switcher
requirements.text: Data MUST NOT silently retarget a query because another sheet, panel or connection became focused.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Native SQL execution records and results
requirements.text: Successful prior result state MUST remain available when a later execution fails unless the user explicitly replaces/discards it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Read-only and mutating SQL classification
requirements.text: Data MUST parse/classify SQL before execution.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Read-only and mutating SQL classification
requirements.text: Provably read-only statements such as ordinary SELECT/CTE SELECT, EXPLAIN and supported metadata introspection MAY execute directly subject to connection permissions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Read-only and mutating SQL classification
requirements.text: Classification MUST be conservative when the dialect/parser cannot prove a statement is read-only.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Protected live-database SQL execution
requirements.text: Before execution Data MUST identify the target, classify statements, inspect likely affected objects, use a transaction/savepoint where supported, determine preview/impact information where technically possible, establish an appropriate recoverable backup/checkpoint strategy when required, show the effect/recovery state and obtain the applicable confirmation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Protected live-database SQL execution
requirements.text: Recovery strategy is backend-aware and may use transaction rollback, savepoint, affected-row before-image capture, table snapshot/copy, database-native snapshot, backup file/provider recovery point, schema export plus affected data or another verified recoverable mechanism.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Protected live-database SQL execution
requirements.text: Data MUST record the strategy actually established.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Protected live-database SQL execution
requirements.text: If the safety contract for the requested live mutation requires rollback/backup protection and Data cannot establish it, execution MUST stop.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Protected live-database SQL execution
requirements.text: Data MUST NOT state or imply that a backup, transaction or rollback exists when it does not.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Protected live-database SQL execution
requirements.text: It MUST NOT blindly retry consequential SQL without operation identity/idempotency or renewed confirmation where required.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > DDL and dependency impact
requirements.text: Before consequential DROP/ALTER/rename operations Data SHOULD identify dependent views, foreign keys, indexes, saved queries, linked Data views, Forms integrations, Visualisations and other known references.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > DDL and dependency impact
requirements.text: DDL impact that cannot be determined reliably MUST be represented as unknown rather than assumed safe.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Manual SQL versus AI-proposed SQL
requirements.text: Read-only SQL should not acquire unnecessary AI-style approval friction.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Manual SQL versus AI-proposed SQL
requirements.text: AI may draft, explain, optimise, fix or generate SQL, but an AI-proposed consequential mutation MUST NOT bypass Data's per-action approval rules.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Manual SQL versus AI-proposed SQL
requirements.text: For external database changes, the proposed SQL and target/impact/recovery information MUST be inspectable before approved execution.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Visual query builder
requirements.text: Data SHOULD provide a no-code/low-code visual query builder for select fields, filters, joins, groups, aggregations, ordering and limits.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Visual query builder
requirements.text: Declared relationships SHOULD inform join suggestions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Transformation pipelines
requirements.text: Data MUST support reusable structured TransformPipeline objects for data cleaning and reshaping.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Transformation pipelines
requirements.text: Nodes may represent Source → Select → Filter → Join → Derive → Group → Output and other registered transforms.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Refresh and stale-data semantics
requirements.text: Refresh failure MUST NOT erase the previous valid result.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Refresh and stale-data semantics
requirements.text: Automatic refresh is permission- and resource-aware; external consequential side effects MUST NOT be hidden inside a data-refresh operation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Visualise mode from the persistent eye icon
requirements.text: A useful Visualise configuration MAY be saved as a DataVisualisation, embedded elsewhere or converted to a persistent chart/view where the representation supports it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Visualise mode from the persistent eye icon
requirements.text: Opening/changing Visualise MUST NOT require restructuring or duplicating the underlying spreadsheet.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Adaptive visualisation inference
requirements.text: Data SHOULD rank sensible visualisations for the current structure instead of presenting every visual type as equally appropriate.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Visualisation catalogue and specialised views
requirements.text: A tier-list view can map entity, ranking field, tier boundaries/order, secondary labels and optional group.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Visualisation catalogue and specialised views
requirements.text: Tiers may derive from explicit categories or user-defined numeric/rule boundaries.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Visualisation catalogue and specialised views
requirements.text: The tier rules MUST be visible/editable rather than inferred invisibly.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Visualisation catalogue and specialised views
requirements.text: Specialised views MUST define their required field roles and accessible non-visual representation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Visualise interaction, saved objects and cross-app reuse
requirements.text: Selecting a graphical mark SHOULD map back to the corresponding row/cell/record and offer Go to source where possible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Charts, pivots and analytical sheets
requirements.text: Data MAY provide analytical/report sheets that compose tables, pivots, charts, metrics and controls.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Cross-app conversion into Data
requirements.text: Data MUST support AI-assisted conversion of structured content from other 9to1 surfaces into native Data structures.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Cross-app conversion into Data
requirements.text: Conversion MUST preserve source provenance and provide Go to source where source identity is retained.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Write, Present, Boards and Canvas conversion semantics
requirements.text: Repeated sections may become records; list fields can become true multi-value cells rather than comma-separated text.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Write, Present, Boards and Canvas conversion semantics
requirements.text: Present → Data can map one slide to one record, repeated cards/objects to rows, native tables to Data tables, chart data to result/source tables where available, speaker notes to optional fields and slide metadata to columns.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Write, Present, Boards and Canvas conversion semantics
requirements.text: Repeated layout semantics SHOULD inform schema inference.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Write, Present, Boards and Canvas conversion semantics
requirements.text: Connected diagrams SHOULD be represented as appropriate node and edge datasets rather than flattened nonsensically into one sheet.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Snapshot versus linked conversion
requirements.text: Refreshing a linked conversion MUST NOT silently discard incompatible local edits; conflicts or schema drift are surfaced.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Data profiling and quality inspection
requirements.text: For selected ranges/tables Data SHOULD provide profiling including row/record count, null/blank count, unique count, inferred/declared type, min/max, mean/median where suitable, value distribution, duplicate detection and invalid/outlier indicators where statistically appropriate.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Data profiling and quality inspection
requirements.text: It MUST NOT label an observation erroneous merely because it is statistically unusual.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Files and source identity
requirements.text: Moving or renaming an underlying source in Files MUST NOT break a stable link when the provider identity remains valid.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Import/export and compatibility boundaries
requirements.text: Native .9to1d features such as nested tables, list-valued cells, records/objects, canonical cross-app references, multidimensional cubes, rich relationships and linked-source mappings may exceed XLSX/ODS capability.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Import/export and compatibility boundaries
requirements.text: Export MUST detect unsupported semantics and present explicit transformations such as expand list to rows/columns, stringify, move nested table to another sheet, flatten hierarchy or export a cube slice/pivot.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Import/export and compatibility boundaries
requirements.text: Data MUST NOT silently flatten rich native content and claim a lossless round-trip.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Forms and other 9to1 integrations
requirements.text: Field type, required state, enum/reference options and validation can seed the generated form.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Forms and other 9to1 integrations
requirements.text: Database/table record editing MAY provide a focused single-record editor, but general form-design capability remains owned by Forms.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > AI context, provenance and analysis
requirements.text: Users MUST be able to inspect value provenance where available: literal/formula/query/transform origin, source cell/table/query/pipeline, refresh status, external connection/source and whether AI modified the value/object.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > AI mutation approval and live-database protection
requirements.text: Switching the AI bar to Write mode, trusting the Agent/app or previously approving another Data action MUST NOT authorise subsequent Data mutations automatically.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > AI mutation approval and live-database protection
requirements.text: For workbook/local analytical changes, the approval surface MUST show the proposed operation/change set sufficiently for the user to understand what will change.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > AI mutation approval and live-database protection
requirements.text: If required live-database rollback/backup protection cannot be established, the mutation MUST stop rather than falsely claim rollback protection.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > AI mutation approval and live-database protection
requirements.text: After an approved live-database mutation, Data MUST verify the actual outcome where feasible, record the canonical Action Graph/audit result and preserve recovery references.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > AI mutation approval and live-database protection
requirements.text: Partial failure MUST be reported truthfully and MUST NOT trigger blind consequential retries.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Automation and integration events
requirements.text: It MUST NOT flood Automations with raw per-cell hover/selection events.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Collaboration and revision conflicts
requirements.text: Independent edits MAY merge when safe; incompatible concurrent mutations to the same canonical object/property surface conflict rather than blind last-write-wins.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Accessibility
requirements.text: Data MUST be keyboard-operable for spreadsheet navigation/editing, formula entry, tables, relational design, SQL authoring/execution, query results, Visualise controls, charts/pivots and transformation/relationship graphs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Accessibility
requirements.text: Every graphical Visualise representation MUST expose a meaningful non-visual equivalent: for example scatter points as an accessible point table, box plots as quartile/statistical values, tier lists as ordered tier/entity lists, and stem-and-leaf as structured textual data.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Accessibility
requirements.text: State MUST NOT rely on colour alone.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Performance and large-data behaviour
requirements.text: Spreadsheet UI MUST virtualise cells/rows/columns so only required visible/nearby content is rendered.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Performance and large-data behaviour
requirements.text: AI context MUST be scoped semantically to relevant ranges, tables, schema, query results or sampled/profiled context.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Performance and large-data behaviour
requirements.text: Data MUST NOT dump an entire million-row workbook into a model prompt simply because the project is open.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Recovery and failure behaviour
requirements.text: Project/workbook saves and schema changes MUST be crash-safe.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Recovery and failure behaviour
requirements.text: Failed imports, refreshes, transforms, SQL executions, exports or Visualise calculations MUST leave previous valid canonical data intact unless the user explicitly accepted a destructive operation whose partial effects are truthfully reported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Recovery and failure behaviour
requirements.text: Data MUST distinguish 'rollback attempted' from 'rollback succeeded'.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Platform capability behaviour
requirements.text: A platform that cannot execute a particular local/provider capability MUST expose CapabilityUnavailable or route to an explicitly configured supported service; it MUST NOT silently substitute incompatible semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Acceptance requirements
requirements.text: Representative XLSX and ODS files round-trip through the declared LibreOffice-derived compatibility path within the documented compatibility contract, and the required donor source/version is present/recorded rather than replaced by a miniature spreadsheet clone.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Acceptance requirements
requirements.text: A consequential external/live SQL mutation is classified, exposes target/impact, establishes the required verified recovery strategy, obtains the applicable confirmation, executes through transaction/checkpoint protection where supported and records the actual outcome.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Data > Acceptance requirements
requirements.text: Data blocks a protected live mutation when required backup/rollback protection cannot be established and never falsely claims recovery succeeded.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Product role and donor-first implementation
requirements.text: The desktop/native product is donor-backed by Files/WinUI and MUST first reach behavioural/layout parity with the selected appropriate donor source before 9to1-specific extensions are treated as complete.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Product role and donor-first implementation
requirements.text: A donor-parity manifest MUST identify the selected donor revision and classify each applicable donor feature as Preserve, Replace with 9to1-native equivalent or Not applicable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Product role and donor-first implementation
requirements.text: Subscription/account infrastructure specific to the donor is not inherited unless independently required by this specification.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Authority and ownership boundaries
requirements.text: Files stores and synchronises durable revisions produced by those apps but MUST NOT attempt to merge paragraphs, spreadsheet cells, Board blocks, Canvas strokes or Git histories generically.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Authority and ownership boundaries
requirements.text: When two clients concurrently modify bytes and no owning semantic merge engine exists, Files MUST preserve both conflicting revisions or expose a structured conflict; it MUST NOT silently choose the newest wall-clock timestamp.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Canonical identity and item model
requirements.text: Every 9to1-hosted file and folder MUST have a stable FileID or FolderID independent of name, path, sort position or parent.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Canonical identity and item model
requirements.text: Rename and move MUST preserve identity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Canonical identity and item model
requirements.text: Paths are human-facing projections of hierarchy and MUST NOT be used as canonical identity by other 9to1 apps.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Canonical identity and item model
requirements.text: Hosted file metadata MUST include at least FileID, ParentFolderID, Name, ItemType, content/media type, owner/scope, size, created/modified timestamps, current content revision, sync/availability state, sharing state and version metadata.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Canonical identity and item model
requirements.text: Folders MUST expose equivalent stable identity and ordered/queriable child relationships.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Canonical identity and item model
requirements.text: Synced local materialisations of 9to1 Drive items MUST retain metadata linking the local file to the canonical hosted FileID and base/current remote revision.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Canonical identity and item model
requirements.text: Identity MUST NOT be reconstructed from pathname alone.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Locations and provider abstraction
requirements.text: Files MUST expose all storage roots through one typed Location/Provider abstraction.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Locations and provider abstraction
requirements.text: Connected cloud providers MAY be added through adapters.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Locations and provider abstraction
requirements.text: Every provider MUST declare capabilities explicitly, including read, write, rename, move, copy, trash, permanent delete, versions, sharing, offline availability, search, streaming, server-side copy/move, change feeds and any provider-specific constraints.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Locations and provider abstraction
requirements.text: The UI and APIs MUST disable/report unsupported operations rather than pretending parity exists.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Locations and provider abstraction
requirements.text: Provider authentication and secrets MUST be stored through secure credential references.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Locations and provider abstraction
requirements.text: Provider-specific OAuth/tokens MUST NOT be persisted in plaintext Files configuration or logs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Desktop shell, tabs and views
requirements.text: The CUI desktop shell MUST preserve the donor’s applicable tabbed browsing, navigation history, breadcrumbs/address bar, command toolbar, sidebar/location hierarchy, selection behaviour and view-management semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Desktop shell, tabs and views
requirements.text: Session restore MUST reopen the prior tab/location set where available; unavailable removable/network locations restore into an explicit unavailable state rather than being silently discarded.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Desktop shell, tabs and views
requirements.text: Grid/list/details and other applicable donor view modes MUST be supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Desktop shell, tabs and views
requirements.text: Sort, group, visible columns, thumbnail size and compatible folder/view preferences MAY persist per-folder or per-location according to provider capability.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Folder colour customisation
requirements.text: Files MUST support native folder-colour customisation independently of any OneDrive-specific donor capability.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Folder colour customisation
requirements.text: It must work for local folders and 9to1-hosted folders and should work for connected-provider folders where provider capability or Files-owned metadata permits.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Folder colour customisation
requirements.text: A provider that lacks native folder-colour metadata MUST NOT force Files to disable the feature if the presentation override can safely be stored by Files.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Folder colour customisation
requirements.text: Where compatible with sync/account policy, folder-colour metadata may follow the canonical folder across devices.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Folder colour customisation
requirements.text: Files MUST expose the same typed operation to Dulche and Automations, enabling actions such as changing selected/project folder colours without GUI automation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Native 9to1 creation and project integration
requirements.text: Files MUST replace Office-centric creation defaults with first-class 9to1 creation entries.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Native 9to1 creation and project integration
requirements.text: The toolbar/context New menu MUST include at least Folder, Write document, Presentation, Spreadsheet/Data artifact, Board, Canvas and Build project when the current location/provider can store the requested artifact.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Native 9to1 creation and project integration
requirements.text: Creation MUST invoke the owning app’s canonical API rather than having Files manufacture private document internals.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Native 9to1 creation and project integration
requirements.text: Files MUST support Create Build project here and Create Build project from this folder for appropriate folders.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Native 9to1 creation and project integration
requirements.text: App/project folders MAY expose a project-aware representation so users see a meaningful project entity instead of internal managed metadata by default.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Native 9to1 creation and project integration
requirements.text: Advanced inspection MAY reveal underlying files when the owning app permits it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Native 9to1 creation and project integration
requirements.text: Files MUST respect app-managed/protected metadata markers and warn/block casual destructive edits that would corrupt managed project state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > 9to1 Drive integration
requirements.text: 9to1 Drive MUST appear directly in the normal Files sidebar/location tree alongside local drives and other providers.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > 9to1 Drive integration
requirements.text: Hosted storage MUST NOT open into a separate incompatible cloud-files UI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > 9to1 Drive integration
requirements.text: A file uploaded through cakemods.com and later opened in desktop Files MUST refer to the same FileID/content revision, not a separately imported desktop copy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > 9to1 Drive integration
requirements.text: Hosted storage MUST expose quota/allocation, used space and pending/reserved upload space where applicable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > 9to1 Drive integration
requirements.text: Quota exhaustion MUST fail structurally and MUST NOT leave invisible orphan uploads.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Rapid push-based sync architecture
requirements.text: Sync is a core correctness requirement. 9to1 Drive MUST use event/push-driven incremental synchronisation as the normal connected path.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Rapid push-based sync architecture
requirements.text: Polling/full rescans are recovery/fallback mechanisms and MUST NOT be the primary source of ordinary change propagation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Rapid push-based sync architecture
requirements.text: The server MUST produce ordered change events for filesystem-level changes including create, rename, move, metadata change, content-revision commit, delete, restore, share/ACL changes and relevant availability/sync metadata changes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Rapid push-based sync architecture
requirements.text: Duplicate/replayed operation IDs MUST be idempotent and MUST NOT perform consequential mutations twice.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Rapid push-based sync architecture
requirements.text: Ordinary metadata operations such as rename/move/create MUST be pushed immediately after commit and processed continuously by connected clients.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Optimistic local operations
requirements.text: User-initiated structural operations SHOULD feel immediate.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Optimistic local operations
requirements.text: Files MAY optimistically apply a local rename/move/create to the UI before the remote round trip, but MUST record the operation durably as Pending with OperationID, expected/base revision and inverse/recovery metadata.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Optimistic local operations
requirements.text: If validation fails, Files MUST reconcile/reverse the optimistic state and display the structured reason; it MUST NOT leave the UI pretending the server accepted a rejected mutation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Sync and availability state
requirements.text: Hosted items MUST expose explicit sync/availability state rather than a generic spinner.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Sync and availability state
requirements.text: Internal implementations MAY maintain separate content and metadata states so lightweight metadata can become synced while content transfer continues.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Sync and availability state
requirements.text: AvailableOffline means content is currently materialised and may be evicted by managed cache policy only when safe.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Sync and availability state
requirements.text: AlwaysAvailable means the user has pinned the content and Files MUST retain a local copy until the user changes that policy or storage becomes critically unavailable and the user explicitly resolves the situation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Sync and availability state
requirements.text: Hydration MUST expose progress/failure and MUST NOT claim the item is locally available before durable content validation completes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Manual sync and sync-on-demand
requirements.text: Files MUST provide visible manual sync controls, including Sync now, Sync this item, Sync this folder/selection, Pause sync, Resume sync, retry eligible failures and refresh/reconcile from cloud.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Manual sync and sync-on-demand
requirements.text: Sync now MUST flush eligible pending local mutations, request current server deltas since the durable cursor, retry eligible transfers, reconcile conflicts that have deterministic policy and report the resulting pending/error/conflict state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Manual sync and sync-on-demand
requirements.text: It MUST NOT discard unsynced changes merely to match cloud state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Offline-first behaviour
requirements.text: Locally materialised files/folders MUST remain usable offline according to their owning app/file-format capabilities.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Offline-first behaviour
requirements.text: While offline, Files MUST allow safe queued structural operations including create folder, rename, move, delete/restore and reorganisation, and it MUST allow edits to locally available content through the owning app.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Offline-first behaviour
requirements.text: Free up space MUST verify that the canonical hosted revision is durable and equivalent/newer before evicting local bytes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Offline-first behaviour
requirements.text: Items with unsynced local content MUST NOT be evicted.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Offline-first behaviour
requirements.text: AlwaysAvailable items MUST NOT be evicted by normal cache cleanup.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Real-time filesystem collaboration
requirements.text: Files MUST provide real-time collaboration for filesystem structure and Files-owned metadata.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Real-time filesystem collaboration
requirements.text: Connected authorised clients viewing the same hierarchy should receive live create, rename, move, delete/restore, share/ACL and metadata updates without requiring manual refresh.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Real-time filesystem collaboration
requirements.text: Structural mutations MUST carry stable OperationID, actor/caller identity, target object ID, base/expected revision, operation type and result revision.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Real-time filesystem collaboration
requirements.text: Simultaneous incompatible structural edits MUST produce a deterministic RevisionConflict/Conflict object rather than silently letting whichever request arrived last overwrite the other.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Real-time filesystem collaboration
requirements.text: If an owning app has a file open by FileID and another collaborator moves/renames that file, Files MUST publish LocationChanged/metadata events while preserving FileID.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Real-time filesystem collaboration
requirements.text: Files receives/commits durable revisions from that collaboration layer and exposes version/storage metadata, but it MUST NOT run a second generic content-collaboration engine over the same file.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Transfers
requirements.text: Copy, move, upload, download and provider-transfer operations MUST be represented as durable Transfer jobs with TransferID, item set, source/destination, bytes/items totals where known, progress, state, retryability, error list and pause/resume/cancel support where technically possible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Transfers
requirements.text: Hosted uploads/downloads MUST use resumable/chunked transfer when the service/provider supports it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Transfers
requirements.text: Files/Home restart MUST resume from validated committed chunks where possible rather than restarting large transfers from zero.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Transfers
requirements.text: Transfer completion MUST include integrity validation where hashes/checksums are supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Transfers
requirements.text: Integrity failure is a failed transfer and MUST NOT be represented as successful-with-warning.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Transfers
requirements.text: Destination conflicts MUST use explicit policy: Ask, Replace, KeepBoth or Skip, with ApplyToRemaining where appropriate.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Transfers
requirements.text: Automated callers MUST specify a policy or receive ConflictRequiresDecision.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Version history and durable revisions
requirements.text: 9to1 Drive files MUST have durable version history.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Version history and durable revisions
requirements.text: Each durable revision MUST include VersionID/RevisionID, timestamp, actor/source, parent/base revision where relevant and content identity/hash where available.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Version history and durable revisions
requirements.text: Restoring an older revision MUST create a new current revision or otherwise preserve the later history rather than deleting it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Version history and durable revisions
requirements.text: Owning apps MAY commit incremental/semantic collaboration checkpoints, but Files stores the durable file/artifact revision boundary supplied by the app.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Version history and durable revisions
requirements.text: Files MUST not reinterpret app-specific internal history as generic filesystem versions unless the owning app explicitly publishes those revisions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Trash, delete and recovery
requirements.text: Normal hosted deletion MUST be soft/recoverable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Trash, delete and recovery
requirements.text: Trash records MUST preserve stable item ID, original parent/location, deletion timestamp and restoration metadata.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Trash, delete and recovery
requirements.text: Deleting a Files container or reference MUST NOT silently cascade-permanently-delete separately owned embedded/project artifacts unless the owning app explicitly defines cascade semantics and Files presents the impact before execution.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Sharing and ACLs
requirements.text: Hosted files/folders MUST support first-class sharing using stable account/team/organisation principal IDs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Sharing and ACLs
requirements.text: Folder permission inheritance MUST distinguish inherited from direct grants.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Sharing and ACLs
requirements.text: Moving an item between differently permissioned folders MUST calculate/result in an explicit effective permission change and MUST NOT silently retain/remove direct grants contrary to the configured inheritance policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Sharing and ACLs
requirements.text: Shared with Me MUST reference canonical objects owned elsewhere rather than cloning them into the recipient’s Drive.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Sharing and ACLs
requirements.text: If public/link sharing is supported, link shares MUST use revocable ShareID/token state with explicit permission level and optional expiry/password where implemented.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Sharing and ACLs
requirements.text: Raw file URLs MUST NOT themselves imply authority.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Search, metadata and previews
requirements.text: Files MUST support filename/folder search plus indexed metadata/content search where provider/file-type policy permits.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Search, metadata and previews
requirements.text: Common item metadata MUST include provider/location, type, size, relevant timestamps, owner/sharing, sync/offline state, current revision and hashes/integrity data where available.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Search, metadata and previews
requirements.text: App-specific metadata MUST be namespaced/versioned.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Search, metadata and previews
requirements.text: Files MUST provide preview/thumbnail contracts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Search, metadata and previews
requirements.text: Owning apps/providers MAY register read-only preview renderers for native artifacts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Search, metadata and previews
requirements.text: Preview MUST NOT mutate the source artifact or require launching a full app window unless no lightweight preview capability exists.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Open routing, context actions and drag/drop
requirements.text: Native 9to1 artifacts MUST expose enough type/version metadata that routing is not dependent solely on filename extension.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Open routing, context actions and drag/drop
requirements.text: Users MAY choose alternate compatible handlers where supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Open routing, context actions and drag/drop
requirements.text: Installed apps MAY contribute typed registered context actions based on item type/capability, such as Open in Write, Add to Board, Open in Picture, Create Build project from folder or other ecosystem actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Open routing, context actions and drag/drop
requirements.text: Context actions MUST be declared through Home’s registry and MUST NOT inject arbitrary untrusted shell code into Files.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Open routing, context actions and drag/drop
requirements.text: Drag/drop and clipboard operations MUST preserve operation intent, source identity and provider capability.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Open routing, context actions and drag/drop
requirements.text: Cross-provider drag MUST make copy-vs-move semantics explicit.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Open routing, context actions and drag/drop
requirements.text: A cut/paste MUST NOT delete the source until destination commit succeeds.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > AI bar and privacy
requirements.text: Files MUST host the global persistent contextual AI bar.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > AI bar and privacy
requirements.text: Selecting a private local file MUST NOT silently upload file content to a cloud model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > AI bar and privacy
requirements.text: Context handoff MUST identify the exact file/revision being provided and whether bytes/content leave the device.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > AI bar and privacy
requirements.text: Files MUST remain fully functional with AI disabled/unavailable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > AI bar and privacy
requirements.text: AI is additive and MUST NOT replace essential manual file-management UI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Operation journal, undo and change feed
requirements.text: Consequential filesystem operations MUST be recorded in a durable operation journal with OperationID, actor/caller, target object IDs, source/destination where applicable, base/result revisions, state and structured error/result.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Operation journal, undo and change feed
requirements.text: Safely reversible operations such as rename, move and soft-delete SHOULD expose undo by performing a real inverse storage mutation against current revision checks.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Operation journal, undo and change feed
requirements.text: Undo MUST NOT be UI-only fiction and MUST fail explicitly if intervening changes make the inverse unsafe.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Operation journal, undo and change feed
requirements.text: Files MUST expose a resumable typed change feed with stable event IDs/cursors for create/change/move/share/delete/restore/sync-state and other supported filesystem events.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Properties and sync diagnostics
requirements.text: A Properties/details surface MUST expose stable identity, path/location, provider, type, size, timestamps, owner/sharing, sync/offline state, current version/history access, app association and provider-specific metadata where available.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Properties and sync diagnostics
requirements.text: Files MUST provide clear sync diagnostics for 9to1 Drive, including current connectivity/server contact, pending uploads/downloads, pending structural operations, conflicts, paused/error state, offline-pinned usage and local cache usage.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Properties and sync diagnostics
requirements.text: Item-level errors MUST expose local/base/cloud revision information where relevant and provide Resolve/Retry/View details actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Safety and filesystem edge cases
requirements.text: Provider adapters and local materialisation MUST define handling for illegal/reserved filenames, case sensitivity, path length, path traversal, symlinks/reparse points and unsupported metadata.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Safety and filesystem edge cases
requirements.text: Remote names MUST NOT escape the intended local sync root or overwrite unrelated local paths.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Safety and filesystem edge cases
requirements.text: Filesystem shortcuts/symlinks MUST remain distinct from 9to1 artifact references/shortcuts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Safety and filesystem edge cases
requirements.text: Copying a reference MUST NOT accidentally clone the referenced canonical artifact unless the user explicitly chooses duplication.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Files API
requirements.text: Every additional donor-parity and 9to1-native user-visible operation MUST have an equivalent typed Files or owning-app action under the global API-parity rule.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Failure behaviour
requirements.text: Files MUST return structured failures including ItemNotFound, RevisionConflict, NameConflict, ConflictRequiresDecision, PermissionDenied, ProviderUnavailable, ProviderCapabilityUnsupported, QuotaExceeded, Offline, TransferInterrupted, IntegrityFailed, SyncConflict, FileInUse, StorageUnavailable, InvalidName, DestinationUnavailable, HomeServiceUnavailable and structured partial bulk results in addition to the global error contract.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > Platform behaviour
requirements.text: Web Files exposes hosted/provider-accessible content but MUST NOT pretend to have arbitrary access to the browser user’s local filesystem.

requirements.group_title: Shared Files organisation shell and operations
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > TF-F01 — Shared Files organisation shell and operations
requirements.text: The New menu MUST expose the ten organisation types at compatible locations, alongside existing native document creation.

requirements.group_title: Shared Files organisation shell and operations
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > TF-F01 — Shared Files organisation shell and operations
requirements.text: A provider lacking native metadata MAY use the existing Files-owned metadata capability; unsupported storage or write permissions MUST be explained before creation rather than falling back to an ordinary folder without consent.

requirements.group_title: Shared Files organisation shell and operations
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > TF-F01 — Shared Files organisation shell and operations
requirements.text: New files created from a virtual view use an explicit Files destination, initially the organisation's configured backing location; the location MUST be inspectable/changeable before creation.

requirements.group_title: Shared Files organisation shell and operations
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > TF-F01 — Shared Files organisation shell and operations
requirements.text: Organisation commands MUST include Add existing, New item, Rename, Open, Open in new tab/window, Show original location, Properties, Share, view/layout settings, Remove from this organisation and the separately labelled original-file delete action when permitted.

requirements.group_title: Shared Files organisation shell and operations
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > TF-F01 — Shared Files organisation shell and operations
requirements.text: Dragging an existing item into a contextual collection adds a reference by default; the drop indicator MUST state Add reference, Move original, Copy original or Reorder as appropriate.

requirements.group_title: Shared Files organisation shell and operations
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > TF-F01 — Shared Files organisation shell and operations
requirements.text: The default MUST NOT unexpectedly move or duplicate source bytes.

requirements.group_title: Shared Files organisation shell and operations
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > TF-F01 — Shared Files organisation shell and operations
requirements.text: All organisation types MUST support nesting with every other type, including ordinary folders, subject only to explicit provider capabilities and coherent containment rules.

requirements.group_title: Shared Files organisation shell and operations
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > TF-F01 — Shared Files organisation shell and operations
requirements.text: Owned containment MUST be acyclic; reference resolution MUST detect recursion and avoid infinite expansion.

requirements.group_title: Shared Files organisation shell and operations
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > TF-F01 — Shared Files organisation shell and operations
requirements.text: Smart query results MUST not recursively ingest their own collection.

requirements.group_title: Shared Files organisation shell and operations
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > TF-F01 — Shared Files organisation shell and operations
requirements.text: A normal folder-style contents view MUST be available for every specialised type without converting its data.

requirements.group_title: Shared Files organisation shell and operations
requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Files > TF-F01 — Shared Files organisation shell and operations
