requirements.top_section: Accounts, web services, cloud storage and integrations
requirements.text: Disconnecting an account MUST NOT automatically delete unrelated local 9to1 artifacts previously imported from it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Accounts, web services, cloud storage and integrations > Disconnect and revocation
requirements.top_section: Accounts, web services, cloud storage and integrations
requirements.text: For linked/synchronised objects, the UI must explain what local data remains, what becomes unavailable and whether any pending remote operations are abandoned.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Accounts, web services, cloud storage and integrations > Security invariants
requirements.top_section: Accounts, web services, cloud storage and integrations
requirements.text: Every external operation must pass both provider scope/capability validation and the relevant 9to1 permission boundary.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Accounts, web services, cloud storage and integrations > Security invariants
requirements.top_section: Accounts, web services, cloud storage and integrations
requirements.text: Connection/account identity, remote-object identity, provenance and provider limitations must remain explicit across app boundaries.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Accounts, web services, cloud storage and integrations > Security invariants
requirements.top_section: Accounts, web services, cloud storage and integrations
requirements.text: Logs, exports and Den records must not contain plaintext reusable provider secrets.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Product role and boundary
requirements.text: Planner MUST expose local/native planning and provider-backed calendar/task data through one coherent typed model without duplicating canonical external or 9to1 entities.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Donor and upstream contract
requirements.text: Implementers MUST NOT silently choose a donor and allow donor-specific storage or behaviour to become public Planner authority.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Donor and upstream contract
requirements.text: Mature calendar standards, provider APIs and the shared 9to1 frameworks MAY be used as implementation references where they do not contradict this specification.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Primary views and navigation
requirements.text: Planner MUST provide Today, Day, Week, Month, Agenda and Tasks views.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Primary views and navigation
requirements.text: The sidebar MUST expose the user's calendars/task lists plus three optional modules — Schedule, Countdown and Assignments.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Primary views and navigation
requirements.text: Each optional module can be enabled, hidden and reordered by the user.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Primary views and navigation
requirements.text: Hiding a module removes its navigation surface only; it MUST NOT delete its data.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Agenda
requirements.text: It MUST group and order upcoming events and other relevant due/scheduled Planner entities by date/time while preserving each item's canonical identity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Agenda
requirements.text: Agenda SHOULD surface at least events, scheduled PlannerTasks and Assignment deadlines.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Agenda
requirements.text: It MAY surface other Planner milestones such as selected Countdowns when the user has enabled that integration.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Canonical entity model
requirements.text: Schedule and ScheduleItem — optional structured day-plan entities.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Canonical entity model
requirements.text: Countdown — optional user-defined target-date/time entity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Canonical entity model
requirements.text: Assignment and AssignmentItem — optional structured deadline/work-completion entities.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > PlannerEvent
requirements.text: PlannerEvent MUST contain at least EventID, CalendarID, Title, Description?, Start/End or all-day date span, TimeZone semantics, Location?, Recurrence?, References[], Reminders[], Status, CreatedAt, ModifiedAt, owner/scope, source/provider metadata and revision.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > PlannerEvent
requirements.text: An Event may reference a meeting, Maps route, Files/Write/Present/Board/Canvas/Data artifact, Mail thread/message, Space, Automation output or other registered 9to1 entity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > PlannerEvent
requirements.text: Referencing an entity MUST NOT duplicate its canonical payload.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > PlannerTask
requirements.text: PlannerTask MUST contain at least PlannerTaskID, Title, Description?, Status, TaskListID?, DueAt/date?, ScheduledStart?, ScheduledEnd?, Recurrence?, Priority?, References[], Reminders[], CreatedAt, ModifiedAt, owner/scope and revision.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > PlannerTask
requirements.text: Scheduling a PlannerTask onto the calendar assigns ScheduledStart/ScheduledEnd to the same PlannerTaskID; Planner MUST NOT manufacture a duplicate Event merely to render the task in a time-grid.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > PlannerTask
requirements.text: Removing it from the time-grid may clear the scheduled window without deleting the task or its due date.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Time zones, all-day values and daylight saving
requirements.text: Timed Event/Task values MUST use real timezone-aware semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Time zones, all-day values and daylight saving
requirements.text: A user travelling or changing device timezone MUST NOT silently change the intended meaning of the event.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Time zones, all-day values and daylight saving
requirements.text: All-day items are date-based and MUST NOT drift onto an adjacent date through UTC conversion.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Recurrence and occurrence identity
requirements.text: Recurring Events, PlannerTasks, Assignments and Countdowns MUST use a recurrence definition rather than pre-creating an unbounded list of copies.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Recurrence and occurrence identity
requirements.text: Editing a repeating item MUST support the applicable scopes This occurrence, This and following, and Entire series.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Recurrence and occurrence identity
requirements.text: A modified/skipped occurrence is stored as an exception; modifying one occurrence MUST NOT flatten the entire series into unrelated records.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Recurrence and occurrence identity
requirements.text: Infinite recurrence MUST never be materialised eagerly.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Reminders and Home notifications
requirements.text: An entity MAY own multiple reminder rules such as at start, relative minutes/hours/days before, or a custom trigger supported by the reminder contract.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Reminders and Home notifications
requirements.text: Snoozing a reminder changes reminder state/next notification time and MUST NOT rewrite the Event/Task/Assignment's actual start or due time.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Optional sidebar module: Schedule
requirements.text: Schedule MUST show, at minimum, current item start/end, elapsed time, remaining time, percentage elapsed and percentage remaining.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Optional sidebar module: Schedule
requirements.text: It MAY additionally show an item's share of the containing schedule, but that percentage must be labelled distinctly from time-progress percentage.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Optional sidebar module: Schedule
requirements.text: ScheduleItem contains stable ScheduleItemID, title, start/end, optional colour/icon/location, References[] and optional links to EventID, PlannerTaskID or AssignmentID.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Optional sidebar module: Schedule
requirements.text: Schedules MAY be reusable/recurring and support date-specific exceptions without destroying the base pattern.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Optional sidebar module: Countdown
requirements.text: Countdown entries have stable CountdownID, Name, TargetDate/TargetDateTime, timezone/all-day semantics, icon/image/category metadata where used, recurrence?, References[] and optional linked EventID/AssignmentID.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Optional sidebar module: Countdown
requirements.text: The dashboard MAY vary displayed precision by proximity, for example days when far away and hours/minutes/seconds when close, while preserving the same target.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Optional sidebar module: Assignments
requirements.text: AssignmentItem has stable AssignmentItemID, AssignmentID, parent/nesting relationship?, title/description, Required/Optional classification, completion/progress state, optional weight, optional assignee and revision.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Optional sidebar module: Assignments
requirements.text: Required and optional items remain distinguishable in UI, API, Automations and completion rules.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Assignment progress and completion
requirements.text: Assignments MUST support partial completion rather than only Done/Not Done.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Assignment progress and completion
requirements.text: Required statuses include at least Not Started, In Progress, Completed and Cancelled; overdue is derived from the due date versus completion state and MUST be queryable even if represented visually as a status badge.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Assignment progress and completion
requirements.text: Progress MAY be automatically calculated from required items, manually set for work that cannot be represented as a checklist, or calculated using explicit item weights.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Assignment progress and completion
requirements.text: By default, an Assignment cannot be marked Completed while required items remain incomplete.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Assignment progress and completion
requirements.text: A user may explicitly override that rule where permitted, with a visible warning/impact confirmation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Assignment progress and completion
requirements.text: Automation/API calls must make an equivalent override explicit rather than silently bypassing required items.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Assignment progress and completion
requirements.text: Assignment views MUST include useful states such as Due soon, Overdue, In progress, Completed and All, with filters/grouping such as due date, course/project/team, priority and assignee where data exists.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Team assignments
requirements.text: Assignments MAY have an owner, assignees/contributors and item-level assignees.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Assignment Automations and extension workflows
requirements.text: Planner exposes Assignment events/state to Automations, but Planner itself MUST NOT secretly send external communications as a built-in overdue side effect.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Assignment Automations and extension workflows
requirements.text: A user may create an Automation such as: when an Assignment becomes overdue and is incomplete, draft or send a Mail extension request to the relevant person.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Cross-app typed references
requirements.text: Planner references MUST use the owning app's canonical stable IDs and permissions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Cross-app typed references
requirements.text: A referenced artifact may render a preview/embedded surface only through the owning app's declared reference/embed contract.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Cross-app typed references
requirements.text: If a referenced entity is unavailable, revoked or deleted, the Planner item remains valid and surfaces the reference as unavailable/broken; Planner MUST NOT delete the Event/Task/Assignment simply because one attachment/reference disappeared.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Maps and travel integration
requirements.text: Planner Events MAY carry both Location and a canonical Maps RouteID.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Maps and travel integration
requirements.text: Planner may display current route summary/duration and can offer a departure reminder derived from Event start minus current route duration minus an explicit user buffer.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Maps and travel integration
requirements.text: Derived travel reminders MUST NOT rewrite the Event's actual start time.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Mail integration
requirements.text: Mail may create or update Planner items through typed Planner actions while retaining a reference to the source MessageID/ThreadID.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Mail integration
requirements.text: AI-extracted date/time/title values that are materially uncertain must be reviewable rather than silently committed as certain facts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Meetings, attendees and external side effects
requirements.text: Events MAY support attendees, invitations, meeting references/links and RSVP state where the local/provider capability supports them.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Meetings, attendees and external side effects
requirements.text: When saving a change can send invitations, updates or cancellations externally, Planner MUST distinguish local/save-only behaviour from save-and-notify/send behaviour where the provider supports that distinction.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > External calendars and provider capability model
requirements.text: Provider capabilities MUST be explicit and queryable, including relevant support for read/write, recurrence, attendees, free/busy, reminders, meeting links, colours/categories, calendar sharing, task support and push/change feeds.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > External calendars and provider capability model
requirements.text: Unsupported operations must be hidden/disabled or return a structured ProviderCapabilityUnsupported error.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > External calendars and provider capability model
requirements.text: Connected-provider changes should use incremental change feeds/push where supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > External calendars and provider capability model
requirements.text: Provider sync state distinguishes pending/synced/conflict/failed where relevant; conflicts MUST NOT be resolved by blind last-write-wins.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Search, filtering and global discovery
requirements.text: Planner search MUST cover Events, PlannerTasks, Assignments, Countdowns and Schedule entities where enabled.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Search, filtering and global discovery
requirements.text: Filters MAY include date range, calendar/list, status/completion, category/project/course, assignee/attendee, location and referenced entity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Import and export
requirements.text: Planner MUST support iCalendar/.ics import and export for representable calendar data.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Import and export
requirements.text: Importing data creates/links canonical Planner/provider entities according to the selected destination semantics; it MUST NOT create duplicate copies when a stable imported/provider identity already maps to an existing entity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Persistent AI bar
requirements.text: Planner MUST host the global persistent Dulche AI bar.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Persistent AI bar
requirements.text: Natural-language changes such as moving a set of tomorrow's events MUST resolve against stable entity/occurrence IDs rather than inferred screen coordinates.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Automations integration
requirements.text: Planner recurrence remains Planner state; repeating Events/Tasks MUST NOT be implemented as hidden Automations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Planner API
requirements.text: Every additional user-visible Planner operation — including provider actions, sidebar-module operations, recurrence edits, assignment item manipulation, reminder management and import/export — MUST expose an equivalent supported typed action/query.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Persistence, sync, history and recovery
requirements.text: Calendar/Event/PlannerTask/Assignment/Schedule/Countdown changes use revision-aware mutations; partial failure must not leave a recurrence series or Assignment hierarchy half-updated.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Persistence, sync, history and recovery
requirements.text: Offline/reconnect queues MUST preserve operation identity/idempotency.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Accessibility
requirements.text: Planner MUST be keyboard-operable across calendar grids, Agenda, task/assignment lists, Schedule and Countdown.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Accessibility
requirements.text: Screen readers MUST be able to identify item type, title, date/time/due state, recurrence and applicable progress.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Platform capability behaviour
requirements.text: Planner MUST provide useful supported native behaviour on Windows and 9to1-OS plus a useful web version under the global web contract.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Platform capability behaviour
requirements.text: Native clients MAY have richer OS notification/calendar integration; web may depend on browser notification/background constraints.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Platform capability behaviour
requirements.text: Capability differences are explicit and MUST NOT silently downgrade the canonical planning state or turn the web app into a read-only viewer.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Performance and resource behaviour
requirements.text: Large Agenda/task/Assignment lists MUST virtualise.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Performance and resource behaviour
requirements.text: Schedule live-progress and Countdown ticking MUST update efficiently without causing full Planner-tree rerenders each second.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Performance and resource behaviour
requirements.text: Background timers should coalesce/update at the precision actually visible to the user.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Failure behaviour
requirements.text: Planner MUST return structured failures for EventNotFound, PlannerTaskNotFound, AssignmentNotFound, ScheduleNotFound, CountdownNotFound, InvalidRecurrence, InvalidTimeZone, RevisionConflict, PermissionDenied, ProviderCapabilityUnsupported, ProviderSyncConflict, ReferenceUnavailable, ReminderUnavailable and ImportUnsupportedConstruct, plus the global error contract.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Acceptance requirements
requirements.text: Schedule can be enabled as an optional sidebar module and shows live elapsed/remaining time plus percentage elapsed/remaining for the current item.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Acceptance requirements
requirements.text: Countdown can be enabled as an optional sidebar module, supports standalone and linked targets, and linked targets update without duplicated dates.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Acceptance requirements
requirements.text: Assignments can be enabled as an optional sidebar module and persist partial progress, required/optional items, nested/weighted items where configured, due state, team assignments and completion rules.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Planner Burrows
requirements.text: Native items may have one BurrowID or be Unassigned; the All view includes authorised items across burrows without duplicate identities.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Planner Burrows
requirements.text: Users MUST be able to create, rename, reorder, select, set a default, archive/recover and delete a burrow; assign/reassign/unassign existing events, PlannerTasks, assignments and other supported planning items; and filter normal Planner views by burrow or All/Unassigned.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Planner Burrows
requirements.text: Burrow membership may be local 9to1 metadata and MUST NOT silently move or duplicate the external item.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Planner > Planner Burrows
requirements.text: Deleting a burrow MUST preview its item count and reassign its items to a chosen authorised burrow or Unassigned; it must not delete the events/tasks/assignments.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Product role and donor strategy
requirements.text: The whole Connect application MUST use an open-source donor/reference for mature real-time communications behaviour.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Product role and donor strategy
requirements.text: The selected donor revision and applicable licensing obligations MUST be recorded in the donor-parity manifest before implementation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Product role and donor strategy
requirements.text: Connect MUST NOT replace Thunderbird mail behaviour with a reduced chat-derived email implementation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Product role and donor strategy
requirements.text: Connect MUST use a modern native CUI design consistent with 9to1. Proprietary donor services or branding MUST be replaced with 9to1-native equivalents where required.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Architecture and canonical entities
requirements.text: Connect MUST maintain stable canonical identities for at least UserID, ProfileID, OrganisationID, MembershipID, RoleID, ConversationID, RoomID/ChannelID where applicable, MessageID, ThreadID, CallID, ParticipantID, ContactRelationshipID, ReportID, IncidentID, EnforcementActionID and BanEvasionCaseID.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Architecture and canonical entities
requirements.text: Display names, usernames, email addresses, phone numbers, room names and mutable paths MUST NOT be used as canonical identity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Architecture and canonical entities
requirements.text: The product MAY provide unified navigation/search/notifications over both, but MUST NOT merge email and real-time messaging into one incompatible storage/protocol model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Architecture and canonical entities
requirements.text: Connect SHOULD use canonical 9to1 services rather than duplicating them.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Architecture and canonical entities
requirements.text: Shared files SHOULD reference canonical Files objects when applicable; assignments/tasks SHOULD reference canonical Planner objects where appropriate; Home owns notifications/permissions; Dulche provides AI; Contacts/people services own canonical contact data where defined.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Conversations, organisations and hierarchy
requirements.text: Connect MUST support one-to-one conversations, group conversations, organisation/team rooms or channels, threaded replies, reactions, message edits, message deletion according to policy, typing indicators, read state/receipts where enabled, presence/availability controls, mentions, attachments/media and conversation search subject to encryption/indexing constraints.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Conversations, organisations and hierarchy
requirements.text: Users MAY belong to multiple organisations simultaneously.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Conversations, organisations and hierarchy
requirements.text: Organisations MUST support nested teams/departments/groups and explicit role/membership relationships, including organisational hierarchies such as management/employee or school leadership/department/teacher/student structures.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Conversations, organisations and hierarchy
requirements.text: Hierarchy MUST be represented through stable role/membership data rather than inferred only from room placement or display names.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Conversations, organisations and hierarchy
requirements.text: Role and organisation policy MAY govern room creation, membership management, announcement rights, moderation powers, task assignment and administrative settings, but organisation policy MUST NOT silently override personal privacy protections that are not genuinely necessary for the organisation to operate.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail mode
requirements.text: Users MUST be able to use Mail as a complete manual email client with AI unavailable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail mode
requirements.text: Connect MUST provide coherent navigation between Mail and real-time communications while preserving the different underlying protocols, privacy properties and provider semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail mode
requirements.text: Mail MAY remain independently deep-linkable and launchable where the package/shell architecture supports app shortcuts, but such launch targets resolve to the Mail mode of the canonical Connect application rather than creating a second incompatible Mail implementation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Native messaging encryption and privacy
requirements.text: Native Connect conversations MUST use end-to-end encryption by default.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Native messaging encryption and privacy
requirements.text: Ordinary native Connect users MUST NOT be offered a misleading normal-chat mode that silently downgrades private communication to server-readable plaintext merely for implementation convenience.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Native messaging encryption and privacy
requirements.text: The implementation MUST follow the platform-wide Privacy Ceiling and apply stricter communications protections where required.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Native messaging encryption and privacy
requirements.text: Content decryption keys MUST be available only to authorised endpoint devices/participants under the declared trust model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Native messaging encryption and privacy
requirements.text: Servers MUST NOT possess a universal content-decryption key or silent moderation/decryption backdoor while the product claims E2EE.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Native messaging encryption and privacy
requirements.text: Multi-device encryption MUST define device identity, device trust, key distribution, verification, rotation, lost-device handling, session recovery and cryptographic backup/recovery.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Native messaging encryption and privacy
requirements.text: Recovery MUST NOT introduce a server-held master key that silently allows universal message decryption.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Native messaging encryption and privacy
requirements.text: Connect MUST minimise communication metadata separately from content encryption.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Native messaging encryption and privacy
requirements.text: Participant graphs, timestamps, delivery state, IP/network information, device identifiers, routing metadata and notification data MUST be collected/retained only as required for operation, safety or declared policy and MUST NOT be presented to users as E2EE-protected when they are observable to infrastructure.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Native messaging encryption and privacy
requirements.text: Notification delivery MUST minimise plaintext leakage.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Native messaging encryption and privacy
requirements.text: Notification previews of encrypted conversations MUST use the most private technically reliable path and MUST respect user settings; push providers MUST NOT receive unnecessary message content.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Native messaging encryption and privacy
requirements.text: Search/indexing over encrypted content SHOULD occur locally or through another architecture that preserves the declared E2EE model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Disappearing messages
requirements.text: Connect MUST support disappearing-message policies at conversation and/or message scope.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Disappearing messages
requirements.text: Policies MAY include predefined and custom expiry periods and MUST expose the active expiry state visibly enough for participants to understand it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Disappearing messages
requirements.text: Expiry MUST be represented canonically and reconcile across authorised devices, including devices that were offline at the expiry time.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Disappearing messages
requirements.text: Expired content MUST be removed from ordinary conversation history and applicable local indexes/caches according to the declared lifecycle.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Disappearing messages
requirements.text: Connect MUST NOT claim that disappearing messages prevent screenshots, manual copying, external capture or information already legitimately disclosed outside the conversation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Disappearing messages
requirements.text: Quoted/replied-to message representations MUST NOT preserve the full expired content indefinitely unless an explicit retention/evidence rule requires it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Disappearing messages
requirements.text: Safety reports/evidence records that lawfully and transparently retain reported content are separate from ordinary disappearing-message history and MUST have their own access, purpose and retention policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > SMS and RCS
requirements.text: Connect MUST support SMS and RCS where the current platform, telephony stack, carrier/provider and user permissions allow it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > SMS and RCS
requirements.text: SMS/RCS identities and transport state MUST remain distinct from native Connect messaging.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > SMS and RCS
requirements.text: The UI MUST truthfully represent the protection of the actual transport used.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > SMS and RCS
requirements.text: Ordinary SMS MUST NOT be labelled end-to-end encrypted.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > SMS and RCS
requirements.text: RCS MUST show E2EE only when encryption has actually been negotiated/supported for that conversation and participant set.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > SMS and RCS
requirements.text: If an intended RCS message would fall back to SMS, any material change in privacy/security capability MUST be represented clearly enough that the user is not led to believe the stronger state still applies.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > SMS and RCS
requirements.text: Transport fallback MUST NOT reuse an E2EE badge/state from the prior route.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Voice and video calling
requirements.text: Connect MUST provide mature one-to-one and group voice/video calling with expected modern functionality including incoming/outgoing calls, ringing, missed calls, call history, join/leave/reconnect, participant roster, grid/speaker layouts, pin/spotlight where applicable, microphone mute/unmute, camera enable/disable, camera switching, input/output device selection, screen/window/application sharing, optional system-audio sharing where supported, reactions, raise hand, in-call text chat, picture-in-picture/full-screen and accessible keyboard/screen-reader controls.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Voice and video calling
requirements.text: Calls MUST use end-to-end encrypted media wherever the selected call architecture supports the native Connect trust model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Voice and video calling
requirements.text: Signalling and sensitive call state SHOULD receive equivalent or stronger protection where technically feasible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Voice and video calling
requirements.text: Infrastructure MUST NOT claim stronger privacy than the actual transport provides.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Voice and video calling
requirements.text: Microphone, camera and screen-capture permissions MUST be explicit, visible and revocable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Voice and video calling
requirements.text: Joining a call MUST NOT silently enable the camera or microphone contrary to the user's saved/default state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Voice and video calling
requirements.text: The UI MUST continuously and unmistakably show local mic/camera/screen-share state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Voice and video calling
requirements.text: Call infrastructure MUST minimise retained metadata, and self-hosted/private infrastructure SHOULD be supported where compatible with the donor/protocol architecture.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Voice and video calling
requirements.text: TURN/relay/direct-connect behaviour and the associated exposure of participant network addresses MUST be documented and privacy-aware.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Voice and video calling
requirements.text: Background blur, noise suppression, gain control, camera filters/effects, virtual backgrounds and similar media processing SHOULD run locally where technically practical.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Voice and video calling
requirements.text: A cosmetic filter MUST NOT silently upload raw camera/microphone content to an external processor.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Recording, transcription and AI participation
requirements.text: Starting recording MUST use a Request Recording workflow rather than an immediate unilateral record action.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Recording, transcription and AI participation
requirements.text: Before recording begins, every current participant MUST explicitly approve the recording request.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Recording, transcription and AI participation
requirements.text: Approval is scoped to that recording session and MUST NOT become a permanent blanket permission.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Recording, transcription and AI participation
requirements.text: When recording is active, all participants MUST receive a persistent, unmistakable recording indicator.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Recording, transcription and AI participation
requirements.text: A participant joining after recording has started MUST be informed before/while joining that recording is active and MUST explicitly acknowledge/approve participation under the recording state before their media is included.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Recording, transcription and AI participation
requirements.text: A new participant's refusal MUST prevent their media from being recorded and, where the architecture cannot isolate them, MUST pause/stop recording until consent is resolved.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Recording, transcription and AI participation
requirements.text: Recording state, requester, participant approvals, start/stop times and resulting artifact identity MUST be auditable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Recording, transcription and AI participation
requirements.text: Recordings MUST be stored as permissioned canonical artifacts with explicit owner/access/retention policy rather than hidden provider blobs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Recording, transcription and AI participation
requirements.text: Recording permission MUST NOT imply permission for transcription, AI summarisation or remote model processing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Recording, transcription and AI participation
requirements.text: Adding Dulche, an Agent, transcription service or other non-human processor to a human conversation/call MUST be visible to affected participants where it can receive their communication.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Contact and communication privacy controls
requirements.text: Connect MUST provide first-class Block, Mute and Contact Settings controls.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Contact and communication privacy controls
requirements.text: Blocking and muting MUST be semantically distinct: mute suppresses attention/notifications according to user policy; block prevents the blocked identity from contacting/interacting with the blocker through applicable Connect channels and MUST be enforced beyond merely hiding content locally.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Contact and communication privacy controls
requirements.text: Contact Settings MUST allow the user to control, where applicable, who can directly message them, call them, video call them, add/invite them to groups, see presence/last-active, see read receipts and access profile/contact fields.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Contact and communication privacy controls
requirements.text: Unknown contacts MAY be routed to message/contact requests rather than the primary inbox.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Contact and communication privacy controls
requirements.text: Per-conversation notification/mute controls, read-receipt controls, presence controls, privacy/discoverability controls and block lists MUST be available without requiring AI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Reporting and Trust & Safety
requirements.text: Connect MUST provide a first-class Report workflow for inappropriate, abusive, fraudulent or illegal content/behaviour.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Reporting and Trust & Safety
requirements.text: Reporting MUST be possible from messages, conversations, calls, contacts/accounts and relevant media where evidence is available.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Reporting and Trust & Safety
requirements.text: Because native Connect messaging is E2EE, routine server-side moderation MUST NOT silently scan all decrypted private conversations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Reporting and Trust & Safety
requirements.text: A participant-initiated report MAY deliberately disclose selected reported messages/media and the minimum necessary surrounding context/provenance to the Trust & Safety system.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Reporting and Trust & Safety
requirements.text: The reporting UI MUST make the disclosure scope understandable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Reporting and Trust & Safety
requirements.text: A Report MUST NOT automatically become a verified violation or count as an offence merely because it exists.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Reporting and Trust & Safety
requirements.text: Trust & Safety must distinguish Report, Incident and EnforcementAction as separate canonical objects.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Reporting and Trust & Safety
requirements.text: Prompt-like content inside evidence MUST NOT be able to override moderation policy or system instructions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Moderation AI
requirements.text: Connect MAY use an intelligent AI-assisted Trust & Safety evaluator to triage reports, correlate evidence, identify repeat patterns, create/maintain structured Incident records and recommend or apply policy-defined protective restrictions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Moderation AI
requirements.text: The moderation AI MUST NOT expose a direct free-form conversational prompt surface to ordinary users.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Moderation AI
requirements.text: Users interact through structured report/appeal flows; they MUST NOT be able to directly prompt the moderation model to punish another user.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Moderation AI
requirements.text: The evaluator SHOULD produce structured results including alleged policy category, evidence reviewed, provenance, confidence/uncertainty, severity, verified prior Incidents where policy permits, pattern/repetition state, recommended action, automatic-action eligibility and human-review requirement.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Moderation AI
requirements.text: User accusation volume alone MUST NOT be treated as proof.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Moderation AI
requirements.text: Automatic detection/evaluation MUST resist coordinated false-report campaigns, duplicate-report amplification, fabricated evidence where provenance can be checked, prompt injection within evidence and circular reliance on previous unverified allegations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Moderation AI
requirements.text: Dismissed/overturned reports/incidents MUST NOT continue increasing enforcement severity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Moderation AI
requirements.text: Protective restrictions MAY be applied quickly when needed to stop ongoing harm, including reporter-specific contact blocking, temporary DM/call restrictions, new-contact limits, invitation restrictions, media restrictions or rate limits.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Severe-offence ban threshold
requirements.text: Ordinary disagreements, unpopular opinions, isolated low-level rudeness or weak/ambiguous reports MUST NOT result in a Connect-wide ban.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Severe-offence ban threshold
requirements.text: Multiple unverified or dismissed reports MUST NOT accumulate as though they were convictions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Severe-offence ban threshold
requirements.text: Enforcement SHOULD be proportionate below the severe-ban threshold and MAY include warnings, temporary communication restrictions, feature-specific suspension, contact/request limits, group-invite restrictions, rate limiting or temporary account suspension according to policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Severe-offence ban threshold
requirements.text: Every ban MUST reference the applicable policy category, supporting IncidentIDs/evidence basis, decision source, effective time, duration/permanence, review status and appeal state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Severe-offence ban threshold
requirements.text: The system MUST preserve the distinction between evidence, analysis and final enforcement.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Severe-offence ban threshold
requirements.text: Permanent or long-duration account-wide sanctions SHOULD require stronger evidentiary confidence and/or human review according to severity and policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Severe-offence ban threshold
requirements.text: Clearly malicious automated/scam accounts with strong evidence MAY be restricted rapidly without artificial delay merely because the final action is severe.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Appeals
requirements.text: Affected users MUST have a clear appeal mechanism for significant restrictions and bans.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Appeals
requirements.text: Appeal review MUST inspect the evidence and enforcement decision rather than merely rerun the identical model prompt and automatically return the same result.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Appeals
requirements.text: Overturned enforcement MUST remove or appropriately quarantine the sanction's contribution to future escalation/ban-evasion logic.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Appeals
requirements.text: Audit history MAY retain the historical decision for accountability, but it MUST NOT continue operating as an active verified offence.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Ban-evasion and alternate-account detection
requirements.text: An active Connect ban MUST NOT be trivially circumventable by creating or switching to another account.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Ban-evasion and alternate-account detection
requirements.text: Connect MUST provide a privacy-preserving Ban Evasion Risk Engine capable of identifying likely alternate accounts used to evade an active severe sanction.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Ban-evasion and alternate-account detection
requirements.text: Detection MUST be purpose-limited to security/abuse enforcement and MUST comply with the Privacy Ceiling.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Ban-evasion and alternate-account detection
requirements.text: It SHOULD combine multiple relevant signals rather than relying on one simplistic identifier.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Ban-evasion and alternate-account detection
requirements.text: Signals MAY include verified account relationships, device/account linkage legitimately available to 9to1, authentication attributes, repeated malicious behavioural patterns, overlap of abuse targets, timing patterns, organisation relationships and payment/entitlement linkage where applicable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Ban-evasion and alternate-account detection
requirements.text: Shared IP address, household, school/workplace network, carrier NAT, VPN use or a shared device MUST NOT by itself establish that two accounts belong to the same banned person.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Ban-evasion and alternate-account detection
requirements.text: The engine MUST distinguish low-, medium- and high-confidence linkage.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Ban-evasion and alternate-account detection
requirements.text: Low-confidence matches SHOULD trigger additional verification, monitoring within permitted bounds or temporary protective limits rather than automatic permanent inheritance of the original ban.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Ban-evasion and alternate-account detection
requirements.text: High-confidence evidence tied to a severe active ban MAY cause the alternate account to inherit/continue the restriction according to policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Ban-evasion and alternate-account detection
requirements.text: Every suspected linkage MUST create a BanEvasionCase with evidence/signal references, original EnforcementActionID, confidence, decision and review/appeal state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Ban-evasion and alternate-account detection
requirements.text: Banned-account linkage MUST NOT depend on weakening E2EE or reading unrelated private messages.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Ban-evasion and alternate-account detection
requirements.text: Signals from an overturned/dismissed ban MUST be removed from active enforcement decisions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Ban-evasion and alternate-account detection
requirements.text: Anti-alt detection MUST NOT evolve into a general-purpose cross-service fingerprinting system unrelated to preventing sanction evasion.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > AI and encrypted communication boundary
requirements.text: Dulche MAY assist with permitted Connect tasks such as drafting, summarisation, search, action extraction and organisation, but encrypted communication content is not automatically AI context.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > AI and encrypted communication boundary
requirements.text: The user/organisation policy and the local/cloud Privacy Ceiling determine what content may be exposed.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > AI and encrypted communication boundary
requirements.text: A local AI route MAY process authorised content locally according to permissions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > AI and encrypted communication boundary
requirements.text: Sending decrypted chat/call/email content to a cloud model requires an authorised cloud-processing route and MUST NOT occur merely because the cloud model is the global fallback.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > AI and encrypted communication boundary
requirements.text: Agents MUST be emailable, callable and textable through Connect.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > AI and encrypted communication boundary
requirements.text: Agents MUST appear as addressable Agent contacts rather than requiring users to open a separate Agent chat before contacting them.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > AI and encrypted communication boundary
requirements.text: Channel addresses/endpoints MUST resolve to the same canonical Agent identity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > AI and encrypted communication boundary
requirements.text: Incoming contact MUST route to that Agent and its authorised runtime; responses MUST return through the relevant Connect channel with conversation/call/run correlation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > AI and encrypted communication boundary
requirements.text: A message or call from a third party MUST NOT automatically acquire the account owner's permissions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > AI and encrypted communication boundary
requirements.text: Unsupported or disconnected transports MUST be reported accurately.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Connect Agent-channel API and acceptance
requirements.text: Tests MUST deliver an email, call and text to the intended canonical Agent through each supported configured route and verify its response on that route; cover revoked caller access, disconnected or unsupported transport, failed delivery and prevention of duplicate external sends.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Connect Agent-channel API and acceptance
requirements.text: A required route lacking a working supported implementation remains an explicit gap, not a completed parity claim.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Connect API and events
requirements.text: Connect MUST expose typed APIs for conversations/messages, organisations/memberships/roles, contacts/privacy controls, calls, SMS/RCS routing where supported, reporting, safety state and user-authorised actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Connect API and events
requirements.text: Minimum Connect API families MUST include conversation list/get/create/update/membership, message send/edit/delete/react/thread, contact/block/mute/settings, organisation/membership/role, call start/join/leave/media-state/screen-share/record-request/record-state, report/create/status/appeal, and change/event subscriptions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Connect API and events
requirements.text: Every consequential action MUST use stable IDs, structured results, revision/conflict semantics and the global permission/audit contract.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Connect API and events
requirements.text: Trust & Safety internal APIs MUST be separately permissioned from ordinary client APIs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Connect API and events
requirements.text: Direct user clients MUST NOT receive privileged moderation-model prompt access or arbitrary enforcement mutation authority.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Failure and recovery
requirements.text: Connect MUST provide structured failures including ConversationNotFound, MembershipDenied, EncryptionStateUnavailable, DeviceNotTrusted, KeyRecoveryRequired, TransportUnavailable, SMSFallbackRequired, CallUnavailable, MediaPermissionDenied, RecordingConsentRequired, RecordingConsentDeclined, ParticipantConsentPending, ReportNotFound, EvidenceUnavailable, EnforcementDenied, AppealUnavailable, BanEvasionReviewRequired and ProviderCapabilityUnsupported in addition to global errors.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Failure and recovery
requirements.text: Network interruption MUST preserve unsent messages/call state truthfully, reconcile delivered/read state after reconnect and avoid duplicate sends.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Failure and recovery
requirements.text: Encryption/session recovery MUST NOT silently reset conversation security or create a new unverified device identity without disclosure.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Product role and donor strategy
requirements.text: It MUST be a fully capable manual email client with AI disabled or unavailable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Product role and donor strategy
requirements.text: AI is additive: it may summarise, search, draft, rewrite and triage, but core reading, composition, sending, organisation, search, offline use and account management MUST remain directly usable without AI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Product role and donor strategy
requirements.text: Donor reuse MUST comply with the selected source version and licensing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Product role and donor strategy
requirements.text: Legacy donor chrome, menus, dialogs, pane styling or dated interaction patterns MUST NOT be reproduced merely for parity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Product role and donor strategy
requirements.text: The final product MUST be a modern, clean, native CUI Mail interface designed for 9to1.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Product role and donor strategy
requirements.text: A Mail donor-parity manifest MUST identify the selected donor revision and classify applicable capabilities as Preserve, Replace with 9to1-native equivalent or Not applicable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Modern CUI shell and responsive layout
requirements.text: The default desktop layout MUST use a clean three-pane structure: navigation/account sidebar, message/conversation list and reading pane.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Modern CUI shell and responsive layout
requirements.text: Visual separation MUST be subtle and CUI-native rather than relying on heavy boxes, legacy toolbars or nested window chrome.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Modern CUI shell and responsive layout
requirements.text: Message content should receive the majority of visual emphasis.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Modern CUI shell and responsive layout
requirements.text: Users MUST be able to select reading-pane right, reading-pane bottom or reading-pane off, plus supported density options.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Modern CUI shell and responsive layout
requirements.text: Smaller windows MUST responsively collapse the layout into two-pane or single-pane navigation without squeezing unreadable columns.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Modern CUI shell and responsive layout
requirements.text: The message list MUST prioritise sender/avatar or initials, subject, concise preview, timestamp, unread/important state and attachment/category indicators.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Modern CUI shell and responsive layout
requirements.text: Low-frequency controls MAY appear on hover/selection while common quick actions such as archive, delete, star and snooze remain directly discoverable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Modern CUI shell and responsive layout
requirements.text: The reading pane MUST present a compact sender/recipient/date header, clear reply/reply-all/forward/other actions and an uncluttered message body.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Modern CUI shell and responsive layout
requirements.text: Long conversations MUST support collapsing older messages/quoted sections without losing access to full content.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Modern CUI shell and responsive layout
requirements.text: The final client MUST not expose donor-native UI surfaces.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Modern CUI shell and responsive layout
requirements.text: Settings, account management, compose, security prompts and advanced inspection must all use 9to1 CUI unless an OS-level credential/security dialog is explicitly required.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Sidebar and navigation
requirements.text: Mail MUST provide a unified top-level navigation including Unified Inbox, Starred/Favourites, Snoozed, Drafts, Sent, Scheduled, Outbox, Archive, Junk and Trash where the effective connected-account capabilities permit them.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Sidebar and navigation
requirements.text: Unified views are query/projection surfaces over canonical provider/account messages and MUST NOT duplicate messages into a separate mailbox.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Sidebar and navigation
requirements.text: Provider-native structures MUST be preserved.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Sidebar and navigation
requirements.text: Gmail-style labels, Outlook categories/folders and generic IMAP folders MUST NOT be flattened into one simplistic hierarchy when that would break provider behaviour.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Account and provider model
requirements.text: Every connected mailbox MUST have stable AccountID identity independent of mutable email address/display name.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Account and provider model
requirements.text: MailAccount MUST store at least provider type, provider account identity, primary address/display name, supported capability set, authentication reference, sync configuration, signature configuration and sending configuration.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Account and provider model
requirements.text: Mail MUST support generic IMAP + SMTP as a baseline and provider-native adapters where beneficial, including Gmail/Google and Outlook/Microsoft.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Account and provider model
requirements.text: Provider adapters MAY expose richer push, label, thread, archive, snooze, scheduled-send or search behaviours while remaining behind the common Mail contract.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Account and provider model
requirements.text: Provider capabilities MUST be discovered/declared explicitly, including labels vs folders, archive, snooze, scheduled send, native search, push/change feed, undo send, aliases/from identities, read receipts, encryption/security features and provider-specific actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Account and provider model
requirements.text: Unsupported actions MUST be hidden/disabled or return ProviderCapabilityUnsupported rather than appearing functional.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Account and provider model
requirements.text: Credentials/tokens MUST be stored through secure credential references.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Account and provider model
requirements.text: Token refresh, revoked access, reauthentication, app-password/provider-password flows and certificate errors MUST be handled without deleting valid local cached mail.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Message, thread and folder identity
requirements.text: Mail MUST maintain stable local canonical identities for AccountID-scoped messages and threads.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Message, thread and folder identity
requirements.text: Message records MUST include MessageID, AccountID, provider-native message ID, Internet Message-ID where present, ThreadID/provider conversation identity where applicable, folder/label state, timestamps, sender/recipients, flags and provider change/revision token where available.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Message, thread and folder identity
requirements.text: Internet Message-ID MUST NOT be assumed globally unique enough to serve as the sole database identity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Message, thread and folder identity
requirements.text: Provider-native thread identity MUST be preserved when available.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Message, thread and folder identity
requirements.text: Generic IMAP MAY use a deterministic local threading model, but Mail MUST distinguish local grouping from provider-native conversation identity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Message, thread and folder identity
requirements.text: Mail MUST NOT automatically merge threads across separate accounts solely because subjects or Message-ID relationships appear similar.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Message rendering and privacy
requirements.text: Mail MUST safely render plain-text and HTML email, inline images, quoted replies, signatures and attachments.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Message rendering and privacy
requirements.text: HTML MUST be sanitised; arbitrary message script/executable application code MUST NOT execute in the trusted Mail surface.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Message rendering and privacy
requirements.text: Remote images/external tracking resources MUST be blocked, privacy-proxied or otherwise privacy-controlled by default according to Mail privacy settings.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Message rendering and privacy
requirements.text: The UI MUST provide a clear per-message/per-sender Load remote content/trust action rather than silently leaking message opens.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Message rendering and privacy
requirements.text: Mail MAY offer tracking-protection features such as known tracking-pixel blocking or privacy-preserving remote-image proxying, but protection state MUST be visible and breakage must be recoverable by the user.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Compose and drafts
requirements.text: Compose MUST use a clean CUI editor that can operate as a focused pane/window and provides From identity/account, To, Cc, Bcc, subject, rich-text body, plain-text mode, attachments, inline images, signatures, reply/reply-all/forward and provider-supported message options.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Compose and drafts
requirements.text: Recipient fields SHOULD progressively disclose Cc/Bcc rather than permanently consuming space.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Compose and drafts
requirements.text: The composer SHOULD use Home’s Shared Productivity Engine for supported rich-text primitives, while exporting through an email-compatible formatting pipeline that produces valid email-safe HTML plus a plain-text alternative.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Compose and drafts
requirements.text: Unsupported rich shared objects MUST be explicitly converted/attached rather than silently mangled.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Compose and drafts
requirements.text: Drafts MUST autosave and survive app/process restart.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Compose and drafts
requirements.text: Local/provider draft conflicts MUST preserve both revisions or surface a conflict rather than silently overwriting newer user text.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Compose and drafts
requirements.text: FromIdentity MUST be separate from AccountID so provider-supported aliases can define address, display name, Reply-To and signature independently.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Attachments and Files integration
requirements.text: Attachments MUST expose stable AttachmentID scoped to MessageID plus filename, MIME type, size, Content-ID where relevant, download/cache state and security state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Attachments and Files integration
requirements.text: Attachment bytes MAY hydrate on demand according to offline/cache policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Attachments and Files integration
requirements.text: Attachment actions MUST integrate with Files/Home handlers, including Open, Save, Save to 9to1 Drive, Save all, Add to Board and Open in compatible owning 9to1 app where applicable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Attachments and Files integration
requirements.text: Attachment saving creates a normal Files item and MUST not alter the original message.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Attachments and Files integration
requirements.text: Compose MUST support Attach from Files across local files, 9to1 Drive and authorised connected providers.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Attachments and Files integration
requirements.text: A future/share-link mode MAY send a hosted Files link instead of attaching bytes, but it MUST be an explicit access-semantic change rather than an invisible optimisation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Sync, push and offline behaviour
requirements.text: Mail sync MUST use the fastest reliable provider mechanism available: provider push/change streams, webhooks or IMAP IDLE/incremental change tokens first; periodic polling/full mailbox scans only as fallback/recovery.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Sync, push and offline behaviour
requirements.text: Mail MUST provide Sync all, Sync this account, Sync this folder, Retry failed sync, Pause sync and Resume sync controls plus clear sync diagnostics including last successful contact, pending operations and errors.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Sync, push and offline behaviour
requirements.text: Offline use MUST support configurable caching of headers, recent/full message bodies and attachments on demand, plus selected folders/messages available offline.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Sync, push and offline behaviour
requirements.text: Offline-safe mutations including read/unread, star, label/category, move, archive, delete/restore, draft updates and queued sends MUST enter a durable operation journal and reconcile on reconnect using provider change tokens/revisions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Send pipeline, Outbox and Undo Send
requirements.text: Outgoing messages MUST have explicit lifecycle states including Draft, Queued, Sending, Sent, Failed and Cancelled.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Send pipeline, Outbox and Undo Send
requirements.text: An offline Send enters Outbox/Queued and MUST NOT be represented as Sent until the provider accepts the message.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Send pipeline, Outbox and Undo Send
requirements.text: Mail MUST support client-side Undo Send through a configurable local hold delay before provider submission, even when a provider has no native undo.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Send pipeline, Outbox and Undo Send
requirements.text: After irreversible provider submission, Mail MUST NOT claim that the send remains undoable unless the provider genuinely supports cancellation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Send pipeline, Outbox and Undo Send
requirements.text: Send failures MUST remain visible/retryable in Outbox with the actual provider/transport error and must not silently discard the draft/message.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Scheduled send
requirements.text: Scheduled send MUST use provider-native scheduling when available.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Scheduled send
requirements.text: Otherwise Mail may use a reliable 9to1 server/cloud scheduler or device-local scheduler only when its execution guarantees are accurately represented.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Scheduled send
requirements.text: The UI MUST identify execution location/guarantee as Provider scheduled, 9to1 cloud scheduled or This device scheduled.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Scheduled send
requirements.text: Device-local schedules MUST clearly state that execution depends on the device/runtime being available; they MUST NOT masquerade as guaranteed server scheduling.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Search and smart views
requirements.text: Mail search MUST support sender, recipient, subject, message body where indexed/available, attachment name, date range, account, folder/label, read/unread, attachment presence, categories/labels and starred state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Search and smart views
requirements.text: Provider-native search MAY be used but cached/offline content MUST also support local indexed search where policy permits.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Search and smart views
requirements.text: Users MUST be able to save supported queries as smart views/folders.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Search and smart views
requirements.text: Smart views are dynamic queries over canonical messages and MUST NOT duplicate messages.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Rules and automation integration
requirements.text: Mail MUST support convenient message rules/filters for provider/local-supported triggers such as sender, recipient, subject and message metadata with actions such as move, label/category, mark read, star, notify or hand off to Automations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Rules and automation integration
requirements.text: Cross-app consequential workflows MUST be represented through Automations/typed app APIs rather than hidden arbitrary scripts inside Mail rules.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Rules and automation integration
requirements.text: Rule execution MUST be auditable and idempotent where replay is possible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Snooze, archive and delete semantics
requirements.text: Snooze MUST hide/deprioritise a message/thread until a specified time and restore it to the appropriate attention view.
