requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Snooze, archive and delete semantics
requirements.text: Provider-native snooze is preferred where available; a 9to1 metadata-layer implementation MAY be used only if it preserves provider consistency.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Snooze, archive and delete semantics
requirements.text: Archive and Delete MUST be provider-aware.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Snooze, archive and delete semantics
requirements.text: Archive may mean removing an Inbox label or moving to a configured Archive folder depending on provider.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Snooze, archive and delete semantics
requirements.text: Delete MUST distinguish remove-current-label/folder, move to Trash and permanent delete where the provider exposes those concepts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Signatures, aliases and contacts
requirements.text: Mail MUST support per-account and per-FromIdentity signatures with rich-text plus plain-text fallback.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Signatures, aliases and contacts
requirements.text: Signature selection may be automatic per identity but remains user-editable in the composer.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Signatures, aliases and contacts
requirements.text: Recipient autocomplete SHOULD use authorised shared Contacts/people services and provider contacts where configured, with local recipient history as fallback.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Signatures, aliases and contacts
requirements.text: Mail MUST NOT make its message database the canonical contacts store.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Notifications
requirements.text: Mail MUST publish typed notifications through Home Notifications for events such as new important mail, send failure, authentication required and significant sync error.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Notifications
requirements.text: Notifications MUST deep-link to the exact AccountID/ThreadID/MessageID or relevant settings surface.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Notifications
requirements.text: Mail MUST NOT implement a second incompatible notification centre; Home owns notification history/preferences/OS bridging.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Persistent AI bar and AI action boundary
requirements.text: Mail MUST host the global persistent bottom AI bar.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Persistent AI bar and AI action boundary
requirements.text: Its context snapshot may include AccountID, current folder/view, selected MessageIDs/ThreadIDs, DraftID and selected recipients/content according to current permissions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Persistent AI bar and AI action boundary
requirements.text: Supported AI experiences MAY include summarise thread, identify action items, draft/rewrite a reply, conversational mailbox search, triage suggestions and creation of typed cross-app actions such as Planner items or saving attachments.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Persistent AI bar and AI action boundary
requirements.text: Ordinary conversational AI MUST NOT silently send email merely because it generated a draft.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Persistent AI bar and AI action boundary
requirements.text: An explicitly authorised Agent/Automation MAY send autonomously only when its effective permission/trust scope permits Mail.Send.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Persistent AI bar and AI action boundary
requirements.text: Mail content provided to Dulche MUST obey local/cloud privacy policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Persistent AI bar and AI action boundary
requirements.text: Selecting a mailbox/thread MUST NOT implicitly upload the whole mailbox to a cloud model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Persistent AI bar and AI action boundary
requirements.text: Context scope such as selected messages, current thread or explicit mailbox search MUST be represented and permission-filtered.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Security, phishing and remote-content safety
requirements.text: Mail MUST provide conventional safety signals without claiming infallible detection, including clear actual sender address vs display name, suspicious-link/attachment warnings, executable attachment restrictions and provider/header authentication information such as SPF/DKIM/DMARC results where available.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Security, phishing and remote-content safety
requirements.text: Read receipts MUST require user/provider policy approval and MUST NOT be automatically sent solely because a sender requested one.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Security, phishing and remote-content safety
requirements.text: Provider spam/junk systems SHOULD be used when available; generic accounts may use local classification/rules.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Security, phishing and remote-content safety
requirements.text: Mark Junk/Not Junk MUST update provider state when supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > OpenPGP, S/MIME and advanced mail features
requirements.text: Where supported by the selected mature donor source and target platform, Mail MUST preserve applicable OpenPGP and S/MIME signing/encryption workflows, certificate/key management and message verification/decryption behaviour unless a documented parity exception exists.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > OpenPGP, S/MIME and advanced mail features
requirements.text: Advanced message inspection MUST expose message source/raw MIME, headers, Internet Message-ID and provider/debug details without making these advanced controls dominate the default reading experience.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Print and export
requirements.text: Messages/threads MUST support print and supported export such as PDF, .eml and applicable text/HTML forms.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Print and export
requirements.text: Export MUST preserve attachments only when the selected format/workflow explicitly supports them.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Mail API
requirements.text: Every additional user-visible Mail operation and preserved donor capability MUST have an equivalent typed API/domain action under the global API-parity rule.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Failure behaviour
requirements.text: Mail MUST return structured failures including AccountNotFound, AuthenticationRequired, ProviderUnavailable, ProviderCapabilityUnsupported, Offline, SyncFailed, MessageNotFound, ThreadNotFound, DraftConflict, SendFailed, SendRejected, AttachmentUnavailable, MailboxQuotaExceeded, RateLimited, PermissionDenied, InvalidRecipient, EncryptionKeyUnavailable, CertificateError and structured partial bulk outcomes in addition to the global error contract.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Platform behaviour
requirements.text: Native Windows/9to1-OS Mail MUST support configured local caching/offline behaviour and Home-integrated notifications/files/model services.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Connect and Mail > Mail > Platform behaviour
requirements.text: Web Mail uses authenticated server/provider APIs and the same canonical account/message identities where available, but browser storage/offline capabilities MUST be capability-negotiated rather than assumed identical to native.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Cards
requirements.text: Include a visual editor, plus the AI bar and other things required by acceptance criteria and general rules (eg CUI).

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Cards
requirements.text: Cards should be simple to use and support bulk editing/creation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Cards
requirements.text: There should also be a floating search bar at the top of the screen, and a sidebar to change subjects/topics and navigate easily.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Cards
requirements.text: Cards should support markdown visual formatting (bold, headers, italics, etc), font changing, background colour, image/graph insertion, and free drawing on the card.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Cards
requirements.text: Cards should have both an editable front side and back side.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Cards
requirements.text: The Cards app should also have a viewer/editor mode, changing how you interact with the cards.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Cards
requirements.text: Users MUST be able to group cards by set, topic or a custom grouping configuration and change that view from the sidebar context menu or Cards settings.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Cards
requirements.text: Ratings MUST persist as personal review evidence and update Study progress when a valid topic link exists, as specified in LE-08 and LE-10.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Cards
requirements.text: It MUST ship through the normal app catalogue, modular installer, Files/open-with and registered preview/editor paths, with the global launch screen, settings, permissions and contextual AI bar.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Cards
requirements.text: A platform constraint must be declared and tested, not hidden behind an empty app shell or assumed mobile fallback.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Cards
requirements.text: Shared deck content and a user's ReviewRecord are distinct: review state records principal, CardID, optional TopicID, red/amber/green rating, evidence type and reviewed-at time without publishing another learner's private progress.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Cards
requirements.text: Front/back content MUST preserve the specified formatting, font choice, background colour, images, graphs and freehand ink as editable structured data through the Shared Productivity Engine and owning object contracts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Cards
requirements.text: Import/export reports unsupported constructs and preserves the source; it does not silently discard unknown required fields.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Cards
requirements.text: A rating MUST persist on the card's personal review record.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Cards
requirements.text: When a valid Study topic link exists, it MUST submit attributed evidence to the existing Study service and update linked views.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Cards
requirements.text: Inline Spaces flashcards and Revision Bank entries must be able to open/save the same canonical set.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Cards
requirements.text: Large sets MUST virtualise card views and bound image/graph/ink caches.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Product role and runtime principle
requirements.text: Forms MUST support simple no-code creation without exposing advanced complexity by default, but the product ceiling MUST NOT be limited to the capabilities of conventional survey builders.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Canonical project model
requirements.text: Field has stable FieldID, FieldType, label/help/content, response schema, required/validation state, appearance/layout state, marking configuration where applicable, Data binding where applicable and Revision.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Builder workspace and preview
requirements.text: Common tasks MUST NOT require the node editor.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Builder workspace and preview
requirements.text: Preview MUST NOT create a separate approximation that can diverge from published behaviour.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Core field and component types
requirements.text: Custom/reusable Form Components may contain multiple child fields and layout/logic, for example Address, Person details, Emergency contact or Rating + comment.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Table input and repeating structured responses
requirements.text: Forms MUST provide a real TableInput field, not merely a multiple-choice grid.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Table input and repeating structured responses
requirements.text: TableInput defines typed columns, optional fixed rows, respondent-added rows, minimum/maximum row count, required columns, per-cell/row validation, calculated columns, dropdown/reference columns, duplicate rules and Data bindings.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Table input and repeating structured responses
requirements.text: A table input may write multiple related Data records rather than serialising an entire table into one string.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Table input and repeating structured responses
requirements.text: For example an expense report may submit one parent Report record plus one related Expense record per entered row.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Native modes: Form, Test and Quiz
requirements.text: After each answer the runtime may show correct/incorrect/partial state, explanation/feedback and then advance according to mode settings.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Native modes: Form, Test and Quiz
requirements.text: Mode semantics MUST be expressed through the common runtime/state system rather than three independent engines.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Custom modes and state-machine runtime
requirements.text: Built-in Form/Test/Quiz behaviour SHOULD be representable as first-party presets over the same runtime concepts so custom modes do not fork core response, Data, accessibility or publishing infrastructure.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Marking engine and multiple accepted answers
requirements.text: Normalised matching can optionally ignore case, trim/collapse whitespace, normalise Unicode and ignore selected punctuation/diacritics according to author settings.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Marking engine and multiple accepted answers
requirements.text: Example: a question asking for the name of the central processor may accept 'CPU' and 'Central Processing Unit' as equivalent accepted answers without requiring AI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Regex validation and marking
requirements.text: The builder MUST include a regex tester with live example inputs, invalid-pattern diagnostics and clear indication of full-match versus partial-match semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Regex validation and marking
requirements.text: Forms MUST NOT execute unbounded or unsafe regex behaviour in a way that can freeze the runtime; implementations use bounded/safe regex execution appropriate to the platform.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > AI, human and hybrid marking
requirements.text: AI marking uses a structured rubric with expected concepts/criteria, maximum points, optional sample correct/partial/incorrect answers, required/forbidden concepts and feedback policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > AI, human and hybrid marking
requirements.text: Marking mode may be deterministic automatic, mathematical/symbolic, AI, manual human or hybrid.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > AI, human and hybrid marking
requirements.text: Hybrid workflows can let deterministic rules resolve obvious answers, invoke AI for unresolved open responses and optionally require human moderation before release.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Partial credit, grading and feedback
requirements.text: Assessments support points, weighted questions, partial credit, criterion/rubric scoring, optional penalties where explicitly configured and section/category subtotals.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > LaTeX and visual mathematics editor
requirements.text: Forms MUST provide first-class mathematical authoring.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > LaTeX and visual mathematics editor
requirements.text: MathExpression uses LaTeX-compatible canonical representation but can be edited through a visual equation editor so authors/respondents are not required to know LaTeX.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Graph plotter and graph-response questions
requirements.text: Forms MUST include a native mathematical graph plotter/editor for quiz/test content.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Graph plotter and graph-response questions
requirements.text: MathExpression, GraphDefinition and related primitives SHOULD be reusable shared mathematical objects across Forms, Write, Present and other 9to1 surfaces rather than privately reinvented.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Question banks, randomisation, attempts and timing
requirements.text: Retry policies may target only incorrect questions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Question banks, randomisation, attempts and timing
requirements.text: Server-authoritative timing is required for multiplayer and integrity-sensitive modes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Forms and Data bidirectional integration
requirements.text: A FormField may bind to a stable Data TableID/FieldID rather than a physical spreadsheet column letter.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Forms and Data bidirectional integration
requirements.text: Data may also define or evolve Form fields.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Forms and Data bidirectional integration
requirements.text: Forms changes may similarly propose/add Data fields where the binding policy permits.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Data schema synchronisation policies
requirements.text: Schema synchronisation MUST be migration-aware.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Data schema synchronisation policies
requirements.text: Deleting or changing a Data field that has historical Form responses MUST NOT delete or reinterpret historical answers silently.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Full node editor and logic graph
requirements.text: Forms MUST expose the full shared 9to1 Node Graph Framework for advanced behaviour.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Full node editor and logic graph
requirements.text: Graph validation MUST detect incompatible ports, unreachable states where knowable, missing targets, cycles that would create uncontrolled update loops and client/server trust-boundary violations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Form events, conditions and actions
requirements.text: Actions include show/hide, enable/disable, required/optional, set/calculated value, jump to page/state, show message/content, add/remove repeating item, populate options, perform permitted Data lookup, trigger authorised Automation, mark/score, submit/block submission and custom-mode state transitions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Form events, conditions and actions
requirements.text: Security-critical validation and consequential actions MUST execute or be verified server-side; client-side visibility logic alone cannot be treated as an access-control or integrity boundary.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Appearance, theme and layout system
requirements.text: Forms MUST provide substantially deeper appearance control than conventional survey builders while preserving responsive accessibility.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Appearance, theme and layout system
requirements.text: Greater design freedom MUST NOT allow the form author to bypass minimum accessibility constraints such as semantic labels, focus order, contrast, tap targets or colour-independent state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Reusable components and templates
requirements.text: Reusable components preserve structured child fields, validation, layout and optional logic while allowing controlled instance overrides.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Publishing, versions and response compatibility
requirements.text: Editing Draft MUST NOT mutate the currently published experience until the author publishes/activates the new version according to policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Publishing, versions and response compatibility
requirements.text: Publishing states include at least Draft, Published/Accepting responses and Closed, with optional scheduled open/close where the platform supports it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Response model, save/resume and editing
requirements.text: Historical answer values MUST remain attached to the field/version schema that produced them rather than being reinterpreted based only on the latest field label.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Multiplayer live-session runtime
requirements.text: Typical first-party session states include Lobby, Starting, QuestionActive, Marking/Reveal, RoundTransition and Finished, but custom modes may define richer state machines using the same runtime.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Joining, teams and host control
requirements.text: Live sessions support short join codes, QR/share links, CAKE ID authenticated joining, guest nickname joining where allowed, private/invite-only sessions, organisation/class restrictions, maximum participants, late-join rules and optional spectators.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Joining, teams and host control
requirements.text: Team scoring/answer semantics may use one nominated answer, shared answer, majority vote, fastest member, average/aggregate scoring or custom graph-defined policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Conversational and interview modes
requirements.text: Custom modes may create turn-based conversational experiences such as job interviews, oral quizzes, panel discussions or AI quizmaster sessions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Conversational and interview modes
requirements.text: The interviewer can be an authorised human or configured AI agent; next questions may depend on prior structured answers/context.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Conversational and interview modes
requirements.text: Conversational responses are stored as structured turn/question/answer records with speaker/participant identity and optional rubric results, not only one giant transcript.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Multiplayer timing, reconnection and fairness
requirements.text: Clients MUST NOT decide whether an answer arrived before timeout, who buzzed first, the final score or whether a participant is eliminated.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Multiplayer timing, reconnection and fairness
requirements.text: Speed scoring MUST use a documented server-side policy and SHOULD avoid pretending millisecond differences are perfectly fair when network latency materially affects participants.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Multiplayer timing, reconnection and fairness
requirements.text: A short connection loss MUST NOT silently erase prior responses or create a duplicate participant.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Anti-cheat and assessment integrity
requirements.text: Forms MUST provide configurable anti-cheat/integrity controls, with stronger options available for Tests and live assessments while making clear that browser-based controls reduce opportunities but cannot guarantee that cheating is impossible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Anti-cheat and assessment integrity
requirements.text: Such signals MUST NOT automatically prove misconduct; they are contextual evidence and may be unreliable on some platforms.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Anti-cheat and assessment integrity
requirements.text: High-integrity deployments MAY integrate approved kiosk/lockdown or proctoring capabilities where separately configured, supported, legally permitted and appropriately disclosed/consented.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Anti-cheat and assessment integrity
requirements.text: Forms MUST NOT secretly access camera, microphone, screen or other sensitive capabilities.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Anti-cheat and assessment integrity
requirements.text: Server-side validation, marking, attempt state and scoring MUST not trust client-supplied authority.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Anti-cheat and assessment integrity
requirements.text: Question/answer payload delivery SHOULD minimise unnecessary early exposure: the runtime need not send future protected questions/correct answers to clients before they are authorised to see them.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Live scoring and AI/human judging
requirements.text: ScorePolicy is structured and inspectable; speed bonuses are optional.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Live scoring and AI/human judging
requirements.text: The runtime MUST NOT silently disadvantage a participant because one model call completed more slowly.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Scoreboards and participant views
requirements.text: Scoreboards may show full live ranking, top N, team standings, personal position only, anonymous ranking, knockout/bracket/lives state or remain hidden until the end.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Privacy, abuse prevention and public access
requirements.text: Responder identity requirements and privacy/consent text must be explicit.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Privacy, abuse prevention and public access
requirements.text: Submission events MUST NOT leak response content to Automations, hosts or integrations that lack the required permission.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Automation and typed events
requirements.text: Events expose stable IDs and minimal required metadata.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Accessibility
requirements.text: Builder and published runtime MUST be keyboard-operable and screen-reader compatible for field entry, navigation, maths editor alternatives, graph-response controls, table input, validation, quiz feedback and multiplayer participation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Accessibility
requirements.text: State MUST NOT rely on colour alone.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Accessibility
requirements.text: Graph/math questions provide accessible textual/equation representations and non-pointer input paths for required operations where feasible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Accessibility
requirements.text: Multiplayer score/rank changes should not create unusable constant announcements; meaningful state updates are summarised appropriately.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Performance and realtime behaviour
requirements.text: Published forms load only the assets/question state required for the current permitted experience.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Performance and realtime behaviour
requirements.text: One slow participant or AI-marking task MUST NOT freeze the whole host interface.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Recovery and failure behaviour
requirements.text: A failed publish MUST leave the prior published version available unless explicitly withdrawn.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Forms > Platform capability behaviour
requirements.text: A platform that lacks a configured capability exposes CapabilityUnavailable or a documented fallback; it MUST NOT silently change answer schema, marking or assessment-integrity semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Product role
requirements.text: AI Studio MUST support both project-backed artifacts and direct editing of canonical Dulche entities.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Navigation and landing page
requirements.text: AI Studio MUST use a clean persistent sidebar organised into Home, Projects, Build, Test & Debug, Resources and Templates.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Navigation and landing page
requirements.text: Build MUST expose Harnesses, Agents and Tools.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Navigation and landing page
requirements.text: Test & Debug MUST expose Playground, Evaluations, Test Suites and Replay.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Navigation and landing page
requirements.text: Resources MUST expose Schemas, Model Routers, Generative UI and Run Profiles.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Navigation and landing page
requirements.text: The landing page MUST provide prominent New Harness, New Agent and New Tool actions plus Recent, Favourites/Pinned, Templates, search and Open/Import where applicable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Navigation and landing page
requirements.text: Search, Recent, Favourites and Templates MUST use real persisted metadata/entities and MUST NOT be static mock content.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Project model
requirements.text: Every AI Studio project MUST have stable ProjectID, ProjectType, Name, Version, CreatedAt, ModifiedAt, owner/scope, project files/resources, dependency references, permission metadata and revision history.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Project model
requirements.text: In the current release scope ProjectType MUST distinguish at least Harness and Tool.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Project model
requirements.text: Display names are not identities and MAY be duplicated.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Project model
requirements.text: Opening a project MUST NOT automatically execute model/tool work.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Project model
requirements.text: Project-backed artifacts MUST support create, open, save, duplicate, rename, history/versioning, validate, test, export/import where applicable, delete/recover and dependency inspection through typed APIs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Harness Builder
requirements.text: A new Harness MUST start from a functional selected template or validated baseline rather than an empty non-working shell.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Harness Builder
requirements.text: A Harness definition MUST be able to configure model/provider policies, prompts/instructions, context/session handling, tools, persistent Dulche Agents, Dulche Subagents/parallelisation, Skills, Plugins, MCP capabilities, permissions, budgets/limits, checkpoints/recovery, logging/Action Graph, structured outputs, Generative UI and supported APIs/entry points.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Harness Builder
requirements.text: Harness Builder MUST distinguish persistent Den-backed Dulche Agents from transient Dulche Subagents.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Harness Builder
requirements.text: Harnesses MAY invoke both where allowed, but they are separate identity, memory and lifecycle concepts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Harness Builder
requirements.text: Generated/configured Harness source and configuration MUST remain inspectable/editable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Harness Builder
requirements.text: Harness Builder MUST NOT lock the user into an opaque private runtime that cannot be reproduced, validated or debugged.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Harness Builder
requirements.text: Harness projects MUST support Preview/Test using the same Dulche runtime contracts used by normal execution.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Harness Builder
requirements.text: Test UI MUST expose the effective model/provider, tools, Agents/Subagents, permissions, selected context, usage/timing, Action Graph, structured errors and outputs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Harness Builder > Harness advanced graph
requirements.text: Harness Builder MAY use the Home-owned Node Graph Framework for advanced orchestration.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Harness Builder > Harness advanced graph
requirements.text: Supported graph logic may include request/event entry points, routing/classification, conditionals, model selection, Agent invocation, Subagent fan-out/merge, tools, retries, approvals, state and typed outputs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Harness Builder > Harness advanced graph
requirements.text: Basic Harness creation MUST remain possible without graph editing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Agent Builder
requirements.text: It creates and edits the canonical Dulche Agent entity stored in Den; it MUST NOT create a separate incompatible AI Studio-only Agent project or use AI Studio as the Agent runtime host.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Agent Builder
requirements.text: Agent Builder MUST follow a Workspace-Agents-style structured editing workflow rather than a GPT-style conversational creation wizard.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Agent Builder
requirements.text: The actual Agent configuration is visible and editable directly from the beginning; AI assistance may modify that configuration through typed Agent/graph APIs but MUST NOT hide the resulting state behind an opaque builder conversation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Agent Builder
requirements.text: The primary editor header MUST provide updated/save state plus Automations, Preview, Share and overflow actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Agent Builder
requirements.text: The default-visible configuration sections MUST be Plugins / Connectors, Skills and Knowledge / Files, followed by a collapsed More Options disclosure and then the directly editable Instructions document.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Agent Builder > Plugins / Connectors
requirements.text: Entries are stable references; Agent Builder MUST NOT clone Plugin/connector definitions into the Agent.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Agent Builder > Skills
requirements.text: Missing, incompatible, disabled or unauthorised Skills MUST be visibly diagnosed before activation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Agent Builder > Knowledge / Files
requirements.text: Knowledge scope, provenance and permissions must remain inspectable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Agent Builder > More Options
requirements.text: More Options MUST be collapsed by default and contain Availability, Default Model and Quick Actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Agent Builder > More Options
requirements.text: The UI MAY remember the user’s local expanded/collapsed preference without changing Agent semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Agent Builder > More Options
requirements.text: Agent Builder MUST validate capability mismatches before activation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Agent Builder > More Options
requirements.text: Quick Actions are named manual Agent entry points with stable QuickActionID, label, optional icon/description, predefined instruction or named graph entry, optional typed InputSchema, context requirements, confirmation policy and order.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Agent Builder > Instructions and assistant
requirements.text: Agent Builder SHOULD expose a contextual assistant rail with actions such as Test this agent, Add advanced logic and Improve this agent plus an Ask anything input.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Agent Builder > Instructions and assistant
requirements.text: AI modifications use typed definition/graph APIs and the resulting concrete configuration MUST remain visible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Agent Builder > Agent advanced logic, preview and revisions
requirements.text: Advanced logic MAY define lifecycle hooks, routing, conditional behaviour, Agent-to-Agent delegation, Skill/Plugin/tool invocation, state, retries, approval gates and other authorised behaviour.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Agent Builder > Agent advanced logic, preview and revisions
requirements.text: It MUST NOT silently permit production side effects simply because the Agent is being previewed.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Agent Builder > Agent advanced logic, preview and revisions
requirements.text: Scheduling or event-triggering an Agent MUST create a real Automation rather than an Agent-private timer.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Agent Builder > Agent advanced logic, preview and revisions
requirements.text: Agent definitions MUST have stable AgentID and DefinitionRevision.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Agent Builder > Agent advanced logic, preview and revisions
requirements.text: Prior valid revisions SHOULD be rollback-capable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Agent Builder > Visual animated-avatar builder
requirements.text: AI Studio MUST provide a visual animated-avatar builder within the existing Agent Builder workflow.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Agent Builder > Visual animated-avatar builder
requirements.text: It MUST support visually editing the avatar, its animation states, transitions and event-to-animation mappings; previewing activity and conversational reactions; saving and reopening the configuration; and assigning the result to an Agent.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Agent Builder > Visual animated-avatar builder
requirements.text: Authoring MUST update the canonical Den-backed Dulche Agent and referenced assets rather than creating an incompatible AI Studio-only Agent or runtime.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Agent Builder > Visual animated-avatar builder
requirements.text: The builder MUST expose the canonical Dulche Agent presentation fields and referenced assets, including static fallback, activity states, transitions and conversational reaction mappings.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Agent Builder > Visual animated-avatar builder
requirements.text: Preview MUST simulate presentation events without executing the corresponding real-world task or widening permissions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Agent Builder > Visual animated-avatar builder
requirements.text: Equivalent authorised AI Studio/Agent APIs MUST support the visible editing, preview, save, reopen and assign operations with revision-conflict and asset-validation errors.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Agent Builder > Visual animated-avatar builder
requirements.text: Acceptance MUST cover a saved/reopened coding animation, a joke/laugh reaction and reduced-motion/static fallback on the same Den-backed Agent.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Tool Builder
requirements.text: Supported first-class output types MUST include Skill, Plugin and MCP.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Tool Builder
requirements.text: Additional package kinds MAY be added without weakening stable identity, manifest, schema, dependency, permission, validation and version requirements.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Tool Builder
requirements.text: Creating a Tool MUST begin with an explicit type-specific template rather than forcing Skill, Plugin and MCP concepts into one generic editor.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Tool Builder > Skill Builder
requirements.text: Skill projects MUST support name/icon/description, directly editable instructions/workflows, examples, resources/files, required Plugins/MCP dependencies, supported contexts, declared permissions, version and a real Test Skill action against Dulche.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Tool Builder > Skill Builder
requirements.text: Skills are primarily declarative and MUST NOT gain arbitrary executable code solely because they are Skills.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Tool Builder > Skill Builder
requirements.text: Executable behaviour must use declared authorised tool/Plugin/MCP dependencies.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Tool Builder > Plugin Builder
requirements.text: Plugin projects MUST support versioned manifest editing, actions/tools, typed input/output schemas, permission/risk declarations, external account connections, optional CUI surfaces, dependencies, secure secret references, tests and package/install workflows.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Tool Builder > Plugin Builder
requirements.text: Plugin UI surfaces MUST use approved CUI contracts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Tool Builder > Plugin Builder
requirements.text: Plugin Builder SHOULD provide preview/testing of those surfaces without granting their actions permissions automatically.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Tool Builder > MCP Builder
requirements.text: MCP projects MUST support client/server role, transport/process/endpoint definition, capability schemas, tools/resources/prompts where supported, authentication references, permissions, compatibility/versioning, test client/server operation and logs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Build — Tool Builder > MCP Builder
requirements.text: MCP Builder MUST support both consuming an MCP server and intentionally exposing approved 9to1 capabilities through server mode without bypassing their original permission model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Shared builder assistant
requirements.text: Harness Builder, Agent Builder and Tool Builder SHOULD use a consistent contextual builder-assistant pattern.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Shared builder assistant
requirements.text: Natural-language requests such as 'add a GitHub tool and require approval for merge actions' MUST resolve to actual manifest/graph/permission changes that remain directly inspectable rather than only producing explanatory prose.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Test & Debug — Playground
requirements.text: A Playground run MUST show result content, Generated UI where present, effective model/provider, effective instructions/context, tool/Agent activity, permissions, usage/timing, errors and Action Graph.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Test & Debug — Playground
requirements.text: It SHOULD support Save as Evaluation Case, Save as Test, Open in Agent Builder and Create Harness from this where applicable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Test & Debug — Evaluations
requirements.text: Evaluation targets MAY include Dulche Agents/revisions, Harnesses, Skills, Plugins/tools, model/model-router policies and other supported reusable definitions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Test & Debug — Evaluations
requirements.text: Every EvaluationSuite MUST have stable EvalSuiteID, name, target/configuration, Cases, Graders, selected RunProfile/environment, optional baseline and revision metadata.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Test & Debug — Evaluations
requirements.text: An EvaluationCase MAY define input, context, expected properties, expected output schema, required actions, forbidden actions, cost/latency limits and scoring/rubric criteria.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Test & Debug — Evaluations
requirements.text: Cases MUST preserve input/source provenance and target revision.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Test & Debug — Evaluations
requirements.text: Supported grader families SHOULD include deterministic exact/schema checks, tool/action assertions, state assertions, rubric/LLM grading, human review and authorised custom Tool/Plugin graders.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Test & Debug — Evaluations
requirements.text: Results MUST distinguish deterministic facts from model-graded judgements.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Test & Debug — Evaluations
requirements.text: Evaluation runs SHOULD support multiple repetitions/seeds where stochastic variation matters and MUST allow comparison against a baseline without pretending one run proves overall quality.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Test & Debug — Test Suites
requirements.text: Tests MAY assert expected node/path, expected or forbidden tool/action calls, permission requests, schemas, output types, state transitions, retry behaviour and structured errors.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Test & Debug — Test Suites
requirements.text: Tests MUST be runnable manually and through typed/CI-capable APIs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Test & Debug — Test Suites
requirements.text: Agent activation, Tool install or Harness deployment MAY require configured mandatory suites to pass.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Test & Debug — Test Suites
requirements.text: A failed test MUST preserve the exact target revision, Run Profile, effective dependencies and Action Graph needed to reproduce the failure.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Test & Debug — Replay & Debugger
requirements.text: Users MUST be able to branch/replay from a valid node with controlled changes such as different model, Agent revision, instructions, context, tool result, capability availability, permission simulation or Run Profile.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Test & Debug — Replay & Debugger
requirements.text: Replay MUST use Dulche restart/fork semantics and preserve side-effect safety.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Test & Debug — Replay & Debugger
requirements.text: Replaying from before a consequential action MUST NOT blindly repeat an externally completed action without idempotency/explicit user-authorised behaviour.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Resources — Schema Builder
requirements.text: Every reusable schema MUST have stable SchemaID, version/compatibility metadata, field/type/constraint definitions and reverse dependency visibility.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Resources — Schema Builder
requirements.text: The editor SHOULD support both structured visual editing and raw schema/source editing for technical users.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Resources — Schema Builder
requirements.text: Changing a shared schema MUST show affected dependants and compatibility impact before activation rather than silently breaking consuming Agents/Tools/Harnesses.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Resources — Model Router Builder
requirements.text: Rules MAY route by modality, task classification, context size, required tools/capabilities, latency, cost budget, privacy/local-only constraints, Agent, surface or other typed request metadata.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Resources — Model Router Builder
requirements.text: Router policies MUST have deterministic precedence and explicit fallback rules.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Resources — Model Router Builder
requirements.text: The builder SHOULD visualise routes using the shared Node Graph Framework where useful while retaining a simpler rules view.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Resources — Generative UI Builder
requirements.text: It MUST support component hierarchy, typed state/bindings, approved typed actions, responsive behaviour, accessibility metadata, theming, fallback representation and preview.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Resources — Generative UI Builder
requirements.text: AI-generative definitions MUST explicitly constrain which components/actions can be generated and MUST NOT permit arbitrary trusted executable code.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Resources — Generative UI Builder
requirements.text: Preview SHOULD cover supported desktop/narrow/mobile widths, light/dark themes, reduced motion, keyboard operation and accessibility semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Resources — Run Profiles
requirements.text: A RunProfile MAY define model/fallback policy, budgets, timeouts, logging level, mock/sandbox connectors, permission simulation, concurrency/Subagent limits and network/privacy policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Resources — Run Profiles
requirements.text: Profile identity and revision MUST be recorded in runs/evaluations/tests for reproducibility.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Context Inspector
requirements.text: It MUST distinguish Agent/Harness instructions, active Skills, Space/context instructions, selected artifacts, retrieved chunks, memory items, tool schemas, summarised context and omitted material.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Context Inspector
requirements.text: For each context item, Context Inspector SHOULD show source identity/revision, provenance, full/summarised/retrieved status, token/size estimate where available, retrieval metadata and why it was selected or omitted.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Context Inspector
requirements.text: It MUST NOT imply that omitted sources were considered by the model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Permission Simulator
requirements.text: It MUST show Allowed, Ask or Denied outcomes plus the contributing Agent, surface, Space, project/entity, caller/organisation and Home trust/policy decisions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Permission Simulator
requirements.text: The simulator MUST explain the controlling reason for a denial/approval requirement and MUST use the same permission-resolution contracts as real execution.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Dependency Inspector
requirements.text: It MUST highlight missing dependencies, updates, disabled packages, revoked permission/access, version/schema incompatibility, inaccessible source and dependency cycles.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Dependency Inspector
requirements.text: Clicking a dependency SHOULD open/inspect the canonical entity where permitted.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Comparison view
requirements.text: Comparison MAY show side-by-side outputs plus evaluation scores, deterministic test results, tool/action differences, Action Graph differences, latency, tokens/cost, errors, retries, selected context and effective model/provider.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Comparison view
requirements.text: Model-quality comparisons SHOULD support multiple repetitions where needed rather than overgeneralising from one stochastic run.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Documentation Generator
requirements.text: It MUST be able to derive relevant identity/version, purpose, availability, dependencies, permissions, actions/APIs, schemas, examples, errors and compatibility information.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Documentation Generator
requirements.text: Supported outputs MAY include Markdown, HTML, Write documents, developer-site documentation or other typed export targets.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Documentation Generator
requirements.text: Regeneration/update MUST reflect the canonical definition and MUST NOT silently overwrite hand-authored material without an explicit merge/replacement workflow.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Templates
requirements.text: Templates MUST be real inspectable versioned starter definitions/projects.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Templates
requirements.text: Supported template families SHOULD include Harness, Agent, Skill, Plugin, MCP, Evaluation, Test Suite, Schema, Model Router, Generative UI and Run Profile where appropriate.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Validation, install and deployment boundaries
requirements.text: AI Studio MUST clearly distinguish authoring, validation, test/preview, build/package, install, activate and deploy/run concepts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Validation, install and deployment boundaries
requirements.text: All validation MUST use the same canonical Dulche/Home schema, dependency, model-capability, permission and runtime contracts used after activation/install.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > AI Studio API
requirements.text: User-visible operations across builders, test/debug tools and resources MUST have equivalent typed APIs under the global API-parity rule.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Failure behaviour
requirements.text: AI Studio MUST return structured failures including ProjectNotFound, AgentNotFound, InvalidDefinition, ValidationFailed, DependencyMissing, DependencyConflict, SchemaIncompatible, ModelCapabilityMismatch, PermissionDenied, PreviewSideEffectDenied, EvaluationTargetUnavailable, GraderUnavailable, TestAssertionFailed, ReplayPointUnavailable, ReplaySideEffectConflict, ContextUnavailable, RunProfileUnavailable, RouterInvalid, DocumentationGenerationFailed and RevisionConflict in addition to the global error contract.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > AI Studio > Acceptance requirements
requirements.text: Harness advanced graph uses the shared Home Node Graph Framework and remains optional for simple Harnesses.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Product role and editing-first boundary
requirements.text: Picture MUST support professional-grade manual editing, simple object-first workflows, non-destructive composition, AI-assisted editing, generative image creation, sketch-to-image conversion and advanced vector tooling while remaining approachable to users who do not want to manage low-level layer structure.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Product role and editing-first boundary
requirements.text: Core crop/transform/colour/vector/text/drawing/export workflows MUST remain fully usable when AI is disabled, unavailable or disallowed.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Shared-engine reuse and fast feature parity
requirements.text: Picture MUST reuse the mature shared engines already used by Write, Present, Canvas and Boards whenever capability overlaps.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Shared-engine reuse and fast feature parity
requirements.text: It MUST NOT create Picture-private duplicates of shared drawing, text, shape, selection, transform, clipboard, accessibility, undo/history or embedded-object semantics merely for implementation convenience.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Shared-engine reuse and fast feature parity
requirements.text: Where Picture needs a capability that logically belongs in one of these shared engines, the implementation SHOULD extend that shared engine centrally and enable the new capability for other eligible apps rather than fork it inside Picture.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Canonical Picture document model
requirements.text: Picture MUST use a versioned editable PictureDocument rather than treating the current rendered bitmap as the sole source of truth.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Canonical Picture document model
requirements.text: A document has stable DocumentID, optional backing FileID/source revision, canvas/artboard geometry, colour profile, background, canonical ElementGraph/LayerGraph, linked assets, edit history/revisions, metadata and document revision.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Automatic composition mode and manual layers
requirements.text: Picture automatically creates/updates the internal objects, masks, adjustment state and generated fills required to keep the edit non-destructive.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Automatic composition mode and manual layers
requirements.text: Manual Layer mode is an optional advanced view over the SAME canonical document model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Automatic composition mode and manual layers
requirements.text: Switching between automatic and manual views MUST NOT flatten or convert the document.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Automatic composition mode and manual layers
requirements.text: Automatic mode may group implementation details into understandable objects such as Subject, Background, Text or Generated Object while preserving the full internal structure for advanced inspection/editing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Layer and composition semantics
requirements.text: The canonical layer/composition graph MUST support at minimum RasterImage, VectorShape, VectorPath, Text, Drawing/Ink, GeneratedObject, Adjustment, Fill, Mask, Group, Artboard/Canvas, Background and Linked/Smart Asset element families.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Layer and composition semantics
requirements.text: Adjustment/effect nodes SHOULD remain non-destructive and apply to explicit target scope rather than permanently rewriting source pixels.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Layer and composition semantics
requirements.text: A user can rasterise/flatten selected content explicitly, but Picture MUST NOT silently flatten editable content merely because a tool is easier to implement that way.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Selection and semantic object extraction
requirements.text: Picture MUST provide a mature selection system including rectangle, ellipse, lasso, polygonal/freehand lasso, brush/refine, colour/range selection and smart/semantic selection where AI/vision capability exists.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Object-first editing
requirements.text: A selected object/subject MUST support direct Move, Resize, Rotate, Duplicate, Delete/Erase, Replace, Isolate, Recolour/Restyle and front/back ordering actions where compatible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Object-first editing
requirements.text: The original underlying elements MUST remain revision-addressable so the edit can be undone/reverted or regenerated.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Raster editing
requirements.text: Core raster editing MUST include at least:

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Raster editing
requirements.text: Raster operations SHOULD be represented as non-destructive adjustments/masks/transform state where technically practical.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Raster editing
requirements.text: An operation that must bake pixels MUST create a revision boundary with reversible history.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Vector creation and editing
requirements.text: Picture MUST provide powerful vector creation/editing suitable for serious illustration, asset and graphic-design work, with depth comparable to mature Photoshop-class vector/path tooling while keeping common actions simple.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Text objects
requirements.text: Picture text tools MUST support font family/style/size, colour/fill/stroke, line height, alignment, tracking/kerning where supported, transform/rotation, text box/area text, point text and appropriate effects.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Text objects
requirements.text: Advanced vector-text behaviours such as text on path and convert to path SHOULD reuse the vector engine.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Text objects
requirements.text: Text must remain editable as text until the user explicitly converts/rasterises it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Drawing and painting
requirements.text: Picture MUST reuse the shared Rnote-derived drawing engine for sketching, painting/markup and mask/selection brush workflows rather than implementing a separate stroke format.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Drawing and painting
requirements.text: Picture may expose a simplified context-specific toolbar, but underlying stroke behaviour/serialisation remains shared.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > AI editing and generative operations
requirements.text: AI editing is a first-class core Picture capability rather than an optional afterthought.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > AI editing and generative operations
requirements.text: Picture MUST support typed, revisioned AI operations including object removal, object replacement, generative fill, generative erase, generative expand/outpainting, background remove/replace, object move/resize with scene reconstruction, style/appearance change, image restoration/enhancement, upscaling, relighting/recolour assistance and prompt-based region/full-image editing where the configured model/tool supports them.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > AI editing and generative operations
requirements.text: AI operations MUST target explicit DocumentID/ElementID/SelectionID/MaskID/revision context rather than inferred screen coordinates.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > AI editing and generative operations
requirements.text: Results become canonical editable Picture state or explicit generated variants; they MUST NOT silently overwrite the only source.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Generative image creation
requirements.text: Picture MUST create new images from text prompts, sketches, reference images, mixed prompt+reference+sketch inputs and supported style/composition guidance.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Sketch-to-image
requirements.text: Users can draw a rough composition/shape layout with the shared drawing engine, optionally annotate regions with text or references, and generate a detailed image while retaining the original sketch and generation relationship.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Sketch-to-image
requirements.text: Sketch-to-image MUST support iterative workflows such as sketch -> generate -> edit -> select region -> regenerate/refine.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Sketch-to-image
requirements.text: The user may preserve the sketch as an editable overlay/reference rather than losing it after generation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > AI-assisted composition
requirements.text: Picture MAY support high-level composition instructions such as rebalance composition, reposition subject, change background, restyle a poster, convert a rough concept to a polished visual or convert a sketch to a clean vector-like design.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > AI-assisted composition
requirements.text: These MUST resolve to inspectable canonical Picture mutations/variants rather than an opaque final bitmap when the requested operation can remain editable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Non-destructive adjustments and edit stack
requirements.text: Picture MUST preserve non-destructive editability for transforms, crop, colour/light adjustments, effects, masks, vector/text objects and generative operations where technically possible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Non-destructive adjustments and edit stack
requirements.text: Invalid reordering that would change unsupported dependency semantics must be rejected or require an explicit bake/convert step.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Smart/linked assets
requirements.text: The user can explicitly embed/freeze/snapshot a linked asset when a self-contained result is required.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Crop, canvas and artboards
requirements.text: Crop MUST support Free, Original, common ratios such as 1:1, 4:3, 3:2, 16:9 and 9:16, plus custom ratio and straighten/rotation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Crop, canvas and artboards
requirements.text: PictureDocument MAY support one or more artboards/canvases for vector/graphic workflows.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Effects, blend and masks
requirements.text: Picture MUST support mature effect/blend workflows including opacity, blend modes, blur/sharpen, shadow/glow and other registered effects where the rendering backend supports them.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Effects, blend and masks
requirements.text: Effects should be non-destructive and target explicit elements/groups/masks.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Effects, blend and masks
requirements.text: Clipping/masking behaviour must be deterministic and preserved through save/reopen.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Presets
requirements.text: AI-assisted presets MAY exist but MUST record which operations are deterministic versus model-generated.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Comparison and preview
requirements.text: The editor MUST provide Original/current comparison and SHOULD provide split/side-by-side before/after.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Comparison and preview
requirements.text: Preview rendering may use reduced resolution for interactivity but final export/save renders from the canonical source/revision at declared quality.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > File formats and import
requirements.text: Picture MUST support mature viewing/import/edit/export workflows for common raster formats including JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP and TIFF, plus HEIF/HEIC, AVIF and other formats where maintained codec support exists.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > File formats and import
requirements.text: Animated/multi-frame formats MUST preserve animation unless the user explicitly chooses a flattening conversion.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > File formats and import
requirements.text: SVG/vector import/export SHOULD preserve editable vector structure where compatible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > File formats and import
requirements.text: RAW support MAY be capability-dependent but, where enabled, must preserve the RAW source and use a non-destructive development/render path.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > File formats and import
requirements.text: Unknown/unsupported format features must be surfaced rather than silently stripped.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Animated and multi-frame images
requirements.text: A tool that would flatten animation MUST warn and require an explicit convert/flatten path.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Colour management and HDR
requirements.text: Picture MUST honour embedded colour profiles and alpha/transparency. sRGB is the safe baseline; wide-gamut/HDR display/edit behaviour is capability-negotiated where supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Colour management and HDR
requirements.text: Unsupported profiles/HDR paths must use a declared fallback/transform rather than silently displaying materially wrong colour.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Colour management and HDR
requirements.text: Final export MUST allow appropriate colour-profile handling and warn when a target format cannot represent the working colour space/dynamic range.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Metadata and privacy
requirements.text: Unknown metadata should be preserved through non-destructive round trips where possible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Metadata and privacy
requirements.text: Export/privacy controls MUST support preserving metadata, removing location metadata and removing all removable metadata where the target format supports it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Files and canonical asset identity
requirements.text: Picture MUST NOT create a hidden duplicate file store.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Persistent AI bar
requirements.text: Picture MUST host the global persistent Dulche AI bar.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Persistent AI bar
requirements.text: AI MUST NOT simulate raw pointer gestures when semantic object/selection APIs exist.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Picture API
requirements.text: Shared drawing/text/shape/selection/clipboard primitives SHOULD use their owning shared API namespace where that is the canonical operation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Picture API
requirements.text: Picture MUST NOT duplicate the same shared action under incompatible semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Collaboration and conflict handling
requirements.text: Independent edits may merge where the canonical object graph proves them non-conflicting; concurrent incompatible edits to the same element/mask/layer/revision MUST surface a conflict rather than blind last-write-wins.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Security and generated content
requirements.text: Picture MUST NOT upload local/private images to a remote model/provider when the effective privacy policy forbids it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Security and generated content
requirements.text: Embedded metadata/scripts MUST NOT acquire application execution privileges.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Accessibility
requirements.text: Picture's Create/Edit/Generate/Browse surfaces MUST be keyboard-operable for required workflows.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Accessibility
requirements.text: Image descriptions/alt text MAY be stored/edited where applicable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Platform capability behaviour
requirements.text: Picture MUST provide useful Windows, 9to1-OS and web editing/creation experiences over the same PictureDocument model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Platform capability behaviour
requirements.text: The web app MUST NOT degrade into a read-only image viewer.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Performance and resource behaviour
requirements.text: Picture MUST use resolution-appropriate decode, GPU acceleration where suitable, incremental/tiled rendering for very large images, bounded preview/thumbnail caches, background full-quality rendering and cancellable long-running jobs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Performance and resource behaviour
requirements.text: Interactive edit previews may use reduced-resolution proxies, but final save/export renders from canonical source content at requested quality.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Performance and resource behaviour
requirements.text: Large layer/vector graphs should avoid full-document rerenders when only a bounded element/region changes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Failure behaviour
requirements.text: Picture MUST return structured failures including DocumentNotFound, ElementNotFound, InvalidSelection, InvalidMask, UnsupportedFormat, UnsupportedCodecFeature, ColourProfileUnsupported, HDRUnsupported, RevisionConflict, LinkedAssetUnavailable, GenerationUnavailable, GenerationFailed, InvalidGenerationRegion, ExportUnsupportedFeature, RenderFailed, PermissionDenied and CapabilityUnavailable in addition to shared engine/model errors.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Picture > Acceptance requirements
requirements.text: Save, Save Copy and export preserve the editable source while producing interoperable rendered/vector outputs with explicit flattening where required.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Product role and native-generation principle
requirements.text: All generated audio components MUST be native, structured Wave components whenever the requested result can be represented by Wave's own sequencer, synthesis, effect, speech or clip systems.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Product role and native-generation principle
requirements.text: AI MUST NOT normally return an opaque arbitrary waveform as the canonical result for music, sound effects, speech or other structured generative workflows.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Shared media/audio engine
requirements.text: Wave MUST share its core audio/media primitives with Motion, Present and other eligible 9to1 surfaces rather than creating incompatible per-app audio engines.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Shared media/audio engine
requirements.text: GStreamer is an approved maintained media backend and GStreamer Editing Services or an explicitly documented equivalent may be used where appropriate.
