requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Shared media/audio engine
requirements.text: Backend choice MUST preserve the public Wave project/action contracts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Canonical project model
requirements.text: Timeline editing MUST be non-destructive by default.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Main workspace and transport
requirements.text: Wave's primary workspace is a multitrack timeline with transport, track controls, selected clip/component inspector and optional mixer/effects/sequencer/spectral panels.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Main workspace and transport
requirements.text: Transport MUST include:

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Main workspace and transport
requirements.text: Keyboard-first editing shortcuts are required for repetitive timeline operations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Recording
requirements.text: Wave MUST support robust microphone/device recording including input-device selection, mono/stereo/multichannel where available, input monitoring, level meters/clipping indication, record-arm per track, count-in/pre-roll/post-roll, punch-in/punch-out, overdub, loop/take recording and pause/resume.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Multitrack, mixer, routing and buses
requirements.text: Wave MUST support multiple simultaneous audio tracks for voice, music, sound effects, ambience, generated content, imported media and multiple takes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Multitrack, mixer, routing and buses
requirements.text: Advanced routing may be hidden by default but the canonical project supports it where exposed.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Effects and parameter automation
requirements.text: Effect/track/instrument parameters may be automated over time using native automation lanes/curves.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Spectral editing and repair
requirements.text: Wave MUST provide Waveform, Spectrogram and combined Waveform+Spectrogram views.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Spectral editing and repair
requirements.text: AI-assisted cleanup MAY isolate speech, remove/reduce noise, reverb, clicks, breaths/coughs, restore damaged recordings and perform other model-backed repair, but outputs remain represented as native derived clips/effect operations/revisions rather than silently overwriting the source.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Audio enhancement and denoising tools
requirements.text: Wave MUST expose first-class Enhance Audio and Denoise tools for selected clips, tracks, time ranges and imported or recorded audio.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Audio enhancement and denoising tools
requirements.text: At minimum it MUST be able to combine appropriate noise/hum reduction, de-click/de-pop, de-reverb where available, clarity/EQ correction, dynamics/level correction and loudness normalisation; speech-focused enhancement MAY use model-backed processing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Audio enhancement and denoising tools
requirements.text: Denoise MUST provide an automatic one-click path plus an advanced path with strength/amount and preview/bypass.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Audio enhancement and denoising tools
requirements.text: Where the selected backend supports noise-profile learning, Wave MUST allow a selected region to be used as the noise profile.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Audio enhancement and denoising tools
requirements.text: Enhancement and denoising MUST be previewable, undoable and non-destructive.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Audio enhancement and denoising tools
requirements.text: Long-running model-backed processing MUST expose progress and cancellation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Audio enhancement and denoising tools
requirements.text: Applying enhancement MUST NOT silently modify unrelated clips, tracks, effects or master routing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Music Sequencer
requirements.text: Wave MUST include a first-class native music sequencer.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Native instruments and sampling
requirements.text: The sequencer MUST provide a versioned instrument registry.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Native instruments and sampling
requirements.text: Native instrument families MAY include synthesizers, drums/percussion, sampler instruments and other maintained engines.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Native instruments and sampling
requirements.text: AI may choose/configure instruments, write notes/patterns, create arrangement structure, automate parameters and mix tracks, but MUST produce the same native Sequencer/Instrument/Effect objects a user can inspect and edit manually.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > AI music generation
requirements.text: A request such as 'make a two-minute upbeat electronic track' MUST generate a native music project/section: tempo and meter, sequencer tracks, instrument choices/settings, editable note/pattern data, arrangement, automation and effects/mix state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > AI music generation
requirements.text: AI may iterate by editing native structures: 'make the chorus heavier' changes relevant patterns/instruments/automation/effects; 'change the chord progression' rewrites note/chord events while preserving unrelated project structure.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Sound Effects Builder
requirements.text: Wave MUST include a native Sound Effects Builder for procedural/constructed sound effects.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Sound Effects Builder
requirements.text: The builder SHOULD use the Home Node Graph Framework for editing/visualisation where appropriate, with Wave-specific realtime audio nodes and execution handled by the Wave audio engine.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Sound Effects Builder
requirements.text: The UI SHOULD offer simple high-level macro controls for common users while allowing advanced users to open the complete patch graph.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Text to Speech
requirements.text: Wave MUST include native Text-to-Speech components.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Text to Speech
requirements.text: Speech may be split into utterances/paragraphs/regions and aligned on the timeline without flattening into an anonymous generated waveform.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Text to Speech
requirements.text: Export may render speech to ordinary audio, but the editable Wave project retains the speech component.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Other generated native components
requirements.text: AI should build Wave-native source/processing structures — for example layered samplers plus filters/envelopes/automation for ambience — instead of defaulting to opaque audio generation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Other generated native components
requirements.text: When a capability fundamentally requires an externally generated waveform that cannot be represented by existing native generators, that waveform MAY enter Wave only as an explicit GeneratedSample source asset with model/provenance metadata.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Other generated native components
requirements.text: It MUST then be treated like a normal editable sample/clip, and the UI must not pretend it has native sequencer/patch editability.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Other generated native components
requirements.text: Native structured generation remains the default and required path whenever representable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Custom censorship
requirements.text: Wave MUST include Custom Censorship for a selected clip, track, time range or whole-project audio scope.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Custom censorship
requirements.text: Word and phrase rules use time-aligned transcription where available; theme rules MAY use supported model-backed semantic classification.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Custom censorship
requirements.text: Detection MUST produce reviewable candidate time ranges before application, and the user MUST be able to add, remove or adjust matches to correct false positives and false negatives.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Custom censorship
requirements.text: Controls MUST include pre/post padding and fades, and MAY optionally redact matched text from captions/transcripts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Audio separation and derived stems
requirements.text: Stem splitting MUST be exposed as a first-class Split Stems tool rather than only as an AI command.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Audio separation and derived stems
requirements.text: The UI MUST offer every separation mode supported by the configured backend, including common modes such as Vocals/Instrumental, Vocals/Drums/Bass/Other, speaker separation and Foreground/Background where available.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Markers, regions and chapters
requirements.text: Markers/regions may carry names, colours/categories, notes and references without changing underlying clip data.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Motion and Present interoperability
requirements.text: Motion and Wave MUST share compatible audio asset/clip/effect/timeline primitives.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Import and export
requirements.text: Wave import MUST support common maintained codecs/formats through the shared media backend.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Persistent AI bar
requirements.text: Wave MUST host the global persistent Dulche AI bar.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Persistent AI bar
requirements.text: It MUST NOT simulate timeline mouse gestures when semantic APIs exist.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Wave API
requirements.text: Shared media operations SHOULD use their owning shared API namespace when that is canonical.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Automation and integration events
requirements.text: Wave emits meaningful typed events such as project/revision changes, recording completed, export completed, render failed and generated component changed; it MUST NOT flood Automations with raw per-sample or pointer events.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Collaboration and revision conflicts
requirements.text: Independent object edits MAY merge when safe; incompatible concurrent edits to the same canonical object surface conflict rather than blind last-write-wins.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Collaboration and revision conflicts
requirements.text: A running render/export/recording is pinned to the required source/project revision and MUST NOT silently switch to a newly edited revision mid-job.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Accessibility
requirements.text: Wave MUST be keyboard-operable for transport, clip selection/editing, sequencer editing, mixer controls, transcript editing and generated-component workflows.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Accessibility
requirements.text: Waveforms/spectrograms provide semantic time/level/frequency information and non-pointer equivalents for required operations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Accessibility
requirements.text: Meters, clipping, mute/solo, automation and error states MUST NOT rely on colour alone.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Performance and realtime safety
requirements.text: The realtime audio path MUST remain isolated from blocking UI, disk, AI/model, network and export work.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Platform capability behaviour
requirements.text: Wave MUST provide useful Windows, 9to1-OS and web editing/creation experiences over the same canonical project model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Wave > Platform capability behaviour
requirements.text: Web MUST remain a useful multitrack/sequencer/editor experience rather than a static player.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Product role and native project principle
requirements.text: Normal edits such as trimming, crop, speed changes, transforms, masks, effects, colour changes, captions, keyframes, procedural animation and AI-assisted mutations MUST remain inspectable editable project state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Product role and native project principle
requirements.text: Rendering, proxies, previews, caches and exports are derived outputs and MUST NOT silently replace canonical project state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Shared engines and dependency boundaries
requirements.text: Motion MUST reuse shared 9to1 engines aggressively wherever the underlying capability belongs to more than one product.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Shared engines and dependency boundaries
requirements.text: Shared capability MUST live in the appropriate shared engine/library rather than requiring another app UI process or duplicating private implementations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Shared engines and dependency boundaries
requirements.text: Dependency direction MUST remain acyclic and engine-oriented.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Shared engines and dependency boundaries
requirements.text: Motion MUST NOT require the Picture or Wave UI processes merely to crop an image or adjust audio.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Shared engines and dependency boundaries
requirements.text: If Motion needs a capability that Picture, Wave, Present or another surface also materially needs, the implementation SHOULD be placed in the owning shared engine rather than copied.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Canonical project model
requirements.text: Masks, EffectInstances, AnimationTracks, Keyframes, Titles/TextObjects, CaptionTracks, CaptionCues, analysis records and Motion node-graph objects MUST have stable identity and revision-aware state where they are addressable/editable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Main workspace and contextual editing
requirements.text: Panels MAY be docked, resized, collapsed, moved or hidden, but the initial workspace MUST avoid exposing an unnecessarily large professional-panel wall to a new user.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Main workspace and contextual editing
requirements.text: Direct manipulation in the Viewer/Canvas MUST mutate the same canonical properties and typed actions used by the Inspector, keyboard operations, APIs and AI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Main workspace and contextual editing
requirements.text: The viewer MUST NOT maintain a separate UI-only transform or mask state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Timeline and non-linear editing
requirements.text: Motion MUST provide a professional multi-track NLE timeline with accurate frame/timecode semantics, in/out ranges, source/sequence viewing, snapping, multi-selection, markers, grouping, linked audio/video, track controls and nested sequences.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Timeline and non-linear editing
requirements.text: Transport MUST support ordinary play/pause, frame stepping and efficient shuttle/scrub control, including keyboard-first operation such as J/K/L-style transport where appropriate.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Timeline and non-linear editing
requirements.text: Editing operations MUST be deterministic at the sequence timebase and MUST NOT depend on pixel coordinates in the timeline UI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Timeline and non-linear editing
requirements.text: Video tracks may contain video, images, Picture assets, titles/text, vector graphics, shapes/ink, generated media, adjustment/effect layers, nested sequences and other registered compatible visual elements.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Source media, proxies, preview and cache
requirements.text: Motion MUST separate canonical source media from proxy media, decode caches, analysis caches, preview renders and final render output.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Source media, proxies, preview and cache
requirements.text: Editing against a proxy MUST preserve the same canonical source identity, timing, ElementID and project semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Source media, proxies, preview and cache
requirements.text: Motion MUST support automatic proxy generation, user-requested proxies, configurable proxy resolution/codec where supported, per-asset proxy state, background generation, lower-resolution viewer playback and render/pre-render caching.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Source media, proxies, preview and cache
requirements.text: Final render/export MUST use canonical source media at requested output quality unless the user explicitly chooses a proxy-derived or otherwise lower-quality source path.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Source media, proxies, preview and cache
requirements.text: Missing or stale proxies/caches are recoverable derived-state problems and MUST NOT make the canonical project invalid.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Viewer, transforms and visual composition
requirements.text: Transform and visual-property edits MUST be represented by canonical property mutations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Viewer, transforms and visual composition
requirements.text: Motion MUST support layered compositing with opacity, blend modes, alpha, masks, mattes, track mattes, chroma/luma keying, nesting/precomposition, adjustment layers and explicit compositing order where supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Animation and keyframes
requirements.text: Suitable numeric, vector, colour, mask, effect, text and generated-component properties MUST be animatable through a common parameter-animation system rather than each feature inventing incompatible keyframe storage.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Animation and keyframes
requirements.text: Motion MUST provide easing presets and a graph/curve editor for advanced editing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Animation and keyframes
requirements.text: Shared Present animation/timing primitives SHOULD be reused when semantics are compatible, while Motion remains authoritative for timeline/frame-based video state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Advanced node editor
requirements.text: Motion MUST include a full visual node editor for advanced compositing, effects, transitions, motion graphics and procedural animation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Advanced node editor
requirements.text: Branching graphs MUST NOT require destructive intermediate renders merely because an operation is non-linear.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Advanced node editor
requirements.text: Render/cache intermediates MAY be produced for performance, but graph topology, parameters and inputs remain canonical.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Advanced node editor
requirements.text: The normal Motion UI MUST remain usable without nodes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Motion graph types and reusable graph assets
requirements.text: Graphs may be embedded in one project or saved as reusable presets/components.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Motion graph types and reusable graph assets
requirements.text: Shared-definition instances MUST have explicit semantics for edit-this-instance, detach/copy or update-shared-definition; editing one instance MUST NOT unexpectedly rewrite every use.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Motion graph types and reusable graph assets
requirements.text: Registered custom node types MAY be supplied through the broader 9to1 extension system subject to capability, trust and permission rules.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Motion graph types and reusable graph assets
requirements.text: First- or third-party node providers MUST participate in typed graph contracts rather than injecting arbitrary UI-only behaviour.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Custom transitions
requirements.text: Transitions MUST support ordinary built-in transitions and reusable MotionTransitionGraph assets.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Procedural animation and property drivers
requirements.text: Keyframes, procedural graphs, tracking and linked values MUST interoperate through one canonical parameter-source model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Procedural animation and property drivers
requirements.text: The Inspector MUST make it clear what currently drives a property.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Procedural animation and property drivers
requirements.text: Example: a title may follow tracked subject position, retain hand-authored keyframed movement and add a small procedural noise offset without baking thousands of frame values.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Masks, tracking and rotoscoping
requirements.text: Manual drawing/path editing SHOULD reuse shared Picture/Rnote-derived primitives where semantics match.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Masks, tracking and rotoscoping
requirements.text: Motion SHOULD support point, planar, subject or object tracking according to configured backends.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Masks, tracking and rotoscoping
requirements.text: Tracking data is structured and may drive transforms, masks, effects, text or procedural graphs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Masks, tracking and rotoscoping
requirements.text: Model-assisted subject/object segmentation and rotoscoping MAY initialise or update masks, but users MUST be able to inspect and correct results.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Masks, tracking and rotoscoping
requirements.text: Tracking or segmentation MUST NOT silently destroy source media.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Colour pipeline
requirements.text: Motion MUST include first-party colour correction/grading suitable for normal production.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Colour pipeline
requirements.text: LUT import/use, histograms/scopes and per-clip or adjustment-layer grading SHOULD be supported where the backend permits.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Colour pipeline
requirements.text: Sequence/project colour-space state MUST explicitly represent SDR/HDR and managed-colour configuration where supported rather than relying on hidden backend defaults.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Effects, titles and graphics
requirements.text: Titles and graphics MUST remain native structured objects rather than pre-rendered video.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Effects, titles and graphics
requirements.text: Complex title/graphic systems MAY use Motion node graphs while retaining the same canonical object identity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Captions and transcript-based editing
requirements.text: Motion MUST support time-aligned transcription and first-class CaptionTrack/CaptionCue objects.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Captions and transcript-based editing
requirements.text: Export MUST support appropriate sidecar, embedded and burned-in caption output according to chosen container/backend capability.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Captions and transcript-based editing
requirements.text: Transcript-based edits such as deleting a spoken phrase or removing long pauses MUST translate into ordinary native timeline edits after preview/validation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Audio and Wave interoperability
requirements.text: Open/Edit in Wave MUST preserve canonical asset/clip/timing references so advanced audio work can return to Motion without a lossy export-edit-import cycle.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > AI-assisted editing
requirements.text: AI-generated edits MUST remain inspectable, undoable/revisioned project state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > AI-assisted editing
requirements.text: AI MUST NOT render an opaque replacement video and declare the structured editing task complete when Motion can represent the requested result natively.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Generative and model-backed video workflows
requirements.text: Subject to installed/configured provider capability, Motion MAY provide video generation, image-to-video, generated B-roll, object/background removal, semantic segmentation, smart reframing, scene/shot detection, motion/subject tracking, video restoration/denoise, enhancement/upscaling, frame interpolation, slow-motion generation, generative fill, temporal inpainting and frame/outpainting/extension.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Generative and model-backed video workflows
requirements.text: When the model inherently returns raster/video frames that cannot reasonably be decomposed into lower-level Motion objects, Motion may create a GeneratedVideoAsset with stable identity, model/provider provenance, generation parameters, source references and revision metadata.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Generative and model-backed video workflows
requirements.text: Native-generation rules MUST NOT be misinterpreted as requiring generated video pixels to be decomposed into fake editable vectors.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Media analysis and indexing
requirements.text: Motion MAY maintain source/revision-aware analysis metadata for cuts/scenes, transcript/speech, silence, audio peaks, motion, tracked subjects/objects, semantic tags and other useful signals supported by configured analysis backends.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Media analysis and indexing
requirements.text: Unchanged media SHOULD NOT be repeatedly reanalysed merely because a project was reopened.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Files, asset identity and offline media
requirements.text: Moving or renaming an underlying File MUST NOT detach a Motion reference.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Files, asset identity and offline media
requirements.text: Generated, proxy, cache and rendered assets MUST be distinguishable from canonical source identity and carry appropriate provenance/derivation metadata.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Import, export and render queue
requirements.text: Motion import MUST support maintained video, image and audio formats exposed by the approved shared media backend.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Import, export and render queue
requirements.text: Backend-specific IDs MUST NOT leak into the canonical public Motion project contract.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Import, export and render queue
requirements.text: Export MUST support sequence/project render, selected range, frame stills, audio-only output, caption/subtitle output and appropriate individual-clip/component exports.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Import, export and render queue
requirements.text: Motion MUST provide a render queue/background-job model with stable job identity, progress, cancellation, typed failure state and safe retry.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Import, export and render queue
requirements.text: Export/render MUST be pinned to the intended project/source revision and MUST NOT silently switch to newly edited state mid-job.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Motion API
requirements.text: Shared media, Files, Picture and other shared-domain operations SHOULD use the owning shared API namespace when that is canonical.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Motion API
requirements.text: First-party UI capabilities MUST NOT exist only as inaccessible private UI commands.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Automation and integration events
requirements.text: It MUST NOT flood Automations with raw frame, pointer or realtime preview events.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Collaboration and revision conflicts
requirements.text: Independent object edits MAY merge when safe; incompatible concurrent edits to the same canonical object or property MUST surface conflict rather than blind last-write-wins.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Collaboration and revision conflicts
requirements.text: Running proxy, tracking, generation, render and export jobs are pinned to their required source/project revisions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Collaboration and revision conflicts
requirements.text: Their results MUST record which revision/input produced them.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Accessibility
requirements.text: Motion MUST be keyboard-operable for transport, timeline selection/editing, track controls, inspector properties, captions, keyframes, render jobs and graph editing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Accessibility
requirements.text: Pointer-only gestures cannot be the sole route for required editing operations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Accessibility
requirements.text: Visual states such as lock, disable, offline, clipping, selection and errors MUST NOT rely on colour alone.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Accessibility
requirements.text: Viewer/canvas operations that normally use direct manipulation MUST expose equivalent numeric/semantic controls.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Performance and realtime preview safety
requirements.text: Motion MUST decode/render frames on demand using bounded caches rather than loading entire long-form or high-resolution sources into memory.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Performance and realtime preview safety
requirements.text: GPU acceleration and hardware decode/encode SHOULD be used where safe and available, with explicit capability fallback. 4K/8K and otherwise heavy media remain workable through proxies, reduced preview quality, caching and tiling according to available hardware rather than an architecture that assumes full-resolution residency.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Performance and realtime preview safety
requirements.text: Interactive editing MUST remain responsive while background jobs run.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Performance and realtime preview safety
requirements.text: Preview quality MAY adapt under load, but canonical time/frame calculations and final requested render quality MUST remain deterministic and source-based.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Recovery and failure behaviour
requirements.text: Project saves/autosaves MUST be crash-safe and preserve canonical project integrity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Recovery and failure behaviour
requirements.text: A crash or termination during proxy generation, analysis, tracking, generation, render or export MUST leave the project valid and the derived job recoverable/retryable where feasible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Recovery and failure behaviour
requirements.text: Partial derived output MUST NOT be reported as complete.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Recovery and failure behaviour
requirements.text: Undo/redo and revision history MUST restore structured project changes without requiring source media to be rewritten.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Platform capability behaviour
requirements.text: A platform may disable an unavailable codec, hardware encoder, node provider or model-backed feature with explicit CapabilityUnavailable state, but MUST NOT silently create an incompatible project schema.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Motion > Acceptance requirements
requirements.text: Keyboard and assistive-technology paths can perform required timeline, property, caption, graph and render-queue operations without pointer-only dependency.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Product role and ambition
requirements.text: Games MUST be based on a maintained fork of Godot as its primary game-engine donor and MUST preserve mature applicable engine functionality unless this specification explicitly replaces it with a 9to1-native equivalent.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Product role and ambition
requirements.text: Games MUST also integrate a maintained Blender-derived modelling/rendering toolset deeply enough that modelling feels like part of the same product rather than an external export/import workflow.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Product role and ambition
requirements.text: Because 9to1 is substantially open source, implementation MAY integrate Blender-derived code as deeply as is technically useful while preserving all applicable licence/source-distribution obligations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Product role and ambition
requirements.text: The donor-parity/source manifest MUST identify the exact Godot and Blender revisions, licences, modified components and redistribution obligations used by a release.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Product role and ambition
requirements.text: Games MUST expose at least two first-class workspaces over the same canonical project/assets: Development and Creation/Rendering.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Product role and ambition
requirements.text: A user MUST be able to use Creation/Rendering without building a game.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > CUI-native editor
requirements.text: The user-facing editor MUST be rebuilt as a coherent 9to1 CUI experience rather than exposing donor-native editor chrome as the final interface.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > CUI-native editor
requirements.text: Existing mature donor capability MAY remain behind the shell, but navigation, inspector, asset browser, scene graph, editors, dialogs, settings, errors and workflows MUST follow 9to1 interaction conventions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > CUI-native editor
requirements.text: Games MUST host the normal persistent floating Dulche AI bar.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > CUI-native editor
requirements.text: The AI bar receives only authorised project/editor state and MUST be able to reason over semantic scene, script, component, material, animation, profiler and error data through typed Games APIs.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > CUI-native editor
requirements.text: It MUST NOT rely on generic Computer Use to manipulate the Games editor when a typed Games action exists.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > CUI-native editor
requirements.text: The Godot UI authoring workflow MUST be upgraded/rebuilt around the canonical CUI Visual Builder.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > CUI-native editor
requirements.text: Game HUDs, menus, overlays, dialogue, inventories, maps, settings, responsive layouts and other game UI MUST use the same high-quality visual layout concepts and reusable components as CUI while compiling/running efficiently inside Games.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > CUI-native editor
requirements.text: Game UI remains part of the canonical game scene/component model and MUST NOT become a disconnected design-only artifact.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Canonical scene graph and purposeful components
requirements.text: Games MUST preserve a powerful scene/node graph foundation while providing higher-level purposeful components for common game concepts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Canonical scene graph and purposeful components
requirements.text: Stable SceneID, EntityID, NodeID, ComponentID, ResourceID, AssetID and ProjectID identities MUST be used; mutable names/paths are not canonical identity.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Canonical scene graph and purposeful components
requirements.text: The scene graph MUST support ordinary low-level engine nodes for expert use and high-level purpose-built entities/components for rapid development.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Canonical scene graph and purposeful components
requirements.text: Purposeful components MUST have real runtime semantics, typed APIs, inspectors, events, extension points and Dulche understanding.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Canonical scene graph and purposeful components
requirements.text: They MUST NOT be decorative prefab labels over unrelated scripts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Canonical scene graph and purposeful components
requirements.text: Games MUST favour composition.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Canonical scene graph and purposeful components
requirements.text: Complex built-ins such as Player Character or Car SHOULD be composed from inspectable native primitives plus first-party CUI gameplay components rather than implemented as one opaque monolithic class.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Shared graph infrastructure with Automations
requirements.text: Games and Automations MUST share the same canonical node-graph editor/data infrastructure and backend concepts for GraphID, NodeID, typed ports, typed connections, groups, comments, subgraphs, search, selection, snapping, minimap, copy/paste, undo/redo, versioning, validation, keyboard accessibility, semantic API access and execution/debug visualisation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Shared graph infrastructure with Automations
requirements.text: Sharing the graph infrastructure MUST NOT force all graphs through one execution runtime.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Shared graph infrastructure with Automations
requirements.text: Games MUST expose only context-relevant nodes by default.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Shared graph infrastructure with Automations
requirements.text: A shader graph MUST NOT show Send Email merely because Automations uses the same graph infrastructure.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Shared graph infrastructure with Automations
requirements.text: C#/C++/GDScript donor and low-level implementation code may remain behind engine adapters or in preserved imported external sources; they are not selectable public application-authoring languages.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Intuitive API design contract
requirements.text: The public Games API MUST describe game intent rather than mirror internal engine plumbing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Intuitive API design contract
requirements.text: Where an operation has a clear domain action, the high-level API MUST expose that action directly.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Intuitive API design contract
requirements.text: Similar simple verbs SHOULD include SetPosition, MoveTo, Rotate, Show, Hide, Enable, Disable, Open, Close, Play, Stop, Spawn, Destroy, Give, Take, Attach and Detach where semantically appropriate.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Intuitive API design contract
requirements.text: Public APIs MUST use consistent names, strong typing, sensible defaults, concise parameters and direct discoverability.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Intuitive API design contract
requirements.text: Internally complex operations such as replication, authority resolution, component traversal or persistence SHOULD be handled by Games when the desired intent is unambiguous.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Intuitive API design contract
requirements.text: Advanced low-level APIs MAY expose explicit replication, authority, memory, rendering and engine primitives for expert use.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Intuitive API design contract
requirements.text: Their existence MUST NOT make low-level plumbing the normal or documented path for ordinary game logic.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Intuitive API design contract
requirements.text: API design quality MUST include human and AI interpretability: a competent developer or model SHOULD normally be able to infer the purpose of a high-level operation from its name, target type and typed parameters without reading engine implementation details.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Shared and individual state semantics
requirements.text: Games MUST use shared and individual as the canonical high-level state/replication qualifiers.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Shared and individual state semantics
requirements.text: The aliases shar and indiv MUST be accepted as equivalent shorthand where the Games language/parser supports these declarations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Shared and individual state semantics
requirements.text: The runtime handles the required identity, replication and join/reconciliation plumbing.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Shared and individual state semantics
requirements.text: The API SHOULD infer natural scope when it is unambiguous so developers do not repeatedly specify individual for obviously per-player state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Shared and individual state semantics
requirements.text: The high-level model MUST avoid forcing developers to maintain maps keyed by PlayerID merely to represent ordinary per-player state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Multiplayer/replication intent
requirements.text: For ordinary gameplay, developers SHOULD specify desired state, ownership and visibility rather than manually implement RPC direction, player-ID dictionaries, replication callbacks, joining-player reconstruction, local/server copies and reconciliation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Multiplayer/replication intent
requirements.text: High-level operations such as Door.Open(shared), UI.Show(LevelComplete, individual), Inventory.Give(Key, individual) or a shared world-state update SHOULD compile/route into the appropriate authoritative replication mechanism.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Multiplayer/replication intent
requirements.text: Games MUST still expose advanced networking primitives for specialised games, but high-level APIs are authoritative for common development and MUST remain deterministic, inspectable and debuggable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Declarative keybind system
requirements.text: Games MUST provide a canonical human-readable keybinding definition file, provisionally named keybinds.cui, that is understood by the editor, runtime, CUI APIs, visual graphs, Dulche and generated settings UI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Declarative keybind system
requirements.text: Keybind definitions MUST be semantic rather than hard-wired gameplay code.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Declarative keybind system
requirements.text: shared Keybind means the declared binding is common for the applicable game/profile scope. individual Keybind means each player may have a separately resolved/remappable binding. shar and indiv are accepted shorthand.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Declarative keybind system
requirements.text: Games SHOULD support readable controller-layout names rather than forcing numeric button indices, including semantic/positional forms such as Controller.Letters.Down, Controller.Letters.Left, bumpers, triggers, D-pad, LeftStick and RightStick.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Declarative keybind system
requirements.text: Composite input shorthand MUST be supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Declarative keybind system
requirements.text: A declaration equivalent to shared Keybind Movement { Keyboard(WASD); Controller(LeftStick); } MUST produce one typed movement input rather than four unrelated actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Declarative keybind system
requirements.text: Keybind consumption MUST be simple.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Declarative keybind system
requirements.text: Corresponding release/hold/value-change/input events SHOULD follow the same readable event family.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Declarative keybind system
requirements.text: The input subsystem MUST resolve device hot-swap, keyboard/controller/touch source, player ownership, remapping, persistence and appropriate input value types without requiring ordinary gameplay code to poll physical devices.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Declarative keybind system
requirements.text: Individual/remappable bindings MUST have ready-made CUI settings components for rebinding, conflict detection, reset-to-default, clearing, device-specific display and per-player persistence.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Declarative keybind system
requirements.text: Duplicate bindings MAY be legal; conflicts in the same active context should warn rather than be silently rejected.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Declarative keybind system
requirements.text: The system SHOULD support input contexts, chords/combinations and typed analogue/gesture inputs without requiring developers to build timing/device-selection infrastructure from scratch.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Prebuilt object and gameplay library
requirements.text: Games MUST ship an optional, substantial first-party library of production-usable drag-and-drop entities, components and complete gameplay systems so creators can begin with working mechanics rather than blank scenes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Prebuilt object and gameplay library
requirements.text: The library MUST include at least a configurable basic/stick-man-style player character with full movement, crouch, jump, sprint and swimming support; starter vehicles including a car, plane, boat and submarine; environmental systems including water and lava; and common interactive/world primitives.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Prebuilt object and gameplay library
requirements.text: Starter content MUST be fully usable without opening its implementation, while remaining inspectable, extensible and replaceable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Prebuilt object and gameplay library
requirements.text: It MUST NOT be a set of disconnected demos or opaque sample projects.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Prebuilt object and gameplay library
requirements.text: The standard Player Character inspector MUST expose substantial high-level configuration rather than only speed/jump toggles.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Prebuilt object and gameplay library
requirements.text: It SHOULD expose at least Movement Speed, Acceleration, Sprint Speed, Limited Stamina, Stamina Level/Maximum, per-action stamina consumption for walking/sprinting/jumping/crouching/swimming where applicable, Stamina Replenish Delay, Stamina Replenish rate, Crouch Speed, Jump Height, Air Control, Can Sprint, Can Crouch, Can Jump and Can Swim, plus appropriate advanced movement/collision settings.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Prebuilt object and gameplay library
requirements.text: Inspector sections MUST progressively reveal dependent settings.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Prebuilt object and gameplay library
requirements.text: Disabling Limited Stamina SHOULD hide/de-emphasise irrelevant stamina controls; disabling Crouch SHOULD collapse crouch-only parameters.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Prebuilt object and gameplay library
requirements.text: An Advanced disclosure SHOULD expose expert parameters without turning the default inspector into an unstructured wall of fields.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Prebuilt object and gameplay library
requirements.text: Starter vehicles MUST similarly expose meaningful tuning such as acceleration, maximum speed, braking, steering response, traction, suspension/buoyancy/aerodynamic values and feature toggles appropriate to the vehicle type.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Prebuilt object and gameplay library
requirements.text: Water SHOULD expose working swimming/buoyancy/current/wave/underwater behaviour and integrate automatically with compatible Player/vehicle components.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Prebuilt object and gameplay library
requirements.text: Lava SHOULD expose fluid-like behaviour where desired plus damage/ignition/heat/visual properties.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Prebuilt object and gameplay library
requirements.text: Built-in environment systems MUST interoperate through shared typed contracts rather than custom one-off scripts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Prebuilt object and gameplay library
requirements.text: The library SHOULD also include reusable systems such as health/damage, inventory, interaction, quests, dialogue, checkpoints, save/load, respawning, teams, rounds, scoring, racing, pickups, simple AI/navigation and common multiplayer/lobby/spectator features.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Prebuilt object and gameplay library
requirements.text: Each applicable built-in entity MUST expose a contextual catalogue of optional first-party CUI feature components that the creator can enable through simple checkboxes/toggles.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Prebuilt object and gameplay library
requirements.text: For Player Character, examples MUST include optional components such as Double Jump and Ragdoll Properties/behaviour, and SHOULD include other appropriate features such as Fall Damage, Mantling, Climbing, Sliding, Wall Running, Dash, Stamina, Oxygen, Footsteps, Head Bob, Camera Shake, Interaction, Inventory, Health, Regeneration, Knockback, Swimming and other mature starter behaviours.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Prebuilt object and gameplay library
requirements.text: Enabling an optional component MUST add/activate the corresponding CUI component and reveal its configurable properties.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Prebuilt object and gameplay library
requirements.text: Double Jump, for example, SHOULD be able to expose maximum jumps, second-jump height, reset rules, stamina cost and contextual restrictions without requiring the creator to open code.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Prebuilt object and gameplay library
requirements.text: Ragdoll SHOULD be able to expose activation conditions, body/joint behaviour, collision, recovery and replication-related settings while relying on native skeleton/physics primitives underneath.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Prebuilt object and gameplay library
requirements.text: Native engine components SHOULD be reserved for fundamental high-performance primitives and engine facilities such as transforms, identity, core rendering, low-level physics/collision, audio primitives, input routing, replication primitives, navigation and animation/runtime infrastructure.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Prebuilt object and gameplay library
requirements.text: Higher-level authored gameplay behaviours MUST use editable CUI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Prebuilt object and gameplay library
requirements.text: First-party CUI components MUST expose source code to the project/user according to the 9to1 open-source distribution model and MUST be usable unchanged, parameter-tuned, extended, duplicated/forked or replaced by developer code.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Prebuilt object and gameplay library
requirements.text: Custom developer CUI components MUST participate in the same inspector and discovery model as first-party components.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Prebuilt object and gameplay library
requirements.text: A developer-defined component compatible with Player SHOULD be able to appear in the same contextual component picker with automatically generated CUI settings for eligible exposed properties.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Prebuilt object and gameplay library
requirements.text: Component metadata MUST support dependencies, compatibility, stable identity/version, display name/category, exposed settings, events/actions and migration information.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Prebuilt object and gameplay library
requirements.text: When enabling a component requires another component, Games SHOULD offer to enable the dependency rather than leave a silently broken configuration.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Prebuilt object and gameplay library
requirements.text: Disabling an optional component SHOULD preserve its configuration by default so re-enabling restores it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Component inspector generation
requirements.text: CUI components MUST be able to declare user-editable settings through concise metadata/attributes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Component inspector generation
requirements.text: Games MUST generate a polished CUI inspector automatically for standard supported property types rather than requiring every component author to build a bespoke editor panel.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Component inspector generation
requirements.text: Metadata SHOULD support user-facing name, description/help, units, numeric ranges/steps, enum choices, grouping, advanced disclosure, conditional visibility, asset/entity pickers, validation and safe defaults.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Component inspector generation
requirements.text: Auto-generated inspectors MUST remain overrideable/extensible when a component genuinely requires a specialised editor.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Component events and state
requirements.text: Reusable components MUST publish semantic typed events and inspectable state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Component events and state
requirements.text: For example, a character component SHOULD be able to expose events such as Jump, SprintStart, SprintEnd, StaminaEmpty, EnterWater and LeaveWater plus readable state such as IsSprinting, IsCrouching, IsSwimming and Stamina.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Component events and state
requirements.text: Consumers MUST be able to subscribe through CUI, visual graphs and Dulche-compatible typed actions without inspecting private implementation fields.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Component versioning and project safety
requirements.text: First-party library components MUST be versioned.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Component versioning and project safety
requirements.text: Existing projects MUST NOT silently change behaviour merely because the globally installed library was updated.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Component versioning and project safety
requirements.text: Projects MAY pin component versions and receive explicit migration/upgrade flows with change previews where practical.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Component versioning and project safety
requirements.text: Creators MUST be able to fork a first-party component into project-owned code.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Component versioning and project safety
requirements.text: Once forked, it becomes project-owned and MUST NOT be overwritten by later library updates.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Rendering and graphics engine
requirements.text: Games MUST invest in a high-end modern rendering stack capable of producing visually exceptional games and rendered scenes rather than treating rendering as donor parity only.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Rendering and graphics engine
requirements.text: The engine SHOULD independently implement capabilities comparable in outcome to modern virtualised-geometry and dynamic-global-illumination systems without copying proprietary source code, algorithms that are not legally available, trademarks as product features or confidential implementation detail.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Rendering and graphics engine
requirements.text: Rendering goals SHOULD include highly scalable detailed geometry, automated/low-touch LOD handling, GPU-driven rendering where beneficial, visibility/occlusion systems, geometry streaming/clustering as appropriate, dynamic global illumination, indirect lighting, reflections, modern shadows, temporal reconstruction/upscaling, large-world rendering, physically based materials and predictable profiling/quality controls.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Rendering and graphics engine
requirements.text: Creators SHOULD be able to achieve high geometric detail with much less manual LOD authoring than conventional pipelines while retaining explicit expert control when needed.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Rendering and graphics engine
requirements.text: Every advanced renderer feature MUST expose truthful hardware/platform capability detection, quality fallbacks, performance diagnostics and deterministic project settings.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Rendering and graphics engine
requirements.text: Unsupported hardware MUST degrade gracefully rather than silently producing broken scenes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Landscape, world and procedural tools
requirements.text: Games MUST provide first-class landscape/world creation rather than requiring an external terrain package for normal use.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Landscape, world and procedural tools
requirements.text: Landscape tooling SHOULD include sculpting, smoothing, erosion-style operations, heightmaps, layers, splines, roads, rivers, lakes/oceans, biome painting, foliage, procedural scattering, world/region streaming, large-world coordinates, landscape collision/navigation generation and runtime deformation where supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Landscape, world and procedural tools
requirements.text: Procedural world generation MUST be able to use the shared graph editor infrastructure through a dedicated generation GraphType with terrain/foliage/geometry/scatter/environment nodes and a specialised generation runtime.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Landscape, world and procedural tools
requirements.text: World tools MUST integrate with the canonical scene graph, materials, physics, navigation, Files/assets, Dulche and build/export pipeline.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Material and shader tools
requirements.text: Games MUST provide a strong native material/shader authoring environment using the shared graph infrastructure with a dedicated material/shader GraphType and renderer/compiler backend.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Material and shader tools
requirements.text: The material system SHOULD support reusable functions/subgraphs, instances, parameters, layers, procedural inputs, normal/displacement workflows, physically based shading, transparency, subsurface/clearcoat/anisotropy where the renderer supports them, decals, terrain materials, preview scenes and performance/complexity diagnostics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Material and shader tools
requirements.text: The beginner path MUST support high-quality materials without requiring shader source code.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Material and shader tools
requirements.text: Experts MUST retain access to lower-level shader code and advanced render hooks where supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Integrated Blender-derived modelling
requirements.text: Games MUST provide built-in professional modelling tools derived from Blender and redesigned/integrated for the Games workflow rather than behaving as a loosely launched external application.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Integrated Blender-derived modelling
requirements.text: The modelling environment SHOULD cover mesh modelling, selection modes, transform/extrude/bevel/inset workflows, modifiers, sculpting, retopology, UV editing, texture/vertex painting, rigging, weight painting, animation, procedural/geometry workflows, simulations and high-quality rendering/compositing capabilities where appropriate.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Integrated Blender-derived modelling
requirements.text: CUI interaction and contextual tooling SHOULD make common modelling tasks substantially easier to discover and perform than raw donor workflows while preserving advanced depth for expert users.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Integrated Blender-derived modelling
requirements.text: A selected scene asset SHOULD be editable in the modelling workspace and returned to the same canonical asset/scene relationship without manual export/import round trips.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Integrated Blender-derived modelling
requirements.text: Changes MUST flow through the normal asset revision/undo/source-control model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Integrated Blender-derived modelling
requirements.text: Creation/Rendering mode MUST be useful as a standalone modelling/rendering application.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Integrated Blender-derived modelling
requirements.text: A user MUST be able to create, model, light, animate and render an asset/scene even when the project contains no playable game logic.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Asset pipeline and cross-app integration
requirements.text: Games MUST integrate with Files as the canonical 9to1 file/project substrate where applicable and SHOULD integrate cleanly with Picture, Wave and other media/creation apps for textures, images, audio/video and generated assets without unnecessary duplicate exports.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Asset pipeline and cross-app integration
requirements.text: Assets MUST have stable identity, source/import settings, derived/cache state and dependency tracking.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Asset pipeline and cross-app integration
requirements.text: Reimport MUST preserve intentional scene/component references wherever possible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Asset pipeline and cross-app integration
requirements.text: Build integration SHOULD provide source-control-aware project workflows, diffs where semantically possible, branches and code review without corrupting binary/derived asset state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Asset pipeline and cross-app integration
requirements.text: Terminal MUST expose supported Godot/Games CLI/build/export workflows.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Dulche in Games
requirements.text: Dulche MUST operate semantically through Games APIs and project data.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Dulche in Games
requirements.text: It SHOULD be able to answer questions such as why a character falls through a floor, create or modify typed scene components, tune exposed parameters, create scripts, diagnose errors, analyse profiler output, modify materials/graphs, assemble starter systems and perform authorised project edits.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Dulche in Games
requirements.text: Dulche MUST prefer existing first-party/native components over generating redundant custom implementations when they satisfy the user's request.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Dulche in Games
requirements.text: If a user asks for a third-person character that can sprint, crouch and swim, Dulche SHOULD assemble/configure the applicable existing components rather than reinventing those systems in new code.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Dulche in Games
requirements.text: AI-generated Games changes MUST remain inspectable through normal scene/script/graph diffs and undo/revision mechanisms.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Dulche in Games
requirements.text: AI assistance MUST NOT create hidden state that cannot be reproduced through supported project structures.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Build, run, debug and export
requirements.text: Games MUST preserve mature Godot-derived project run/debug/export capability and improve it where required for the 9to1 workflow.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Build, run, debug and export
requirements.text: Running a game, running the current scene, attaching a debugger, breakpoints, errors, remote scene inspection, profiler data and platform export MUST remain first-class.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Build, run, debug and export
requirements.text: The editor MUST clearly separate editor state from running-game state while allowing safe live inspection and supported hot-edit/hot-reload behaviour.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Build, run, debug and export
requirements.text: Export targets SHOULD preserve applicable mature donor platform coverage subject to the selected donor revision, platform SDK/licence availability and 9to1 release support.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Build, run, debug and export
requirements.text: Unsupported export targets MUST be reported truthfully rather than exposed as fake buttons.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Relationship with Play
requirements.text: A Games project MAY explicitly expose a typed Play-compatible interface so Dulche Agents can participate through purpose-built game actions/state.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Relationship with Play
requirements.text: Generic Computer Use MUST NOT be used as a hidden fallback for controlling arbitrary game executables, anti-cheat surfaces or unsupported games.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Games API families
requirements.text: Games MUST expose typed API families for projects, scenes/entities/nodes/components, resources/assets, transforms, gameplay state, input/keybinds, graphs, UI/CUI Visual Builder, materials, animation, physics, navigation, audio, rendering, landscapes/worlds, modelling integration, build/run/debug/export and component-library discovery/installation/configuration.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Games API families
requirements.text: High-level APIs and advanced APIs MUST remain clearly layered.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Games API families
requirements.text: The existence of a low-level API MUST NOT allow implementation agents to omit the intuitive high-level operation required by this specification.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Games API families
requirements.text: Every mutation MUST use stable identities, structured results, revision/conflict semantics and the global Home permission/audit model where actions cross normal trust boundaries.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Failure and recovery
requirements.text: Games MUST preserve project integrity across editor crashes, failed imports, failed builds, hot-reload errors, graph compilation errors, component upgrade failures and interrupted modelling/render operations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Failure and recovery
requirements.text: Autosave/recovery MUST NOT silently overwrite a newer valid source revision.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Failure and recovery
requirements.text: Errors MUST identify the relevant ProjectID/SceneID/EntityID/ComponentID/GraphID/AssetID and provide actionable context.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Failure and recovery
requirements.text: High-level APIs MUST return structured errors rather than swallowing engine exceptions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Failure and recovery
requirements.text: Component/library upgrades, donor migrations and project format migrations MUST be transactional or recoverable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Failure and recovery
requirements.text: A failed migration MUST leave the previous valid project state recoverable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Games > Acceptance requirements
requirements.text: Games is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage proves at least: a real maintained Godot-derived engine/editor; native CUI rebuild; Development and standalone Creation/Rendering workflows; deeply integrated Blender-derived modelling; CUI Visual Builder game UI; canonical scene graph and purposeful components; shared node infrastructure with Automations plus specialised graph runtimes; exclusive CUI application/gameplay authoring; absence of public GDScript dependency; verified typed native-adapter interoperability; intuitive high-level APIs; shared/individual plus shar/indiv semantics; declarative keybinds and Event.KeyPress-style semantic input; robust per-player remapping; configurable starter Player with detailed movement/stamina/swim controls; contextual optional CUI components including Double Jump and Ragdoll; custom CUI component inspector integration; starter car/plane/boat/submarine; water/lava environment systems; reusable gameplay systems; high-end rendering; strong landscape/procedural tools; strong materials/shaders; semantic Dulche operation; safe project/version migration; mature run/debug/export; and explicit separation from Play.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Play > Game definitions and matches
requirements.text: A GameDefinition describes reusable game rules/configuration and MUST have stable GameDefinitionID plus version/revision.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Play > Game definitions and matches
requirements.text: It MAY define title/description/category, contestant limits/roles, teams, rounds/turn structure, state schema, visibility rules, available typed actions, timing policy, scoring/judging policy, win/elimination conditions, capability profile, UI/Generative UI definition, model requirements and template provenance.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Play > Game definitions and matches
requirements.text: A Match is one concrete execution of a GameDefinition and MUST have stable MatchID, GameDefinitionID/GameRevision, Contestants, MatchState, current round/turn, scores, timing state, judge policy, visibility policy, status, ActionGraphID, created/updated timestamps and recovery/checkpoint metadata where supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Play > Game definitions and matches
requirements.text: Later edits to the game definition MUST NOT silently alter an in-progress Match.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Play > Contestants
requirements.text: Every contestant MUST have stable ContestantID within the Match and a contestant type such as Human, DulcheAgent or SessionAgent.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Play > Contestants
requirements.text: Agent contestants MAY additionally reference canonical AgentID/DefinitionRevision or a session-scoped temporary Agent configuration, model policy, team, display identity, score/status and applicable game capability profile.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Play > Contestants
requirements.text: Play MUST NOT clone them into private Play Agents.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Play > Contestants
requirements.text: They MAY have name/personality/strategy/model configuration for the Match but MUST NOT become permanent Den Agents unless the user explicitly saves/promotes them.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Play > Contestants
requirements.text: Play MAY provide built-in contestant archetypes such as careful/accurate, fast/risky or balanced where appropriate.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Play > Contestants
requirements.text: Such behavioural profiles may influence strategy/timing but MUST NOT alter objective truth, answer keys or hidden game rules.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Play > Contestant selection and automatic filling
requirements.text: Game setup MUST support manual contestant selection from available Dulche Agents plus automatic creation/filling of remaining SessionAgent slots.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Play > Contestant selection and automatic filling
requirements.text: The user may specify opponent count, model/Agent mix, team structure and broad difficulty/strategy policy where the GameDefinition supports it.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Play > Contestant selection and automatic filling
requirements.text: Play MAY support model-vs-model style matches by assigning different explicit model policies to SessionAgent contestants, provided each still participates through the same contestant/action contract.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Play > Contestant selection and automatic filling
requirements.text: The UI MUST disclose the effective model/Agent configuration when that distinction is relevant to the game.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Play > Isolation, visibility and fairness
requirements.text: Play MUST enforce contestant-specific context isolation at the runtime/data layer rather than relying only on instructions such as 'do not cheat'.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Play > Isolation, visibility and fairness
