requirements.text: Always-active AI is a configurable service mode and MUST NOT grant blanket access to microphone, files, external services or other sensitive capabilities.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > AI-aware RAM optimisation
requirements.text: The default OS must be aggressively memory-efficient without sacrificing specified functionality or quality so local models can use more of the machine. 9to1-OS should lazy-load non-critical services/surfaces, suspend or trim eligible inactive apps, reclaim caches, use appropriate compression/zram and memory mapping, avoid duplicated runtime state and unload inactive models/compatibility environments when policy permits.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > AI-aware RAM optimisation
requirements.text: An optional Prioritise AI memory policy may reclaim eligible caches/background apps/models more aggressively to make room for a requested local model.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > AI-aware RAM optimisation
requirements.text: Dulche/runtime should report what can be reclaimed and coordinate with the OS resource manager rather than simply failing at the first memory-pressure condition.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > GUI-first administration
requirements.text: Common useful system-administration operations that Ubuntu frequently exposes primarily through Terminal SHOULD have first-party CUI.NET workflows wherever they can be represented safely and coherently.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > GUI-first administration
requirements.text: Terminal remains fully available for advanced/unrestricted workflows, but ordinary maintenance must not require memorising shell commands.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > GUI-first administration
requirements.text: Friendly GUIs should call stable typed system services/APIs rather than merely concatenate opaque shell strings.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > GUI-first administration
requirements.text: Where a shell tool is the only practical backend, arguments must be structured, privilege requirements declared and output/errors/progress handled safely.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Terminal safety and privileged destructive operations
requirements.text: The warning should identify resolved targets and expected consequence where feasible.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Terminal safety and privileged destructive operations
requirements.text: Script/program execution cannot be perfectly predicted; recognised dangerous privileged operations should still pass through the system safety broker where technically possible, without claiming semantic proof over arbitrary executable code.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Multiple users and administrator policy
requirements.text: Enforcement MUST occur below the normal app UI so renaming a binary, launching through Go/Terminal/Shelf or invoking an Agent does not trivially bypass policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Multiple users and administrator policy
requirements.text: Managed restrictions must be visible and attributable ('Managed by administrator/school policy') rather than presented as broken UI.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Multiple users and administrator policy
requirements.text: Administrators require auditability of policy changes and clear recovery controls; administration must not silently expose another user's private content unless an explicit policy/capability legitimately grants that access.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > First-party apps and deep OS integration
requirements.text: First-party apps MUST behave as native OS components and register applicable typed integration with Go, Automations, Dulche, notifications, taskbar/layers, Desktop Spaces, widgets, system search/indexing, Files/open-with/default apps, share/clipboard/drag-drop, URI routes, permissions, External App Integrations, background tasks, crash/System Log, updates, backup/recovery, theming/accessibility and resource management.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > First-party apps and deep OS integration
requirements.text: Automations is a particularly strong integration requirement: apps should expose supported typed triggers/actions/events through the shared Automation framework rather than implementing incompatible private automation engines.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > First-party apps and deep OS integration
requirements.text: First-party apps should expose lifecycle information allowing safe trim/suspend/resume under memory pressure without losing unsaved work.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Setup and first-run experience
requirements.text: 9to1-OS MUST provide a friendly graphical CUI.NET installer and first-run/OOBE experience.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Setup and first-run experience
requirements.text: A normal installation MUST NOT require interacting with the traditional Linux text/terminal installer or memorising shell commands.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Setup and first-run experience
requirements.text: Advanced/technical options may be exposed through expandable UI without making them mandatory for ordinary users.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Setup and first-run experience
requirements.text: The setup flow should cover applicable language/region, keyboard, accessibility from the first screen, networking, installation target/disk choices, encryption, timezone, user creation and administrator role, optional managed school/organisation setup, privacy/telemetry choices, update preferences, restore from an existing 9to1 backup/profile, initial appearance/Desktop-Space choices and optional Dulche/model/provider onboarding.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Setup and first-run experience
requirements.text: Critical-stage failure MUST NOT be presented as successful installation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Recovery environments
requirements.text: It should expose Continue/boot normally, automatic startup repair, restore a previous healthy snapshot, undo the latest system update, safe mode, package/system repair, filesystem/disk checks, disable problematic drivers or shell extensions, recover/reset shell configuration, inspect System Log, backup/restore, advanced Terminal and supported repair/reinstall-with-data-preservation flows.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Recovery environments
requirements.text: The stock/default recovery path MUST remain available as an emergency fallback if the custom CUI recovery environment is damaged or cannot launch.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Recovery environments
requirements.text: The custom and stock recovery paths must obey the existing boot-safety contract: ordinary snapshot restore, repair and rollback do not rewrite firmware or bootloader code.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > System updates, recovery and backups
requirements.text: Terminal/package-manager commands remain optional advanced interfaces, never the required normal update path.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > System updates, recovery and backups
requirements.text: The system should confirm successful boot/health before retiring rollback state and provide a friendly recovery environment with restore previous snapshot, repair OS/package database, safe mode, diagnostic logs and extension/driver disablement.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > System updates, recovery and backups
requirements.text: Ordinary backup/snapshot restoration and update rollback MUST NOT overwrite or restore firmware or bootloader code as part of the rollback transaction.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Software and package management
requirements.text: It may show multiple sources for the same product and explain meaningful differences instead of silently choosing an arbitrary provider.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > System Log and crash diagnostics
requirements.text: Crash records should group repeated failures, support export/diagnostic bundles and permit user-authorised Dulche analysis such as explaining why a component repeatedly crashed.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > System Log and crash diagnostics
requirements.text: Diagnostic information MUST NOT be silently uploaded.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Task Manager and other donor-backed utilities
requirements.text: The same donor fallback rule applies to Settings and other required CUI system utilities when an appropriate Ubuntu/GNOME app exists and no different donor has already been assigned.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Search and AI modes
requirements.text: AI mode MUST NOT fabricate applications, files, settings or entities that do not exist and MUST surface ambiguity when multiple plausible targets remain.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Universal provider model
requirements.text: Providers may expose search, suggestions, recent items, result categories, previews, aliases, quick actions, indexing/change notifications and query-time-only results.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Universal provider model
requirements.text: Go may search applications, files/folders, settings, people/contacts, LLM Spaces/conversations where authorised, Boards, Planner tasks/events, Maps places, Shelf items/collections, Build repositories/branches, Build projects, browser history/bookmarks where enabled, installed tools, Plugins/extensions and registered system actions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Canonical identity
requirements.text: Its local index may cache identifiers, search fields, aliases, presentation metadata, permissions and freshness state, but MUST NOT create a competing canonical copy of a file, document, project, place, person or other result merely because it is searchable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Ranking and context
requirements.text: Ranking may combine exact/prefix/fuzzy match, aliases, keywords, recency, frequency, pins/favourites, current app, active project, current canonical object, Desktop Space, user-enabled Background Learning and provider relevance.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Typed actions
requirements.text: Go may invoke these actions directly where appropriate but MUST NOT reproduce another app's private business logic.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Filters and previews
requirements.text: Go supports optional user-selectable filters/categories such as Apps, Files, People, Settings, Places, Projects and Actions plus provider-defined categories where useful.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Filters and previews
requirements.text: Results may expose compact CUI previews supplied from canonical provider data.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Indexing, privacy and freshness
requirements.text: Search results MUST be permission-filtered before display, including for restricted folders/projects, managed user profiles and lock-screen contexts.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Indexing, privacy and freshness
requirements.text: Stale/offline remote results must be marked with their freshness state and invalid/deleted results removed rather than accumulating as zombie entries.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Scoped reuse
requirements.text: The same Go framework may be embedded as a scoped picker/search surface in Launcher, Files, Shelf and other apps, and Dulche may query Go for authorised entity discovery.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Performance and failure isolation
requirements.text: Opening Go should be effectively immediate.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Performance and failure isolation
requirements.text: Local providers should stream results incrementally; slow remote providers MUST NOT block applications, local files, settings or cached results.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Go acceptance requirements > Universal Model Picker
requirements.text: On 9to1-OS, the Universal Model Picker is the OS-hosted presentation of the same canonical Dulche/Home model/provider state used by regular 9to1. Model identities, provider connections, ordered Model Routes, active/background routing, category overrides, fallbacks, permissions and usage state MUST remain interoperable across Home and 9to1-OS rather than becoming separate OS-only configuration.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Go acceptance requirements > Universal Model Picker
requirements.text: 9to1-OS may host the picker natively while Windows regular 9to1 hosts it through Home, but both clients MUST read/write the same versioned routing contracts and Dulche model catalogue.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > OS resource and policy integration
requirements.text: When a selected local model requires additional memory, the picker integrates with the 9to1-OS resource broker to show required/available/reclaimable RAM/VRAM and may request permitted reclamation before declaring the model unavailable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > OS resource and policy integration
requirements.text: It MUST distinguish Installed, Unloaded, Loading, Loaded, Offloaded/Partially loaded where supported and Unavailable due to resources.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > OS resource and policy integration
requirements.text: Model ordering MUST never bypass those restrictions; policy-ineligible candidates are filtered before route selection.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Shared-routing invariant
requirements.text: Requests from regular 9to1/Home and 9to1-OS use the same eligibility-first routing semantics: determine required capabilities and policy constraints, filter the configured route, then choose the highest-priority eligible available model and fall through only on classified model/provider-routing conditions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Compatibility backends
requirements.text: Additional compatible backends MAY be registered later through the same framework.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Automatic package routing
requirements.text: Opening or double-clicking a supported foreign application package MUST route through the compatibility framework automatically.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Automatic package routing
requirements.text: Executable/package type should be determined from trusted file metadata/signature/MIME inspection where available rather than relying only on filename extension.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Automatic package routing
requirements.text: When there is one clear eligible default, routing should proceed without unnecessary questions.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Automatic package routing
requirements.text: When multiple viable frameworks exist or the user requests control, the UI may ask which framework/backend to use.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Per-application framework defaults
requirements.text: If the selected backend cannot satisfy the app, the framework reports why and may offer other eligible backends rather than silently executing through an unrelated path.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Per-application framework defaults
requirements.text: Global defaults may exist for Windows packages and APK packages, but per-app rules take precedence where valid.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Windows: Wine path
requirements.text: Ordinary users MUST NOT need to manually run winecfg, winetricks, edit registry state or construct WINEPREFIX environment variables.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Windows: Wine path
requirements.text: Advanced views may expose equivalent controls and raw technical details when useful.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Windows: Wine path
requirements.text: Applications SHOULD normally use isolated managed Wine environments so dependency/runtime changes, repair, backup and uninstall do not corrupt unrelated apps.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Windows: Wine path
requirements.text: Applications may deliberately share an environment when required, but that relationship must be explicit.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Windows: WinBoat-style environment path
requirements.text: It may expose configurable CPU, RAM, storage, hardware acceleration, networking, shared folders, USB/device passthrough, graphics configuration and individual-app/RemoteApp-style window integration where supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Windows: WinBoat-style environment path
requirements.text: Individual Windows applications should appear as normal 9to1-OS windows where technically possible; a full Windows desktop remains available as a fallback/advanced mode.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Android/APK compatibility path
requirements.text: 9to1-OS MUST support Android APK applications through the same Compatibility Framework using an Android/APK compatibility layer.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Android/APK compatibility path
requirements.text: Android applications should participate in Go, taskbar/taskbar layers, window switching, Desktop Spaces, notifications, Files/open-with/share flows, Shelf and other applicable 9to1-OS integrations.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Android/APK compatibility path
requirements.text: The Android compatibility layer MUST NOT require the user to launch a separate Android desktop merely to start an installed APK unless a full Android environment is explicitly requested.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Android/APK compatibility path
requirements.text: The user may choose a backend and persist it for that Android app; otherwise 9to1 selects the highest-priority eligible configured default.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Unified installation experience
requirements.text: Opening a supported .exe, .msi, .apk or other registered foreign package invokes a single compatibility installation flow showing detected application/package identity, recommended backend, destination environment, required permissions, storage/resource estimate and relevant compatibility warnings.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Unified installation experience
requirements.text: The GUI package manager may also install Windows software through Winget or other approved Windows sources and Android packages through approved configured package sources where supported.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Native-feeling OS integration
requirements.text: Compatibility apps may expose Automations/Dulche actions only through typed supported bridges.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Graphics, gaming and input
requirements.text: Windows or Android games can integrate with Gaming Desktop Space telemetry/controls where the backend exposes the required data.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Resource and lifecycle management
requirements.text: Compatibility environments must preserve application/user state safely across suspend/resume and OS memory pressure.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Resource and lifecycle management
requirements.text: The OS MUST NOT simply terminate a managed environment and discard unsaved guest/application state to satisfy a memory target.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Snapshots, repair and updates
requirements.text: Backends supporting snapshots/checkpoints should expose them through the unified manager, particularly before major guest/runtime changes.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Snapshots, repair and updates
requirements.text: Guest Windows/Android update behaviour remains explicit and must not be confused with host OS updates.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Snapshots, repair and updates
requirements.text: Repair/reset operations should be scoped to the selected app/environment and preserve unrelated environments.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Diagnostics and recovery
requirements.text: Dulche may analyse these diagnostics and invoke typed repair/configuration APIs but should not replace a supported manager operation with arbitrary host shell automation.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Managed-user policy
requirements.text: Launching through Go, Files, Shelf, Terminal, Dulche or another app MUST NOT bypass the same compatibility policy.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Compatibility Framework acceptance requirements
requirements.text: The user may choose among eligible frameworks and can persist a default framework per application; valid per-app defaults are remembered and editable.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > 9to1 OS distribution > Compatibility Framework acceptance requirements
requirements.text: Backend-specific complexity remains available for advanced users but is not required for ordinary installation, launch, repair or troubleshooting.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Explicitly deferred scope > Training Lab
requirements.text: Release-candidate AI Studio implementations MUST NOT expose Training Lab as an in-scope project type, navigation/sidebar entry, New Project option or partially functional placeholder.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Open product and release decisions
requirements.text: Visual spacing and proportions may follow the approved mockups and category conventions within confirmed semantics.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Open product and release decisions
requirements.text: DEC-002 — Multi-Agent Chat: participant selection, automatic orchestration and turn-taking policy, and whether humans may participate.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Open product and release decisions
requirements.text: Two differently coloured usage/context measures in one compact progress circle are required; exact geometry remains a visual refinement.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Open product and release decisions
requirements.text: DEC-005 — Assistants and Teams: whether Main may be visibly renamed while keeping its permanent Main role; handoff confirmation/branching details; permanent Team conversation organisation beyond its main group chat; member roster editing/conflict policy; default coordination mode; leader absence/fallback and contested delegation; default All/Relevant/None coordination-chat visibility and edge-case definition of “Relevant”.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Open product and release decisions
requirements.text: Main selection, one durable Main per Assistant, both coordination modes and all three visibility options remain required.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Open product and release decisions
requirements.text: DEC-007 — Shopping: product-versus-offer grouping and user-toggle behaviour; supported merchant/provider integrations; optional price-watch/alert sourcing and display; recommendation disclosure and advanced sorter defaults.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Open product and release decisions
requirements.text: Required/Preferred matching, Direct/Similar/Other tabs, digital product handling and Haven-selected currency conversion remain required.

requirements.section: 9to1 Development Specification v2 > Open product and release decisions
requirements.text: The three views must preserve one canonical Space and must never silently discard configured behaviour.
